title: Defining epidemiologically relevant units of cholera transmission in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Much remains unknown about cholera transmission dynamics in Africa. Applying both traditional phylogeographic techniques and innovative methods for combining epidemiologic and genomic data, we identified three to four distinct “cholera transmission units” within which cross-border cholera transmission has been more frequent. These units can be grouped into two major transmission clusters, one in Western Africa and bordering countries and one spanning the Central, Eastern, and Southern regions. Simulation studies show that these clusters can be used to assess the risk of international spread of introduced cholera strains and identify heterogeneities in the speed of international spread based on outbreak location. Our methods further allow us to infer cholera incidence attributable to specific lineages in the absence of sequencing data. This work has clear implications for cholera control.

title: Dual-discipline or governance decoupling? How corporate governance and ESG disclosure shape the earnings management-financial performance nexus in an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between earnings management (EM) and financial performance (FP) in Vietnamese listed firms, while investigating the moderating roles of corporate governance (CG) and environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure within this nexus. Design/methodology/approach This study employs panel data from 303 non-financial listed firms over the period 2017–2024. A two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimator is applied to address endogeneity, simultaneity bias and dynamic persistence. Marginal effects are estimated to examine how EM affects FP across CG and ESG disclosure levels. Findings The findings show that the effect of EM on FP is contingent upon governance quality and ESG disclosure. When these mechanisms operate jointly, EM is more effectively constrained. Conversely, when ESG disclosure is high but governance quality is weak, the negative impact of EM becomes more pronounced, particularly for real EM. The findings are consistent with an expectation trap mechanism, whereby higher ESG disclosure may increase stakeholder expectations, while misalignment between disclosure and governance is associated with stronger negative market reactions. Overall, the evidence suggests that transparency alone is insufficient without credible internal governance. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by develop…

Evaluating the Geometric Brownian Motion Model for Gold Price Movements (XAU/USD) across Market Conditions
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of the Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) model in predicting prices and estimating the risk of XAU/USD under stable and unstable economic conditions. Daily closing price data are divided into in-sample and out-of-sample periods, where return and volatility parameters are estimated from the in-sample data and applied in Monte Carlo simulations. Prediction accuracy is assessed using the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), while risk is measured using Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). The results indicate that MAPE values exceed 20% in both economic conditions, suggesting that the predictive accuracy of the GBM model remains moderate. Although the model performs slightly better during stable periods, the difference is not statistically significant. In contrast, risk estimation results show that VaR and ES range between 58% and 59%, with higher values observed during unstable periods. This reflects an increase in market risk driven by higher volatility. Overall, the findings suggest that while GBM is capable of capturing the general movement of gold prices, it has limitations in accurately predicting price levels and capturing extreme market fluctuations, particularly during periods of economic instability.

title: Balancing workload and workplace conditions: unlocking employee performance in Indonesia’s service sector
abstract: Purpose: to examine how workload and work environment affect employee performance in service-sector companies in Indonesia. Method: this study employed a quantitative survey approach involving 117 employees from service-sector companies in West Java, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire with a seven-point Likert scale and analyzed using regression analysis, including validity, reliability, collinearity, and hypothesis testing. Findings: workload and work environment have positive and significant effects on employee performance. Workload emerges as a stronger predictor than work environment, while both variables collectively explain a substantial proportion of variations in employee performance. These results highlight the importance of balanced workload distribution and a conducive work environment in improving employee performance in Indonesia's service sector. Implications: organizations should optimize workload distribution according to employee competencies and improve physical and non-physical workplace conditions to strengthen employee performance, productivity, and organizational effectiveness. Originality: lies in providing empirical evidence on the relationships between workload, work environment, and employee performance by integrating job demands–resources theory in the context of service-sector companie…

title: Transforming government through public service universities: an integrative framework for AI-enabled governance capacity
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine when universities with an explicit public-service mission can contribute to artificial intelligence (AI) governance capacity in public organisations. Design/methodology/approach A problem-driven conceptual synthesis integrates public management reform, policy and dynamic capabilities, institutional logics, higher education, boundary work and training transfer. A targeted supplementary literature search supports comparison with the closest explanations. Findings The Intelligent Public Service University (IPSU) framework links mission framing, internal coordination arrangements and four established transfer functions: formation, circulation, translation and embedding. It specifies conditional relationships, not a universal sequence. Agency uptake depends on workplace authority, administrative context, information sensitivity and institutional independence. Proximal capacity is distinguished from public value and from legitimacy, which may also arise symbolically. Research limitations/implications The propositions require comparative and longitudinal testing. The synthesis establishes neither causal effects nor the superiority of any university type or transfer portfolio. Practical implications Universities and agencies can use the framework to diagnose disconnections between education, institutional governance and workplace use, selecting propor…
venue: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy

title: Exploring and Addressing Pre-Service Teachers’ Ability to Correlate Macroscopic Phenomenon with its Microscopic Explanation and Symbolic Representation in Science
abstract: In this research study, the ability of pre- service teachers to correlate macroscopic explanation of scientific phenomenon with its microscopic explanation and representation at symbolic level has been explored and addressed also. Twenty pre service teachers were asked to explain the process of boiling of water, freezing of water and the dissolution of sugar in water at macroscopic, microscopic and symbolic level. The findings revealed that pre service teachers could not correlate the macroscopic explanation with its microscopic explanation and symbolic representation. The limited understanding of pre service teachers with respect to shapes of molecules, molecular geometry and strength of different bonds was addressed. The implications of findings for teacher education program have been discussed.

title: Market Penetration Strategies of Sid’s Farm: Challenges and Solutions in General and Modern Trade in Pune
abstract: A new premium dairy brand has to win over retailers and shoppers before it can count on repeat purchases, and dairy's short shelf life makes that harder. This paper is a descriptive, exploratory case study of how Sid’s Farm tried to do this in two Pune retail channels: General Trade (GT) in Ravet and Modern Trade (MT) at Deli Essentials, Baner. The data come from an on-the-job training placement between 21 May and 21 July 2026, and include face-to-face conversations with retailers and customers, a 53-store retailer audit, and direct observation of merchandising and sampling. In GT, 27 of the 53 retailers approached (50.9%) showed interest, 21 (39.6%) placed a first order, and 13 of those 21 (61.9%) were recorded as reordering. Govind and Amul appeared in 94.3% and 88.7% of audited stores, so a newcomer is clearly competing with entrenched brands. In MT, about 30–35 customer interactions were observed. Price was the main objection, High Protein Curd and Paneer attracted the most interest in a store below a gym, and moving products to the front of the freezer and running two weekend Cow Dahi sampling sessions were followed by purchase interest. Overall, GT penetration was driven by the retailer and hinged on margin, reliable supply, returns support and cold-chain care, while MT penetration was driven by the shopper and hinged on visibility, trial and health-focused messaging. The…

title: How Chinese transnational higher education graduates navigate the domestic labour market by mobilising multiple forms of capital
abstract: Purpose This article investigates how Chinese graduates from transnational higher education (TNHE) programmes navigate the domestic labour market, highlighting how employability is shaped by the mobilisation of human, social, cultural, identity and psychological capital within hierarchical credentialing and employer recognition structures. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on qualitative interviews with twenty TNHE graduates, the study explores how these forms of capital are strategically deployed to negotiate employment opportunities in China. Findings TNHE participation enhances human, cultural, identity and psychological capital, and facilitates the development of programme-mediated weak-tie social capital, while strong-tie family-based social capital remains largely independent of TNHE. However, employability outcomes depend on how graduates strategically mobilise multiple forms of capital in interaction with employer recognition, credential hierarchies and access to social networks. A few graduates remained unemployed, indicating that the capital acquired through TNHE does not automatically translate into labour-market success. Originality/value This study contributes to employability research by showing that TNHE does not uniformly generate employability advantages, but instead shapes how graduates' existing forms of capital are recognised, activated and converted withi…

title: A Study on Market Dynamics, Competitive Landscape, Import Economics and Trading Viability of Bisphenol A and Chloroprene Rubber for Atul Ltd
abstract: India imports almost all of its Bisphenol A (BPA) and Chloroprene Rubber (CR), yet published market reports say little about who imports these chemicals, from where, and at what duty-adjusted cost. This study examines whether bulk import for resale is commercially viable for Atul Ltd., a leading Indian chemicals manufacturer, or whether each material is better used purely as manufacturing feedstock. A descriptive and analytical design was applied to 3,103 cleaned BPA import transactions (approximately 432,700 MT; FY2022–FY2026) and 10,346 cleaned CR shipment lines (100,584 MT; FY2021-22 to FY2025-26), supplemented by secondary market, pricing and regulatory sources. Importers were classified as manufacturers or traders, duty and free-trade-agreement (FTA) structures were mapped by country of origin, and landed-cost and margin models were built from first principles. BPA imports are highly concentrated: Grasim Industries (about 44%) and Atul (about 24%) together hold roughly two-thirds of volume, manufacturers account for about 90%, and about 82% of volume enters duty-free from FTA partners, leaving a pure trading model with an indicative gross margin of only about 0.8%. In CR, Japan supplies 57.9% of imports at zero duty under the India–Japan CEPA, whereas other origins bear a 10% basic customs duty; an indicative resale earns a net margin of about 3.8% on full-duty origins aga…

title: Calidad de servicio en las instituciones educativas de Trujillo
abstract: El objetivo del presente estudio consistió en determinar el nivel de la calidad de servicio en las instituciones educativas de educación básica regular de Trujillo, 2024. Por tal razón, el cuestionario fue usado como instrumento y fueron 100 docentes de la provincia de Trujillo los que participaron como muestra. Los datos recopilados se procesaron usando la estadística descriptiva. Los resultados demostraron que el nivel de la calidad de servicio en las instituciones educativas de educación básica regular de Trujillo, 2024 es excelente; lo cual evidenció que estas brindan un servicio de calidad dentro de lo esperado a los y las estudiantes.

title: Багш мэргэжлээр суралцаж буй оюутнуудын мэргэжлийн сонирхолд үзүүлэх зарим нөлөөллийг судалсан нь
abstract: In the current era of rapid digital transformation and the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education, pre-service teachers are required not only to use information and communication technologies but also to apply AI in educational activities ethically, responsibly, and safely. This study aims to examine how pre-service teachers’ AI and digital ethics competence relates to their teaching competence and teaching interest. The study examined the statistical relationships among AI and digital ethics competence, teaching competence, and teaching interest among 311 pre-service teacher students. Data were collected using a five-point self-assessment questionnaire, and factor and regression analyses were conducted. The results revealed that AI and digital ethics competence was positively associated with both teaching interest and teaching competence, while teaching competence demonstrated a moderate positive relationship with teaching interest. These findings suggest that AI and digital ethics competence may support teaching interest both directly and indirectly through teaching competence. Based on these findings, the study recommends integrating AI, digital ethics, and responsible AI use into teacher education curricula in conjunction with professional pedagogical methods and practical teaching experiences.

title: From Telangana to Berlin: A Case Study of Cross-Border B2B Market Entry, Prospect Development and Multi-Channel Outreach in the European Industrial Battery Sector
abstract: Cross-border business development in specialized industrial markets requires a sequence of research, prospect qualification and relationship-building activities before commercial outcomes can be assessed. This paper examines how an India-based advisory team organized early-stage B2B market development for an industrial battery-sector client targeting European buyers. It adopts a qualitative, descriptive single-case design based on the author's participation in a project undertaken in 2026, supported by non-confidential process documentation and published literature. The case describes four linked activities: industry and market scanning; prospect identification and segmentation; lead-stage management; and coordinated outreach through professional networking, telephone contact and email. Rather than testing channel effectiveness, the study develops an operational account of how these activities can be combined within a small advisory team. Its contribution is a process framework and four propositions for future empirical examination concerning qualification discipline, channel complementarity, contextual adaptation and continuity of documentation. Proprietary prospect records, contact information and campaign outcomes are not disclosed. The paper is therefore an exploratory account of process design, not a statistical evaluation of outreach performance or export success. Keyword…

title: Actitudes hacia la inclusión educativa en estudiantes de formación inicial docente - Trujillo 2026
abstract: La inclusión educativa constituye un desafío vigente en la formación docente, que exige actitudes favorables hacia la diversidad del alumnado. El estudio identificó el nivel de actitudes hacia la Inclusión Educativa en estudiantes de Formación Inicial Docente de los programas de Educación Inicial, Primaria y Secundaria de la Facultad de Educación y Ciencias de la Comunicación de la Universidad Nacional de Trujillo, 2026. Se empleó un enfoque cuantitativo, con un método descriptivo y un diseño no experimental observacional. con una muestra no probabilística de 134 estudiantes del IX ciclo, a quienes se aplicó una escala Likert de 35 ítems validada por juicio de expertos. Los resultados evidencian que el 85,9% presenta un nivel Alto, el 12,6% Medio y el 1,5% Bajo. Educación Primaria registró la mayor proporción en nivel Alto (96,6%) y Educación Inicial la menor (66,7%). Se concluye que la actitud favorable predomina, aunque no garantiza una formación integral para la inclusión.

title: Job-tied accommodation in the UK rental market: a national portrait
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to profile job-tied accommodation in the UK rental market: prevalence, payment terms, location and occupants. Design/methodology/approach This study uses the Annual Population Survey 2024 household data set: 18,001 renting employees in private households, weighted to UK totals. Estimates are occupant-level; the tied item refers to any household member’s job. Findings Tied accommodation houses 4.3% of UK renting employees (about 369,000); four-fifths pay rent. Prevalence peaks in agriculture, among large sectors in public administration and in southern regions outside London. Some 51% of occupants work in managerial, professional or associate-professional roles (39% of others), largely reflecting sector composition. Occupants hold degrees more often (44% versus 37%), are more often partnered and longer-tenured and show no detectable raw pay penalty. Conditional cash pay is 3.5% lower (interval includes zero), and 9% lower in sole-employed households (model-based). There the occupational contrast holds, a commute gap emerges and the degree gap disappears. Research limitations/implications Estimates are cross-sectional and non-causal and exclude communal employer housing. Practical implications In the private-household rental market, employer-linked housing has a disproportionately professional occupant profile and overlaps with key-worker housing. Original…

title: Continuing Professional Development for Filipino Educators: A Systematic Literature Review on PLCs, Reflective Practice, and In-Service Training Models
abstract: Continuous professional development (CPD) under Philippine law and teaching professionalism standards remains underexplored in the literature. The present study synthesizes existing research on CPD for Filipino teachers, its relation to professional communities and learning-enhancement practices, and teachers’ professional development. The PRISMA procedure was used to accurately extract data from a small Scopus dataset. In summary, the study analyzed 177 sources in two stages. 61 empirical studies published or soon to be published were selected for the analysis. Four main themes have been highlighted: (a) While in-service training is fundamentally episodic, lecture-based, and weakly evaluated, needs-based, experiential, and technology-driven training courses are beginning to surface; (b) Professional learning communities, Learning Action Cells, and lesson study are collaborative models that foster collegial and pedagogical progress factor, but performance is hampered by workload issues, leadership dilemmas, and Filipino culture, especially in terms of pakikisama and hiya; (c) while reflective practice can be enriched by means of mentoring during practicum, feedback, and action research, it is never organized or maintained; and (d) the pre-service-in-service continuum lacks coherence and research capacity.

Digital service innovation and ecosystem value co-creation: the moderating role of B2C contexts under service-dominant logic
abstract: Purpose This study investigates digital service innovation as a socio-technical driver of ecosystem value co-creation in manufacturing. Guided by Service-Dominant Logic, it uncovers how digital service innovation – comprising smart interactive services and smart working technologies – enables resource liquefaction and usage-phase co-creation, while examining how market orientation (business-to-consumer versus business-to-business) conditions this relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative analysis was conducted on a sample of 303 manufacturers. Hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling applied to a higher-order construct that captures smart working technologies and smart interactive services through reflective and formative structures. Findings Results confirm that digital service innovation serves as a foundational engine for ecosystem value co-creation. However, business-to-consumer environments significantly amplify this relationship compared to business-to-business settings, where structural inertia and competency barriers create interaction friction. Furthermore, smart working technologies and smart interactive services demonstrate an essential socio-technical synergy. Originality/value This research advances Service-Dominant logic by unpacking digital service innovation from a conceptual black box into a multidimensional…

The authorisation of crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) in the EU under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR)
abstract: As its title denotes, this study develops on the authorisation of crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) in the European Union (EU) under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR). It is structured in three Sections as follows: Section A develops on the relevant provisions of MiCAR relating to the conditions for a person to be allowed to provide crypto-asset services within the EU and the single passport regime (Article 59), as well as the application for authorisation (Article 62 and the related Delegated and Implementing Regulations), and the assessment of that application by national competent authorities (NCAs), leading to the granting or refusal of authorisation (Article 63) in accordance with the “three step” procedure set out in these two Articles. The focus of Section B turns to some specific related provisions, namely, the governance arrangements under Article 68 and the identification, prevention, management and disclosure of conflicts of interest under Article 72. Read together with Articles 62-63, these Articles reflect the MiCAR’s emphasis on effective corporate governance, sound risk management and the mitigation of conflicts of interest as essential safeguards for the provision of crypto-asset services. The concluding remarks are included in Section C.

title: Stakeholder engagement in digital health: a relational, system-level and process-oriented approach
abstract: Purpose The term stakeholder engagement (SE) is widely used in digital health. Yet, empirical research remains fragmented regarding who contributes, how engagement is enacted, and how stakeholder input relates to implementation and governance. This study aims to synthesise this evidence and develop a framework for understanding SE within digitally mediated healthcare services. Design/methodology/approach The study combines a systematic scoping review of 54 empirical studies published up to 31 December 2025 with reflexive thematic analysis and a service research-informed conceptual synthesis. Two consultation workshops involving eight digital health stakeholders refined the framework's conceptual boundaries, internal relationships and contextual relevance. Findings The review identifies four themes: SE framings; recurring stakeholder role–contribution logics; practices ranging from informing to collaborating; and relational, technological, organisational, resource, and institutional conditions shaping engagement. The conceptual synthesis integrates these themes into a three-dimensional framework. The relational dimension connects stakeholder contributions, participatory practices, and decision influence. The system-level dimension configures stakeholder groups, roles, and contributions across interdependent micro, meso, and macro levels. The processual dimension represents SE as…

title: The Functional Role of Personal Data in Digital Service Transactions: Property Implications and Platform Obligations in Private Law
abstract: Abstract Digital services are increasingly supplied in exchange for personal data rather than money. This Article examines the functional role of personal data, using European Union law as its principal doctrinal reference and Vietnam as an illustrative case study. Rather than treating personal data as property, it argues that private law should focus on its functions in digital exchange. Personal data operates as contractual counter-performance, a productive asset, and a source of platform power, generating property-like implications without requiring full propertization. The Article develops a functional private-law framework for platform obligations and contributes to contemporary debates on data-based contractual exchange.

title: El impacto del WOM en la calidad del servicio: estrategias para mejorar la experiencia del cliente
abstract: El presente artículo de revisión examina el impacto del word of mouth (WOM) en la calidad del servicio y propone estrategias basadas en evidencia para mejorar la experiencia del cliente. Mediante un análisis exhaustivo de la literatura científica actual, se destacan los factores que influyen en la generación y propagación del WOM, así como su relación con la percepción de calidad y la satisfacción del cliente. Los hallazgos revelan que el WOM, tanto tradicional como electrónico (e-WOM), ejerce una influencia significativa en el comportamiento del consumidor, las ventas, la lealtad y el desempeño empresarial, superando el impacto de la publicidad tradicional. Se establece una relación bidireccional entre la calidad del servicio y el WOM, mediada por la satisfacción del cliente. El e-WOM impacta directamente en la percepción de la calidad y en las decisiones de compra. Por lo tanto, las estrategias de gestión del WOM deben adaptarse a los nuevos canales digitales y abordar proactivamente la reputación en línea. Las conclusiones respaldan un enfoque holístico que integre la calidad del servicio, la satisfacción del cliente y la gestión estratégica del WOM, tanto tradicional como digital, para obtener una ventaja competitiva significativa, fomentar la lealtad, impulsar las ventas y construir una sólida reputación en el mercado.

title: Antecedents of consumer attitude towards online private label brands: a study of an emerging Asian market
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the digital signals and mechanisms involved in shaping consumer attitude towards online private label brands (OPLBs) in an emerging digital market under conditions of heightened uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach A multi-method design focused on the cosmetics and personal care sector was employed. Study 1 used a survey of 637 OPLBs consumers in Pakistan. Study 2 employed a 2 × 2 experimental design that manipulated social media influencer reputation and heuristic cues (high vs low) and included 232 participants. Findings Social media influencer reputation, consumer confidence and bandwagon positively affect consumer attitude towards OPLBs. While heuristic cues have no direct effect in the survey, experimental evidence shows that they influence attitude under conditions of heightened salience. Across both studies, consumer confidence and bandwagon effect mediate the effects of social media influencer reputation and heuristic cues on consumer attitude towards OPLBs. Originality/value This study extends signaling theory by positioning OPLBs as a distinct digital retail context in which consumers rely heavily on externally observable digital signals. It develops a unified signaling framework explaining how source-based credibility signals and popularity-based engagement signals shape consumer attitude through receiver-side mechanisms of eval…

title: RUNX3-ERG Cooperation Orchestrates Endothelial Gene Regulation and Vascular Homeostasis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcriptional regulation is fundamental to vascular homeostasis, ensuring vessel stability and function. Disruption of this regulation underlies pathological angiogenesis in cancer and vascular malformations. While RUNX3 (Runt-related transcription factor 3), a Runt-domain transcription factor, is established as a tumor suppressor and regulator of lymphocyte development, its role in endothelial cells has remained unknown. METHODS: To define the vascular function of RUNX3, we generated endothelial-specific RUNX3 knockout mice and analyzed postnatal retinal angiogenesis and oxygen-induced retinopathy. Mechanistic insights were obtained through assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing data analysis, coimmunoprecipitation, proximity ligation assay, electrophoretic mobility shift assay, and chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (ChIP-qPCR). RESULTS: Loss of endothelial RUNX3 induced hypersprouting angiogenesis with excessive tip cell formation and reduced DLL4 (delta-like ligand 4) expression. RUNX3 deficiency disrupted vascular integrity by lowering VE-cadherin (vascular endothelial cadherin) and claudin-5 levels, while increasing ICAM1 (intercellular adhesion molecule 1) expression, retinal hemorrhage, and leukocyte infiltration. Implementing Continuous Performance Management For Indonesian Civil Servants After The 2022 Ministerial Regulation: A Systematic Literature Review of Studies Published In 2022–2025
abstract: Ministerial Regulation of Administrative and Bureaucratic Reform Number 6 of 2022 replaced the annual, administrative appraisal of Indonesian civil servants with a continuous cycle of planning, monitoring, performance dialogue, appraisal and follow-up, supported by the electronic performance application e-Kinerja. This study synthesizes empirical evidence on how this reform has been implemented. Following PRISMA 2020, five search strings retrieved 130 records; after removing duplicates and screening, 45 journal articles published between 2022 and 2025 were analyzed thematically. Most studies were qualitative case studies in district and municipal governments, and publication output rose sharply in 2024–2025. Seven themes emerged. The most frequent concerned the readiness of the e-Kinerja system and infrastructure (22 studies), reported benefits for transparency and accountability (18 studies), and limited employee capacity to formulate performance targets (16 studies). Critical findings show that digitalization has not automatically changed performance behavior, performance dialogue is rarely institutionalized, ratings remain vulnerable to formalism and leniency, and the link between ratings and performance-based allowances is not perceived as fair. The review recommends strengthening supervisors' coaching capacity, calibrating ratings across units and conducting more quantitat…

title: Chemical Regulation of Multiscale Crack Healing in Cementitious Materials by Active Components of Crystalline Admixtures
abstract: Abstract Crystalline admixtures facilitate crack self-healing in cementitious materials via precipitation and ion migration, yet the specific chemical roles of individual active components remain poorly understood, limiting insight into the underlying healing mechanisms. To address this issue, sodium carbonate, sodium silicate, and calcium formate were selected as representative active components of crystalline admixtures and comparatively investigated through single-component analysis. The self-healing behavior of mortar was evaluated based on crack width evolution, relative water flow ratio, compressive strength retention, chloride migration coefficient, pore structure characteristics, and the structure and composition of healing products. The results indicated that all three functional admixtures promoted crack healing by inducing precipitation reactions, while exhibiting distinct roles at different scales. Sodium silicate showed the most pronounced effect on internal microcrack healing and pore structure refinement. After preloading and curing, the compressive strength retention of mortar containing sodium silicate increased to 90.4%, and the chloride migration coefficient decreased to 5.43 × 10–12 m2/s, accompanied by a noticeable reduction in large pores. In contrast, calcium formate performed better in macroscopic crack closure. Mortar incorporating calcium formate achie…

title: Direct regulation of a tRNA modification enzyme by ppGpp links stress signaling to translational control and biofilm development
abstract: Transfer RNA (tRNA) modifications influence decoding efficiency and translational fidelity, yet how they are integrated into bacterial signaling networks remains poorly understood. Here, we identify a direct connection between stress signaling and codon-specific translational regulation. We show that the alarmone guanosine tetraphosphate (ppGpp) directly inhibits MnmE (TrmE), a conserved tRNA-modification GTPase required for methylaminomethyl (mnm) modification of wobble uridine. High-resolution ribosome profiling in Bacillus subtilis revealed that loss of MnmE selectively increases ribosome pausing at AAG codons and reprograms translation of a subset of genes, including small open reading frames. Among these is a previously unrecognized AAG-containing leader peptide that controls expression of the biofilm repressor AbrB. Consistent with this mechanism, mnmE mutants exhibit constitutive extracellular matrix production and bypass the biofilm defect of a relA mutant. Together, these findings establish a pathway linking ppGpp signaling, tRNA modification, codon-specific translation, and multicellular development.

title: Beyond Digestion: The Gastrointestinal Tract at the Centre of Metabolic Regulation
abstract: Traditionally, gastrointestinal (GI) and metabolic disease have been considered separate clinical entities with the GI tract viewed primarily as a conduit for digestion and nutrient absorption, while the metabolic regulation was largely attributed to the liver, pancreas, and adipose tissue. Recent evidence, has challenged this distinction and has demonstrated that the intestine functions as a major endocrine, immune, and metabolic organ playing a key role in metabolic health. The emergence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the success of incretin-based therapies, and the metabolic benefits of bariatric interventions highlight the increasingly interconnected nature of gastrointestinal and metabolic health. In this perspective, we propose a gut–metabolic network framework in which the intestine serves as a central integrator linking the metabolic system together. This framework extends beyond the conventional gut–liver axis and helps explain the multisystem effects of contemporary therapies. We discuss key mechanistic pathways, therapeutic convergence between gastroenterology and metabolic medicine, and important gaps in current clinical practice, including limited metabolic phenotyping and fragmented care models. Recognizing the gut as a central regulator of metabolic health may enable more integrated approaches to patient care, research, and t…

title: Canopy conductance regulation and water use strategies in poplar plantations in North China under dry versus wet years
abstract: Canopy conductance ( g c ) is a key physiological and ecohydrological parameter controlling canopy transpiration, stomatal regulation and vegetation–atmosphere carbon–water exchange. However, the extent to which the environmental regulation of g c pathways shifts between contrasting hydroclimatic conditions remains poorly understood. This study investigates the adaptive responses of g c to interannual variability in atmospheric moisture availability, aiming to clarify whether stomatal strategies undergo significant transitions under contrasting hydrological conditions. The study was conducted in a plantation of Populus × euramericana (Dode) Guinier cv.'Zhonglin-46' in Minquan County, Yellow River Basin, China. Sap flow was monitored using the thermal dissipation method, with supporting meteorological data collected from an instrumented flux tower, during the growing seasons of 2022 (dry year) and 2025 (wet year). We systematically compared the temporal dynamics of g c and its differential responses to environmental drivers at both daily and half-hourly scales. Analytical methods included Pearson correlation analysis to examine linear associations, random forest to evaluate the relative importance of environmental factors, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to disentangle direct and indirect effects. title: Reducing blood transfusion vital signs monitoring frequency in a cancer center: a best practice implementation project
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction: Frequent vital signs monitoring during blood transfusion is standard practice to detect adverse reactions. However, intensive monitoring has increased nursing workload without clear added benefit for stable patients. Objective: This project aimed to implement an evidence-based, reduced-frequency vital signs protocol for blood transfusions and evaluate monitoring and documentation compliance during blood transfusion administration in an ambulatory cancer center in Singapore. Methods: Using JBI's seven-phase Evidence Implementation Framework, the team conducted a baseline audit, identified barriers through JBI's Getting Research into Practice (GRiP) approach, implemented change strategies, and conducted follow-up and sustainment audits over 11 months. Outcomes included compliance with monitoring and patient education. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages). Results: Baseline compliance with the existing protocol was 0% (n = 30). After implementation, compliance with the reduced-frequency protocol increased to 60% (n = 30) and reached 100% at sustainment (n = 10). Patient education improved from 17% at baseline to 96% post-implementation and 100% at sustainment. No adverse events were reported during the implementation period. Conclusions: Implementing an evidence-based reduction in vital signs monitoring frequency for …

Analysis of Geometric Transformations in Automatic Door System Response with a Motion Sensor
abstract: Automatic sliding doors are usually studied as electronic systems, yet their motion offers a concrete context for geometric transformations. This study analyses how translation, reflection, and dilation describe the motion of a two-panel automatic sliding door at the main entrance of a shopping mall in Cirebon, Indonesia. The door was observed in 12 sessions over four days, with approximately 10–15 opening–closing cycles recorded per session, and the panel positions and opening widths were documented on video and mapped onto a Cartesian plane. Each panel moved by a pure horizontal translation along its rail, and the translations of the two panels were reflection-symmetric about the vertical centre line of the doorway. The representative opening width was 30 cm for a single user, 75 cm for two to three users, and 100 cm for a crowd. Taking the single-user opening as the reference aperture, the larger openings correspond to dilation factors k = 2.50 and k = 3.33 about the centre of the door, while the panels themselves remain rigid. Because detection distance and the number of users varied together and the door’s control logic was not accessible, these factors describe the observed openings rather than the controller’s rule. The door thus illustrates a composition of isometries combined with a change of scale of the aperture and can serve as a contextual resource for teaching geo…

title: Prediction of Compressive Strength of Activated Binary Cement Mortars Using Response Surface Methodology and Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: This study investigates the prediction of the compressive strength of activated binary cement mortars containing ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS) using two complementary modelling approaches: response surface methodology (RSM) and an artificial neural network (ANN). A database of 96 mix–curing combinations was assembled from the published literature on activated slag cement systems. Four input parameters were considered: slag replacement ratio (0–70 %), slag fineness (Blaine, 320–650 m²/kg), curing temperature (20–80 °C) and curing time (1–90 days). The output variable was the 1- to 90-day compressive strength (9–64 MPa). A second-order RSM polynomial was fitted and analysed by ANOVA, while a back-propagation feed-forward ANN with a 4–9–6–1 architecture and hyperbolic tangent activation was trained using the L-BFGS algorithm. The ANN reached R² = 0.996 and RMSE = 0.92 MPa over the whole dataset, clearly outperforming the RSM model (R² = 0.785, RMSE = 6.83 MPa). Sensitivity analysis showed that curing time was the dominant predictor (62 %), followed by slag fineness (22 %), curing temperature (8 %) and slag replacement ratio (8 %). The results confirm that ANN is a more reliable surrogate for the highly non-linear hydration kinetics of activated slag mortars and can be used to support mix-design decisions and reduce experimental effort.

title: A Mathematical Model for Predicting Teacher Training Demand in Kenya
abstract: Since independence in 1963, Kenya has expanded teacher training through teacher training colleges, universities, and postgraduate programs in response to rising enrollment, curriculum reforms, and changing educational needs. Despite this expansion, Kenya continues to face mismatches between the supply of trained teachers and the employment capacity of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC), between supply and demand by subject combination, and between supply and regional deployment. Currently, nearly 40% of university students in Kenya enroll in education- related programs. Of these, less than 10% are absorbed immediately after graduation. The majority wait for up to ten years or more to be employed. Hence, there is a backlog of about 350, 350,000 unemployed teachers. Simultaneously, the country is short of teachers for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM)- related subjects. This shortage is likely to be magnified as 60% of all senior school students are required to take the STEM pathway. Equally, there is a mismatch between the supply and the regional distribution of teachers, with some regions experiencing an acute shortage while others have an oversupply. This study develops a mathematical model for predicting teacher training demand in Kenya by integrating historical trends in learner enrollment, teacher recruitment, pupil–teacher ratios, attrition, infra…

title: Elucidating mechanisms associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress at the placental and fetal brain axis in response to oxycodone exposure
abstract: Prenatal oxycodone (Oxy) exposure has been associated with several neurodevelopmental outcomes in newborns. However, the molecular mechanisms involved in Oxy-induced placental and fetal brain damage during gestation remain unknown. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is a cellular stress response triggered by the accumulation of unfolded proteins, which activates the unfolded protein response. Here, we hypothesized that Oxy exposure induces ER stress in the fetal brain-placental axis. To test this hypothesis, we used three model systems: in vitro primary neurons, primary mixed neuroglial cells, and an in vivo model of maternal Oxy exposure. Quantitative Reverse Transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) was employed to detect mRNA expression of ER stress mediators, such as Binding Immunoglobulin Protein (Bip), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), spliced X-box binding protein 1 (sXBP1), and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP). Immunoblot analysis was also used to detect protein expression of ER stress mediators, such as Bip; phosphorylated and total forms of inositol-requiring transmembrane kinase/endoribonuclease 1α (p-IRE1α and t-IRE1α) and protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase α (p-PERKα and t-PERKα); phosphorylated eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (p-eIF2α); and sXBP1. Further, we detected pro-apoptotic markers such as Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim),…

title: Analysis Of Product Demand Forecasting Using Time Series Methods
abstract: This research is motivated by the uncertainty of product demand at the Si Geboy Tea Cracker Factory, which causes both overproduction and underproduction. This study aims to assist the Hikmat Si Geboy Tea Cracker Factory in forecasting demand for the January 2026 period. The analytical tools used were the Moving Average, Weighted Moving Average, and Exponential Smoothing methods, with forecast accuracy tested using MAD, MSE, and MAPE. The data. The results showed that the MA 3-Period method predicted a demand of 7,932 dozen, with a MAD of 452.26, MSE of 288.050, and MAPE of 5.54%. The WMA 3-Period method predicted a demand of 7,724 dozen, with a MAD of 425.74, MSE of 266.599, and MAPE of 5.19%. ES α = 0.1 predicted a demand of 8,168 dozen, with a MAD of 418.22, MSE of 252.198, and MAPE of 5.24%. ES α = 0.5 predicted a demand of 7,810 dozen, with a MAD of 420.95, MSE of 264.257, and MAPE of 5.25%. ES α = 0.9 predicted a demand of 7,460 dozen, with a MAD of 398.99, MSE of 259.721, and MAPE of 4.93%. The conclusion from the three methods is that the most suitable method for forecasting cracker demand for January 2026 is the Exponential Smoothing method with α = 0.9 because it has the best accuracy compared with the other methods, as indicated by its lower MAD, MSE, and MAPE values.

Elafibranor improves biochemical response and favorably modifies GLOBE and UK-PBC prognostic scores in primary biliary cholangitis: analyses from the phase III ELATIVE® trial
abstract: Abstract Background Elafibranor demonstrated significant biochemical response in patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in the phase III ELATIVE ® trial. Biochemical response can be defined using various criteria, and prognostic tools such as GLOBE and UK-PBC predict estimated transplant-free survival and mortality. Here, we assess the efficacy of elafibranor across different biochemical response criteria and prognostic scores. Methods Using Week 52 data from ELATIVE ® , biochemical response was analyzed according to Paris I, Paris II, Barcelona, Toronto, Momah/Lindor, deep biochemical response, and complete biochemical response criteria. GLOBE and UK-PBC scores were calculated at baseline through Week 52; risk scores at baseline and Week 52 were used to estimate transplant-free survival rates at 5, 10, and 15 years, and were analyzed in subgroups of patients according to achievement of biochemical response. Results Responder rates at Week 52 favored elafibranor over placebo across all criteria: Paris I (68.9% versus 47.2%), Paris II (43.0% versus 5.7%), Barcelona (54.7% versus 0%), Toronto (51.9% versus 9.4%), Momah/Lindor (51.9% versus 9.4%), deep biochemical response (14.2% versus 0%), and complete biochemical response (9.3% versus 0%). Biological legacy of large-scale coastal reclamation: Potential oxygen demand from pre-existing benthic biomass
abstract: Coastal-enclosure assessments commonly emphasize external organic loading, sediment processes, and hydrological exchange but rarely account for living benthic biomass that may become a transient internal organic load after habitat conversion. Omitting this pool may leave early post-closure oxygen budgets incomplete, particularly where water exchange and oxygen renewal are restricted. We evaluated this biological legacy in Saemangeum, Korea, using a three-step analysis: (1) estimating the pre-closure benthic carbon inventory and its complete-decomposition oxygen-demand upper bound; (2) using reanalyzed laboratory data to assess the temporal plausibility of rapid biomass loss and field-observed intertidal macrofaunal deficits to constrain potential demand; and (3) comparing the field-constrained estimates with standing dissolved-oxygen inventories across three effective receiving-water volumes. The compiled inventory contained 9,384 t C and yielded an all-component upper bound of 25,023 t O 2 ; excluding the transferred bacterial estimate reduced this value to 14,461 t O 2 . At 120 days after closure, the net biomass-deficit and taxon-resolved minimum-loss estimators yielded potential demands of 3,547 and 4,663 t O 2 , respectively, equivalent to 54.0% and 70.9% of the intertidal macrofaunal upper bound. The corresponding point-estimate demand-to-inventory ratios exceeded one at …

title: Immediate early response 3 promotes airway epithelial inflammation and represents a therapeutic target in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
abstract: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airway inflammation, yet clinically useful biomarkers and mechanistically validated therapeutic targets remain limited. Here, we aimed to identify and functionally validate smoke-responsive regulators of airway epithelial inflammation in COPD and establish an interpretable prediction framework by integrating population-based clinical data, multi-omics analyses, genetic causal inference, and experimental validation. Methods Complementary clinical and molecular investigations used separate populations. Interpretable machine-learning models classified recorded COPD status in CHARLS, with validation across survey waves. Independent lung transcriptomic analyses integrated differential expression, co-expression networks, 113 machine-learning configurations, and single-cell profiling. Two-sample Mendelian randomization examined genetically predicted IER3 expression in relation to FEV 1 /FVC. Functional effects of IER3 were evaluated through AAV-mediated silencing in cigarette-smoke–exposed mice and siRNA knockdown in cigarette-smoke-extract–stimulated bronchial epithelial cells. Drug screening and molecular simulations prioritized candidate compounds for further investigation. Case Report: Concurrent breast myeloid sarcoma and ductal carcinoma in situ—multimodality imaging findings and differential treatment response
abstract: Myeloid sarcoma (MS) is an uncommon extramedullary manifestation of myeloid neoplasms, and breast involvement is rare. We report concurrent breast MS and ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) in a 49-year-old woman who was referred for evaluation of cervical lymphadenopathy and subsequently underwent breast imaging for a rapidly enlarging palpable left breast mass. Mammography and ultrasonography showed a dominant noncalcified mass and separate calcification-associated lesions in the outer breast. Site-specific core biopsies identified MS in the noncalcified mass and concurrent MS and high-grade DCIS in a calcification-associated mass; an axillary lymph node also showed MS. Subsequent hematologic evaluation demonstrated BCR-ABL1-positive chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) with 3.5% bone marrow blasts, with extramedullary MS establishing blast-phase disease. MRI and FDG PET/CT performed after pathologic diagnosis demonstrated the extent of breast and extramammary disease. Approximately 5 weeks after initiation of systemic therapy, the enhancing breast lesions had markedly decreased on MRI. On follow-up ultrasonography, the mass component of the mixed MS and DCIS lesion also decreased, whereas the associated calcifications persisted. Mastectomy subsequently demonstrated residual DCIS without residual MS. Recognition of the different imaging patterns allowed separate sampling of morphologic…

title: Case Report: Durable response to tislelizumab monotherapy in microsatellite-stable, BRAF V600E-mutant right-sided colon cancer with extremely high PD-L1 expression
abstract: Colorectal cancer with proficient mismatch repair (pMMR)/microsatellite stable (MSS) status is generally intrinsically resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitors; tumors with concomitant BRAF V600E mutations are highly aggressive, and conventional chemotherapy and targeted therapies have limited efficacy, resulting in a lack of effective personalized treatment options in clinical practice. This report describes a case of locally advanced right-sided colon adenocarcinoma that was pMMR/MSS, harbored a BRAF V600E mutation, and exhibited high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression (tumor proportion score [TPS] > 95%). The patient developed intestinal obstruction after failure of first-line conversion therapy. After undergoing palliative gastrojejunostomy and cecostomy, she developed gastroparesis and a liver abscess. Given the extremely high PD-L1 expression, tislelizumab monotherapy was initiated before the patient’s general condition had fully recovered. After three cycles, the patient’s performance status improved significantly. She then received a combination of tislelizumab and raltitrexed for two cycles; however, chemotherapy was discontinued due to raltitrexed-induced liver injury, and the patient continued maintenance therapy with tislelizumab monotherapy, achieving a partial response (PR) as the best outcome. After nine cycles of maintenance therapy, a new mass app…

title: The stroma-vascular compartment: central facilitator of the damage response and repair across organs
abstract: Abstract Tissue injury initiates a complex, multicellular programme whose outcome i.e. functional repair or irreversible fibrosis, is determined by the coordinated activity of the stroma-vascular compartment (SVC). This network of resident fibroblasts, vascular mural cells, endothelial cells and immune populations acts as a gatekeeper of tissue integrity. Following ischaemia, trauma, or mechanical damage, extracellular danger signals are sensed by pattern-recognition receptors and transduced into cell type-specific metabolic and mechanical responses. An initial inflammatory wave clears cellular debris, after which endothelial sprouting and matrix deposition proceed toward scar maturation; a collagen-rich structure whose geometry ultimately governs future perfusion. Epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring enforce each of these transitions while simultaneously imprinting a memory that skews subsequent responses in the context of ageing, diabetes, chronic inflammation or clonal haematopoiesis. Targeting the SVC, rather than the parenchyma alone, now underpins therapeutic strategies spanning precision senolytics, engineered stromal cell grafts, and biomechanically instructive scaffolds.

title: When evaluating ideas exposes the evaluator: leader impostor thoughts and the obstruction of employee creativity
abstract: Purpose Leaders’ evaluation and development of employee ideas shape employee creativity. Yet how leaders respond to employee ideas when they perceive others to evaluate their professional competence more favorably than they evaluate it themselves, and how these responses are subsequently associated with employee creativity, remain largely underexplored. Grounded in self-presentation theory, this study examines how leader impostor thoughts are associated with different responses to employee ideas, identifies employee creative reputation as a boundary condition, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for organizational idea management practices. Design/methodology/approach The hypothesized model was tested across two complementary studies: a three-wave multisource field study with 176 matched supervisor-employee dyads, and a 2 × 2 between-subjects scenario experiment involving 248 managers. Findings Consistent results were observed across both studies. Leader impostor thoughts were positively associated with leader idea rejection when employee creative reputation was low, but negatively associated with creative-idea developmental feedback when employee creative reputation was high. The field study further showed that both conditional pathways are linked to lower employee creativity, forming two distinct obstructive patterns: selection-based obstruction and develo…

title: Gestión educativa y motivación laboral en una Institución educativa pública en Santa Elena, Virú (2024)
abstract: La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre la gestión educativa y la motivación laboral en una institución educativa de Virú, durante el 2024. El estudio se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cuantitativo, con diseño no experimental, alcance descriptivo - correlacional y corte transversal. La población estuvo conformada por 37 docentes, por lo que se empleó una muestra censal que comprendió la totalidad de la población. La gestión educativa fue analizada mediante las dimensiones institucional, pedagógica, comunitaria y administrativa, mientras que la motivación laboral comprendió las dimensiones intrínseca y extrínseca. Para la recolección de datos se aplicaron dos cuestionarios mediante la técnica de la encuesta. El procesamiento y análisis de la información se realizó mediante SPSS y Excel. Los resultados evidenciaron una correlación positiva y muy alta entre las dos variables, concluyendo que existe una relación directa entre la gestión educativa y el nivel de motivación laboral docente en la institución educativa estudiada.

title: From data to direction: a cybernetic system of strategic prediction under bounded rationality
abstract: Purpose This study adopts a conceptual and design-oriented approach by integrating bounded rationality, sensemaking, strategy-as-practice, and second-order cybernetics. It develops a mechanism-based model of strategic prediction structured as a second-order cybernetic system in which outcome feedback updates the observer's interpretive state across prediction cycles. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a conceptual and design-oriented approach by integrating bounded rationality, sensemaking, strategy-as-practice, and second-order cybernetics systems. This study proposes that strategic prediction operates through three stages: pattern-based complexity reduction, categorical interpretation, and directional inference. Outcome discrepancies either regulate subsequent actions or update the observer's interpretive state, allowing similar patterns to produce different strategic directions across prediction cycles. The findings demonstrate that prediction does not require analytical optimization but can emerge through simplified and interpretable mechanisms based on second-order cybernetics. Findings The study proposes that strategic prediction operates through a three-stage system: pattern-based complexity reduction, categorical interpretation, and directional inference. These stages form a recursive process in which action outcomes update subsequent interpretations and may …

title: Beyond career development: Understanding employees’ intention to stay through occupational well-being
abstract: Orientation: Employee retention is a strategic concern in the banking industry because of its implications for organisational performance and sustainability. Research purpose: This study examines the effect of career development on employees’ intention to stay and the mediating role of occupational well-being based on Conservation of Resources (COR) Theory. Motivation for the study: Previous findings on the relationship between career development and intention to stay have been inconsistent, highlighting the need to investigate the underlying mechanism. Research approach/design and method: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 191 employees of PT Bank Muamalat Indonesia Tbk in the Sulawesi, Maluku, and Papua Region, Indonesia. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Main findings: Career development positively and significantly affects occupational well-being and intention to stay. Occupational well-being also positively affects intention to stay and partially mediates the relationship between career development and intention to stay. Practical/managerial implications: Organisations should strengthen structured career development through accessible training, supervisor support and career advancement opportunities while fostering employees’ occupational well-being. Contribution/value-add: This study extends COR Theory by …

title: A Study on the Role of India Post Payments Bank in Promoting Financial Inclusion in Rural India
abstract: Financial inclusion is meaningful when people can access financial services and use them with confidence, safety and convenience. In rural India, banking access can be affected by distance, documentation requirements, limited familiarity with digital tools, connectivity and uncertainty about how to resolve transaction problems. India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) uses the postal network alongside digital banking services to help address these barriers. This paper studies IPPB’s role in promoting rural financial inclusion, drawing on the author’s OJT report and practical exposure to customer-facing banking activities. The internship activities described in the report include Know Your Customer (KYC) updates, Aadhaar and PAN verification, account-opening assistance, mobile banking registration, digital-payment awareness and customer-query resolution. The report also cites IPPB’s FY 2024–25 institutional indicators: 11.67 crore customers as of March 2025, 77% rural customers, more than 1.64 lakh banking access points, 1,289 crore digital financial transactions, 5.12 crore Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) beneficiaries and 4.25 crore mobile app downloads. The bank’s official annual report describes growth in customers, deposits and digital engagement, supporting the importance of its combined physical and digital model. citeturn0search12 The research uses a descriptive and exploratory …

title: Gestión de recursos humanos y desempeño laboral de los trabajadores de la Municipalidad Distrital de Olmos.
abstract: El estudio tuvo como objetivo determinar la relación entre la gestión de recursos humanos y el desempeño laboral de los trabajadores de la Municipalidad Distrital de Olmos, 2024. La población estuvo conformada por 228 empleados municipales, a quienes se les aplicó un cuestionario previamente validado por juicio de expertos. Se evidencia en los resultados que la gestión de recursos humanos se encuentra estrechamente relacionado con el desempeño laboral, ya que una adecuada gestión genera acciones que se relacionan directamente con la efectividad, rendimiento y motivación de los trabajadores. Se concluye que la gestión de recursos humanos en la municipalidad tiene una relación directa con el desempeño laboral de los trabajadores, esto debido a través de una adecuada selección de personal, capacitación continua, motivación, evaluación del desempeño y un buen clima laboral.

title: Enabling or weakening? Artificial intelligence and ambidextrous green innovation
abstract: Purpose This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption shapes firms' ambidextrous green innovation by inducing differential effects on exploratory and exploitative activities from an attention-based perspective. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the attention-based view, we theorize that AI adoption reconfigures organizational attention and technological capabilities, leading to divergent effects on green innovation. Using panel data from Chinese listed firms, we employ regression analyses to test these arguments. Findings AI adoption exerts a double-edged effect on ambidextrous green innovation. It significantly promotes exploratory green innovation by redirecting managerial attention toward forward-looking strategic issues, while suppressing exploitative green innovation by institutionalizing routine processes and reducing sustained attention to incremental improvements. Furthermore, Confucian cultural embeddedness, negative media coverage and institutional ownership strengthen the positive effect of AI on exploratory green innovation and mitigate its negative effect on exploitative green innovation. Practical implications These findings suggest that managers should align AI adoption with balanced attention allocation to avoid overemphasizing exploratory innovation at the expense of incremental improvements. title: Energy and carbon emissions in information technology projects: a systematic review and an integrated sustainable software framework
abstract: Purpose This paper examines the extent to which information technology projects (ITP) measure and integrate energy and carbon emissions into planning and execution and proposes a structured framework for embedding environmental sustainability into ITP. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted using a three-stage process of planning, conducting and reviewing. Inclusion and exclusion were governed by the PRISMA method across three databases (Scopus, Web of Science and ProQuest), covering 2012 to 2024. Thematic synthesis was applied to 72 academic papers and 16 grey literature sources to identify emergent themes through open, axial and selective coding. Findings Five interconnected themes were identified: Sustainable IT Skills, Sustainable IT Strategy, Implementing Sustainable IT, Sustainable IT Operations and Sustainable IT Regulations. The Integrated Sustainable Software (ISS) Framework is proposed to address these gaps by providing a structured, methodology-agnostic approach to integrating sustainability into ITP governance and execution. Research limitations/implications Future research should examine framework adoption in practice and explore sector-specific sustainability metrics. Practical implications The ISS Framework provides project managers and IT leaders with actionable guidance for embedding carbon and energy metrics into project gover…

title: DETECTION OF EARNINGS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THROUGH DISCRETIONARY LOAN LOSS PROVISIONS AT RURAL BANKS IN WEST JAVA, CENTRAL JAVA, AND EAST JAVA DURING THE SAK EP TRANSITION PERIOD (2023–2025)
abstract: This study examines whether the transition from the rule-based PPAP provisioning regime to the judgment-based CKPN regime under the Indonesian Financial Accounting Standards for Private Entities (SAK EP) is accompanied by a change in the intensity of earnings management through discretionary loan loss provisions (DLLP) in rural banks (Bank Perekonomian Rakyat/BPR). The novelty of the study lies in using 2023–2025 as a transition window that combines the last two years of the PPAP regime and the first year of the CKPN regime in a single sample, allowing the link between the scope of accounting discretion and income smoothing to be observed among small, unlisted banks, a segment rarely examined in the bank earnings management literature. Panel data of 556 conventional BPRs (1,649 bank-year observations) in West Java, Central Java, and East Java are analysed using a two-stage estimation approach. The results show that non-performing loans are an important determinant of loan loss provisions, whereas pre-managed earnings are positively associated with DLLP, consistent with income smoothing. This association is weak under the PPAP regime but becomes markedly stronger in the first year of CKPN adoption, accompanied by a higher share of banks showing strong discretion, mostly in the form of over-provisioning. The findings enrich positive accounting theory by suggesting that the intens…

title: Conceptualising and designing experiential consumer logistics: a literature synthesis towards a value-based framework
abstract: Purpose The value of last-mile delivery is no longer confined to functional performance but increasingly involves consumers' experiences. Despite growing recognition of experiential value, research in this area remains fragmented and underdeveloped. Thus, this study aims to develop a value-based conceptualisation of experiential consumer logistics (ECL) through a synthesised literature review. Design/methodology/approach A two-study literature review design was employed. Study 1 synthesises the logistics literature to conceptualise the value configurations and experiential mechanisms underlying ECL. Building on this conceptualisation, Study 2 integrates insights from the service design literature to examine how experiential value can be systematically reinforced. Findings Study 1 conceptualises ECL based on two analytical dimensions, value proposition (high-touch vs high-tech) and value appreciation (individualised vs networked), leading to four principal value configurations labelled as: traditional, technology-based, ethical and platform-enabled logistics. Furthermore, Study 2 identifies two complementary service design approaches for reinforcing experiential value: accommodating (relationship building and design for invisibility) and empowering (design for visibility and community building), each aligned with distinct configurations of ECL. title: Reported enterprise deployment readiness of privacy-preserving artificial intelligence: a governance and information management perspective
abstract: Purpose Privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) technologies increasingly support data-driven decision-making while safeguarding sensitive information. However, peer-reviewed evidence documenting governance integration and operational deployment remains limited. This study examines how the peer-reviewed academic literature documents the technical maturity, governance integration, and operational implementation of privacy-preserving AI systems relevant to enterprise information systems. Design/methodology/approach A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-compliant systematic literature review examined 22 peer-reviewed studies published from 2018 to May 2026. The review synthesized evidence on privacy–utility trade-offs, governance integration, fairness, operational readiness, and implementation maturity. We used Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and a proposed Translational Readiness Index (TRI) to classify readiness evidence reported in the included studies. Findings Privacy-preserving AI systems demonstrated favorable privacy–utility trade-offs in the reviewed academic literature, with privacy budgets of e = 1–3 preserving approximately 85–96% of baseline predictive performance. Federated learning combined with differential privacy was the dominant implementation architecture. Most included studies demonstrated intermediate te…

Zakat Management as a Tool for the Economic Empowerment of the Muslim Community: An Empirical Study of BAZNAS’s Role in Improving Community Well-Being
abstract: Productive zakat management by the National Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) is often assumed to linearly alleviate poverty without examining operational barriers at the field level. This study aims to analyze zakat management by the National Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) of City X as an instrument for the economic empowerment of the Muslim community and its impact on community well-being. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews with BAZNAS representatives and mustahik, observation, and documentation studies. The results reveal that the business capital program increased average income by 25–30%, but it also faced critical operational barriers, including fragmented mustahik data that is not yet digitally integrated, limited competence of amil human resources in micro business management, and minimal sustainability of post-distribution mentoring, which often triggers bias in assessing program success. This study recommends practical implications for BAZNAS to accelerate the digitalization of its database and to institutionalize a sustainable business mentoring unit in order to improve zakat governance comprehensively. This study concludes that optimizing zakat as an instrument of economic independence cannot rely solely on the amount of funds allocated, but requires governance reform through database digitalization and the strengthening of sustaina…

Risks of financing innovation in public policies for economic grant
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a model to predict technological risks and manage innovation financing for a local economic grant program. Design/methodology/approach A study was carried out with a sample of 284 innovation projects approved in 14 public calls from a regional scientific and technological support foundation over 10 years. Findings The results indicated that the greater the innovative capital of subsidized companies, the lower the levels of different risks associated with the economic subsidy program. Practical implications It presents a practical contribution to the local economic grant program, as an alternative to increase knowledge of how to carry out this type of analysis to other institutions that foster innovation, in addition to establishing more understanding on how to measure the risks of these transactions and which variables are their determinants. Originality/value The proposal of this research can be used to estimate prediction models of different risk levels, which have demonstrated a certain capacity to carry out this prediction or it can be used to assist the decisions of financing institutions in the selection of projects to be financed.

title: Linking Operations and Accounting in an Emerging Import-Export Business: An Illustrative Case Study of Imexshwetej Global LLP, Pune
abstract: Small trading firms in India grow in a market that rewards speed, yet many of them run their operations and their accounts as two separate worlds. This paper looks at how the operational and accounting sides of a young import-export business depend on each other, using Imexshwetej Global LLP as the case. The firm is a Pune-based trading LLP, established on 25 September 2025, that deals in health and wellness products, agricultural products, food staples, spices, seafood, edible oil and dairy. The study draws on an on-the-job training (OJT) placement during April to July 2026, in which the researcher observed the order-to-payment cycle, studied trade and accounting documents, and organised what was seen into measurable indicators. Because company accounts are confidential, the quantitative part of the paper uses a clearly labelled illustrative dataset: monthly financials from October 2025 to July 2026 (combined revenue of ₹141.3 lakh) and a sample of 60 transactions (24 imports and 36 exports) for May to July 2026. Within this dataset, 54 of 60 transactions (90.0%) were completed on time, half of the six delays traced back to documentation or packing clarification, 95.0% of transactions carried complete supporting documents, and 46.4% of the closing receivable balance of ₹4.20 lakh was older than 30 days. Product-level analysis showed that revenue share and margin do not move to…

title: INFLUENCE OF SCHOOL MANAGEMENT POLICIES AND COMMUNITY RELATIONS ON TEACHERS’ JOB PERFORMANCE IN SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN OGUN STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined the influence of school management policies and community relations on teachers’ job performance in public senior secondary schools in Ogun State. Four hypotheses were tested. The study adopted survey research design. The population comprised 134 principals and 3,095 teachers in public senior secondary schools in Ogun-East Senatorial District. The study sampled 175 teachers and 35 principals from 35 senior secondary schools using simple random sampling and purposive sampling techniques. Three validated research instruments titled: School Management Policies Questionnaire (r = .70), School Community Relation Questionnaire (r = .74), and Teachers’ Job Performance Rating Scale (r = .71) were adapted from previous studies in literature, and were used for data collection. The null hypotheses formulated for the study were tested using Pearson’s Product-Moment Correlation (PPMC) and multiple regression analysis at .05 level of significance. Findings showed that there was a significant moderate positive relationship between school management policies and teachers’ job performance (r = .57, p < .05), there was a significant low positive relationship between school community relation and teachers’ job performance (r = .32, p < .05), there was a significant composite contribution of school management policies and school community relation to teachers’ job performance (…

title: The Influence Of Electronic Word Of Mouth And Halal Certification On Purchase Decisions For Wardah Products On Tiktok (Survey Of Wardah Consumers In Tasikmalaya)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to identify and analyze the influence of Electronic Word Of Mouth and Halal Certification on the Decision to Purchase Wardah products on Tiktok. The research method used was a survey, with data collected directly via a questionnaire administered to 100 respondents selected from Wardah product consumers in Tasikmalaya who had previously made purchases on Tiktok. The technique used was multiple linear regression. Based on the results of this study, it was found that there is a significant simultaneous influence of Electronic Word Of Mouth and Halal Certification on Purchasing Decisions. Electronic Word Of Mouth has a significant partial influence on Purchasing Decisions, and Halal Certification has a significant partial influence on the Decision to Purchase Wardah products among consumers in Tasikmalaya.
