title: HM-CDSS: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework with Conservative Q-Learning and Retrieval-Augmented Clinical Reasoning for Sepsis Decision Support
Saturn’s Evolutionary History and Seismology: Survival of Deep Stably Stratified Regions in Evolutionary Models of Saturn Consistent with Ring Seismology
abstract: Abstract With recent advances in the modeling of the solar system giant planets, rapid progress has been made in understanding the remaining questions pertaining to their formation and evolution. However, this progress has largely neglected the significant constraints on the interior of Saturn’s structure imposed by the observed oscillation frequencies in its rings. Here, we study initial conditions for Saturn’s evolution that, after 4.56 Gyr of evolution, give rise to planetary structures admitting oscillation frequencies consistent with those observed via Saturn’s ring seismology. Restricting our attention to models without compact rocky cores, we achieve simultaneous good agreement with most observed properties of Saturn at the level of current evolutionary models and with key frequencies in the observed oscillation spectrum. Our preliminary work suggests that Saturn’s interior stably stratified region may be moderately less extended (∼0.4–0.5 R Sat ) than previously thought, which is important for reconciling the seismic constraints with evolutionary models. We also tentatively find that the deep helium gradients inferred by previous, static structural modeling of Saturn’s ring seismology may not be required to reproduce the observed seismology data.

title: Toward UAV-assisted Wi-Fi sensing via deep neural networks: a benchmark study on activity and gesture recognition
abstract: Purpose Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) sensing is a candidate technology for future Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted, device-free human sensing. This paper benchmarks convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for CSI-based activity and gesture recognition under a controlled, repeated protocol, as a first step towards selecting models for resource-constrained platforms. Design/methodology/approach Two public CSI datasets collected with fixed indoor Wi-Fi infrastructure were used: UT-HAR (activity recognition, 7 classes) and Widar (gesture recognition, 22 classes, body-coordinate velocity profile). Two VGG-inspired CSI-adapted networks (CSI-VGGNet-S and CSI-VGGNet-D), GoogLeNet and DenseNet were compared with four retrained SenseFi baselines (MLP, ResNet-18, LSTM and CNN-GRU). All models were trained with three random seeds under one common budget (at most 20 epochs, early stopping on a held-out validation partition), and the test partitions were used once per run. Sliding-window overlap in UT-HAR was quantified, and recording-level (UT-HAR) and cross-user (Widar) splits were used to probe generalization. No UAV hardware or UAV-collected CSI was used. Findings CSI-VGGNet-D achieved the highest mean test accuracy on UT-HAR (96.80 ± 0.87%) and on Widar (74.43 ± 1.31%). Depth alone did not predict accuracy: GoogLeNet and DenseNet varied strongly across seeds on U…

title: Deep Galerkin method computation for high machinery cooling with microbial swimmers in viscoelastic nanofluids with non-Fourier and non-Fick fluxes
abstract: Purpose Efficient thermal management remains a critical challenge for modern spacecraft due to increasing power densities and extreme operating conditions. This study aims to investigate the flow, heat and mass transfer characteristics of third-grade nanofluid containing microbial swimmers over a horizontal cylinder under the influence of an inclined magnetic field, incorporating non-Fourier heat flux and non-Fick mass flux models. Design/methodology/approach The highly nonlinear coupled system of ordinary differential equations is solved numerically using the deep Galerkin method (DGM), a robust physics-informed deep learning approach. Findings The effects of key parameters such as thermal relaxation parameter (λ1), concentration relaxation parameter (λt), curvature parameter (γ) and third-grade viscoelastic fluid parameter on velocity, temperature, concentration and motile density profiles are thoroughly analyzed. Quantitative results show that an increase in the thermal relaxation parameter reduces the skin-friction coefficient by approximately 13% (from 3.417 to 2.968) while decreasing the local Nusselt number and increasing the local Sherwood and density numbers. A similar trend is observed with the concentration relaxation parameter. Microbial swimmers significantly enhance micro-convection and the inclined magnetic field together with the relaxation parameters provide ef…

title: Does national governance shape the effects of economic policy uncertainty on capital allocation efficiency?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how economic policy uncertainty (EPU) affects firms’ capital allocation efficiency (CAE) and whether national governance (NGI) reduces uncertainty-driven investment inefficiencies. Design/methodology/approach This study uses unbalanced panel data of non-financial firms listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange 500 index over the period 2016–2024. CAE is measured as the inverse of investment inefficiency, estimated through investment inefficiency residuals. Panel data quantile regression (PDQR) is used to capture the heterogeneous effects of EPU, and NGI is included as a moderating factor. The PDQR models control for firm-level characteristics, as well as year and sector fixed effects. The results remain robust under system generalized method of moments estimation, addressing potential endogeneity concerns. Findings EPU significantly improves firms, with stronger effects observed at the higher quantiles (Q50 and Q75). NGI significantly moderates the relationship between EPU and CAE, although it does not have a direct effect on CAE. The findings indicate that the impact of EPU on firms’ CAE varies with the quality of national governance. Practical implications The findings highlight that EPU exerts a disciplining effect on CAE, particularly for moderately and highly inefficient firms. While NGI does not reduce inefficiency directly, a stronger institu…

title: Role uncertainty in AI-enabled organizational change: linking perceived AI adoption to job stress
abstract: Purpose This study examines the employee-side implications of perceived organizational artificial intelligence (AI) adoption by focusing on role-related uncertainty. In this study, perceived organizational AI adoption refers to employees’ perceptions of the extent to which their organization has implemented and integrated AI technologies into its work processes. Drawing on role theory, it investigates whether perceived organizational AI adoption is associated with job stress through role ambiguity and whether change communication weakens this indirect association. Design/methodology/approach The hypotheses were tested using three-wave survey data collected from 355 employees working in Japanese organizations that had adopted AI technologies in their work processes. Perceived organizational AI adoption and change communication were measured at Time 1, role ambiguity at Time 2, and job stress at Time 3, with four-week intervals between waves. The hypotheses were examined using confirmatory factor analyses, hierarchical regression analyses, and bias-corrected bootstrapping procedures. Findings Perceived organizational AI adoption was positively associated with role ambiguity, which in turn was positively associated with job stress. Change communication moderated the association between perceived organizational AI adoption and role ambiguity, such that the association was weaker at…

THE IMPACT OF EXISTENTIAL UNCERTAINTY ON THE CONSTRUCTION OF LIFE PERSPECTIVE IN ADULTS UNDER MARTIAL LAW
abstract: The problem of the impact of experiencing existential uncertainty, caused by the state of martial law in Ukraine, on the process of constructing life perspective by adults is examined in the article. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that the prolonged war has actualized for a significant part of the population the experience of losing stability, disruption of habitual life orientations, and the inability to predict their own future, which directly affects psychological well-being and the individual's capacity for self-determination. The main theoretical approaches to understanding existential uncertainty within existential-humanistic psychology are analyzed, as well as contemporary Ukrainian studies on the psychological consequences of war. The features of life perspective as a complex dynamic system that integrates value orientations, life goals and plans, as well as the mechanisms of its transformation under extreme stress are investigated. The empirical study was conducted on a sample of 76 respondents aged 18 to 60, divided into three groups: civilians without displacement experience, internally displaced persons, and veterans/military personnel with combat experience. A complex of psychodiagnostic tools was used, including the «Existential Scale» to determine the level of existential fulfillment, and the «Zimbardo Time Perspective Inventory» to study in…

title: Dynamics of tuberculosis via NSFD scheme with nonlinear incidence, relapse, reinfection, and saturated treatment
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the most prevalent infectious diseases worldwide and continues to pose a major public health challenge. This study presents a TB model using a nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) scheme that incorporates nonlinear incidence, relapse, reinfection, and saturated treatment effects. The discrete model is designed to preserve the key qualitative properties of the continuous system, including positivity, boundedness, and invariance of the feasible region. The disease-free and endemic equilibria are analyzed, and their local stability conditions are established using the Jury criterion. The basic reproduction number is derived and is consistent with that of the corresponding continuous model. Furthermore, the bifurcation analysis reveals that the model can exhibit either forward or backward bifurcation, indicating the possibility of bistability and disease persistence even when the basic reproduction number is less than one. To better reflect real-world dynamics, the model parameters are estimated using TB incidence data from Indonesia for the period 2000–2024. Numerical simulations, including the dynamical behavior around equilibria, global sensitivity analysis, epidemiological outcome sensitivity, and bifurcation diagrams, further support the analytical results. The robustness of the proposed NSFD scheme and its performance relative to classic…

Prokinetic effect of ferulic acid ethyl ester on gastrointestinal motility in mice: an integrated in silico and in vivo study
abstract: Abstract Gastrointestinal paralysis and dysmotility remain clinically relevant conditions associated with delayed intestinal transit, feeding intolerance, prolonged hospitalization, and limited effective pharmacological treatment options. Among these disorders, postoperative ileus (POI) is a common complication after abdominal surgery characterized by transient suppression of coordinated gastrointestinal motility. The present study investigated the effects of ferulic acid ethyl ester (FAEE) on intestinal motility and explored its underlying mechanisms using integrated in silico and in vivo approaches. Gastrointestinal transit was assessed in mice by the charcoal meal test under normal conditions and in an experimental POI model induced by intestinal manipulation. In normal mice, FAEE (50 and 100 mg/kg, p.o.) significantly increased intestinal transit. In POI animals, FAEE (50 mg/kg) significantly attenuated the postoperative delay in intestinal transit. Biochemical analyses showed that FAEE reduced MPO activity, NOx, and MDA levels, while restoring SOD activity and GSH content. Pharmacological studies further indicated that the prokinetic effect of FAEE involves cholinergic and calcium-dependent pathways, as atropine and verapamil significantly attenuated its effects. In contrast, pharmacological blockade of opioid and 5-HT3 receptors did not significantly alter the prokinetic …

title: Social innovation in longevity based on social prescribing: a conceptual and intervention model
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore innovation from the perspective of social prescribing. The model has been developed within the framework of the TRANSIS LAB (Transborder Living Lab on Social Innovation for Longevity) project, funded by the European Territorial Cooperation Programme Spain–France–Andorra (INTERREG POCTEFA programme), which is developing six pilot experiences in social innovation for longevity in four regions of Spain and France. Design/methodology/approach The conceptual and intervention model with social innovation in longevity for rural areas based on social prescribing has been developed using a combined methodology. On the one hand, a review of the specialised literature has been carried out, which has helped to define the social innovation model. On the other hand, this model has been developed into a tool that measures social fragility. This tool has been validated and tested through its application to 34 elderly people and 14 professionals involved in social intervention with older people in situations of fragility in rural environments. Findings The article offers two main results. The first is a conceptual model linking social innovation and social prescribing in rural areas. The second is a social innovation tool for developing pilot projects in rural areas based on social prescribing. The tool enables the measurement of social fragility and thus acti…

Sulfur Vacancy-Engineered ZnIn2S4 Nanosheets Integrated with CoS1.097 for Enhanced Visible Light-Driven Nitrogen Photofixation
abstract: Abstract Herein, S-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts integrating sulfur vacancy-engineered ZnIn2S4 (Sv-ZnInS) with CoS1.097 (CoS) were successfully synthesized via a simple hydrothermal reaction. The formed CoS/Sv-ZnInS heterostructures exhibited considerably high catalytic activity toward visible light-driven photocatalytic nitrogen (N2) fixation. Notably, the optimized 3CoS/Sv-ZnInS sample achieved an ammonia yield of 18.18 ± 0.39 mg·L–1 after 1 h of visible-light illumination, which was an approximately 2.4-fold enhancement relative to pristine Sv-ZnInS. The S-scheme charge separation and transfer pathway was elucidated via in situ irradiated X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, noble-metal loading, and band structure analysis. The underlying N2 photofixation mechanism was systematically investigated using density functional theory calculations and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy. The results revealed that N2 photofixation over the 3CoS/Sv-ZnInS catalyst occurred via a multistep proton-coupled electron transfer. Our findings indicate that S-scheme CoS/Sv-ZnInS heterojunctions may offer a viable route toward visible light-driven photocatalytic N2 fixation.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals microbial and metabolic signatures associated with neutral detergent fiber digestibility in dairy cattle
abstract: Abstract Background The rumen microbiome is central to fiber degradation in dairy cows, yet the precise functional and metabolic networks driving variations in neutral detergent fiber (NDF) digestibility remain poorly understood. Elucidating these microbiome-host interactions is critical for improving forage utilization and advancing sustainable dairy production. Results Employing an integrative metagenomics-metabolomics approach, we characterized the rumen microecology of lactating dairy cows exhibiting high and low NDF digestibility phenotypes ( n = 10/group). Metagenomic profiling revealed a significant enrichment of fibrolytic taxa ( Prevotella sp., Lachnospiraceae bacterium) and carbohydrate-active enzymes in the high-NDF group (HI). In addition, species-level differential abundance testing showed that Methanobrevibacter spp. was more abundant in the low-NDF group (LO) than in the HI group, whereas no archaeal differences were detected at the phylum or genus levels. Functional and metabolomic analyses indicated broader enrichment of amino acid degradation functions and higher concentrations of major volatile fatty acids (VFAs) in HI cows, consistent with stronger overall ruminal fermentation activity. Furthermore, VFAs and microbial composition explained 54.3% and 43.0% of the variation in NDF digestibility, respectively. An exploratory machine learning model based on sele…

Amyloid–Chitosan Aerogels for Multi-Contaminant Water Purification under Batch and Rapid Flow-through Conditions
abstract: Abstract The increasing production of chemically diverse contaminants from industrial, municipal, and healthcare activities has motivated the need for developing innovative wastewater treatment strategies. For example, pharmaceuticals, including ibuprofen (IBP) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX), and toxic heavy metals, such as hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) and nickel (Ni(II)), have been increasingly detected in aquatic environments. Traditional water treatment strategies did not account for the removal of such contaminants in mind. Herein, we present a class of protein–polysaccharide composite aerogels constructed from bovine serum albumin (BSA) amyloid fibers and chitosan as adsorbents for the removal of these pharmaceutical and heavy metal contaminants. Amyloid fibers were prepared via acid-induced self-assembly, and chitosan was incorporated post-fibrillation in tunable ratios, followed by crosslinking and freeze-drying to yield highly porous and mechanically durable aerogel networks. Overall, the incorporation of a higher ratio of chitosan resulted in enhanced available surface area, mechanical strength, and structural stability, which collectively contributed to improved adsorption processes. Adsorption was evaluated for individual contaminants between pH 3 and 9, whereby IBP and SMX exhibited optimum removal at pH 6 (up to 92% for SMX), Cr(VI) between pH 3 and 6 (over 97%), and N…

title: Multi-centennial precipitation reconstructions for Dublin: comparing documentary-instrumental and circulation-based approaches
abstract: Long precipitation records are needed to place recent droughts and wet periods in their historical context. This study combines documentary weather accounts, early rain-gauge measurements, atmospheric-circulation and temperature indices, and tree-ring isotope evidence to reconstruct precipitation for contrasting lowland and upland water-resource domains for the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). We develop and evaluate three reconstruction products: a monthly documentary-instrumental reconstruction extending to 1711 (the Jenkinson series); a monthly statistical ensemble, combining Lasso and Random Forest models, extending to 1748; and a tree-ring δ 18 O reconstruction of May-August precipitation extending to 1200 CE. Monthly reconstructions are evaluated against 1 km gridded observations over their common overlap period, 1865–1977. Both monthly reconstructions reproduce observed rainfall variability, but the documentary-instrumental Jenkinson reconstruction generally shows stronger agreement at monthly, seasonal, annual and event scales. The statistical ensemble provides an independent, circulation-informed estimate but produces smoother variability and underestimates some extremes. The tree-ring reconstruction shows weaker interannual agreement with Dublin rainfall but supplies a substantially longer perspective on summer hydroclimatic variability. However, superior performance agains…

title: Pathways to progress: navigating the evolving field of PIDs and associated conditions — proceedings from the IPOPI Global Multi-Stakeholders’ Summit (July 2025)
abstract: Introduction In July 2025, the International Patient Organisation for Primary Immunodeficiencies (IPOPI) held its fourth consecutive Global Multi-Stakeholders’ Summit, bringing together key stakeholders and experts in primary immunodeficiencies (PIDs) and related fields to discuss current challenges and opportunities for improving patient care. Methods This edition focused on current and projected trends to 2035 in artificial intelligence and quantum computing, the gap between primary and secondary immunodeficiencies, and the role of preventive medicine in patients’ quality of life. Results Stakeholders from all around the world gathered to examine current knowledge gaps, needs and avenues to improve the care of patients with immunodeficiency in the next ten years. Discussion Recommendations on how digital technologies can contribute to equitable access to innovative therapies are proposed. Mechanisms by which multidisciplinary teams can work together to improve the care of patients with immunodeficiencies are outlined, including how innovative screening and care plans can reduce the risk of multiorgan involvement and complications in these patients. Within the next decade, digital tools in conjunction with improved multistakeholder collaborations is most likely to contribute to the collection of standardised data, inclusive studies, and personalised treatments that will prolon…

title: Anticipated vs enacted telework: the roles of self-management and interpersonal trust in schedule flexibility and work-life balance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether telework evaluations and the relationships among key telework-related constructs differ between a low-experience, prospective context and a context of enacted telework. Design/methodology/approach The study compares anticipated and enacted telework perceptions using two independent surveys of Romanian employees: a 2018 survey in which respondents evaluated telework as a hypothetical work arrangement (n = 1,180) and a 2020 survey in which respondents reported their actual telework experience during the COVID-19 pandemic (n = 1,142). The analysis combines mean comparisons with partial least squares structural equation modelling and multi-group analysis. Because the samples are independent, the design permits a contextual between-sample comparison but does not trace within-person change from anticipation to experience. Findings Structural relationships differ across the two samples. In the 2018 anticipated-telework sample, self-management is positively associated with schedule flexibility, whereas in the 2020 enacted-telework sample this association is negative. Interpersonal trust is positively associated with schedule flexibility in both samples, with a larger estimated path coefficient in the 2020 sample. The association between schedule flexibility and work-life balance is also stronger in the 2020 sample. These results indicate betwe…

title: The generative AI duality trap: a knowledge governance perspective on knowledge diversity and epistemic convergence in AI-augmented organisations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine a knowledge management (KM) puzzle: why generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use relates to knowledge diversity expansion in some organisations and epistemic convergence in others. The authors develop the GenAI duality trap, a cross-level knowledge governance framework in which artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated knowledge outcomes track governance design, not technological capability alone. Design/methodology/approach A multi-source design combines organisational surveys (n = 67), employee measures (n = 1,247) and sentence-bidirectional encoder representations from transformers(SBERT)-derived semantic diversity indices. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and partial least squares multi-group analysis (PLS-MGA) test nine hypotheses across three institutional regimes (Bradford, 2023), with cluster-robust and multilevel diagnostics for the nested data. Findings Knowledge governance relates to diversity through human–AI interaction quality. Transparency, decentralised access and AI literacy investment are associated with critical engagement, which, in turn, relates to perceived and semantic diversity. Institutional regime moderates all three pathways, most weakly for access, with associations strongest in market-driven and attenuated in state-driven regimes. Research limitations/implications Knowledge governance…

title: Jilted at the altar: understanding the consequences of M&A withdrawal for the abandoned firm
abstract: Purpose The aim of this paper is to analyze and typify the strategic consequences of M&A withdrawal for abandoned firms once the private negotiation phase is over. Design/methodology/approach Due to the exploratory nature of the research question, this research follows a qualitative methodological approach using a multiple case study of six announced acquisitions that ended in withdrawal in the Spanish banking industry using 503 media news and the firms' annual reports. Findings M&A withdrawal is a stressful and disturbing event for the abandoned firm. After withdrawal some abandoned firms survive and recover while others do not. Strategic behaviors that allow stability and flexibility help to explain why some firms recover while others collapse. Originality/value The paper improves knowledge about strategic consequences for abandoned targets of being jilted at the altar through the lens of resilience research.

Cultivating standard workers in construction: a tripartite evolutionary game analysis
abstract: Purpose The shortage of skilled workers has become one of the barriers in the transition toward construction industrialization. This study aims to deconstruct the complex behavioral interactions among key stakeholders – general contractors, labor subcontractors and construction workers – to promote workforce cultivation. By introducing government intervention as a regulatory variable, the research seeks to design a mechanism to solve the problem of skilled workers shortage in the construction industry. Design/methodology/approach This study employs evolutionary game theory to develop a tripartite model involving general contractors, labor subcontractors and workers. Two distinct scenarios – with and without government involvement – are analyzed to determine the evolutionary stable strategies. Furthermore, MATLAB-based numerical simulations are conducted to simulate the situation of stakeholders' behaviors in cultivating standard workers. Findings Government intervention can promote the cultivation of standard workers, but its effectiveness depends on how policies are implemented. Governments should adopt a prudent and rational approach when deciding whether to focus support on labor subcontractors and workers or to incentivize all relevant stakeholders. Given that stakeholders differ in their sensitivity to government incentives and penalties, targeted and differentiated measur…

title: Mapping innovative culture: a validated multidimensional scale for China's water engineering sector
abstract: Purpose This study develops and validates a multidimensional, theory-driven scale for assessing innovative culture in China's water engineering sector, differentiating motivational, capability-related, environmental and behavioral conditions surrounding innovative work. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the componential theory of creativity, self-determination theory and organizational support for innovation theory, a 20-item scale was developed and tested with 222 mid- and senior-level managers in Chinese water engineering organizations. Content validation and pilot testing were followed by exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and measurement-invariance testing across experience groups. The benefit dependency network (BDN) was used only as a conceptual framework for positioning the validated dimensions within broader benefit-realization logic; its relationships were not statistically tested. Findings Results support four dimensions: intrinsic motivation, domain-relevant skills, work environment and creativity-relevant processes. The dimensions demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity and model fit, supporting a multidimensional rather than undifferentiated representation of innovative culture in the sampled organizations. Practical implications The validated scale provides organizations with a diagn…

title: Pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction in hemodialysis: an overlooked cardiorenal interface and a target for dialysis prescription
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension is an under-recognized cardiovascular complication of advanced chronic kidney disease, especially in maintenance hemodialysis. It links kidney failure, chronic volume stress, left-heart disease, pulmonary vascular remodeling, arteriovenous access flow, and right-ventricular dysfunction. This review frames pulmonary hypertension as central to the cardiorenal interface in hemodialysis and summarizes epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, diagnosis, and phenotyping. Echocardiography is the main screening tool, but pressure estimates should be interpreted according to dialysis timing and volume status. Right-heart catheterization remains essential to define phenotype and guide management. Treatment should target modifiable drivers: euvolemia without excessive ultrafiltration, optimized left-heart disease care, assessment of high-flow vascular access, and treatment of respiratory or hematologic contributors. Empirical pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapy should be avoided without hemodynamic confirmation. Pulmonary-artery denervation is promising in heart-failure pulmonary hypertension with mild to moderate CKD, but its role in hemodialysis remains unknown.

title: The financial burden of climate disasters on household's health expenditure: evidence from Australia
abstract: Introduction Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of natural disasters. While a growing literature documents their effects on psychological well-being, less is known about their implications for household medical expenditure. This study examines the relationship between direct exposure to weather-related disasters and out-of-pocket pharmaceutical expenditure. Methods We use nationally representative longitudinal data from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey covering 2009-2021. Individual fixed-effects models account for time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity and control for a rich set of socioeconomic and demographic characteristics. Results Exposure to weather-related disasters is associated with significantly higher out-of-pocket pharmaceutical expenditure. This association is concentrated among individuals without private health insurance. An analysis of potential transmission mechanisms further shows that disaster exposure increases the likelihood of reporting several physical and mental health conditions. Discussion The findings suggest that the economic costs of climate-related disasters extend beyond physical damage and public reconstruction spending, affecting household welfare through higher pharmaceutical expenditure. The concentration of this burden among individuals without private health insurance highlights th…

title: Exchange rate flexibility and monetary policy autonomy: a reality or an illusion? Econometric test of the Mundell−Fleming trilemma in the context of emerging countries
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to assess the degree to which flexibilization of the exchange rate regime can be an optimal option for achieving monetary policy autonomy. This could only be attained by putting the revelations of Mundell’s trinity under econometric examination in the context of emerging countries. Design/methodology/approach The methodology unfolds in three complementary stages. First, the authors assess the degree of monetary policy autonomy in each country by estimating the dynamic correlation between domestic interest rates and the US federal funds rate using the DCC-GARCH models. This provides a time-varying measure of the sensitivity of domestic interest rates to external monetary shocks. In the second stage, ANOVA and Bartlett’s tests are used to determine whether monetary policy autonomy differs significantly across exchange rate regimes. Finally, in the third stage, the authors estimate a random-effects panel model incorporating the three pillars of the Mundell trilemma (monetary policy autonomy, exchange rate regime and capital account openness) to provide a comprehensive empirical assessment of their interactions within emerging economies. Findings This study provides empirical evidence that no country is immune to the “Soft Power” exerted by US interest rates on the monetary conditions of peripheral countries. However, flexible exchange rate regimes provide r…

title: Impact of Likelihood Approximation Choices on the Performance of Markov-Switching GARCH Models: Evidence from Thirty Global Financial Assets
abstract: Markov-Switching GARCH (MS-GARCH) models are widely used to capture changing volatility regimes in financial returns, but their exact likelihood is computationally intractable because it requires summing over an exponentially growing number of possible regime histories. Several approximation methods have been developed to solve this problem, yet there is little systematic evidence on how these methods compare when applied to real financial data with diverse distributional properties. This gap is important: choosing the wrong approximation method can lead to materially different parameter estimates, convergence failures, and unreliable risk assessments. This study addresses the gap by comparing four likelihood approximation methods for MS-GARCH(1,1) models across thirty financial assets from five market types: equities, bonds, cryptocurrencies, derivatives, and foreign exchange. The four methods are Gray’s moment-matching collapsing procedure, the Plug-in approximation, five-point Gauss-Hermite Quadrature, and a Particle Filter using sequential importance resampling with 1,000 particles. Models are estimated under two specifications: a baseline (internal volatility dynamics only) and an exogenous (cross-market spillover conditioning) version, giving 220 experimental cases in total. Assets are grouped into four kurtosis categories - low (K<10), medium (10≤K<20), high (20≤K<50), a…

abstract: Abstract The aim of this article is to construct specific Poisson transforms mapping differential forms on the sphere S 2 n + 1 $S^{2n+1}$ upper S Superscript 2 n plus 1 endowed with its natural CR structure to forms on complex hyperbolic space. These transforms have coclosed harmonic values, descend to the BGG (Rumin) complex, and intertwine the differential operators in that complex with the exterior derivative. Passing to the Poincaré ball model, we analyze boundary asymptotics, proving that the values of our transforms admit a continuous extension to the boundary in degrees ≤ n $\leq n$ less than or equals n . Finally, we show that, composing the exterior derivative with the transform in degree n , one obtains an isomorphism between the kernel of the Rumin operator in degree n and a dense subspace of the L 2 $L^2$ upper L squared -harmonic forms on complex hyperbolic space. This provides a realization of the discrete series representations of S U ( n + 1 , 1 ) $SU(n+1,1)$ upper S upper U left parenthesis n plus 1 comma 1 right parenthesis with trivial infinitesimal character in spaces of differential forms on the compact manifold S 2 n + 1 $S^{2n+1}$ upper S Superscript 2 n plus 1 . These developments are motivated by a programme of the third author to prove some instances of the Baum-Connes conjecture. The first part of the article is valid in a much more general setting; …

Integrating Islamic financial and audit governance for strengthening Merah Putih cooperatives in Indonesia
abstract: Purpose – This study aims to develop an empirically informed conceptual model that integrates these dimensions into a coherent governance framework. Design – A descriptive qualitative approach was employed using in-depth interviews, observations, and document analysis involving cooperative practitioners, a Sharia Supervisory Board, Sharia auditors, academics, and regulators. The data were analyzed through data reduction, categorization, thematic interpretation, and triangulation to identify recurring governance issues and relationships among the emerging themes. Findings – The findings identify five interconnected components: Sharia Governance, Internal Control System, Sharia Compliance Audit, Financial Transparency and Accountability, and Continuous Monitoring and Evaluation. These components were synthesized into the Integrated Sharia Audit and Sharia Financial Governance (ISAFG) Model, which positions Sharia compliance as a central governance principle linking decision-making, internal control, auditing, reporting, and continuous evaluation. Research Implications – This model provides a theoretical foundation for the development of a governance framework that can be tested in future research. Originality – The study contributes an empirically informed conceptual framework for strengthening Sharia-based cooperative governance.

The Effect Of Operational Efficiency, Liquidity, And Company Size On Financial Performance (A Case Study On The Pharmaceutical Sector Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange From 2020 To 2025)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of operational efficiency, liquidity, and company size on financial performance in the pharmaceutical sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2020-2025. This study used a quantitative research method. The sampling method used in this study was Non-Probability Sampling with a Purposive Sampling technique. The type of data used was secondary data with a research sample of 11 pharmaceutical companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The data analysis method used was panel data regression analysis assisted by Eviews 14 software, and the hypotheses were tested using the F-test and t-test with a significance level of α = 0.05 or 5%. From the regression analysis results, the simultaneous test showed that operational efficiency, liquidity, and company size simultaneously had a significant effect on financial performance. Partially, the operational efficiency variable proxied by BOPO had a significant effect on financial performance, the liquidity variable proxied by Current Ratio had a significant effect on financial performance, while the firm size variable did not have a significant effect on financial performance.

title: Las Normas Internacionales de Información Financiera, su impacto en el desarrollo de las grandes empresas de Trujillo
abstract: El objetivo del estudio fue analizar si la aplicación de Normas Internacionales de Información Financiera (NIIF) impacta en el desarrollo de grandes empresas de Trujillo. El estudio aplicó un muestreo de 42 profesionales pertenecientes a cinco empresas representativas de la ciudad, bajo un diseño no experimental y enfoque inductivo-deductivo. Los resultados evidenciaron que el 56% de los encuestados percibió cambios significativos en sus organizaciones tras implementar las NIIF plenas. Asimismo, el 65.45% afirmó que la transparencia de los informes contables y financieros mejoró, y el 80% reconoció que la confianza de los inversionistas se fortaleció con su adopción. El análisis estadístico en SPSS determinó que las NIIF plenas generan un impacto positivo del 64.8% en el crecimiento del sector, confirmando la hipótesis de investigación. En conclusión, las NIIF constituyen un instrumento clave con el fin de fortalecer la gestión competitiva en las grandes compañías de Trujillo.

title: Financial vulnerability as a determinant of funding source diversification in European firms
abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyse the relationship between the funding source diversification and the vulnerability of European companies in recent years. It examines how business vulnerability and the characteristics of companies (size, sector, age) influence the number of financing sources that companies use. Design/methodology/approach This analysis relies on an econometric framework using a negative binomial regression estimated with data from the SAFE survey. The model controls for potential endogeneity issues and demonstrates strong robustness after undergoing the relevant validation tests. Findings The results show that the size and sector of the company are decisive in explaining diversification. It also confirms that business vulnerability is positively associated with greater financial diversification. In addition, it was observed that, during times of uncertainty companies tend to increase diversification of their financing sources. Although the analysis covers companies of different profiles, small and medium-sized enterprises stand out for their particularly marked response to situations of vulnerability, which highlights the need to understand their financial decisions in contexts of greater restrictions. Research limitations/implications Based on the findings, the study propose key considerations for both financial management and public policy design. Managerial…

title: Modern slavery governance, digital transformation and financial distress risk: evidence from legally grounded text-based accounting measures
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop and validate a legally grounded accounting measurement framework for modern-slavery governance and examines whether the resulting governance measures are associated with firms' financial distress risk. Existing research predominantly relies on ESG ratings, disclosure proxies, or qualitative assessments that do not clearly distinguish externally specified governance obligations from firms' disclosed governance architecture. We address this measurement gap by translating mandatory modern-slavery governance requirements into reproducible firm-level accounting measures and evaluating their informational relevance for accounting-based risk assessment. Design/methodology/approach This research adopts a two-corpus measurement framework. The first corpus comprises mandatory modern-slavery legislation and internationally recognised institutional frameworks issued between 1930 and 2024, including the Tariff Act (1930), California Transparency in Supply Chains Act, UK Modern Slavery Act, French Duty of Vigilance Law, Australian Modern Slavery Act, German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act, Norwegian Transparency Act, the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD), and complementary institutional frameworks including the ILO, OECD, PRI, and the United Nations Guiding Principles. Rather tha…

title: NRBV's strategic capabilities and SDG disclosure: Does this disclosure enhance financial performance?
abstract: Purpose This study aims to extend the sustainable development goals (SDG) disclosure literature by examining the influence of natural resource-based view (NRBV) strategic capabilities, namely pollution prevention, green product innovation and environmental certification, on SDG disclosure practices among Indonesian companies. It also investigates the association between this disclosure and financial performance. Design/methodology/approach This study uses Indonesian companies listed in Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021 to 2024, comprising 1,256 company-year observations from 314 companies. All data for the variables are collected from annual and sustainability reports and analyzed using panel regression. Findings This study demonstrates that NRBV-based strategic capabilities, such as pollution prevention, green product innovation and environmental certification, significantly enhance companies' SDG disclosure. However, such disclosure is associated with lower financial performance due to the substantial costs required to support SDG-related activities. Practical implications The findings of this study provide practical implications for regulators as the commitment for achieving the SDG can be actualized through stricter sustainability regulations. It can be used to encourage companies to integrate strategic capabilities provided by NRBV into business operations…

title: Financial Feasibility, Modelling and Asset Monetisation in Government & Public Sector Project Development: An Embedded Practice-Based Study at a Big Four Advisory Firm
abstract: Most of what we know about capital budgeting comes from studying corporate finance departments. We know far less about the advisory firms that prepare projects for government, even though a large share of India’s infrastructure pipeline passes through their hands. This paper takes a small look inside one of them. I spent my on-the-job training in the Government & Public Sector (G&PS) practice of KPMG’s Indian advisory arm, and I use a work tracker of 33 task-level entries (10 July–24 August 2026), together with sector evidence and fifteen peer-reviewed sources, to ask four questions about how financial analysis is actually done in that setting. The short answer is that a recognisable capital-budgeting pipeline exists (site and demand assessment, then a financial model, then a Detailed Project Report), but public-sector realities bend it: confidentiality, many layers of sign-off, and tender deadlines. I also found that bid and proposal work made up 36% of my logged entries, almost as much as pre-feasibility and modelling (39%). The two are not rivals. They are stages of one chain: win the mandate, do the analysis, protect the commercial terms. I propose a one-page assumption-traceability sheet that ties feasibility findings to model inputs, and I set out a research agenda on how Indian G&PS practices balance advisory and bid work. The evidence comes from one trainee’s vantage po…

Trust gained, trust lost: how service robot anthropomorphism shapes consumer trust in tight and loose cultures
abstract: Purpose This paper aimed to examine the dual pathways through which service-robot (SR) anthropomorphism shapes consumer trust in service robots (CTSR), specifically the positive serial mediating effect of perceived warmth (WA) and perceived competence (CO) and the negative serial mediating effect of perceived identity threat (TH) and discomfort (DI). It further explored cross-cultural differences in consumer attitudes and their underlying reasons from the perspective of cultural tightness-looseness. Design/methodology/approach Five scenario experiments were conducted across three sets of SR picture stimuli, two service settings (hotel and hospital) and two cultures (China and the United States). Findings Both study 1 and study 2 found that anthropomorphism had a double-edged sword effect on CTSR across different sets of SR picture stimuli, service settings and cultures. An exploratory analysis in study 1 further revealed that among Chinese consumers, CTSR and its antecedents did not show significant differences across different service settings. Study 2 results further indicated that Chinese (versus. American) consumers had higher WA, CO and CTSR, along with lower TH and DI and that region-level cultural tightness influenced CTSR and its antecedents, potentially explaining these cross-cultural differences. Practical implications For hospitality managers, this paper offers insig…

title: Housing insecurity and cancer in South Australia: artificial intelligence-enabled insights from a statewide cancer support service
abstract: Objective This study demonstrates the use of a locally hosted, offline artificial intelligence approach to identify, quantify, and describe housing-related needs documented in routine case notes from a statewide cancer support service. Methods In this retrospective, exploratory service evaluation, a locally hosted, offline large language model screened 25,031 staff-generated case notes recorded between December 2020 and December 2025 for housing-related interactions and grouped confirmed interactions into categories based on a predefined framework. Flagged records and categorisation were independently verified by at least two reviewers, and confirmed interactions were summarised descriptively. Results Of 25,031 interactions, 308 (1.23%) were confirmed as housing-related interactions. The most prominent categorisations were lack of support from health and social services (44.16%), financial barriers to housing stability (37.66%), and homelessness or reliance on emergency or crisis housing (36.04%). In more than half of confirmed interactions, housing was not the initial reason for contact and emerged only during discussion. Conclusions Findings highlight the utility of a privacy-preserving artificial intelligence approach to identify, quantify, and describe community needs at the intersection of housing and cancer care within large-scale, routinely collected service data. title: Spatially Programmed Water Access Reconciles Service Stability with Triggered Post-Use Degradation in Biobased Multilayer
abstract: Abstract Sustainable packaging plastics often face a fundamental paradox: the material must resist moisture and remain stable during service, yet undergo controlled disassembly after disposal. Therefore, sustainable materials should not be evaluated solely based on their service performance or degradation rate, but rather on their ability to undergo effective functional transitions at critical stages throughout the lifecycle. Here, we developed a spatially programmed design strategy that addresses these conflicting requirements by regulating not only when and where water enters the material, but also how the degradation proceeds. The film consists of a hydrophilic, pectin-based inner layer, a hydrophobic polylactic acid (PLA) outer layer, and a hydrogen-bonded interface formed via hydrogen bonding. During packaging service, the PLA layer acts as a moisture-shielding skin, maintaining wet stability, barrier performance, and mechanical integrity. A key conceptual advance of this work lies in turning an inherent weakness into a lifecycle-regulating function, where water sensitivity serves as a trigger rather than a limitation. After use, assisted by mechanical damage, water activates the pectin/deep eutectic solvent (DES) phase. The acidic, water-rich microenvironment generated by the pectin/DES supports preferential cleavage near the PLA chain ends, promoting progressive molecula…

title: Integrated Marketing Communication for Trust Building: Wuling Motors in Indonesia's Automotive Market
abstract: This study examines how Wuling Motors employs integrated marketing communication (IMC) to build consumer trust and strengthen its market presence in Indonesia's automotive industry despite the long-standing dominance of Japanese brands. A qualitative case study approach was employed using purposive sampling, in-depth interviews, and thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Wuling's market penetration was achieved through trust-building strategies integrating local legitimacy, consumer experience, and adaptive marketing communication. This study contributes to the existing literature on integrated marketing communication, market penetration, and country-of-origin effects by explaining how IMC strategically reconstructs consumer trust and brand legitimacy for an emerging Chinese automotive brand in a market dominated by established Japanese manufacturers. The findings suggest that managers should prioritize integrated marketing communication to build consumer trust and strengthen market penetration, while policymakers should promote policies that support fair competition and innovation in the automotive industry

title: Public service crisis caused by the influx of Ukrainian refugees from the perspective of the job demands resources model
abstract: Purpose This study examines the well-being of public servants by utilizing the Job Demands-Resources model during a crisis, contributing to research on human resources management in public institutions. Design/methodology/approach The research investigates the potential moderating roles of Public Service Motivation (PSM) and resilience relative to demanding jobs, available resources, and adverse outcomes in an unprecedented scenario-a situation of adversity. The survey was conducted among civil servants directly involved in serving refugees in main provincial offices that had established crisis centers for Ukrainian refugees in Poland between March and May 2023, when demand for work permits rose due to the protracted war. A total of 138 complete responses were collected. The regression models were supplemented using Johnson's Relative Weight Analysis (RWA). Findings Results indicated that respondents faced heightened job demands and limited job resources, leading to significant stress and extended fatigue; however, the anticipated moderating effects of PSM and resilience were not evident. Originality/value The research advances management scholarship by identifying factors that shape mental health and performance measures in public-sector employees operating in extreme conditions. It offers empirical insights into how crisis-induced workloads challenge human resource management…

Intelligent service systems and value co-creation in hotel frontlines
abstract: Purpose Drawing on service-dominant logic, this study examines how mechanical- and feeling-intelligent service systems contribute to value co-creation through distinct customer-engagement pathways and how these effects change over time and following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Design/methodology/approach Using a large-scale dataset of hotel information and online reviews, we conduct text mining to measure key variables and regression analyses to examine the proposed relationships and their changes over time and following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Findings The results show that mechanical-intelligent service systems contribute to co-created value through functional engagement, whereas feeling-intelligent service systems contribute through emotional and social engagement. Additionally, value co-creation driven by both types of intelligent service systems strengthens over time, with a notable surge observed following the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Originality/value This study advances understanding of how intelligent service systems participate in frontline value co-creation in hospitality and provides practical guidance for service firms seeking to deploy such systems strategically in service frontlines.

title: Effect of income trajectory on dental service utilization patterns during the transition from childhood to adolescence: a 10-year cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objectives This study aimed to investigate the influence of income trajectories on dental service utilization patterns during the transition from childhood to adolescence in a Southern Brazilian birth cohort. Materials and methods Children were followed over 13 years (T1, T2, and T3). Income trajectories (stable low/decreasing vs. stable high/increasing) were identified using group-based trajectory modeling based on finite mixture models. Outcomes included frequency of dental visits and reason for the last visit (preventive vs. curative). Socioeconomic disparities were explored using the non-linear Blinder–Oaxaca decomposition method. Results From 639 children at baseline (T1), 449 were followed at T2 and 429 at T3 (67.1% retention). Adolescents from stable high or increasing-income trajectories had a lower prevalence of dental visits for curative reasons (OR = 0.29; 95% CI 0.09–0.90). Decomposition analysis showed that maternal education (9%) and skin color (12.5%) explained only a small portion of these inequalities, suggesting an independent effect of income over time. Conclusions Individuals with increasing income were less likely to use dental services for curative purposes, regardless of race, dental caries, and maternal education, highlighting the impact of economic stability on oral health behaviors. Clinical relevance Income trajectories over time influence th…

title: Pembuktian Digital dan Pertanggungjawaban Pidana Pelaku Penjualan Akun Streaming Premium Ilegal: Perspektif Hak Cipta serta Batasnya terhadap Terms of Service dan UU ITE
abstract: The rise of subscription-based streaming services has been accompanied by the unofficial sale of premium accounts through social media and digital marketplaces in Indonesia. Although such practices are commonly labelled illegal, the label does not automatically establish criminal liability. This study addresses two issues: first, how difficulties in digital evidence and offender anonymity constrain criminal enforcement, and the standing of electronic evidence in linking offenders, accounts, transactions, and copyright-related objects; second, how criminal liability of sellers of illegal premium streaming accounts is constructed under the Copyright Law, and where its limits lie in relation to Terms of Service violations and offences under the Electronic Information and Transactions Law. Using normative legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches, the study analyses primary legal materials and secondary literature through descriptive-analytical qualitative analysis. The findings show that digital infringement leaves no physical trace, so proof depends on authentic, intact, and relevant electronic evidence supported by digital forensics. Criminal liability under the Copyright Law arises only when the act is committed without right or permission, relates to economic rights over protected works, including computer programs, is carried out for commercial use, involves fau…

title: Consumer acceptance and market viability of artisanal granadilla wine in Puno, Peru: a concept test using the marketing mix and purchasing behavior approach
abstract: Background Fruit wines from non-traditional sources offer opportunities to add value to underutilized agricultural resources and generate economic alternatives in regional contexts. In the Puno region of Peru, granadilla ( Passiflora ligularis ) production faces limited profitability due to lack of processing infrastructure and commercial channels. Objective This study analyzes consumer acceptance and market viability of DIVINO artisanal granadilla wine in Puno, Peru, using the marketing mix framework to understand how product, price, place, and promotion elements influence purchasing behavior. Method A concept test was conducted with 50 potential consumers in Puno. Data were collected using a structured 24-item questionnaire measuring marketing mix perceptions and purchasing behavior on a five-point Likert scale. Analysis included descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, and exploratory multiple linear regression. Results Results show favorable product concept perception: availability via WhatsApp and social media reached 83.0% acceptance; personal recommendations, 81.6%; and price of S/27.00 (approximately 8.00 USD), 78.7%. Correlational analysis revealed a significant relationship between Marketing Mix Strategies and Purchasing Behavior (Rho = 0.834, p < 0.01), with Product (Rho = 0.844) and Promotion (Rho = 0.745) dimensions exerting the greatest influence. In thi…

title: Revisiting the efficient market hypothesis for ten sub-sectors of the Istanbul Stock Exchange (BIST): new evidence from non-linear unit root tests with Fourier function
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine the efficient market hypothesis (EMH) for ten sub-sector indices in BIST (Istanbul Stock Exchange) including Services Index (XUHIZ), Food Index (XGIDA), Holding Index (XHOLD), Chemicals Index (XKMYA), Metals Index (XMANA), Technology Index (XUTEK), Banks Index (XBANK), Financials Index (XUMAL), Industrial Index (XUSIN). Design/methodology/approach To analyse the EMH for ten subsector indices in BIST, the ADF, Fourier KPSS (FKPSS) (2006), Fourier ADF (FADF) (2010), KSS (2003), Fourier KSS (FKSS) (2010), Sollis (2009), Omay (2015), Fourier Sollis (FSOLLIS) (2018), Kruse (2011), Fourier Kruse (FKRUSE) (2019) unit root tests are applied. Findings The results of the Fourier KPSS (2006) stationarity test confirm that the EMH is not valid for the variables XMANA, XUTEK, XBANK and XUMAL. Furthermore, the results of the KSS (2003), Sollis (2009), Fourier Sollis (2018), Kruse (2009) and Fourier Kruse (2019) unit root tests also revealed that the EMH is not valid for the variable XMANA. Finally, the results of the Fourier-Sollis (2018) and Fourier-Kruse (2019) unit root tests imply that the EMH is not valid for the variables XKMYA and XBANK. Originality/value This study is a comparison of the results of traditional unit root tests without structural breaks and linear with the results of current unit root tests with structural breaks and non-…

title: Overview of food service hygiene and sanitation at islamic boarding schools in Tasikmalaya
abstract: Food service management in Islamic boarding schools (pondok pesantren) plays a crucial role in supporting the nutritional status and health of students; however, suboptimal hygiene and sanitation practices may increase the risk of foodborne disease. This study aimed to describe the hygiene and sanitation of food service management in two Islamic boarding schools in Tasikmalaya in 2025. The study employed a descriptive qualitative design using observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation. Informants consisted of eight food handlers and two nutritionists. Data were analyzed through editing, coding, classifying, verifying, and concluding stages. Results showed that food handler hygiene practices met the standards at 81% in Boarding School A and 91% in Boarding School B. Kitchen sanitation facilities met the standards at 86% in both schools. Location and building conditions met the standards at 75% in Boarding School A and 92% in Boarding School B. The application of the six principles of food hygiene and sanitation met the standards at 78% in Boarding School A and 92% in Boarding School B. Main deficiencies were found in the use of light-colored clothing, gloves, kitchen door design, waste separation, and food storage. It is concluded that hygiene and sanitation practices in both boarding schools largely met the standards, yet improvements are still needed in personal hygie…

title: The symbolic divide: how human and robotic service rituals shape perception of brand symbolism
abstract: Purpose The rapid adoption of service robots in tourism and hospitality raises questions about their ability to generate brand-related meaning compared to human-led service rituals. Drawing on interaction ritual theory, this study aims to examine how human and robotic service rituals influence perception of brand symbolism through emotional energy and memory and how these effects differ for customers with varying levels of social phobia. Design/methodology/approach Using a multistudy design, this research uses five experiments across airports, hotels and restaurants to test the hypotheses. The inclusion of both Asian and Western respondents across varying service contexts provides preliminary evidence regarding the generalizability of the findings. Findings Human-led service rituals create a stronger perception of brand symbolism than robot-led rituals, with emotional energy and memory as sequential mediators. For high-social-phobia customers, perception of brand symbolism did not differ significantly between the two ritual types, although human-led rituals generated higher emotional energy; for low-social-phobia customers, human-led rituals produced greater perception of brand symbolism and higher emotional energy. Originality/value This study contrasts human and robotic service rituals, identifies sequential mechanisms (emotional energy and memory) and extends interaction rit…

title: Regulatory governance, digital payment systems and tourism service delivery: a comparative study of Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how different regulatory governance configurations are associated with the functionality of digital payment systems, providing valuable insights for tourism and hospitality service performance. It aims to fill the gap regarding the role of financial regulation in building digital service interactions within tourism contexts. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative comparative policy analysis was conducted across three Southeast Asian countries, including Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. These cases represent innovation-facilitating, controlled and precautionary regulatory models. The analysis is grounded in the proposed Regulatory–Payment–Service Interaction Framework, focusing on three key dimensions, transaction flexibility, cross-border interoperability and user trust and compliance assurance. Findings The results suggest that different regulatory configurations are associated with variations in the functionality of digital payment systems. In particular, innovation-facilitating frameworks are associated with higher transaction flexibility and cross-border interoperability. Controlled models foster widespread adoption under structured conditions, while precautionary approaches lean toward stability but limit cross-border integration. These differences reflect service efficiency, accessibility and customer experience in tourism and hospita…

title: Reused over Refurbished: Exploring Smartphone Life Extension in Thailand’s Informal Market
abstract: The rapid turnover of smartphones has created a growing electric waste challenge globally, particularly in emerging economies where formal recycling infrastructure remains limited. Circular economy strategies, such as reuse and refurbishment, offer potential pathways to extend smartphone lifespans, yet consumer preferences and market structures strongly shape their adoption. This study explores the dynamics of smartphone life extension in Thailand’s informal economy, focusing on Bangkok’s second-hand smartphone market. Data were collected through structured interviews with 110 kiosk operators in Bangkok, complemented by stakeholder insights from recyclers and used-phone providers. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted to examine business pathways, purchasing behavior, and factors influencing smartphone life extension. The findings demonstrated that reuse, rather than refurbishment, constitutes the dominant life-extension pathway. Most kiosks preferred smartphones that could be resold with minimal repair, while warranty provision emerged as the strongest enabling factor supporting consumer trust. Inferential analyses showed that prolonged smartphone circulation was significantly associated with product value, reflected in brand and price, whereas external condition and technical functionality were not significantly associated with smartphone age. The Issue of Legal Regulation of the Increase of a Joint-Stock Company’s Authorized Capital by the Amount of Subsidies Received for Capital Investments in Capital Construction Projects
abstract: The paper considers the problem of increasing the authorized capital of a joint-stock company, 100% of which is owned by the state, by the amount of a subsidy received for the purpose of capital investments in capital construction facilities. The problem of increasing the authorized capital at the expense of property (own funds) is characterized, when the latter is understood as components of equity in the sense of accounting, for example, additional capital. It is determined that the budget subsidy has a dual nature: "earmarked budget funding" and "contribution to property", and therefore, for accounting purposes, it is proposed to qualify it as additional capital as part of the organization's own funds.

title: Emergent Roles of RVLMC1 Neurons in Cardiovascular Homeostasis and Systemic Physiological Regulation
abstract: Abstract Purpose of the Review Adrenergic C1 neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM C1 ) have long been recognized for their role in regulating sympathetic activity and arterial blood pressure (BP). However, novel approaches such as genetic targeting, optogenetics, fiber photometry, among others, allowed us to study the biology of these neurons in deeper detail and in non-anesthetized preparations, unraveling previously underappreciated or unrecognized functions. Here we will discuss recent studies that explored the function of RVLM C1 neurons for the sympathetic regulation of BP and also the emergent roles of these cells for other processes involved in systemic physiological regulation. Recent Findings Using selective methods of manipulation and recording of neuronal activity in conscious animals, it was demonstrated that RVLM C1 neurons play a critical role in BP stability across multiple behaviors, including sleep-wake state and postural changes. Besides cardiovascular control, recent evidence shows that these neurons play a critical role in different homeostatic functions such as thermoregulation, immune response, glycemia and in complex behaviors such as anxiety. Summary RVLM C1 neurons are a key hub that integrates interoceptive signals from peripheral systems to regulate BP and other basic physiological functions. Along with their role in cardiovascular regul…

title: Psilocybin modulates nucleus accumbens activity via astrocytic transcriptional regulation
abstract: Abstract Psilocybin is a serotonergic hallucinogen that acts primarily through 5-HT₂A receptor signaling, yet the mechanisms by which it regulates mesolimbic inhibitory tone remain poorly understood. Here we investigated how psilocybin and structurally related synthetic tryptamines modulate inhibitory signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and whether astrocyte-associated mechanisms contribute to this process. Psilocybin-like tryptamines that generalized to the psilocybin cue increased NAc neuronal activity while reducing extracellular GABA levels, identifying diminished NAc GABAergic tone as a neurochemical correlate of psilocybin-like behavioral responses. Consistent with this interpretation, local pharmacological modulation of NAc GABA receptor signaling altered psilocybin-appropriate responding. We next examined the cellular and molecular basis of this GABAergic regulation. Ex vivo whole-cell recordings revealed that psilocin, the active metabolite of psilocybin, reduced tonic GABA current in NAc medium spiny neurons without affecting miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents, indicating preferential modulation of tonic rather than miniature synaptic inhibition. Cell-type-specific analyses further showed that psilocybin selectively reduced intracellular GABA levels in astrocytes, but not neurons. Psilocybin increased astrocytic NFATc4 and ALDH5A1 protein expression toget…

title: Am I Dependent in Order to Be Perfect? A Serial Mediation Model Linking Academic Perfectionism to AI Dependency Through the Impostor Phenomenon, Writing Anxiety, Self-Regulation, and Academic Procrastination
