title: From Digital Attendance to Discipline Transformation: An Empirical Study of Behavioral Visibility, Moral Surveillance, and Religious Self-Regulation
abstract: Digital transformation in education is advancing rapidly, yet empirical understanding of how technology contributes to student discipline development in Islamic education remains relatively limited. This study aims to examine the relationship between the QR-Code Attendance System, Behavioral Visibility, Parental Digital Engagement, Digital Moral Surveillance, Religious Self-Regulation, and Student Discipline Transformation. The study used a quantitative explanatory survey design involving 436 madrasah students who have used a QR-code-based attendance system. Analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares. The results indicate that the QR-Code Attendance System increases Behavioral Visibility, which in turn strengthens Parental Digital Engagement. Parental Digital Engagement is positively associated with Digital Moral Surveillance, which fosters the development of Religious Self-Regulation. Religious Self-Regulation, in turn, contributes to Student Discipline Transformation. All mediation pathways showed strong significance, including full serial mediation from the digital attendance system to student discipline transformation. These findings expand our understanding of the relationships among digital educational governance, family engagement, moral surveillance, and religious character formation, and highlight the importance of integrating techn…

title: Legal Regulation of the Principles of Bioethics and Biolaw in India
abstract: The author provides the analysis of the evolution of the regulation of biolaw and bioethics in India in 1985–2025 (as of early 2026) in the context of socially significant cases of ethical violations (organ trade, abuses in clinical trials, commercial surrogacy), and assessment of the impact of adopted changes on further regulation. Legal regulation of bioethics and biolaw in India has developed in a predominantly reactive manner – in response to practical crises, unlike the directive model of planned codification characteristic of the European Union. The historical core of the system combined the judicial constitutional doctrine of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and delegated regulation by specialized agencies, supplemented since 2021 by parliamentary sectoral legislation; a unified bioethics law remains absent. The research results may be used in Russian doctrine of biolaw and medical law in developing models of comprehensive regulation of bioethical relations.

title: Molecular Insights into Gene Expression Changes in Apoptosis Immune Response and Cellular Regulation Pathways in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients
Composition, frequency, and severity of future rain-on-snow floods in Germany
abstract: In Germany, severe widespread winter floods are often generated by rain-on-snow (ROS) phenomena. Under suitable conditions, when rain falls on the snow cover, the snow can melt and produce extreme amounts of runoff. In a warming climate, the frequency of ROS events is expected to change locally depending on elevation and regionally based on the general climate conditions. Consequently, the characteristics of ROS-driven winter floods are also anticipated to change. To investigate these changes, streamflow for multiple gauge stations in Germany was simulated using an ensemble of Long Short-Term Memory models based on an ensemble of downscaled climate projections. Germany, as a representative mid-latitude country with a considerable portion of historical floods generated by ROS, offers extensive spatial and temporal coverage of hydrological observations spanning long temporal scales, and hence warranting efficient training of the deep learning model. We used an explainable artificial intelligence method, integrated gradients, to examine flood-generating processes, focusing primarily on ROS, for every simulated flood peak. Changes in frequency, feature importance, and a ranking based severity of ROS flood events were assessed for individual streamflow gauges and for widespread floods affecting multiple catchments across four major river basins in Germany. We found that with regard …
venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF PRESIDENTIAL REGULATION NUMBER 32 OF 2024 ARTICLE 7 ON THE COOPERATION BETWEEN DIGITAL PLATFORMS AND PRESS COMPANIES
abstract: Background. Digital platforms such as Google and Facebook now control the dissemination and visibility of news, leaving small and independent publishers economically dependent on them and earning revenue that does not reflect the true value of their content. Indonesia has responded by introducing Publisher Rights through Presidential Regulation No. 32 of 2024, which is grounded in Copyright Law No. 28 of 2014. Research Purpose. This study aims to analyze Google’s approval mechanisms and policies in managing and distributing PorosJakarta.com news content, and to examine how the regulation protects the economic rights of online news publishers, including the challenges of its implementation. Research Method. This qualitative empirical juridical study collected primary data through in-depth interviews with two informants selected through purposive sampling: the Head of Creator Management at PorosJakarta.com and the Chair of the Publisher Rights Committee (KTP2JB), chosen for their positions and direct involvement in news content distribution and Publisher Rights implementation. Secondary data came from legislation, academic literature, official reports, and institutional documents on Publisher Rights. Findings. Google’s control over content visibility limits publisher oversight and reduces potential revenue. Small publishers still have difficulty accessing royalties because they d…

title: Posthumous Reproduction in Russia: Debatable Aspects of Legal Regulation and Law Enforcement
abstract: Based on an analysis of judicial practice and domestic and international theoretical approaches, this article examines controversial issues of postmortem reproduction in the Russian Federation: subjects eligible for this procedure, ethical and legal issues of establishing written consent during one’s lifetime for reproduction during infertility treatment, and the absence of such consent (implied consent) in cases of postmortem biomaterial collection.

title: The Relationship between Need for Cognition and Chemistry Learning Interest among Senior High School Students: A Chain Mediation Model of Chemistry Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulation
abstract: Abstract Chemistry learning interest plays a crucial role in sustaining students’ engagement with chemistry and supporting their long-term development in science learning. Need for cognition is regarded as an important intellectual investment trait that may be associated with students’ willingness to engage in effortful thinking and complex problem solving. Although previous studies have provided evidence for the association between need for cognition and academic interest, the psychological mechanisms underlying this relationship in the context of chemistry education remain insufficiently examined. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the multiple mediating pathways involving chemistry self-efficacy and self-regulation in the relationship between need for cognition and chemistry learning interest. A multiple-mediation model was constructed by drawing on intellectual investment theory and social cognitive theory, with Social Cognitive Career Theory specifically informing the self-efficacy–interest pathway and research on interest development informing the conceptualization of interest. Data were collected from grade 10 students in China (N = 3,431) using scales to measure need for cognition, chemistry learning interest, chemistry self-efficacy, and self-regulation. The results indicated that (1) need for cognition was significantly and positively associated with students’ …

title: Conflicts of Law in the Regulation of State Duties in Summary Proceedings When Applying Tax Benefits
abstract: The article discusses a conflict in Russian law concerning the payment of state duty in writ proceedings before courts of general jurisdiction. The focus is on claims for alimony and unpaid wages, where the law provides both general rules on court fees and special tax benefits. The author shows that these rules may contradict each other in practice, creating uncertainty for courts and claimants. The article examines this issue through alimony and labor disputes, reviews relevant court positions, and suggests ways to make the legislation more consistent.

title: Legal Regulation of the Inclusion of Royalties in the Customs Value of Goods
abstract: The work is devoted to topical issues of legal regulation of the inclusion of royalties in the customs value of goods. The authors conducted a detailed analysis of the regulatory framework of the EAEU and the Russian Federation governing such issues. Criteria have been established according to which a decision is made to include royalties in such a cost of goods. The authors pays special attention to the analysis of the regulatory framework for determining the customs value when importing raw materials. Based on the analysis, contradictions of the current legislation regarding the inclusion of royalties in the customs value were revealed. It has been established that in the current legislation there are legal conflicts associated with such a definition of customs value.

title: Salud intercultural en Pastaza: regulación del uso de plantas medicinales y de la ayahuasca
abstract: Las plantas medicinales y la ayahuasca forman parte de la medicina ancestral amazónica, pero su uso fuera del contexto comunitario plantea riesgos para la salud y dudas sobre su regulación. El artículo analizó el marco jurídico y la evidencia científica sobre el uso de plantas medicinales y de ayahuasca en Pastaza, desde la salud intercultural. Se realizó una revisión documental de normas, instrumentos internacionales y literatura arbitrada etnobotánica, farmacológica y clínica. El análisis, organizado en tres ejes, mostró que el reconocimiento constitucional de la medicina ancestral no se acompaña de criterios específicos de seguridad, dosificación ni protección del conocimiento, y que los riesgos de la ayahuasca derivan de su uso descontextualizado. Se concluye que se requiere una regulación intercultural, elaborada con los sabios y las comunidades. No se recogieron datos primarios.
venue: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales

title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma
abstract: Purpose Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression. Methods RNA-sequencing and clinical data from 80 UM patients were obtained from TCGA. Thirty highly connected hypoxia-related genes were prioritized through protein-protein interaction analysis and evaluated using five complementary survival-based machine learning approaches: LASSO-Cox, CoxBoost, random survival forest, XGBoost-Cox, and Survival-SVM. Genes supported by at least three of the five methods were defined as core candidates and further evaluated by multivariable Cox regression to construct the prognostic model. The prognostic relevance of the model was evaluated in the dependent GSE22138 cohort using metastasis-free survival (MFS) as the clinical endpoint. Survival analysis, ROC, PCA, GSEA, and immune microenvironment analyses were performed. PFKP was further examined for its associations with immune features and experimentally validated through in vitro and in vivo assays. Results Multi-algorithm consensus identified PFKP, ENO3, and FOXO3 as core candidate genes. PFKP showed the stro…

title: Fabrication, characterization, and reliability analysis of 3D printed high frequency, wideband, and flexible carbon-nanotube and graphene-oxide based rectangular patch antennas deployable on curvilinear and deformable surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we extensively report the additive fabrication and characterization of carbon-nanotube and graphene oxide-based 3D printed rectangular patch antennas that can be integrated on curvilinear and deformable surfaces. Our fabricated antennas can be as thin as few microns and demonstrate reflection coefficient ( S 11 ) values that confirm their super-high-frequency (in tens of GHz) and ultra-wideband characteristics. For example, the measured result of S 11 is below −10 dB in the frequency range of 12 GHz–39 GHz (7 GHz–22 GHz or 5 GHz–25 GHz) for printed patch antennas on flat FR4 substrates (or on curvilinear, bendable PLA substrates). In addition, we quantify other characteristics of these printed antenna structures (e.g., radiation efficiency and gain) and also demonstrate good robustness and reliability (in terms of maintaining the performance) of the antenna structures after being subjected to long-term temperature cycling. Additionally, we measure the radiation efficiency of the printed CNT-GO patch antenna on flat FR4 substrates and also obtain simulation results for quantifying the S 11 and the gain of the antenna.

title: A Gap in the Legal Regulation of Jurisdiction in Criminal Cases Involving Jurors
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the issue of jurisdiction in criminal cases before a jury. It has been established that the Criminal Procedure Code of the Russian Federation has a gap in the legal regulation of the rules of jurisdiction in cases where there are circumstances indicating the need to change the jurisdiction at the stage of trial of a criminal case before a jury. As a result, of the conducted research, the author has proposed legitimate options for overcoming the legislative gap, including through the development and implementation of legal mechanisms for changing the composition of the court.

title: YEASTRACT+: the 2026 update with focus on global quantitative transcription regulation data and metabolic engineering applications
abstract: Abstract YEASTRACT+ (http://yeastract-plus.org/) is a tool for the analysis, prediction, and modelling of transcription regulatory data at gene and genomic levels in yeasts. It incorporates three integrated databases: YEASTRACT, PathoYeastract, and NCYeastract, focused on Saccharomyces cerevisiae, pathogenic yeasts, and non-conventional yeasts of biotechnological relevance, respectively. In this release, YEASTRACT+ offers upgraded information on transcription regulation for 13 yeast species, extending the database to two additional yeasts of the basidiomycota phylum, the pathogenic yeast Cryptococcus neoformans, and the biotechnologically relevant Rhodotorula toruloides. A dramatic upgrade in the quality of the data provided occurred, as regulatory associations between transcription factors (TFs) and target genes are now associated with quantitative assessment. Quantitative impact of TFs on gene expression levels enabled the construction and release of two additional analytical tools: quantitative rank by TF, for the prediction of the most relevant TFs underlying a given transcriptomics dataset; and metabolic engineering based on integrating the quantitative impact of TF expression into genome-scale metabolic models. Altogether, this release of YEASTRACT+ provides unparalleled access to massive, curated, quantitative data associated with gene expression control in 13 yeast spec…

title: Frequency of Adherence to Obstetric Anesthesia Best Practices for Cesarean Delivery: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Analysis
abstract: Background: Increasingly, protocols have been developed to optimize obstetric anesthesia care. However, there is a paucity of data on adherence to these guidelines. The primary aims of this study were to utilize the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group (MPOG) database to estimate (1) the rate of adherence to best practice guidelines for cesarean delivery, (2) the association of case- and hospital-level factors with adherence, and (3) the percentage of variability in adherence attributable to the patient-, case-, and hospital-level factors. Methods: The authors performed a multicenter observational cohort study utilizing the MPOG database to review all cesarean deliveries in women age 15 to 44 yr. Best practices were defined based on societal guidelines and included timely antibiotic administration, postspinal systolic blood pressure (SBP) maintenance greater than 90 mmHg, general anesthesia avoidance, prevention of perioperative hypothermia, use of low-dose neuraxial morphine, postspinal vasopressor infusions, and spinal needles 25-gauge or smaller. Covariates of interest included patient-, case-, and hospital-level factors. Results: The authors analyzed 289,047 cesarean delivery cases in the MPOG database from 2015 to 2022. The following adherence outcomes were observed: timely antibiotic administration, 86.2% (99% CI, 86 to 86.3%); postspinal SBP maintenance, 96.7% (99% C…

Integrating AI with BIM for enhanced construction cost and schedule forecasting: a machine learning model with barrier analysis
abstract: Purpose This research identifies the barriers in BIM-AI adoption and demonstrates how the combination of building information modeling (BIM) and artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to improve construction project schedule and cost forecasting through an integrated framework. Design/methodology/approach This study was conducted using a combination of different research methods. The questionnaire survey measured the 43 barriers by means of the relative importance index (RII) and Pareto analysis. A Python-based BIM-AI forecasting framework was developed based on the findings. Random forest, gradient boosting and XGBoost were benchmarked using 5-fold group cross-validation (GroupKFold) with project-level grouping to prevent data leakage. Findings The results indicate that random forest and gradient boosting showed more stable performance in duration prediction (R2 = 0.806), while random forest achieved the highest accuracy in cost forecasting (R2 = 0.909) and was therefore selected for integration into the final BIM–AI framework. In the applied case study, the model achieved a duration R2 of 0.7886 and a cost R2 of 0.4368, reflecting forecast variance due to project uncertainties rather than realized cost savings. The barrier adjustment factor was 1.0857 (8.57%), consistent with FIDIC Sub-Clause 13.8, which limits contractual adjustments to 10%. Research limitations/implicatio…

title: Mitigating systematic underestimation in short-term wind speed forecasting via time-dependent weighted quantile loss (TDWQLoss)
abstract: Abstract Accurate short-term wind speed forecasting is critical for wind power integration. Although deep learning models exhibit strong predictive capability, their performance is often limited by systematic underestimation when optimized with conventional symmetric loss functions. This issue arises from the right-skewed Weibull distribution of wind speed, where the scarcity of high-wind-speed samples induces pronounced data imbalance and leads to biased learning, particularly under longer forecast lead times. To address this problem, we propose a lightweight Time-Dependent Weighted Quantile Loss (TDWQLoss), which introduces a time-dependent quantile weighting mechanism that adjusts penalty strength according to forecast horizon, enabling a more appropriate representation of increasing uncertainty with lead time. We evaluate the proposed method using three representative spatiotemporal models (Conv3D, SimVP, and MFWPN). Experimental results show that TDWQLoss consistently reduces systematic negative bias and improves overall forecasting accuracy across all models and lead times. In addition, it improves performance in event-based metrics, including Probability of Detection (POD) and Critical Success Index (CSI), without requiring any modification to model architectures. These results demonstrate that TDWQLoss provides a simple, architecture-agnostic, and effective strategy for…

title: A physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for reliable probabilistic rainfall forecasting under heavy and extreme rainfall conditions
abstract: Reliable rainfall forecasting requires not only accurate point predictions but also well-calibrated estimates of predictive uncertainty, particularly during heavy and extreme events where forecast errors carry the greatest operational consequence. Deterministic machine learning models provide point forecasts without quantifying uncertainty, while existing probabilistic methods generally derive uncertainty from statistical relationships in the available data without explicitly conditioning it on the physical state of the atmosphere. This study presents a physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for probabilistic rainfall forecasting. A two-stage architecture employs gradient-boosted regression to estimate the conditional mean and a separate heteroscedastic model trained on out-of-fold residuals to estimate the predictive variance. An interpretable Atmospheric Instability Score, constructed from moisture, thermodynamic, synoptic, and dynamic indicators weighted by variance-model feature importance, then scales the predictive variance on a per-sample basis. The framework is evaluated on the WeatherAUS dataset (145,460 daily observations, 49 stations) for next-day rainfall using rolling-origin validation across five expanding windows. Physics-guided calibration is found not to improve average probabilistic skill, as the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) achieves it…

title: Gated Hybrid Network Using CRNN and RNN Models for Time-Series Forecasting and Case Studies
abstract: Time-series forecasting is a critical challenge in industrial applications such as inventory management and energy planning. This paper proposes a gated hybrid network for time-series forecasting that combines feature vectors obtained from convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) branches. Unlike conventional CRNN models, the proposed model feeds the original time-series sequence in parallel to both CRNN and independent RNN branches, enabling each branch to extract complementary temporal features. A squeeze-and-excitation-inspired gating mechanism then adaptively weights and integrates the two feature vectors. Experiments were conducted using six real-world datasets, including automotive sales, electricity consumption, and solar energy data. The proposed model achieved lower mean relative squared error and relative absolute error values averaged across four forecasting periods than autoregressive (AR), autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), Holt–Winters, gated recurrent unit (GRU), and long short-term memory (LSTM) baseline models on most of the datasets, while also demonstrating superior prediction stability. These results suggest that the proposed architecture is suitable for practical industrial forecasting tasks.

title: Dual-branch graph neural network with spatio-temporal fusion for traffic flow forecasting
abstract: Reliable traffic flow forecasting is fundamental to intelligent transportation systems. Existing spatio-temporal models often emphasise either localised variation or long-range dependency, rely on spatial relations that respond too slowly to traffic changes, and fuse multi-branch features in a relatively shallow way. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch spatio-temporal fusion graph neural network (DB-STFGNN). The first branch captures localised coupled dynamics through multi-scale temporal convolution and a hybrid diffusion dynamic graph convolution (HDGCN) module with iterative interaction updates. The second branch employs spatio-temporal multi-head attention to model broader dependencies across nodes and time steps. To strengthen collaboration between the two branches, the authors further introduce a bidirectional cross-attention fusion module (CAFM), which performs cross-branch interaction and feature refinement before prediction. A non-autoregressive prediction head then maps the fused representation to future traffic flow values. Experiments on real-world benchmarks, including PeMS03, PeMS04, PeMS07 and PeMS08, show that DB-STFGNN achieves competitive performance under mean absolute error, root mean square error and mean absolute percentage error compared with traditional spatio-temporal models and mainstream graph-based baselines.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Transport

title: Machine learning prediction of 1-year thrombosis risk in membranous nephropathy: integration of renal pathology and early longitudinal trajectories
abstract: Introduction Patients with membranous nephropathy (MN) have an increased risk of thrombotic events. Existing prediction approaches primarily use clinical and laboratory measurements obtained at a single time point and rarely incorporate renal pathology or early longitudinal changes. This study integrated multiple types of information to predict the occurrence of thrombosis from 4 weeks after discharge to 1 year after being diagnosed with MN. Method This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,070 patients with MN. Patient characteristics, laboratory findings, renal pathological features, and follow-up data were collected. Patients were randomly divided into training and validation sets at an 8:2 ratio. Latent class trajectory modeling identified longitudinal classes from measurements obtained during the index hospitalization for MN diagnosis and at 2 and 4 weeks after discharge. Predictors were selected using LASSO regression. Seven machine learning algorithms were used, including logistic boosting, adaptive boosting, generalized linear model, weighted k-nearest neighbors (kknn), naive Bayes, random forest, and support vector machine. Result Thrombotic events occurred in 150 patients (14.0%). LASSO selected 10 predictors: hypertension history, stroke or myocardial infarction history, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, D-dimer, cystatin C, estimated glomerular filtratio…

title: Advanced parametric inference and prediction for censored data using standard omega distribution: applications to tensile strength and failure time analysis
abstract: Purpose This study presents a framework for parametric inference and prediction of censored data modeled by the standard omega (SO) distribution under progressively Type-II censored sampling schemes. It focuses on developing accurate estimation methods, predicting future failure times, and constructing prediction intervals using classical and Bayesian approaches. Real-world engineering datasets are analyzed to demonstrate the practical applicability of the proposed methodologies to address challenges in engineering involving censored data. Design/methodology/approach Unknown parameters are estimated using MLE, expectation-maximization, product spacing, least squares, and weighted least squares methods, with rigorous demonstration of the existence and uniqueness of MLEs. Confidence intervals are derived using the Fisher information matrix. Bayesian estimation with gamma priors and MCMC methods is applied to compute credible intervals. Prediction methods include best unbiased, conditional median, and Bayesian approaches, with prediction intervals constructed using pivotal, conditional, and HPD techniques. Simulations and optimality criteria guide the selection of sampling schemes, and the methodology is illustrated with two real engineering datasets. Findings The proposed framework proves effective in addressing engineering problems involving censored data. Simulations validate t…

title: Graph-Aware Controlled Continuous Dynamics Network for Information Diffusion Prediction
abstract: Information diffusion prediction aims to infer future user activations from observed cascade prefixes in social networks, where diffusion unfolds as a complex, irregular, continuous-time process. Existing methods typically model dynamic user preferences by discretizing diffusion into temporal graph or hypergraph snapshots. As a result, these methods produce hidden states only at discrete timestamps and do not capture the continuous dynamics between cascade events. Although neural ordinary differential equations provide a natural framework for modeling temporal dynamics, their trajectories are determined by the initial condition and cannot incorporate subsequent observations as direct controls along the evolving path. To address these limitations, we propose CoDyNet, a graph-aware Controlled continuous Dynamics Network for microscopic information diffusion prediction. CoDyNet first learns graphaware user representations from multi-source static relations and dynamic diffusion hypergraphs. It then constructs timestamp-aware control paths that drive a neural controlled differential equation for observation-guided continuous propagation modeling. We further introduce a cascade-aware graph contrastive regularizer that enforces consistency between clean and perturbed static user representations while avoiding co-activated false negatives. The resulting continuous diffusion context an…

title: Hybrid ANN–metaheuristic models for EWQI prediction and hydrochemical assessment in drinking water distribution systems
Summability Methods for Noisy Industrial Reliability Data and Failure Prediction
abstract: Purpose: Industrial reliability records contain impulsive noise, drift, missing intervals, maintenance resets, regime changes, and right censored lifetimes, which complicate the estimation of degradation trends and the prediction of failures. This study examines how classical summability ideas, especially Cesàro averaging and Abel type regularization, can be integrated with robust preprocessing, survival analysis, and prognostics. Research Methodology: The study uses a methodological design that specifies a hybrid workflow of data quality screening, time aware normalization, parallel smoothing at multiple scales, reliability or degradation modeling, blocked temporal validation, uncertainty calibration, and cost aware maintenance decisions, supported by mathematical definitions and generated illustrations. Results: The illustrations show that short windows leave noise, long windows delay warnings, and the cumulative Cesàro mean recovers only about half of a regime shift after 100 cycles, whereas trailing and Abel type means reach about 90% within 18 cycles. In a pump example, smoothing removed two false alarms at the cost of about two days of warning. Conclusions: Summability should be treated as a transparent, tunable preprocessing and diagnostic layer rather than as a substitute for a physically meaningful failure model. Limitations: All numerical illustrations are synthetic, …

title: Prediction of lncRNA–cervical cancer associations using a multi-view collaborative variational autoencoder with knowledge distillation transfer learning
abstract: Introduction Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play critical regulatory roles in the pathogenesis of cervical cancer, and accurate identification of lncRNA–cervical cancer associations is important for understanding the molecular mechanisms of the disease and discovering potential therapeutic targets. However, the extreme scarcity of cervical cancer-specific lncRNA association data constitutes a major bottleneck limiting the performance of existing computational prediction methods. Methods To address this challenge, we propose a Multi-View Collaborative Variational Autoencoder based on Knowledge Distillation Transfer Learning (MVCVAE), which integrates multi-source heterogeneous data fusion and cross-disease knowledge transfer in a task-oriented manner. The multi-view collaborative variational autoencoder constructs dual-view feature representations of lncRNA and disease similarities and employs a symmetric encoder–decoder architecture to learn complex lncRNA–disease association patterns in the latent space. The knowledge distillation transfer learning framework adopts a teacher–student network design: a teacher model is pre-trained on a large-scale dataset containing 12,865 lncRNA–disease associations to learn general association patterns, and the resulting prior knowledge is effectively transferred to a student model targeting 92 cervical cancer associations through feature dist…

Response Inhibition in an Affective Context and Its Relation to Psychopathic Traits
abstract: Background: Psychopathic traits are associated with affective deficits and elevated impulsivity levels, such as those measured by Go/No-go tasks. Previous research assessing the combined effects of psychopathic traits and emotional processing on response inhibition has focused on low cognitive load task designs and found little evidence of valence-dependent effects. Objective: To investigate whether assessing affective response inhibition under low and high cognitive load manipulations reveals interactive effects between psychopathic traits and valence processing on response inhibition. Methods: We assessed 146 student and community participants using the Psychopathic Personality Inventory—Revised (PPI-R). Response inhibition was measured under low and high cognitive load using the parametric Go/No-go task (PGNG) alongside positive, negative, and neutral distractor images. Results: Cognitive load and valence affected performance. Response times were faster and accuracy rates were higher for the low-load (easier) task stage. Negative and positive trials slowed response times and reduced response inhibition performance compared with neutral trials. In terms of psychopathic traits, the PPI-R Self-Centered Impulsivity factor and two of its subscales, Machiavellian Egocentricity and Blame Externalization, correlated negatively with response inhibition across valences and load. Corre…

title: Optimization of Verbascoside Extraction from Jasminum subtriplinerve Blume Collected in Quang Tri Province Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Abstract: This study optimized the ultrasound-assisted extraction of verbascoside from Jasminum subtriplinerve Blume using an ethanol–water solvent system. Verbascoside content under various conditions was determined by HPTLC- Scanning. Key variables and their ranges were initially screened using the one-factor-at-a-time approach and subsequently optimized via response surface methodology with a Box–Behnken design. Ethanol concentration (10–40%), extraction temperature (50–80°C), and extraction time (15–45 min) were selected as independent variables, while verbascoside yield and total extract yield were responses. Under the optimal conditions (33% ethanol, 76°C, 43 min), the verbascoside yield reached 60.12% and total extract yield was 24.46%, with RSD values of 1.77% and 1.49%, respectively. This result provides a scientific basis for the production of a highly concentrated extract of verbascoside from the medicinal plant, opening up applications in medicine and pharmaceuticals. Keywords: Verbascoside, Optimization, Jasminum subtriplinerve.

abstract: Background: Delaying surgery following neoadjuvant concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) may permit continuing tumor cell death and regression over time. This exploratory pilot study examines the influence of extending the time interval from completion of CCRT to surgery on achieving a pathological complete response (pCR) across a rectal cancer cohort. Methods: This pilot analysis reviewed data from 64 patients with Stage II–III rectal cancer who completed neoadjuvant protocols were reviewed. Patients were stratified based on the real-world resting interval between CCRT completion and total mesorectal excision (TME) into Shorter Interval group (<8 weeks, n = 10) and an Extended Interval group (≥ 8 weeks, n = 54). Univariate logistic regression analyzed the impact of resting intervals, alongside clinical stage, tumor grade, and histology on pCR and overall response rates (ORR). Primary outcome included analyzing if a prolonged interval between the completion of CCRT and radical surgery yields superior tumor regression without escalating surgical morbidity, Secondary outcomes included factors influencing pCR. Results: Surgery executed ≥8weeks weeks post-CCRT demonstrated a prevailing, non-significant trend toward significantly higher odds of achieving a pCR compared to shorter intervals (OR = 3.250, 95% CI: 0.369–28.650, P=0.289).

abstract: Purpose: We evaluated whether student and item representations learned from response correctness provide information about examinee and item characteristics, including item response theory (IRT) estimates, and whether this information translates into better response prediction.Methods: We analyzed Korean Medical Licensing Examination (KMLE) responses from 3,259 examinees to 360 items. We froze 64-dimensional representations learned by cyclic dual latent discovery (CDLD) and assessed IRT prediction using nested cross-validation. Exploratory analyses compared the addition of CDLD, 64-dimensional representations based on singular value decomposition (SVD64), or random inputs to augmented response summaries. Across 5 splits, response prediction was compared with Rasch and 2-parameter logistic (2PL) models; 0–40 responses from new examinees were used for adaptation.Results: In exploratory comparisons, adding CDLD to augmented response summaries increased R2 from 0.9289 to 0.9843 for 2PL ability and from 0.8759 to 0.9216 for log discrimination. Fermi-Level Modulation in Graphene Sensors Revealed by Voltage-Dependent Raman Spectroscopy and 3D Waterfall Response Mapping
abstract: Abstract The electronic properties of graphene sensors are governed by the position of the Fermi level, which determines the carrier concentration and consequently controls the electrical conductivity and sensing performance. Although Fermi-level modulation is widely recognized as the fundamental mechanism of graphene-based sensing, its direct experimental correlation with the dynamic sensing response has remained insufficiently explored. In this work, we demonstrate that Raman spectroscopy provides a direct, nondestructive method for quantifying the relative Fermi-level modulation through systematic shifts of the G and 2D Raman bands associated with changes in carrier concentration. The Raman analysis reveals reversible electrical tuning of the graphene electronic structure under source-drain voltage without introducing structural defects, allowing quantitative estimation of the Fermi-level relative displacement. To investigate the dynamic behavior of the same electronic states during sensor operation, low-frequency time–frequency waterfall spectroscopy was employed under chemical and optical stimulation. The results demonstrate that external stimuli induce transient perturbations of the graphene Fermi level, producing characteristic conductivity fluctuations that depend on the magnitude and kinetics of carrier-density modulation. The combination of static (Raman spectroscopy)…

title: Dynamic Response and Vibration Signature of Single Degree of Freedom Steel System
abstract: Introduction/Objective Civil engineering structures face major challenges, particularly earthquakes, which are random phenomena in their intensity and frequency content. The seismic response of structures depends largely on the intensity of an earthquake and especially on its frequency content. The assessment of the dynamic behavior of structures subjected to seismic excitations is therefore essential for understanding their performance. The main objective of this study is the experimental identification of the vibration signature of a single-degree-of-freedom SDOF steel system. Methods Based on the laws of similarity, a 1:6 reduced-scale steel model is developed. In this context, dynamic experiments using the shaking table of the RISAM laboratory (Risk Assessment and Management: University of Tlemcen) are carried out to determine the structural dynamic parameters of this steel system. This is achieved through experimental determination of natural frequency and damping. Acceleration and displacement measurements are also established. The experimental estimation of damping is established using the logarithmic decrement method. Several dynamic analyses are carried out based on the finite element model of the reduced-scale steel system. title: Criticizing the Methodological Realisability of the Value-Free Ideal: A Response to Sikorski
abstract: Abstract The value-free ideal (VFI) has recently been the subject of renewed interest with some authors attempting to defend it in the face of ongoing criticism. A particularly ambitious project is that of the methodological vindication of realisability, which attempts to vindicate the VFI through arguments aimed at scientific methodology and how research practice can be amended to avoid the influence of non-epistemic values. I shall critically review the debate around the strategy of methodological vindication and respond to the attempts at vindicating the VFI. Thereby, I will draw a distinction between two aspects of the classic argument against the VFI usually referred to as the argument from inductive risk (AIR) and show why a distinction between a problem of context-sensitivity and a problem of translation is relevant. Utilizing this distinction, I shall demonstrate why the methodological vindication is ultimately unsuccessful.

Engineered Dielectric Response of Liquid-Filled Interfacial Bubbles in van der Waals Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract Interfacial bubbles in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are typically regarded as unavoidable byproducts of stacking. Here, we show that they can be repurposed as engineered dielectric nanocavities by intentionally trapping selected liquids during assembly. A simple prewetting step before stamp transfer forms liquid-filled bubbles at hBN/graphite interfaces containing acetone, ethanol, H2O, and NaCl(aq), alongside untreated reference bubbles. Electrostatic force microscopy (EFM), crosstalk correction, and finite-element modeling enable quantitative extraction of the effective dielectric constant (εeff) of individual bubbles, revealing higher εeff for all liquid-filled bubbles than for untreated ones. To estimate the apparent core permittivity of the confined contents, each bubble is modeled as a liquid core enclosed by an hBN shell. Simulations of the tip–bubble–substrate geometry yield core dielectric constants (εcore) larger than εeff yet physically consistent with the trapped media. Acetone and ethanol exhibit εcore values close to their expected dielectric properties, whereas water shows a reduced εcore consistent with nanoconfined pure water. Notably, NaCl(aq) shows a larger εcore than pure water, suggesting distinct electrolyte dielectric behavior under nanoscale confinement. This work establishes vdW bubbles as versatile platforms for engineering local elect…

title: Anomaly detection of asset data in power monitoring systems based on knowledge graph reasoning
abstract: Abstract Edge computing nodes face severe constraints on both computing and storage resources, and the dynamic correlation of asset data remains complex within power monitoring systems. To address this challenge, this study proposes an anomaly detection framework that is based on knowledge graph reasoning and tailored for asset data in such systems. The framework first constructs a lightweight embedding method for knowledge graphs, then introduces a time-sliding window mechanism that builds a sequence of dynamic subgraphs, thereby adapting to the dynamic evolution of the network topology. Following this, the approach combines relational attribute modulation with low-rank matrix decomposition, thereby reducing both the model’s global parameter count and its memory overhead. It then proposes a relation-aware lightweight graph attention network. Within this network, a differential projection decoupling mechanism separates the coupling effects between target nodes and relational features. In addition, the approach introduces a sparse attention truncation selection strategy to filter out low-frequency background noise. Based on real datasets collected from substations and distribution networks, the results show that the proposed model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.982 on dataset A and an accuracy of 0.949 on dataset B. The low-rank…

title: Spatial dynamics of tourism and human capital: spillover effects on environmental sustainability
abstract: Purpose This study examines the spatial dynamics of environmental quality in 213 Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics (NUTS)-2 regions across 23 European countries during 2016 and 2020. It evaluates the impact of tourism activity and human capital on environmental sustainability, challenging traditional assumptions about economic growth and environmental quality. Design/methodology/approach A spatial econometric modeling approach is applied to assess the interdependencies between regions. The study incorporates spatial lag and spatial error models to capture spillover effects. The Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis is tested using an alternative specification, while the spatial relationships among environmental quality, tourism, and human capital are analyzed through spatial regression techniques. Findings The results contradict the conventional EKC hypothesis, revealing a convex relationship between economic growth and environmental quality. The study highlights three key findings: (1) environmental quality in a given region is significantly influenced by its neighboring regions, (2) human capital generates positive spillover effects, enhancing sustainability across regional boundaries, and (3) tourism activity produces negative externalities, contributing to environmental degradation beyond local jurisdictions. Research limitations/implications The study…

A Prompt-Optimized Vision-Language Model System for Fine-Grained Fashion Style Recognition
abstract: With the accelerated digital transformation of the fashion industry, accurate clothing style recognition has become essential for intelligent e-commerce retrieval, personalized outfit recommendation, and fashion trend analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs), with their cross-modal semantic alignment and zero-shot inference capabilities, offer an efficient technical pathway for this task. However, when applied to the fashion domain, general-purpose VLMs face several challenges, including vague prompt semantics, insufficient fine-grained discrimination, difficulty in capturing composite style characteristics, and high deployment costs. To address these issues, this paper presents a comprehensive clothing style recognition system based on Qwen3-VL-Plus. A four-level structured prompt template—comprising style definitions, visual feature guidance, and confidence distribution constraints—is introduced to direct the model's attention toward fine-grained attributes such as silhouette, fabric, color, and decoration. A confidence distribution modeling mechanism based on Softmax normalization is proposed to convert cross-modal similarity scores into interpretable confidence distributions, enabling quantitative representation of composite styles. Furthermore, INT8 quantization and inference pipeline optimization are employed to achieve lightweight deployment, allowing the system to operat…

Sistema agroforestal para el uso racional del suelo en Sacrifrancia, Pastaza, Ecuador: estudio de caso
abstract: La degradación del suelo por monocultivo, agroquímicos y deforestación amenaza la producción y la biodiversidad amazónicas. El estudio analizó un sistema agroforestal para el uso racional del suelo en una finca de la zona de Sacrifrancia, en Pastaza. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo con revisión documental de artículos científicos y una entrevista semiestructurada de once preguntas al propietario, quien dirige la finca desde hace dieciocho años. Según su relato, la finca combina maderables, frutales, aromáticas y cacao bajo manejo orgánico, con una poda que deja el material vegetal como abono, mejor calidad del cacao y mayor presencia de fauna silvestre; el apoyo institucional se percibe como limitado. Se concluye que el caso es coherente con lo que la literatura atribuye a la agroforestería, aunque, al tratarse de un solo testimonio sin mediciones, no permite afirmar que el modelo sea replicable.

title: Implementation drivers of blockchain technology for payment processes of construction projects in South Africa: a quantitative analysis
abstract: Purpose Innovative technologies such as blockchain are changing the modus operandi of construction contract execution and project actualisation. Implementing blockchain technology for the payment process seeks to proffer solutions to conventional challenges facing construction contract execution. This study aims to explore the drivers of implementing blockchain technology for the payment process in construction contract administration from a developing economy perspective. Design/methodology/approach The study used a quantitative approach aided by a well-structured questionnaire for data collection from the target respondents. The retrieved data was analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, namely, the Kruskal-Wallis h-test, Student Newman Kauls (post hoc) test and exploratory factor analysis. Findings The principal components extracted from the analysis portrayed three main drivers of implementing blockchain technology for the payment process in the construction industry: automation functionality, enhanced security and transparency and trust. Also, it was revealed that there are diverging viewpoints among the respondents on some of the identified drivers. Practical implications The study’s findings unravel practical insights that can assist in driving the digital transformation of payment processes of construction projects for effective contract administration. title: Evaluating the Circular Economy Performance of Construction and Demolition Waste Management in Taiwan: A DEA and Malmquist Index Approach
abstract: Construction and demolition waste (CDW) is a major industrial waste stream in Taiwan. Conventional indicators such as recycling rates and treated volumes describe throughput, without directly measuring how efficiently regional systems transform resource inputs into reusable products while limiting residual waste. This study evaluates regional CDW circular-economy performance using an input-oriented data envelopment analysis (DEA) framework and the Malmquist productivity index. The original database covered 19 geographic units for 2023–2025; excluding observations with all-zero outputs, the static DEA dataset contained 53 county-year observations for 18 counties and cities. A common pooled frontier was estimated using three inputs (CDW received, licensed treatment/reuse capacity, and estimated treatment cost) and three outputs (treated/reused CDW, recycled product output, and a reciprocal transformation of residual waste). For 2023–2025, the mean Charnes-Cooper-Rhodes (CCR) efficiencies were 0.509, 0.455, and 0.461 and mean Banker-Charnes-Cooper (BCC) efficiencies 0.639, 0.598, and 0.573, respectively. Input correlations were moderate ( r ≤0.578). Slack analysis identified frequent treated-/reused-output shortfalls and input excesses. title: Managing material cost overruns in industrial building projects using a system dynamics approach
abstract: Purpose Material cost overruns remain a persistent challenge in industrial construction projects, driven by interconnected risks such as price volatility, supply chain disruptions and changes in material specifications. This study aims to enhance cost risk management by analysing the dynamic relationships among these key contributing factors. Design/methodology/approach A system dynamics modelling framework was developed to investigate feedback mechanisms and temporal dynamics among nine critical material-related risk factors. These factors were identified through an extensive literature review and expert input, and structured into interconnected sub-models representing core risk domains, including material price volatility, distribution inefficiencies and impacts of specification changes. Findings Nine interconnected material risks collectively drive cost deviations through reinforcing and balancing feedback mechanisms. Baseline simulations showed a 135% cumulative deviation, reduced to 122% through preventive measures, a 10.66% improvement. Procurement optimisation achieved the largest reduction, while improved material planning and warehouse management also strengthened cost control. Originality/value This study proposes an empirically grounded system dynamics framework to examine the interdependent and temporal effects of material-related risks on cost overruns in industria…

Battery-Side Energy Efficiency of Wirelessly Connected Robots Using the Joint Offloading, Compression and Scaling Offloading and Scheduling Policy
abstract: Battery capacity is the binding constraint on how long a fleet of mobile robots can work between charges. In wirelessly connected fleets, the robot battery is shared between three competing consumers: locomotion, onboard computation, and the radio. All energy figures in this paper refer exclusively to the robot battery; the edge server is mains-powered and outside the optimisation scope. Offloading perception to the edge server removes computation from the battery, but it consumes airtime on a shared wireless medium and a late result forces the robot to slow down, lengthening the mission and increasing locomotion energy drawn from the same cell. We develop a battery-side energy model that prices a missed perception deadline in joules through its effect on mission duration, derive the penalty in closed form as λ = 5.18 J, and propose joint offloading, compression and scaling (JOCS), a decentralised per-epoch policy that jointly selects the offloading decision, payload compression level, transmit power, and processor frequency for each pipeline stage. JOCS admits offload requests in decreasing order of battery energy saved per second of airtime consumed, subject to a feasibility test on the self-induced congestion. Simulated over 30 independent channel realisations, JOCS reduced robot battery energy by 22.6% relative to run-to-deadline local execution at eight robots per access p…

title: Conception d’un système spatial d'aide à la décision pour la collecte et la surveillance des maladies animales au Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, Tchad
abstract: Contexte : La province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, située au Tchad, est une zone pastorale importante mais qui demeure vulnérable aux épizooties en raison de la densité et de la diversité de son cheptel. Pour combler le manque d'outils numériques destinés à la surveillance sanitaire animale, un système d'aide à la décision spatiale (SDSS) a été développé dans le cadre du projet Géo Santé, sous la forme d’une application mobile innovante. Objectif : Cette étude avait pour objectifs de présenter la conception et la mise en œuvre du SDSS Géo Santé, et d'évaluer ses contributions effectives dans la province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest. Méthodes : Conçue en collaboration avec les acteurs locaux, l'application a été expérimentée dans treize cantons et a permis d'enregistrer 160 cas sanitaires dans le cadre d’une phase pilote. Les données ont été collectées par des vétérinaires et des techniciens communautaires à l’aide de formulaires numériques géolocalisés intégrant des informations zootechniques, cliniques et spatiales ; les cas recensés correspondent à des suspicions cliniques non confirmées biologiquement. Résultats : Les résultats ont montré une amélioration de la traçabilité des maladies animales suspectées et du suivi des risques sanitaires. Process mining in humanitarian procurement: a scoping review
abstract: Purpose Despite its strong potential to optimize business processes, process mining remains largely unexplored in humanitarian operations. Therefore, this study aims to systematically examine the state of research across process mining in procurement and humanitarian procurement analytics and identify complementarities between the two streams. Design/methodology/approach A scoping review methodology was applied to systematically analyze peer-reviewed studies published between January 2015 and August 2025. Following a structured search and screening procedure, 43 studies were analyzed across two themes: process mining in procurement and humanitarian procurement analytics. Findings The study reveals a clear methodological divergence between the two themes. Process mining studies mainly provide descriptive and diagnostic insights using real event-log data, yet rarely extend to predictive or prescriptive analytics. In contrast, humanitarian procurement research advances prescriptive models but mainly relies on simulated or parameterized data. Predictive applications remain underdeveloped across both themes, while prescriptive models in humanitarian procurement are rarely validated using operational data. The comparison shows that process-mining capabilities, including compliance checking, bottleneck analysis, anomaly detection and process-variant analysis, could provide empirical e…

title: Life cycle management for improving sustainability effectiveness in area-based infrastructure projects: lessons from Thailand
abstract: Purpose Life cycle management (LCM) is increasingly recognized as a strategic approach for improving infrastructure sustainability; however, evidence remains limited on how perceived implementation of LCM practices is associated with perceived sustainability effectiveness across the life cycle of area-based infrastructure projects (AIPs), particularly in developing countries. This study examines these associations in Thai local administrative organizations (LAOs). The Sufficiency Economy Philosophy (SEP) and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) provide the policy context; they are not measured as separate empirical constructs. Design/methodology/approach Literature synthesis and expert screening were used to develop the questionnaire. A total of 645 valid questionnaires from Thai LAOs were analyzed using SPSS Version 28, exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, correlations and multiple regression. Qualitative consultations supported item refinement and interpretation; because participant counts and a formal qualitative coding record were unavailable for this revision, they are not presented as an independently validated mixed-methods strand. How review environments shape review voting: the roles of competition intensity and attention intensity
abstract: Purpose Most platforms feature online reviews with voting functions that act as peer-based social feedback. Beyond prior research that examines how review and reviewer characteristics shape voting outcomes, this study investigates how two environmental factors, competition intensity and attention intensity, affect voting outcomes. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on communication models and uses Poisson Pseudo Maximum Likelihood regression with high-dimensional fixed effects, using 293,670 Yelp reviews from 29,842 reviewers across 11,436 US restaurants to empirically test our communication-based framework. Findings We find that competition intensity reduces the number of votes a review receives, whereas attention intensity increases it. We also show that review deviation and reviewer status mitigate the negative effect of competition; review deviation amplifies, whereas reviewer status weakens, the positive effect of attention. Practical implications Our findings demonstrate that the environment surrounding a review meaningfully shapes how it communicates with readers, guiding users' attention allocation and engagement. The results offer practical implications for reviewers seeking to strategically improve voting outcomes and for platforms aiming to manage information overload and enhance user engagement efficiency. title: Integration of Solar PV and Wind Power into Modern Power Grids: A State-of-the-Art Review
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation now supply a rising share of electricity in many countries, and the systems built around coal, gas, and hydro were not designed for them. Both resources are weather-driven, both connect to the network mostly through power electronics, and both are often located far from load centres. This review examines how these characteristics affect network operation and how the research and industry communities have responded. It covers generation and conversion technologies, the main operational problems (voltage and frequency regulation, falling inertia, power quality, fault behaviour, congestion, and curtailment), and the main remedies: grid-forming converter control, energy storage, hybrid plants, flexible transmission, demand-side flexibility, and data-driven forecasting. The paper adds worked equations, simulated illustrations, and side-by-side comparisons of technologies, control methods, forecasting approaches, and documented system events. Open research problems are identified for networks that must run with very high shares of inverter-based generation. The review is intended as an organized starting point for researchers and engineers working on renewable-rich power systems.

title: Isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant glioma in the post-INDIGO era: advances in classification and management
abstract: Purpose of review Recent advances have reshaped the classification and management of IDH-mutant glioma. Updated molecular diagnostic frameworks, evolving multidisciplinary treatment strategies, and the emergence of mutant IDH inhibitors have introduced new therapeutic opportunities while also raising important unresolved clinical questions. This review summarizes recent developments and ongoing controversies in the post-INDIGO era. Recent findings Recent cIMPACT-NOW recommendations further refine molecular classification and grading criteria for IDH-mutant glioma. Increasing evidence supports maximal safe resection and, in select cases, supramaximal resection, particularly in astrocytoma. Questions regarding the optimal timing and modality of radiation therapy remain unresolved. Comparative studies of chemotherapy regimens continue to demonstrate tradeoffs between efficacy and toxicity. The INDIGO trial established mutant IDH inhibition as a new treatment paradigm, and ongoing studies seek to optimize patient selection and explore new types of IDH-directed therapies. Summary Management of IDH-mutant glioma is becoming increasingly individualized and molecularly driven. Although mutant IDH inhibitors represent a major therapeutic advance, their integration with existing treatment paradigms remains uncertain. Ongoing studies will continue to refine prognostic stratification and m…

title: Human–AI interaction in academic knowledge co-creation: a typology based on a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to knowledge co-creation in academic writing, focusing on systematic literature reviews (SLRs) as a representative and consequential form of structured knowledge production. It develops a typology of human–AI interaction that reveals how intellectual responsibility, decision-making and dialogue are distributed between human researchers and AI systems. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of 120 publications from Scopus and Web of Science was conducted to analyse applications of AI in SLRs. Studies were coded along two dimensions derived from human–AI interaction theory: (1) decision-making delegation and (2) iterative dialogue between humans and AI. Using deductive thematic analysis, the research identified distinct interaction types and synthesised empirical patterns into a transparent framework. Findings The analysis reveals three types of human–AI interaction: AI-Supported, Collaborative and Partner-like. The AI-supported type treats AI as an assistive tool for automating repetitive tasks while preserving full human control. The collaborative type represents dialogical co-creation, where humans and AI engage in iterative prompting and feedback cycles. The partner-like type reflects hybrid partnership and partial delegation, where AI contributes analytical reasoning and interpretation u…

Enhancement mechanism of high temperature stability for in-situ oxide scale on high-entropy carbide coatings induced by rare earth
abstract: Abstract For ultra-high temperature ceramic (UHTC) coatings used in aerospace thermal protection systems, enhancing the oxygen barrier capability and thermal stability of in-situ oxide scale during ablation is crucial for stable service. Herein, a high-entropy design strategy is proposed to boost the compactness and phase stability of oxide scales by leveraging multi-component synergistic effects. Three high-entropy carbide coatings, (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Sm)C (HEC-Sm), (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Er)C (HEC-Er) and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Lu)C (HEC-Lu), with better ablation resistance than ZrC, (Hf-Zr-Ti)C, and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y)C coatings,were designed. HEC-Lu delivers optimal ablation resistance, featuring a linear ablation rate of -0.173 ± 0.012 μm·s-1, superior to HEC-Sm (-0.111 ± 0.032 μm·s-1) and HEC-Er (-0.144 ± 0.022 μm·s-1). This superior performance is correlated with higher Ti retention and stronger calculated Ti-O bonding, increasing Ti content in the oxide scale by 53.85 % and 33.33 % compared to HEC-Sm and HEC-Er, thereby inhibiting volatilization. Rare-earth (Sm, Er, Lu) incorporation can reduce the diffusion coefficients of Ti and O atoms in oxide scales by one order of magnitude at 2573 K compared with TiO2. title: Synergistic Absorption Mechanism in Flexible Polymer Composites Reinforced with Rare Earth Cobaltite and Molybdenum Carbide for EMI Shielding Applications
abstract: Abstract The sudden growth of digital devices and fifth-generation (5G) communication systems has generated increasing concerns regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding in advanced technological applications, due to the high necessity for development of flexible, lightweight and efficient shielding materials. In this study, low thickness polymer composite films based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) polymer that is incorporated with gadolinium cobaltite and molybdenum carbide fillers were successfully fabricated through a solution casting technique. The chemical, structural, and morphological characteristics of the composite films were investigated using XRD, FTIR, FESEM, HR-TEM, tensile strength and contact angle. Thermal stability was assessed through thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and electromagnetic properties were evaluated in terms of complex permittivity and permeability across the X-band frequency range. The EMI shielding was examined in terms of shielding effectiveness due to absorption, reflection, and transmission and further validated using CST software. The selected composite film with an ultralow thickness of ∼0.15 mm exhibited a maximum EMI shielding efficiency of ∼49 dB in the X-band region with the absorption dominant shielding as the primary attenuation mechanism. The composite films displayed an enhanced mechanical strength and hydrophobicity beh…

title: A multi-mechanism partial counterbalancing approach for multi-session esports performance research in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
abstract: Esports performance research increasingly relies on repeated-measures designs, in which each player serves as their own control. Such designs are efficient, but they are vulnerable to order effects: participants improve with practice, tire within a session, and carry the influence of one condition into the next. Competitive gaming makes this problem unusually acute, because skill acquisition in digital games is rapid and session fatigue develops quickly. The conventional remedy, complete counterbalancing, is unattainable once a study tests more than a handful of conditions. This article describes and evaluates a partial counterbalancing strategy that layers four mechanisms: category-level Latin square sequencing, randomisation of values within categories, forward–reverse distribution of sequences across participants, and temporal spacing with session truncation. The strategy was implemented in an 18-week laboratory study of 170 South African Counter-Strike: Global Offensive players, testing six categories of hardware and in-game settings at three values each. Three independent checks were used to evaluate whether order effects had been controlled. Conditions were evenly distributed across testing positions in every setting category. Algorithmicized Administrative Discretion in the Mechanism of Administrative Law Protection of Property: The Normative Nature, Concept, and Procedural Guarantees
abstract: The article examines algorithmised administrative discretion as a mode of exercising the general legal institution of administrative discretion in the digital environment of public administration. It defines the concept and identifies three mandatory elements: a legally established scope of choice, prior digital formalisation and a legally significant impact of the system rule on an individual decision. The concept is distinguished from automation of bound powers, technical error and hidden rulemaking. Using property-related administrative procedures as examples, the article substantiates requirements for reasoning, reconsideration by an authorised official, a legal regime for system parameters, preservation of a digital audit trail and allocation of the burden of proof. It proposes incorporating these safeguards into legislation on administrative procedures and administrative acts.

title: Regulated Remuneration Autonomy in Zambia’s Public Universities Under the Emoluments Commission Act No. 1 of 2022
abstract: The enactment of the Emoluments Commission Act No. 1 of 2022 reshaped Zambia’s public-sector remuneration context, raising questions about the extent to which its provisions qualify the authority of public university councils under the Higher Education Act No. 4 of 2013. This article examines how the two statutes allocate remuneration authority and how national regulatory coherence can be reconciled with the distinct workforce needs of public universities. The article employs doctrinal legal analysis, purposive and contextual statutory interpretation, and documentary analysis, informed by a strategic human resource management perspective. The analysis finds that the Emoluments Commission Act prevails over inconsistent provisions of the Higher Education Act only to the extent of the inconsistency and within the Commission’s statutory jurisdiction over emoluments. It does not displace university councils’ governance and employment responsibilities where these remain legally compatible with the Emoluments Commission Act No. 1 of 2022. The article distinguishes remuneration determination from collective bargaining, job evaluation, workforce planning, implementation and institutional evidence generation. It further argues that harmonisation does not necessarily require uniformity: justified differentiation may be considered where credible evidence demonstrates specific workforce pre…

title: Exergo-energetic evaluation and predictive modeling of a double helical coil air heater for sustainable energy applications
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study in residential heating that focuses on passive and surface engineering strategies to produce significant benefits with minimal geometric modifications. The current double helical coil air heater (DHCAH) synergistically integrates geometric modification and the inherent advantages of helical coil designs. Design/methodology/approach This study experimentally investigates the energetic and exergetic performance of a DHCAH under varying geometrical and flow parameters, including helical tube diameter, fluid flow rate, air velocity and inlet temperature. Nusselt number, friction factor, JF factor, effectiveness, exergy efficiency and sustainability index are evaluated. Subsequently, artificial neural network (ANN) and adaptive physics-guided neural network (PGNN) models are developed and assessed using repeated five-fold cross-validation. Unlike the purely data-driven ANN, the PGNN incorporates experimentally derived thermofluid and thermodynamic consistency relationships through adaptive physics-guided loss terms, ensuring physically admissible predictions without directly solving governing partial differential equations. Findings Experimental results show that the tube-side Nusselt number increases with hot-water flow rate, whereas the shell-side Nusselt number decreases. The 6.4 mm helical tube generally provides higher tube-side heat transfer a…

Reform and Practice of Modern Cryptography Courses in Integrated Undergraduate–Graduate Cybersecurity Education: Science–Education Integration and AI as Dual Drivers
abstract: In order to tackle the problems that exist in integrated undergraduate–graduate cybersecurity education at provincial universities with significant differences in the level of student preparedness, lack of coherence between undergraduate and graduate programs, inability to transform the results of faculty research into instructional resources, and disjointed use of artificial intelligence, the given study uses the Modern Cryptography course which is provided to the undergraduate students, the academic master’s students and the professional master’s students in Cybersecurity at Heilongjiang University as a case study. Design-based action research methodology was employed in order to form a three-level curriculum chain of undergraduate foundations, undergraduate–graduate articulation, and advanced graduate-level research training. Moreover, a four-step mechanism for transforming research outputs into teaching resources was devised, consisting of selecting the research outcome, pedagogical adaptation, implementation in the classroom, and iterative feedback. AI-based learning diagnostics, literature assistance, and learning behavior recording were incorporated in the entire process of instruction. Five dimensions of process-oriented assessment were developed, namely: theoretical knowledge, practical skill, research-focused reading and participation in tasks, innovation capacity, an…
