title: Wastewater Treatment Plants as Anchor Infrastructure for Geothermal Energy in Cold Regions
abstract: Abstract Thermal constraints in cold regions suppress biological treatment, increase energy demand, and elevate greenhouse gas emissions of existing wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), and remain a major barrier to the deployment of adequate sanitation infrastructure in many cold-region communities. Where geothermal resources exist, low-enthalpy hydrothermal heat is well matched to this energy gap. Yet, WWTPs are underrecognized anchors for broader geothermal deployment, providing a continuous, weather-independent thermal offtake through which subsurface CAPEX can be amortized. We reframe geothermal-WWTP integration as a system-level enabler that benefits both parts. Using three cascaded configurations for a full-scale WWTP, a rapid techno-economic analysis identifies three trends: energy and carbon savings/revenues alone are insufficient under realistic policy stacks, whereas crediting the upgrade-deferral value of geothermally enhanced treatment makes the project economically favorable across most policy scenarios. Globally, this triple intersection encompasses ∼11,600 catalogued WWTPs serving ∼280 million people, with a further estimate of ∼48 million people in the same regions beyond current service radii. The opportunity is greatest in cold, remote, and underserved communities, where local geothermal resources, treatment intensification, and community-scale demand togethe…

title: Stablecoins as a Means of Payment. Prospects for Integration into the Existing Legal System of the Russian Federation
abstract: The article is devoted to the issues of legal regulation of stablecoins as a means of settlement. The foreign experience of introducing stablecoins into financial markets is analyzed, as a result of which it is concluded that approaches to regulating their circulation are different. A number of countries are creating a new legal architecture for the creation and circulation of stablecoins, while others, on the contrary, use existing legal regulation mechanisms. The Bank of Russia's approaches to the legal nature of stablecoins and the doctrinal definitions of Russian and foreign scientists were also analyzed, the comparison of which allowed the author to classify them as a type of digital financial assets from the point of view of current Russian legislation.

title: Investigating the efficiency of rural industrial integration development in China: based on the undesirable super-efficiency SBM-Malmquist model
abstract: Promoting rural industrial integration development (RIID) to boost farmers’ income is a core strategy for rural revitalization and common prosperity. A reasonable and objective evaluation of RIID efficiency that jointly accounts for farmers’ income growth and the food-security and environmental constraints entailed by integration is critical for advancing sustainable rural development. This paper applies the super-efficiency SBM model with undesirable outputs and the Malmquist index to measure China’s RIID efficiency across 30 provinces from 2012 to 2023, analyzing its spatio-temporal evolution. The results show that the national annual average RIID efficiency fluctuated between 0.423 and 0.663, exhibiting a three-stage trajectory of “steady rise—fluctuating bottoming-out—accelerated climb” alongside a descriptively observed east–central–west gradient (eastern leading, central following, western lagging) that does not attain statistical significance. The annual average Malmquist index reached 1.060, corresponding to an average annual growth rate of 6.0%, and efficiency catch-up became the dominant driver of productivity growth in the later stage. The exploratory regression further reveals that rural human capital and transportation infrastructure are significantly and positively associated with RIID efficiency. This study integrates farmers’ income growth, farmland non-grain co…

title: Collisional passing alpha energy transport in nearly quasisymmetric stellarators
abstract: Recent advances in stellarator optimisation have found nearly precise quasisymmetric configurations. These are expected to reduce the non-turbulent background plasma transport to acceptable neoclassical levels while removing nearly all collisionless direct orbit losses of alpha particles. Yet, alpha particles under resonant conditions can be very sensitive to collisions, causing concerning energy losses and damaging plasma facing components. For the passing alphas such resonances can happen near rational surfaces in the presence of helical error field departures from quasisymmetry that change the magnetic field direction and magnitude. The cancellation between streaming motion and tangential drift of the alphas enhances the effective collision frequency, allowing the formation of a collisional boundary layer and giving rise to a perturbed distribution function. We develop an analytical model to illustrate and evaluate the resonant plateau transport this mechanism causes by formulating a drift kinetic treatment. The results indicate the associated particle and energy losses can become significant in the vicinity of rational surfaces at values of q equals m divided by n q = m / n $q=m/n$ when error fields with poloidal and toroidal numbers m m $m$ and n n $n$ are present. In addition, we investigate the validity of the quasilinear approximation to the energy flux to show that it …

title: Between vision and realisation: a policy design diagnosis of SDG integration in Saudi Arabia’s higher education transformation
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 higher education reforms structure incentives for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) integration. It offers a diagnostic analysis of how policy design features – especially clarity and ambiguity – shape institutional responses to transversal sustainability agendas and the reform’s contribution to economic diversification. Design/methodology/approach Using qualitative analysis of 42 documents across four tiers – national policies, institutional plans, external evaluations and performance data (2016–2024) – the study applies Matland’s (1995) ambiguity–conflict framework. A hybrid deductive-inductive coding framework operationalises his dimensions, grounded in evidence of temporal, procedural and metric tensions. Findings The diagnostic reveals a policy configuration marked by high clarity on economic ends but interpretive ambiguity in operational means, with latent structural conflict between centralised accountability and professional discretion. Evidence from five universities, ministry dashboards and external evaluations aligns with Matland’s symbolic implementation quadrant: institutions prioritise demonstrable compliance over risk-intensive innovation. SDG mapping and ranking participation outweigh curriculum redesign and interdisciplinary research. Originality/value Reframing the implementation gap as a design patho…

Tuning CO2 Hydrogenation to Carbon Monoxide over Cu@SiO2: The Critical Role of Trace ZnO
abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 hydrogenation to CO via reverse water–gas shift is severely restricted by competing methanol synthesis over Cu@SiO2 catalysts, owing to stable Cu–O–Si linkages that favor formate intermediates. Herein, trace ZnO introduction is proposed to precisely tune catalytic pathways. Characterizations verify trace ZnO disrupts Cu–O–Si bonds, generating highly dispersed metallic Cu0 sites. In-situ DRIFTS demonstrates suppressed formate accumulation and accelerated formate decomposition into CO after ZnO modification. The Cu-0.02ZnO@SiO2 catalyst achieves the optimal performance with 10.4% CO2 conversion, 85.5% CO selectivity and a CO space-time yield of 11.2 mmolCO·gcat–1·h–1. Excess ZnO may induce Cu agglomeration and probable Cu–ZnO interface formation, shifting product preference back to methanol. This study offers a simple strategy using minor metal oxide additives to regulate CO2 hydrogenation selectivity for CO production.

title: DeepANFIS: an interpretable and uncertainty-aware neuro-fuzzy framework for energy disaggregation in smart microgrids
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) facilitates appliance-level energy disambiguation based on aggregate power consumption measurements and is an important facilitator of energy efficiency and demand-side management. However, state-of-the-art NILM methods tend to have low interpretability, low sensitivity to the sampling rate, and difficulty in providing reliable uncertainty information, which delay their effectiveness in practical implementations. To address these issues, we present a new deep adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (DeepANFIS) for joint appliance-state identification and power estimation with enhanced interpretability and uncertainty awareness. The proposed system comprehensively incorporates modular convolutional feature learning with multiple resolutions, fuzzy memory networks with temporal dependencies, hierarchical fuzzy inference, and evidential deep learning. Extensive experiments were conducted on both the UK-DALE dataset and REDD to illustrate the efficacy of DeepANFIS under high-frequency and low-frequency sampling schemes. On the UK-DALE dataset, DeepANFIS attained an F1-score of 0.7122 with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 25.63 W at a sampling frequency of 6 s, along with an F1-score of 0.8371 and a root mean-squared error (RMSE) of 78.03 W at a sampling frequency of 15 min. On the REDD, DeepANFIS obtained a near-perfect F1-score of 0.9869 with an ac…

title: Optimal energy storage configuration for multi-energy microgrids based on hybrid multi-stage robust optimization
abstract: The source-load uncertainty of a multi-energy microgrid shows markedly different fluctuation characteristics across operating scenarios, which makes an energy storage configuration that balances economy and reliability difficult to obtain. This study proposes an optimal energy storage configuration model for multi-energy microgrids based on hybrid multi-stage robust optimization. An electricity–heat–hydrogen multi-energy microgrid model is first established, and its objective minimizes the sum of the annualized storage investment cost and operation cost. A comprehensive-norm ambiguity set constructed from a 1- and an ∞ -norm constraint then characterizes the uncertainty of the scenario probability distribution, a box uncertainty set with an uncertainty budget characterizes the source-load fluctuation within each scenario, and a min–max–max–min hybrid multi-stage stochastic-robust storage capacity model that accounts for the worst-case scenario probability is formulated. Finally, the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm decomposes the model into a master problem and two-level subproblems that are solved iteratively, and the intra-scenario max-min bilevel problem is transformed into an equivalent single-level problem through Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions. Case studies show that the proposed method hedges against both the source-load output uncertainty and t…

title: Pore Engineering of IL@MOF-Derived Carbons via IL-Assisted Double Templating for CO2 Separation
abstract: Abstract The mitigation of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions requires adsorbent materials with tunable pore structures capable of balancing adsorption capacity and selectivity under postcombustion conditions. In this work, a proof-of-concept IL-assisted double-templating strategy is presented to engineer porosity in IL@MOF-derived carbons. The metal–organic framework (MOF) Cu-BTC was used as both carbon precursor and primary template, while the ionic liquid (IL) [C6MIM][B(CN)4] was used as a secondary sacrificial template at low loadings (1–10 wt %). IL@MOF composites with varying IL contents were prepared, carbonized, and subsequently acid-washed to remove residual copper-containing phases formed during carbonization. This enabled the evaluation of how IL loading influences the resulting carbon pore structure and adsorption behavior. Porosimetric characterization shows that IL incorporation promoted the development of additional (ultra)microporosity while simultaneously reducing total accessible pore volume at higher loadings, strongly influencing gas adsorption behavior. CO2 and N2 adsorption–desorption measurements at 303 K revealed a nonmonotonic dependence of CO2 adsorption capacity on IL loading, with a maximum at 2 wt % IL. At higher IL contents, the reduction in accessible pore volume limited adsorption capacity. In contrast, ideal CO2/N2 selectivity at 1 bar increased pro…

title: Structuring strategies for big data analytics and lean six sigma integration in circular construction supply chains
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, validate and structure strategies for integrating big data analytics (BDA) and lean six sigma (LSS) to support circular economy (CE) adoption in construction supply chains. It aims to provide a prioritised strategy framework for sequencing BDA–LSS adoption. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach. Firstly, strategies for promoting BDA–LSS integration CSCs were identified through an extensive literature review and expert consultation. Secondly, the fuzzy delphi method was applied to screen and validate the strategies based on expert consensus, reducing the preliminary list to 24 retained strategies. Thirdly, interpretive structural modelling was used to unfold the direct and hidden interactions among the validated strategies. Finally, Matrice d’Impacts Croisés Multiplication Appliquée à un Classement analysis was applied to classify the strategies into “driving”, “linkage” and “dependent” clusters. The natural resource-based view and institutional theory were used to interpret the results. Findings The findings identify “Integrate BDA–LSS into national plans” and “Top management support” as the strongest system drivers, with each strategy recording the maximum driving power of 24 and the minimum dependence power of two. “Provide targeted financial incentives” and “Advocate for collaborati…

title: Ad-Lib: An Adsorption-Energy Descriptor Library for Physically Interpretable Catalyst Informatics
abstract: Abstract A central challenge in heterogeneous catalyst informatics is developing descriptors that capture catalyst behavior while remaining physically interpretable. Catalyst–reaction-species interactions provide a basis for representing heterogeneous catalytic reactions. Here, a high-throughput density functional theory adsorption-energy library (Ad-Lib) is constructed, and designed descriptors are applied to oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) and CO2 methanation, with OCM as the principal case study. Mapping catalysts in an adsorption-energy-defined interaction space provides a landscape of catalytic performance. The utility of this representation for describing catalytic behavior is further demonstrated through machine learning and SHAP analysis. This work establishes the multidimensional adsorption-energy space as a reaction-informed, physically grounded framework for heterogeneous catalyst informatics.

title: Middle East war-driven energy supply disruptions could influence air pollution in India and China
abstract: Abstract Rapid economic growth has increased energy demand to ~ 11,000 TWh in India and ~ 50,000 TWh in China, where coal accounts for 57.5% and 54.79% of total energy consumption, respectively. Both countries also depend strongly on imported oil, with ~ 45% of India’s and ~ 54% of China’s crude-oil imports originating from the Middle East, creating vulnerability to geopolitical energy-supply disruptions. Here, we investigate whether such disruptions could influence regional air pollution by integrating energy data, sector-resolved emissions, GEOS-Chem simulations, and satellite observations. CEDS indicates SO 2 emissions of ~ 9.15 Mt yr −1 in India and ~ 10.61 Mt yr −1 in China, while GEOS-Chem simulations indicate considerable power-sector contributions to aerosol loading over major energy-producing regions. TROPOMI observations show SO 2 column enhancements of up to ~ 0.6–0.8 DU during the conflict period relative to the corresponding non-conflict reference period. Sulfate constitutes ~ 48% and ~ 42% of aerosol loading over India and China, respectively. However, these SO 2 enhancements cannot be uniquely attributed to increased coal combustion or the Middle East conflict because contemporaneous coal-generation changes were not quantified and atmospheric SO 2 is influenced by multiple emission sources and meteorological processes. The combined evidence therefore identifies a…

title: HỘI NHẬP KINH TẾ QUỐC TẾ CỦA VIỆT NAM - NHỮNG VẤN ĐỀ ĐẶT RA TRONG GIAI ĐOẠN HIỆN NAY
abstract: Sau 40 năm thực hiện công cuộc đổi mới, Việt Nam đã đạt được những thành tựu to lớn trong hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế với những chuyển biến sâu sắc cả về lý luận và thực tiễn, từ chủ trương mở cửa, phá thế bao vây sang chủ động hội nhập, hội nhập toàn diện và hướng tới tự chủ chiến lược, tham gia định hình luật chơi. Tiến trình này góp phần mở rộng không gian phát triển, thúc đẩy cải cách, thu hút nguồn lực và nâng cao vị thế quốc gia. Tuy nhiên, năng lực nội sinh, mức độ tham gia chuỗi giá trị, tính tự chủ chiến lược, chất lượng thực thi cam kết và khả năng quản trị rủi ro còn hạn chế. Bài viết khái quát bốn giai đoạn phát triển, những thành tựu, hạn chế và các vấn đề lớn đặt ra đối với hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế của Việt Nam trong giai đoạn hiện nay. Trên cơ sở đó, bài viết đề xuất chuyển trọng tâm hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế sang việc chuyển hóa kết quả hội nhập thành tiến bộ công nghệ, năng suất cao hơn, sức chống chịu mạnh hơn và vị thế quốc gia được nâng cao. Từ khóa: hội nhập kinh tế quốc tế; độc lập, tự chủ; nội lực

Design Thinking Lesson Exemplars in Basic Education Toward a Transformative Instruction
abstract: Background: Lesson exemplars (LEs) present teachers' best practices for quality instruction, serving as a benchmark for others to innovate in their own classrooms, bringing transformative experiences that foster meaningful, lifelong learning.Aims: In this study, LEs were developed and validated, aligning with the design thinking (DT) as an instructional model.Methods: Descriptive development research was used as the study design, in which three developed LEs were validated by 10 expert teachers with respect to objectives, subject matter, procedures, evaluation, and assignment/agreement/take-home activities. The developed validation tool was then further validated by three expert educators, and the results were analyzed using Kappa Statistics (CVI=1.00; excellent). Moreover, the results of the dry run conducted with ten (10) teachers were analyzed using Cronbach’s Alpha to determine the instrument's reliability (α=0.8559; good). For the analysis of the results, descriptive statistics, such as mean, standard deviation, and rank, were used.Result: The study developed and validated design thinking-based lesson exemplars, making teachers capably blend the iterative, student-centered phases of design thinking (understanding, exploring, materializing) with the structured framework of conventional lesson plans, and received strong approval from teacher-experts for fostering creativity,…

Cultural and Digital Readiness for AI-Integrated Higher Education: A C-TAM-Informed Curriculum Design Framework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) requires higher education institutions to redesign curricula, assessments, and student support rather than merely authorize or prohibit a new tool. This article develops a Cultural-Technology Acceptance Model (C-TAM) as a theory-building curriculum framework. It integrates current studies of university students’ GenAI use with established technology-acceptance research, cross-cultural scholarship, AI-literacy frameworks, backward design, constructive alignment, and assessment reform. The revision explicitly limits the role of pre-GenAI evidence. Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2018 and World Values Survey (WVS) Wave 7 indicators are treated as contextual evidence about the digital and cultural readiness pipeline entering higher education; they are not treated as measures of GenAI acceptance, and no cross-national structural equation model is estimated from them. The synthesis identifies five mechanisms that curriculum designers should anticipate: perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and AI competence, attitudes shaped by trust and ethical risk, social and institutional norms, and culturally patterned expectations about uncertainty and authority. These mechanisms are translated through backward design into aligned learning outcomes, assessment evidence, pedagogy, and support. An AI-Ready Curriculum Reconstru…

title: Classroom physical design and the use of digital technologies: an exploratory observational study across educational stages
abstract: The integration of digital technologies (DT) in education has become a priority for education systems, yet the mere availability of devices does not guarantee their use in the classroom. This exploratory study analyzes the relationship between classroom physical design and the use of digital technologies in real educational practices, drawing on the Pedagogy-Space-Technology (PST) framework, and additionally examines whether the type of session is associated with differences in technology use. A quantitative, cross-sectional observational study was conducted through direct observation of 121 classrooms in Spain and Andorra, from early childhood to higher education. Because classrooms across these stages are not comparable units, analyses were disaggregated into three blocks, with 83 classrooms providing valid technology-use data: early childhood and primary ( n = 21), secondary and vocational ( n = 33), and higher education ( n = 29). Associations between furniture flexibility, physical environment, spatial organization and technology use were tested with Kendall's tau-b, with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within blocks, and differences by session type with the Kruskal–Wallis test. The pattern of associations differed across blocks. In early childhood and primary education, only the quality of the physical environment was associated with technology use ( τ = 0.673). In secondar…

title: Recycling Medical Intravenous Infusion Bags into Sharps Containers: Process Design and System Implementation
abstract: In 2024, Taiwan generated approximately 130,000 metric tons (MT) of medical waste, including about 42,000 MT of hazardous waste. Despite the implementation of circular economy initiatives, most of the medical waste is still incinerated and landfilled, thereby increasing the environmental burden through dioxin emissions and secondary pollution. Current recycling practices are aimed at converting medical plastics into secondary products but face logistical and operational challenges. This study developed a circular recycling system for medical intravenous (IV) infusion bags in Taiwan. In collaboration with two medical institutions, used IV bags were collected, sorted, cleaned, and reprocessed into recycled plastic pellets via a patented recycling-and-pelletization process. The pellets were incorporated into sharps containers, which were returned to participating hospitals, thus establishing a circular material pathway within the healthcare sector. The entire process was independently verified for traceability and regulatory compliance. The containers were assessed for recycled content, safety performance, and cradle-to-gate carbon footprint. The containers complied with ISO 14021 and ISO 23907-1 and were adopted by two hospitals in northern Taiwan. The carbon footprint was estimated as 1.852 kg CO 2 -eq per container, comprising 1.587 kg CO 2 -eq from raw-material acquisition and…

Multidisciplinary collaboration and workflows on heritage building information modelling (HBIM) projects: a framework for improvement
abstract: Purpose Heritage building information modelling (HBIM) projects face significant challenges, especially in relation to multidisciplinary collaboration and project workflows. This paper aims to examine HBIM work processes, presenting a practical framework to improve HBIM workflows and multidisciplinary collaboration occurring on construction heritage projects. Design/methodology/approach An initial deductive literature review provides a foundation for the study by identifying thematic HBIM industry challenges. An inductive, interpretivist and qualitative examination of HBIM combines survey questionnaire with case study and in-depth interviews to provide a holistic understanding of the opportunities and challenges confronting practitioners. Findings Findings indicate that HBIM offers great potential for improving heritage protection, but challenges around data management, human factors, technical issues and training skills remain. A resulting framework for improvement identifies five key outcomes around which improvement depends: team coordination; sharing of knowledge; standards and industry specifications; technical tools and training/education. Recommendations are rooted to case study evidence and practitioner opinion; the paper highlights the need for further research to refine practices globally. Originality/value The research contributes to the Heritage Building Information…

title: An AI-Integrated Constructivist Learning Environment Framework for Thai as a Second Language in Higher Education: Design and Expert Review
abstract: Digital technology is now central to higher education, yet learner engagement is usually measured as an outcome after instruction rather than designed into the learning environment. This study designs an AI-integrated constructivist learning environment (CLE) framework for promoting learning engagement and creative writing, referred to here as the CLE-EW framework, for Chinese university learners of Thai as a second language. The study followed design and development research (DDR). It combined an integrative literature synthesis, a contextual analysis, a theory-driven design synthesis, and expert review. The contextual analysis took place at two universities in Yunnan Province, China, with 120 third-year Thai majors, their two writing instructors, and four support staff. The framework has seven interrelated centers: Problem Base, Learning Resources, Cognitive Tools, Collaboration, Promoting Learning Engagement and Creative Writing, Scaffolding, and Coaching. AI is used in five centers in three bounded forms (rule-based formative feedback, a retrieval-based answer system, and an external generative tool used to seek, collect, organize, and integrate information), while the Collaboration and Coaching Centers are human-led. The rule-based and retrieval-based forms run in the learner’s browser and send no learner writing to an external service. Five experts rated the framewo…

title: Design and User Evaluation of a Mobile-Based Virtual Reality Application for English Vocabulary Learning in Elementary Students
abstract: English vocabulary mastery among elementary school students in Indonesia remains limited, particularly in recognizing everyday household objects, due to conventional teaching methods that rely on passive approaches and the lack of engaging interactive learning media. Although prior work has proposed several virtual reality (VR) applications for vocabulary learning, most stop at content visualization and have not been systematically evaluated using a psychometrically validated instrument designed for child users. This study addresses that gap by designing, developing, and evaluating a mobile-based VR application for fourth-grade students, and by examining (RQ1) the extent to which the application satisfies end-user requirements across five EUCS dimensions, (RQ2) whether the child-adapted instrument is valid and reliable when applied to primary-school respondents, and (RQ3) which dimension yields the lowest score and what design implications it reveals. The application was developed using the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) method, with content adapted from the independent curriculum and focused on household-object vocabulary. The evaluation employed User Acceptance Testing comprising alpha testing using a black-box matrix and beta testing involving 51 fourth-grade students. User satisfaction was measured using a child-adapted End User Computing Satisfaction (EUCS) instr…

title: Baculovirus-Mediated Expression and Functional Characterization of a Glycyrrhizin-Specific Single-Chain Variable Fragment in Sf9 Cells
abstract: Abstract Background Glycyrrhizin (GC) is a major bioactive saponin in licorice plants ( Glycyrrhiza spp.). A GC-specific single-chain variable fragment (GC-scFv) was constructed from anti-GC monoclonal antibody 2H2. To obtain a soluble recombinant recognition reagent for GC immunoassays, GC-scFv was expressed using a baculovirus–insect cell platform. Methods The variable heavy- and light-chain genes were amplified from 2H2 hybridoma-derived complementary DNA (cDNA) and assembled using a (Gly 4 Ser) 3 linker. The construct was transferred through pET-28a(+) and pCold I into pFastBac1Mel, which contains the honeybee melittin signal sequence for secretion in Sf9 insect cells. GC-scFv was recovered by nickel-chelate affinity chromatography and characterized using indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (icELISA). The calibration curve was analyzed by semi-logarithmic regression using triplicate wells at each concentration. Results An anti-T7-tag Western blot detected GC-scFv at approximately 29 kDa in the eluate recovered from culture medium. Free GC produced concentration-dependent inhibition, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 0.46 μg/mL and a semi-logarithmic calibration interval of 0.0488–3.125 μg/mL. The apparent limit of detection and apparent limit of quantification, defined as 10% and 20% inhibition, were 54.2 and 92.8 ng/mL, respectivel…

title: The impact of virtual reality and augmented reality on global brand transformation: insights from immersive advertising among Nepalese adolescents
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) marketing communication on consumer engagement, perceived diagnosticity, brand attitude and purchase intention in an emerging market context. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 408 consumers aged 18 years and above across five cities in Nepal who were exposed to real-world AR and VR brand marketing content. The proposed relationships were tested using structural equation modelling. Findings Perceived immersion significantly enhances consumer engagement and perceived diagnosticity. Both factors positively influence brand attitude, which in turn drives purchase intention. Brand attitude emerged as the strongest direct predictor of purchase intention. The findings indicate significant consumer responses to AR/VR marketing communications, although the effects are statistically small and should be interpreted in light of the passive exposure design. Practical implications This study suggests that AR and VR can effectively enhance consumer engagement and brand attitude by providing immersive and informative product experiences. Marketers should focus on designing interactive and easy-to-use content that clearly demonstrates product benefits. Since brand attitude strongly drives purchase intention, immersive campaigns should prioritise building positive brand perceptions.…

title: Physicochemical, microbial, and sensory characterization of quinoa-based vegan yogurt as a functional plant-based fermented product
abstract: Background This study aimed to develop quinoa-based vegan yogurt products in response to the increasing interest in plant-based diets and to evaluate their sensory, chemical, and microbiological properties. Methods In the first phase, four quinoa-based yogurt formulations were prepared using different starter culture and activation strategies, and fermented under controlled conditions. In the second phase, samples were subjected to sensory analysis by 12 trained panelists and 80 consumer panelists, evaluating appearance, taste, color, aroma, texture, flavor, and overall acceptability. Additionally, functional properties (total phenolic content [TPC] and antioxidant capacity [CUPRAC]) and proximate compositions (crude protein, total fat, and moisture content) were analyzed and compared with a commercially available rice-based vegan yogurt. Results The findings indicated that quinoa-based vegan yogurts are a promising alternative in terms of nutritional value, functional properties, and sensory acceptability. Microbiological analyses revealed viable lactic acid bacteria (LAB) counts ranging from 6.9 to 8.2 log CFU/g, confirming successful fermentation. Conclusion Quinoa-based vegan yogurts exhibit superior protein content, strong antioxidant capacity, and high consumer acceptability compared to commercial rice-based alternatives, demonstrating their strong potential as functional…

title: Genetic diversity analysis using phenotypic and SSR markers with trait association and multivariate analysis in cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.) genotypes
abstract: The low productivity of cowpea is primarily attributed to inadequate utilisation of genetic diversity for the improvement of local cultivars. The present study was conducted to assess genetic diversity utilising 17 yield and biochemical traits along with simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers. Fifty cowpea genotypes were assessed during summer 2024 at Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), India. Genotypes were planted with three replications in a randomised block design. Significant genetic variability was observed in the studied traits. The minimal differences between phenotypic and genotypic coefficients of variation (CV) indicated that the observed variation primarily stemmed from the genetic component. Most traits showed high heritability, with varying levels of genetic advance. Trait association revealed a positive interrelationship among yield-contributing traits, suggesting their utility for selection for cowpea yield improvement. Cluster I possessed better-performing genotypes for yield traits. Principal component analysis emphasised that pods per cluster (PCL), pods per plant (PPL) and clusters per plant (CPL) were the major contributing traits in principal component 1 (PC1). Out of 64 SSR markers screened, 40 showed successful amplification and 18 were highly polymorphic and used for diversity analysis, with an average of 2.94 alleles per mark…

A Fatigue Simulation Approach for Long-Crack Propagation Phase of Radial Tires Using Modified Virtual Crack Closure Technique
abstract: ABSTRACT Tire fatigue failure involves short-crack initiation and long-crack propagation. While the crack energy density effectively predicts short-crack propagation, the simulation of long-crack propagation requires improvement. In this study, we propose a fatigue simulation approach for radial tires using the modified virtual crack closure technique. We prefabricate cracks via hybrid submodel-composite modeling (tie constraint), calculate the strain energy release rate with the modified crack closure technique, and predict crack propagation. Groove crack experiments and finite element simulations on two all-steel radial truck tires verified the effectiveness of this approach. The approach provides a reliable tool for fatigue evaluation, aiding tire durability design and life prediction.

title: Administrative Offenses Constituting in Infringement upon Public Order and Public Safety in the Virtual Space (on the Example of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Tajikistan)
abstract: This article provides a comparative legal analysis of administrative offenses that infringe upon public order and public safety in the virtual space of Russia and Tajikistan. It argues that virtual space possesses characteristics of a public space, but is not identical to it. The fragmentary nature of Tajikistan’s legislation is highlighted, and the authors propose adopting Russian experience to improve the Code of Administrative Offenses of the Republic of Tajikistan, taking into account the principles of legality and proportionality.

abstract: The article presents a socio-philosophical analysis of pacifism and anti-pacifism in secular and religious discourses on war. It traces the evolution of conceptions of violence from its sacralization in religious tradition and its rationalization in the theory of just war to contemporary concepts of nonviolence, moral realism, and the ethical-political critique of the cult of power. Particular attention is paid to the relationship between pacifist and anti-pacifist positions in Christian thought, specifically in the Catholic and Protestant traditions, as well as their correlation with secular concepts of power, war, and political responsibility. Based on an analysis of Judith Butler’s works, the study argues that nonviolence should be viewed not as a manifestation of passivity or moral idealism, but as an active ethical-political practice capable of countering structural violence, affirming social equality, and fostering new forms of solidarity. It is shown that recognizing human vulnerability, interdependence, and the value of every life creates the foundation for rethinking the politics of peace beyond the logic of domination and coercion. The Ukrainian context is analyzed separately, in which the current war has prompted a reevaluation of the relationship between pacifism, the right to self-defense, and civic responsibility. title: Reconfiguring power, trust, and identity in early contractor involvement
abstract: Purpose Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) has emerged as a pivotal mechanism for improving efficiency, innovation, and risk management in complex construction projects, yet its theoretical and institutional foundations remain unsettled. While ECI has been embedded in national procurement reforms and digital collaboration frameworks, persistent gaps remain in cross-jurisdictional validation, governance modelling, and measurement of long-term value. Design/methodology/approach This study presents the most comprehensive systematic mapping of ECI scholarship to date, integrating an 80-paper corpus across three analytical phases spanning 2009–2025, supported by a 100-paper global construction challenge dataset used for contextual comparison. Using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-based screening, bibliometric network mapping, and thematic synthesis, the evaluation identifies how ECI research has evolved from descriptive analyses of delivery performance toward deeper theorisation of governance, identity, trust, and procurement. Findings Results reveal that ECI is consistently positioned as a corrective to chronic industry inefficiencies, such as cost overruns, schedule delays, and design fragmentation- but that empirical studies remain regionally concentrated and methodologically fragmented. The analysis exposes four conceptual architectures that st…

Distribution patterns of saline plant communities and their associations with environmental soil factors in the Circum-Bohai-Sea saline region, China
abstract: Questions The Circum-Bohai-Sea saline region possesses abundant halophytic plant resources; however, the specific composition and distribution patterns of these communities, as well as their complex associations with soil factors, remain insufficiently understood. title: DESIGN AND DEVELOP A PIEZOELECTRIC POWER GENERATOR AND ENERGY HARVESTER UTILIZING HUMAN FOOTSTEPS
abstract: The development of sustainable energy technologies has encouraged the exploration of alternative methods for converting mechanical energy into electrical energy. One promising approach is piezoelectric energy harvesting, which utilizes the pressure generated by human footsteps to produce electrical output. This research aimed to design and developed a piezoelectric power generator prototype and evaluate its voltage output under different human-weight conditions. An experimental research design was employed, involving five participants with body weights ranging from 56 kg to 62 kg. Each participant performed footstep pressure tests on the prototype at a consistent walking pace, with voltage measurements recorded using a digital multimeter across three one-minute trials. The results showed an increasing trend in voltage output as participant weight increased, with average outputs ranging from 10.2 V at 56 kg to 16.3 V at 62 kg. Linear regression analysis revealed a strong positive relationship between participant weight and voltage output, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.9815. The resulting regression equation was y = 0.9991x – 45.368. These findings demonstrate the potential of the developed prototype to generate electrical voltage from human footsteps. Further improvements in material selection, circuit design, energy storage, and prototype durability are recommen…

title: Comparative assessment of freshly cultured microbial bioproducts and a seaweed-based biostimulant for plant growth promotion and root-knot nematode management in capsicum and spinach in Kenya
abstract: Summary Root-knot nematodes (RKN; Meloidogyne spp.) are among the most damaging pathogens of vegetable crops worldwide. They damage roots and reduce yield, with their management becoming challenging because of their wide host range. This study evaluated three microbial bioproducts, Mytech ® ( Purpureocillium lilacinum ), Trichotech ® ( Trichoderma asperellum ) and Regain ® ( Bacillus subtilis ) and a seaweed-based biostimulant (Maximizer ® ) for growth promotion and RKN management in capsicum and spinach. The fungal and bacterial bioproducts were cultured to provide fresh inocula for each experimental trial. In RKN-free pot experiments, Mytech ® and Trichotech ® consistently improved plant height, shoot and root fresh weight and total plant weight in capsicum, whereas Regain ® and Mytech ® enhanced plant height, shoot fresh weight and total plant weight in spinach compared with the non-treated control. In RKN-infected pot experiments, where microbial bioproducts or the seaweed-based biostimulant were applied before nematode inoculation, all treatments using bioproducts and biostimulant improved growth parameters, although responses varied between crops and repeated experiments. All bioproducts and biostimulant treatments significantly reduced nematode infection in both crops. However, significant reductions in nematode density, number of galls and reproduction factor were obser…

Communal verification in group musical competition (douyue): peer evaluation, inter-society authority, and relational outcomes in the traditional Chinese music practice of Xi’an Guyue
abstract: This Hypothesis and Theory article examines group musical competition ( douyue 斗乐) in Xi’an Guyue 西安鼓乐, a tradition of Chinese instrumental ensemble music played by local music societies in and around Xi’an. In douyue , two or more societies perform for, and in response to, one another, either simultaneously from facing positions or in turn on a shared stage, while fellow musicians, elders, and local audiences listen, compare, and comment. The article asks how a society’s musical standing, recognized by its own members, comes to be acknowledged or questioned by other societies, and how this process may affect musicians’ relationships and wellbeing. To address this question, it introduces the concept of communal verification: a provisional, shared appraisal by a knowledgeable community of whether a specific claim made through performance, such as command of a multi-section suite, stylistic accuracy, or ensemble control, is convincing, open to question, or not yet settled. Such appraisals are more likely when performances can be compared, are assessed by what is heard against standards that participants recognize, and remain open to response and later revision. Communal verification differs from simply winning a contest or receiving a score. Under fair and respectful conditions, it may help performers feel heard and respected, whether their claim is recognized or questioned, and …

title: Renewable-Energy-Based Global Supply Chain Network Design for Greenhouse Gas Reduction: A Comparison of Different Assembly Products
abstract: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in global supply chains can be reduced by introducing renewable energy (RE) systems such as solar power generation systems. Some manufacturers commit themselves to the RE100 global initiative that encourages companies to source 100% of the electricity used in their business operations from RE. Thus, suppliers will face the risks of contract termination if suppliers fail to satisfy the target RE utilization rate to reduce GHG emissions. Besides costs, GHG emissions from electricity consumption during component production and GHG emissions from material production differ among suppliers due to differences in the availability of RE and regional energy mixes. Hence, in this study, we proposed a RE-based global supply chain network to reduce GHG emissions using an optimization model to satisfy the target RE utilization rate and GHG reduction rate simultaneously, where we considered the GHG emissions from electricity consumption and material production. In our model, the suppliers were allowed to purchase electricity generated by non-RE systems when they could not fulfill the electricity required to manufacture components from RE systems. We compared the RE utilization rate, GHG emissions, and total cost for two products (laptop and vacuum cleaner). title: AI-driven real-time control architecture for hybrid battery and supercapacitor systems to enhance frequency regulation in high renewable microgrids
abstract: A The growing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation in microgrids poses problems of fast-changing power and low inertia, which pose challenges for frequency regulation. Although traditional battery energy storage systems have the capacity for providing continuous energy supply, they might be subjected to increased stress due to the charging and discharging activities in response to high-frequency disturbances. The current paper aims at presenting an artificial intelligence-based real-time control architecture for the coordinated operation of a battery-supercapacitor hybrid energy storage system in a microgrid characterized by a high penetration of renewable energy sources. The developed architecture is able to make the necessary adjustments based on the values of frequency deviation, rate of change of frequency, renewable generation, load demands, battery state of charge, and supercapacitor voltage. The proposed scheme was simulated using MATLAB/Simulink under the conditions of moderately varying renewable sources, sudden load disturbances, highly intermittent renewables, and a combination of renewable and load disturbances. The maximum frequency deviation was lowered from 0.32 Hz to 0.18 Hz (−43.8%), and the frequency settling time decreased from 4.1 s to 2.6 s (−36.5%). title: Energy distributions of precipitating electrons in Jupiter's auroral regions from combined Juno/JADE and Juno/JEDI measurements
abstract: Jupiter's auroras are produced by magnetospheric electrons precipitating into its atmosphere. The Juno/JADE and Juno/JEDI instruments together measure these electrons over the energy range 100, However, their spectra in Jupiter's auroral regions cannot be accurately reproduced by the widely used kappa distribution, hereafter referred to as the classical single-kappa distribution. We aim to statistically characterize the energy flux distributions of precipitating electrons in Jupiter's auroral regions and to derive a new phenomenological energy distribution, referred to as the 4-kappa distribution, better suited to reproduce the combined JADE+JEDI data. We builT mean electron energy flux distributions in six auroral subregions (the polar, the main, and the outer emission regions, for both hemispheres), combining JADE and JEDI data from PJ3 to PJ35. These data were mapped to the Jovian SIII reference frame using the JRM33 magnetic field model, which accounts for the contribution of the current sheet. We fitted these distributions using MCMC in logarithmic space, testing both the classical single-kappa distribution and the 4-kappa distribution. The mean distributions show an overall monotonic power-law decay, with an energy cutoff visible beyond ∼ 500, in most subregions, although a fraction of the individual spectra depart from this behavior at intermediate energies. title: A Sub-Optimal Control of a Non-linear Vibrating System Excited by a Non-ideal Energy Source
abstract: Abstract Purpose Non-Ideal Systems (NIS) are distinguished by their unique dynamic properties, which present considerable challenges to the application of conventional control techniques. The present study examines non-ideal excitation sources with limited power. Nonlinear phenomena were observed in a range of applications, providing insights for future NIS engineering. Methods The governing equations of Non-Ideal Systems (NIS) with multiple degrees of freedom are derived, accounting for nonlinear damping, stiffness, and time-varying excitations. The implementation of a state-dependent Riccati equation (SDRE) control strategy is proposed as a means to optimise system stability and dynamic performance. Results For the ideal system (case 1, $$a_0 = 0$$ ), the proposed control strategy effectively regulates the system’s response, reducing amplitude and stabilizing the orbits, as confirmed by time-domain and frequency-domain analyses. For the non-ideal system (case 2, $$a_0 > 0$$ ), despite the increased excitation complexity, the controller successfully suppresses vibrations and mitigates nonlinear effects, demonstrating robust performance in both time- and frequency-domain measures. Conclusions The present study focuses on excitation sources that deviate from ideal conditions. Why Cannot Solid Cages Compress Water? A Computational Thermodynamic Activity Linking Hydrogen Storage to Water’s Anomalous Density
abstract: Abstract Core physical chemistry concepts, such as hydrogen bonding, Gibbs free energy, and configurational entropy, rarely appear within a unified pedagogical framework. This article presents an interactive web-based HTML module prompted by a genuine student question: if metal hydrides compress hydrogen, why do crystalline hydrates fail to compress water? The answer is explored through a simplified thermodynamic framework based on ideal configurational mixing entropy. The mathematical limits and maxima of this symmetric pedagogical model provide a unified way to discuss three seemingly disparate macroscopic phenomena: the anomalously low density of ice, the existence of liquid water’s density maximum, and water’s thermodynamic resistance to complete close-packing. Implemented in an upper-division undergraduate Energy Chemistry course (n = 14 enrolled junior chemistry and materials science majors), this 60 min interactive session provided evidence of conceptual gains. To evaluate mechanistic understanding beyond factual recall, student learning was assessed via a rubric-scored preactivity diagnostic and a formative capstone synthesis task. Results indicate a distinct shift in student reasoning, moving away from simple geometric heuristics (like mechanical squeezing) toward rigorous thermodynamic arguments based on Gibbs free energy minimization.

title: Financial feasibility of employee ownership under the Danish succession model
abstract: Purpose We examine the feasibility of employee-financed succession under Denmark's new framework, which lets owners transfer ownership to employees through a cooperative holding structure with deferred capital gains tax. Design/methodology/approach We develop a cash-flow model yielding closed-form feasibility conditions that incorporate the statutory dividend threshold and tax deferral, with simulations and a stochastic extension quantifying liquidity risk. Findings Feasibility turns on short-run liquidity rather than profitability. Because dividends are pro rata, funding a stake of any size requires the operating company to distribute its entire equity value; this “dividend leakage” to non-participating owners is the root of the constraint. The maximum sustainable multiple rises with payout and falls with leverage, leaving high-valuation firms unreachable; a smaller stake does not help, as feasibility is independent of the ownership share. Feasibility therefore hinges on concessions outside the dividend channel: tax-exempt seller gifts or employee contributions. Research limitations/implications The baseline abstracts from bargaining and from heterogeneity beyond payout and leverage; an appendix shows earnings risk tightens the feasible set. Practical implications The results clarify why employee buyouts are viable in some firm contexts but not others and inform the statutory …

title: Persistence of Staphylococcus epidermidis in Cardiopulmonary Bypass Circuits Primed with Plasma-Lyte A: Implications for Circuit Storage Following Contamination
abstract: Background There is limited evidence on how long cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits can remain primed before use or when primed CPB circuits should be disposed of due to loss of sterility or instability of the priming solution. Understanding bacterial persistence in priming solutions is critical for patient safety and institutional protocols. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the survival of Staphylococcus epidermidis in Plasma-Lyte A-primed CPB circuits over time. Methods Three commercially available CPB circuits (Affinity, CAPIOX, and Inspire) from different manufacturers (Medtronic, Terumo, and LivaNova) were primed with Plasma-Lyte A inoculated with S. epidermidis (~1 CFU/mL) to simulate accidental contamination. Following brief recirculation, circuits were stored without circulation at 20–22°C. Samples were obtained aseptically from pre- and post-oxygenator sites on Days 0, 2, 4, 7, 9, and 11. Viable bacterial recovery was reported as colony-forming units per milliliter (CFU/mL) over time. Results Viable S. epidermidis was recovered from all three CPB circuits at both sampling sites through Day 11. Colony counts remained low, fluctuating between approximately 1 and 9 CFU/mL without a consistent increase over time. The highest observed count, 9 CFU/mL, occurred at the Inspire post-oxygenator sampling site on Day 7. Each measurement represented a single observation. Conc…

title: Impact of Tissue Storage on Bioanalytical Data and Live Tissue Science
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Precision oncology increasingly depends on accurate molecular and functional characterization of tumor tissue across genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, epigenetic, and live-cell applications. This review evaluates how commonly used tissue preservation methods, including formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE), fresh, flash-frozen, and cryopreserved tissue, affect downstream analytical fidelity and translational utility. Recent Findings Recent comparative studies demonstrate that FFPE remains effective for histopathology and a few established molecular assays but introduces nucleic acid fragmentation, crosslinking, deamination artifacts, protein modification, and loss of cellular viability. These effects can reduce sequencing efficiency, alter quantitative molecular measurements, and limit applications requiring intact proteins or viable cells. In contrast, flash-frozen and cryopreserved tissues generally provide greater molecular fidelity, while controlled-rate cryopreservation additionally preserves viable cellular populations for single-cell analysis, organoid development, functional precision medicine, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte expansion, and CAR-T manufacturing. Emerging evidence also supports the use of cryopreserved living tumor biobanks for longitudinal and functional testing. Summary No single preservation method is optimal for every appl…

Interfacial Origin of Mn Promotion in Ni/AlO x Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis and Carbon Nanotube Growth
abstract: Abstract Commercial deployment of methane pyrolysis (MP) requires H2 to be produced at a high rate while the solid carbon is recovered as a marketable product such as multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). Various promoters have been explored for Ni-based MP catalysts, including Mn, but the origin of its effect has remained elusive. Here, Ni/AlOx catalysts containing 0 to 5 wt % Mn were used to separate the two roles that Mn plays in activity and stability. The amount of Ni exposed at an oxide boundary correlated with the apparent CH4 reaction order across the series, identifying the Ni–O–Mn perimeter as the site at which CH4 activation is promoted. The same perimeter converted weakly bound NiO into strongly interacting species that resisted encapsulation, linking the rate and the lifetime of the catalyst to a single interface. At 1 wt %, Mn the apparent activation energy fell from 93.9 to 84.2 kJ mol–1, the CH4 reaction order rose from 0.46 to 0.84, and the turnover number increased from 375 to 456 mol C mol Ni–1. At 2 wt %, MnOx began to bury the Ni surface, and above that loading it segregated into a separate phase, so the promotion was lost. Mn also improved the graphitization and conductivity of the MWCNTs formed at the start of the reaction, but this benefit faded as disordered carbon accumulated. title: Green Manufacturing of Iron Fluoride/Fluorinated Carbon Nanocomposite Cathodes from PTFE Waste and Iron Oxides via Mechanochemistry
abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste poses persistent environmental challenges due to its exceptional chemical stability. Meanwhile, the conversion of iron oxides, the major components of abundant natural iron ores, into advanced materials commonly involves multistep processing through refined iron precursors. Herein, we report a closed-loop mechanochemical strategy that integrates PTFE waste upcycling with direct iron oxide fluorination. Compared with conventional iron fluoride synthesis relying on hazardous HF-derived fluorochemicals and refined iron salts, this approach utilizes PTFE waste as a fluorine source and avoids fluoride-containing byproducts. During high-energy ball-milling, mechanochemical activation promotes stable C–F bond cleavage in PTFE and oxygen vacancy generation within the iron oxides. The released fluorine is captured by defect-rich iron oxides to form iron fluoride nanoparticles, while the residual PTFE framework evolves into electrochemically active fluorinated carbon containing reversible semi-ionic C–F bonds. The nanocomposite cathode delivers a capacity of 316.7 mAh g–1 with 70.5% retention after 1000 cycles at 0.25 A g–1, surpassing the one-electron theoretical capacity of FeF3 (237.0 mAh g–1). The enhanced electrochemical performance originates from the synergistic contributions of iron fluoride redox reactions and reversible Faradaic rea…

title: China's urban rail transit carbon peak: when and how – a dynamic life cycle assessment
abstract: China's rapidly expanding urban rail transit (URT) system faces significant environmental challenges, particularly regarding the inflexibility and structural nature of passengers’ urban transportation demands. It is a key issue to assess the carbon peak timeline and related technological roadmap for carbon peaking in China’s URT sector. This study conducts a comprehensive life cycle assessment to evaluate carbon dioxide emissions across different URT life cycle phases. Through input factor identification and scenario modelling, the authors investigate critical factors affecting life cycle emissions and project emission data from 2019 to 2035. The analysis results suggest that there was an 11% reduction in emissions in 2020, which is attributed to the shifts in transportation demand induced by COVID-19. Among various development scenarios, only the ambitious scenario, which involves the adoption of decarbonisation technologies and robust policy enforcement, achieves carbon peaking by 2030. To support emission management, the authors propose a multi-level framework that combines upstream data integration with goal decomposition methodology. This framework is based on macro-level sectoral assessments and the development of technology-specific roadmaps, thereby supporting the sustainability of the URT system in line with China's national climate objectives while maintaining transpo…

title: Does carbon assurance deter corporate greenwashing?
abstract: Purpose This paper investigates whether third-party carbon assurance deters corporate greenwashing. Motivated by competing theoretical perspectives, where assurance may either enhance accountability or provide symbolic legitimacy, we examine whether carbon assurance aligns firms' environmental disclosures with their actual performance. Design/methodology/approach Using 2,276 US publicly listed firm-year observations from 2007–2020, we analyse the association between carbon assurance and greenwashing, measured as the divergence between ESG disclosure and ESG performance. Findings Carbon assurance reduces greenwashing, supporting its monitoring and signalling roles. We document that environmental innovation is a channel for this relationship: carbon assurance is associated with greater environmental innovation, which in turn lowers greenwashing. The effect is concentrated in non-RGGI states and is stronger in less competitive product markets. The results are robust across alternative specifications and endogeneity tests, particularly for assurance level and percentage. Originality/value This study provides the first large-scale evidence that carbon assurance effectively curbs corporate greenwashing and identifies environmental innovation as the key mechanism. The findings inform regulators considering mandatory carbon assurance, and assist investors and creditors evaluating firms…

title: Study of the absorption and emission spectra of polymeric films colored with laser organic dyes
abstract: This study focuses on the absorption and emission (fluorescence) spectra of two organic dyes, Rhodamine and Fluorescein. The dyes are prepared as liquid samples dissolved in a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) polymer solution at different concentrations (0.01, 0.02, 0.03, and 0.04 mM). Solid samples in the form of PVA polymer films doped with Rhodamine and Fluorescein are also prepared using the casting method, in which the dyes are directly mixed with the polymer solution at different concentrations (0.01, 0.02, 0.03, and 0.04 mM), while maintaining a constant film thickness of 120 μm.The absorbance values of all prepared samples are measured using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer. The results indicate that increasing dye concentration affects the linear optical properties of the prepared samples, resulting in increased absorbance and decreased transmittance, consistent with the Beer–Lambert law. Increasing the dye concentration also results in higher calculated linear optical coefficients, including the linear refractive index and linear absorption coefficient, for all samples.Fluorescence spectra are measured using a fluorescence spectrometer, and the fluorescence lifetime and quantum efficiency are calculated to evaluate the emission properties of the studied dyes. title: Evaluation of recovered Carbon black as a sustainable alternative to commercial Carbon black in solid tyre cushion compounds
abstract: Pyrolysis is a sustainable solution for waste tyre (WT) management. Recovered carbon black (rCB), is a second highest by-product of tyre pyrolysis process, contains a high amount of carbon, ash and inorganic impurities. In the present study, rCB derived from WTs was upgraded through magnetic separation, ball milling, and purified treating twice with 2M HCl and once with 2M NaOH at 60⁰C for one hour using 2 g/mL rCB: leachate ratio to obtain demineralized rCB(drCB). Both raw rCB and drCB were characterized by particle size analysis, proximate and ultimate analyses, TGA, ICP-OES, FT-IR, XRD, and iodine adsorption. The drCB exhibited a substantial reduction in ash content from 22.20% to 3.42 % (by weight) and an increase in carbon content up to 94.41 % (% wt). The upgraded drCB was subsequently incorporated into solid tyre cushion compounds as a partial replacement for commercial carbon black (CCB, N550) to evaluate industrial feasibility. Physico-mechanical properties of the drCB compound demonstrated improved modulus, tear strength, hardness, and other properties such as tensile strength, rebound resilience within the industrial standard limits. These findings confirm the technical feasibility of rCB as a partial replacement of the filler in industrial solid tyre cushion compounds, supporting circular economy concept in the rubber and tyre industry.

title: Improved Biomass Production via Enhanced Inorganic Carbon Availability Using Crystalline Calcium Silicate Hydrate in a Marine Oleaginous Diatom Cultivation for Sustainable Aviation Fuel Production
abstract: Abstract Microalgae are promising feedstocks for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) because of their high oil productivity and nonedible nature. In particular, Fistulifera solaris (F. solaris) is an oleaginous marine diatom that has attracted considerable attention as a potential feedstock for SAF production. However, low CO2 solubility limits biomass production. In addition, conventional carbonate-enrichment methods are often species-specific and carbon-intensive. In this study, cultivation using crystalline calcium silicate hydrate (cCSH), a low-cost and environmentally friendly material derived from concrete scrap and waste, was experimentally investigated to improve CO2 enrichment and biomass production. The addition of cCSH increased the dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) concentration in the medium, mainly through the accumulation of bicarbonate ions (HCO3–). In the presence of cCSH, the DIC concentration was approximately 1.5-fold higher, and the biomass production of F. solaris increased 1.4-fold. The impact on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions was calculated for a life-cycle microalgae-based SAF production process to evaluate the environmental impact of cCSH. With the introduction of cCSH, GHG emissions were estimated at 67.1 g-CO2eq/MJ, corresponding to an approximately 24.6% reduction compared with the conventional jet fuel. These results indicate that cCSH is a promising ca…

Size- and Time-Resolved Emission Rates of Particulate Matter Mass, Chemical Constituents, and Oxidative Potential from Indoor Sources
abstract: Abstract We quantified the time- and size-resolved emission rates of particulate matter (PM) mass, its chemical constituents, and OP (via dithiothreitol assay) from six indoor sources in a test chamber (two types of incense, candle, toaster, humidifier, and cigarette). Both the chemical composition and mass-normalized OP (OPm) varied little temporally. However, both the chemical composition and OPm varied with particle size from <0.25 to 10 μm, with quasi-ultrafine particles (Q-UFPs < 0.25 μm) showing the highest OPm. The particle size distribution of the PM emitted from these sources was mostly unimodal, with both PM10 mass and OP emission rate concentrated in the Q-UFP size range. Given the abundance of Q-UFPs in the emitted PM with their high intrinsic OP, we find that 37 ± 3% of the emitted PM10 mass and OP from these sources has the potential to deposit in the respiratory tract, 45 ± 2% of which deposits in the alveolar region. An exploratory exposure assessment suggests that for an equal dose of PM10 mass and OP originating from these indoor sources vs ambient PM, the emissions from the tested indoor sources will likely result in a 76 ± 10% higher dose of alveolar-deposited mass and OP. Collectively, these results emphasize the need to better quantify the size-resolved toxicological properties of PM from myriad indoor emission sources to reliably estimate the result…

The Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) is a prime example of machine-learning (ML) techniques efficiently enriching existing catalogues with classifications and derived physical properties that would be impractical to obtain from spectroscopy or colour selection alone. We applied a pre-trained multi-stage ML pipeline to optical-to-infrared photometry of EMU-PS sources to derive classifications and photometric redshifts, which we used to compute additional radio properties, including luminosities. title: Assessing the Carbon Footprint of Wrap-Faced Retaining Walls: A Comprehensive Life-Cycle Evaluation in Bangladesh
abstract: In the field of geotechnical engineering, there's a growing emphasis on climate-friendly and sustainable approaches, leading to a heightened demand for solutions that integrate technical, ecological, and aesthetic considerations. In response, life cycle assessment (LCA) has become increasingly important as a method for assessing the environmental effects of geotechnical engineering projects. This paper focuses on a soil and water soil and water bioengineering construction project that utilizes geotextile to construct a wrap-faced retaining wall. The objective is to evaluate the wall's contribution to global warming potential (GWP) by evaluating its CO2 emissions. The results highlight the significant environmental advantages of soil and water soil and water bioengineering compared to conventional approaches, especially in terms of global warming potential (GWP). The selection of materials is crucial in determining this benefit, as wrap-faced walls exhibit significantly reduced carbon footprints in comparison to conventional alternatives such as reinforced concrete (RC) walls and mechanically stabilized earth (MSE) walls. abstract: PurposeInterstitial fibrosis is a critical histopathologic feature used in the diagnosis and prognosis of kidney diseases. However, conventional assessment using trichrome-stained slides is limited by interobserver variability and inconsistent stain reproducibility. CFAP47 is involved in sperm head–tail coupling via cooperating with Septin12 and SUN5: gene knockout and protein analysis
abstract: Context Sperm head–tail linkage is essential for maintaining sperm integrity and male fertility. Although CFAP47 is associated with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella, its role in sperm head–tail coupling remains unclear. Aims This study aimed to investigate the role of CFAP47 in sperm head–tail connection. Methods A Cfap47 knockout mouse model was established to assess sperm motility and morphology. Molecular docking, co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays were used to investigate the relationships of CFAP47, Septin12 and SUN5. Key results Cfap47 knockout mice exhibited impaired sperm motility and severe sperm morphological defects, with approximately 70% of sperm displaying abnormal head–tail connection or decapitation. Co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assays demonstrated that CFAP47 cooperates with Septin12 and SUN5. CFAP47 deficiency reduced the protein expression levels and affected their localization at the sperm head–tail junction. Conclusions CFAP47 is essential for sperm head–tail coupling. Implications These findings provide new insight into the molecular basis of sperm head–tail connection.

From policy commitment to lived professional experience: educator wellbeing and leadership values in Malta's National Education Strategy 2024–2030
abstract: This study aims to ask two questions: how does Malta's National Education Strategy 2024–2030 respond to working conditions associated with educator wellbeing, and what would need to change for its commitments to be felt in educators’ everyday work? We bring together Maltese studies from different periods, relevant international research and a structured analysis of policy documents. Across the Maltese literature, concerns recur about workload, educational reform, professional autonomy, consultation, recognition and support. Because the studies used different methods and populations, they cannot show whether these problems remained at the same level over time or what caused them. The Strategy addresses several of these concerns through commitments to wellbeing support, professional participation, recognition, development and less administration. Whether these measures have been implemented successfully remains an open question. We propose a six-level framework that distinguishes policy commitments, wider system conditions, leadership values, observable practices, educators’ immediate experiences and wellbeing outcomes, while recognising that feedback can inform future practice and policy. Trust, respect, care, fairness, recognition and empowerment are proposed leadership values, not measured outcomes. The framework offers a way to evaluate policy implementation without assuming …

title: Translanguaging as a Pedagogical Strategy in Developing Communicative Competence Among English First Additional Language Learners
abstract: Several studies in multilingual contexts reveal that translanguaging challenges linguistic boundaries and norms for social interaction in language teaching and learning. This study was guided by sociocultural theory and communicative language teaching in exploring how translanguaging enhances English First Additional Language learners’ communicative competence. The study adopted a qualitative research approach to explore how translanguaging is used as a pedagogical strategy and how learners experience its contribution to English First Additional Language (EFAL) communicative competence. Participants included one English First Additional Language teacher and twelve Grade 10 English First Additional Language learners who were sampled at a selected secondary school. The qualitative data were generated through non-participant classroom observations and semi-structured learner interviews and analysed using inductive thematic analysis. The study found that translanguaging was effective when employed strategically as temporary scaffolding to clarify meaning, support peer discussion, negotiate concepts, and develop ideas. The study recommends strategic use of translanguaging, drawing from learners’ Sepedi Home Language in facilitating understanding and developing ideas while ensuring learning opportunities in English. abstract: Abstract Background The sinus tarsi approach (STA) is a minimally invasive approach for intra-articular calcaneal fractures. Compared to the extended lateral approach (ELA), STA offers fewer wound complications and allows early operation. After obtaining a sound reduction of posterior facet and hindfoot alignment, the fixation strategy which varies from K-wire to plate can be used. In our study, we focused on Combo and perimeter plates. To evaluate the clinical results between these two plates, we conducted this retrospective clinical study. Methods From January 2022 to July 2025, 38 patients with closed intra-articular calcaneal fractures who received open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with Combo or perimeter plate via the sinus tarsi approach were recruited. abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyze the optimization of Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies of amil (zakat institutions) in Indonesia’s regional National Amil Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) to improve the effectiveness, professionalism and transparency of zakat collection. Design/methodology/approach This research uses the Analytical Network Process (ANP) method to formulate priority strategies for managing amil human resources. ANP was selected because it can capture interdependencies and feedback loops among issues, aspects and strategies. The study’s network structure consists of clusters including Goals, Aspects, Problems and Strategies. Data were collected through pairwise-comparison questionnaires completed by 13 experts, including academics, regulators and practitioners from BAZNAS at national and regional levels, using a 1–9 scale, with consistency ratios (CR) maintained below 0.1. The analysis was conducted using Super Decisions software. Findings This study identifies three key problems in zakat human resource management (HRM): weak leadership, unprofessional recruitment, unclear employment status and low compensation. The highest-priority strategy is promoting leaders as role models of integrity and commitment, consistently rated highly by academics, regulators and practitioners. Other aligned strategies include strict recruitment based on competence (ST.1) and clarifyi…

This study aims to describe the implementation of deep learning strategies in developing early childhood problem-solving skills at TK B UMP Purwokerto through three main principles: meaningful learning (connecting learning materials with children's real-life experiences), mindful learning (fostering children's engagement and focus through simple project-based learning and small-group discussions), and joyful learning (creating an enjoyable learning environment through songs, games, and environmental exploration). abstract: Purpose This paper investigates how environmental and ethical values shape consumer responses in the cosmetics retail context, focusing on detachment from brands that use chemical ingredients or engage in animal testing, as well as preferences for green and cruelty-free products across cultural and generational contexts. Design/methodology/approach We conducted three online survey studies in Italy (n = 310), Thailand (n = 198) and Czechia (n = 535). The first two studies examined how environmental values predict detachment from brands associated with animal testing or chemical ingredients, with brand attitude towards green and cruelty-free products tested as a mediator. The third study analysed how environmental and ethical values predict favourable attitudes towards cruelty-free cosmetics and willingness to purchase such products among Generation Z. Mediation was evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples and the bias-corrected percentile method. Findings In Italy and Thailand, environmental values predict detachment from brands associated with animal testing or chemical ingredients, and this effect is fully or partially mediated by brand attitudes towards green and cruelty-free cosmetics. In Czechia, environmental and ethical values directly predict higher willingness to buy cruelty-free products. Results support an attitude-to-behaviour pathway while revealing cross-…
