Digital operational excellence in retail: a systematic review and dynamic causal framework
abstract: Purpose This study examines how digital technologies integrate with Operational Excellence (OpEx) routines, including Lean Six Sigma, in retail, identifying responsive processes, benefits, evolving KPIs, enablers, barriers, and mitigation strategies, and developing a retail-specific dynamic causal framework. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of 58 peer-reviewed articles from Q1/Q2 journals (2016–2026), following PRISMA guidelines, combined publication mapping, full-text coding, and narrative synthesis to conceptualize Digital-OpEx integration in retail. Findings Digital-OpEx is most evident in inventory, warehousing, logistics, and e-commerce. Digital technologies provide visibility, prediction, and traceability, while OpEx routines provide standardization and continuous-improvement discipline, with implications for customer experience and revenue. KPIs shift from retrospective to real-time, predictive, system-integrated indicators. Adoption depends on digital infrastructure, leadership commitment, employee capabilities, data availability, and system integration; financial, technical, organizational, and ethical barriers persist, though phased rollout and pilot testing aid implementation. title: Transfer Pricing, Capital Intensity, Thin Capitalization, dan Penghindaran Pajak pada Perusahaan Pertambangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2021–2024
abstract: Penerimaan pajak Indonesia masih menghadapi praktik penghindaran pajak, terutama pada sektor pertambangan yang memiliki aset tetap besar, transaksi pihak berelasi, dan kebutuhan pendanaan tinggi. Temuan penelitian terdahulu tentang transfer pricing, capital intensity, dan thin capitalization belum konsisten, dan hubungan ketiganya dengan penghindaran pajak pada periode setelah berlakunya kewajiban dokumentasi transfer pricing dan batas rasio utang terhadap modal masih perlu ditelaah. Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan ketiga variabel tersebut dengan penghindaran pajak pada perusahaan pertambangan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2021–2024. Sampel dipilih secara purposive sebanyak 20 perusahaan (80 observasi; 75 observasi setelah lima pencilan dikeluarkan). Penghindaran pajak diukur dengan cash effective tax rate (CETR), sehingga CETR yang lebih rendah menunjukkan penghindaran pajak yang lebih tinggi, dan data dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda. Transfer pricing berhubungan negatif dengan CETR (B = −1,480; p = 0,008), yang mengindikasikan penghindaran pajak yang lebih tinggi; capital intensity berhubungan positif dengan CETR (B = 1,599; p = 0,040), yang mengindikasikan penghindaran pajak yang lebih rendah; dan thin capitalization tidak berhubungan signifikan (p = 0,345). abstract: This study was conducted based on initial observations of mathematics learning among fifth-grade students at SD Negeri 1 Jatianom. The observations indicated that students’ mathematics learning outcomes were still not optimal, particularly in addition of fractions, and the use of concrete learning media had not been optimally implemented. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effectiveness of plastic waste-based teaching aids in improving students’ mathematics learning outcomes. This study employed a mixed-method approach with a one-group pretest-posttest design for quantitative data and classroom observations for qualitative data. The participants were 20 fifth-grade students selected using total sampling. Data were collected through learning outcome tests and observations of students’ activities during the implementation of plastic waste-based teaching aids. Quantitative data were analyzed by comparing pretest and posttest scores and calculating the N-gain, while qualitative data were analyzed descriptively to describe students’ activities during the learning process. The results showed an improvement in students’ learning outcomes after the implementation of the teaching aids, with the mean score increasing from 43.4 on the pretest to 87.6 on the posttest, while the N-gain was categorized as high. The observation results also indicated that students became more active…

Equilibrium of a rapidly rotating axisymmetric magnetic mirror machine
abstract: A recent paper (Hazeltine et al. 2026 Phys. Plasmas, vol. 33, 072501) has questioned whether the standard result, (ultimately) due to Ferraro, that the plasma angular velocity is approximately constant along individual equilibrium magnetic field lines in a rotating axisymmetric magnetic mirror machine, continues to hold when the rotation becomes sonic or supersonic. In order to resolve this issue, the equilibrium of a rapidly rotating mirror is investigated, starting from first principles, using an ideal two-fluid model with anisotropic pressure. It is found that, as long as the ion gyro-radius is much less than the machine size, and the angular velocity of the plasma is much less than the ion gyro-frequency, the Ferraro result holds good.

The principal understood leadership as service (khadimul ummah), delegated responsibilities according to organisational roles, and retained accountability. abstract: Deep learning in education denotes an approach through which students seek meaning, connect new knowledge with prior understanding, critically evaluate ideas and apply concepts beyond immediate assessment. It differs from surface learning centred on reproduction and memorisation. Foundational investigations distinguished qualitative differences in students’ learning approaches (Marton & Säljö, 1976), while subsequent frameworks connected deep, surface and strategic approaches with learning environments and academic outcomes (Entwistle & Ramsden, 1983; Biggs, 1987). Evidence from higher education suggests that learning approaches and study behaviours have meaningful, though not necessarily large, associations with achievement (Richardson et al., 2012).

title: Interpretable human-label-free deep learning for real-bogus classification with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Time-domain surveys generate large numbers of transient candidates, making real-bogus classification a critical step in automated discovery pipelines. Obtaining reliable human-labeled training sets is costly, while community-provided labels can be noisy and survey-dependent. We aim to develop a real-bogus classification framework for point-like astrophysical transient detections against bogus survey detections, that can be trained without human-labeled data using physically motivated injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data, that remains robust under strong class contamination, and that provides well-calibrated and reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) suitable for downstream decision-making. We combine simulated transient injections with a heavily contaminated survey class and train a dual-network model using an asymmetric co-teaching strategy for classes with different label-noise levels. We evaluate performance on a labeled benchmark subset and analyze the learned representation with latent-space visualization tools. For UQ, we compare standard approaches (Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles) and propose a low-cost hybrid strategy that exploits the dual-network setting to improve calibration. We further extend the evaluation to the light-curve domain to assess recovery of light-curve classes. The method achieves strong real-bogus performance on the labeled s…

title: Does the direct anterior learning curve persist after fellowship training? A single-center comparative cohort study
abstract: Abstract Introduction The direct anterior approach (DAA) for total hip arthroplasty (THA) has historically been associated with a learning curve affecting both operative efficiency and early complications. Whether contemporary adult-reconstruction fellowship training modifies that curve is not established. We compared 90-day complication rates and operative times between newly graduated fellowship-trained DAA surgeons and one experienced DAA surgeon at a single high-volume center. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 600 primary THAs performed via a DAA from a single institution between November 2019 and February 2025 with a minimum of 90-day follow-up. Intra- and post-operative complications were compared between the following two groups: the first 100 cases of each of three junior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons (“Junior”) and the most recent 300 cases of a senior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon (“Senior”). The study was powered to detect a 5% absolute difference in overall complication rates. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were analyzed as exploratory secondary endpoints. Results Operative complications were infrequent in both cohorts, with a numerically higher rate in the Junior group that did not reach statistical significance (Junior 27 [9.0%] vs Senior 20 [6.7%]; absolute difference + 2.3%, 95% CI − 2.0% to + 6.6%, p = 0.362). title: Environment-Aware Deep Learning for Adaptive Dissolved Oxygen Sensing: Resolving the Information Efficiency Paradox in Aquatic Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Continuous high-frequency monitoring of dissolved oxygen (DO) faces a fundamental conflict between excessive energy consumption and substantial data redundancy, whereas conventional fixed-frequency sampling risks frequency aliasing and the omission of acute transient ecological events. To resolve this dilemma, a knowledge-guided, seasonally adaptive dynamic sampling strategy coupled with bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) reconstruction is proposed. Validated via long-term datasets from two hydrodynamically distinct Yangtze River stations, this framework yields three principal findings. First, summer precipitation acts as the primary catalyst for acute hypoxic risks (DO < 5.0 mg/L), whereas winter rainfall predominantly drives reaeration, dictating the nonstationary triggers for dynamic sampling. Second, optimal data decimation exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity governed by site-specific environmental buffering capacities; high-fidelity reconstruction requires merely 22.99% data retention at the hydrodynamically stable Nanjinguan mainstream. Third, a counterintuitive information efficiency paradox is mathematically proven at the highly volatile Chenglingji lake outlet: the dynamic strategy (utilizing 50.23% of data) achieves a Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE) of 0.969, vastly outperforming the uncompressed 100% full-data baseline (KGE = 0.797). title: A Summability Assisted Machine Learning Framework for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Equipment
abstract: Purpose: Industrial Predictive Maintenance (PdM) relies on sensor streams that are noisy, irregular, and affected by changing operating regimes, which can cause machine learning models to overreact to transient spikes or miss slow drift. This study develops a summability assisted machine learning framework that converts noisy time series into stable, interpretable features before prediction. Research Methodology: The study uses a methodological design that combines a literature synthesis, mathematical definitions of finite Cesàro means, weighted means, cumulative and robust summaries, a leakage resistant evaluation protocol, a cost sensitive decision rule, and simulation based illustrations on a synthetic pump record. Results: On the synthetic record, an adjacent window difference and a clipped cumulative sum detected a slow drift that a single sample limit missed while ignoring an isolated spike. Window length governed a clear trade off between false alerts and detection delay, and a worked example showed that a calibrated failure probability of 0.18 justifies inspection when the break even probability is 0.048. Conclusions: Summability features are a low cost and interpretable complement to raw signals, but their value must be demonstrated for each asset class and decision horizon. abstract: Abstract This paper presents a model-based graph reinforcement learning (MBGRL) framework for defending active distribution systems with high penetrations of distributed energy resources (DERs) against cyber-physical threats, particularly false data injection attacks (FDIAs). The proposed approach integrates a learned power-flow surrogate model with a graph neural network (GNN) policy to accelerate convergence, reduce simulator dependence, and capture the spatial structure of distribution networks. Adversarial scenario training further enhances robustness under coordinated load-altering attacks, DER-setpoint tampering, and combined multi-vector FDIAs. Evaluated on the IEEE-123 bus system, the MBGRL framework demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods: it reduces simulator interactions by 54% and training time by more than 60%, while achieving superior operational resilience—lowering voltage violations to 5 (compared with 12 for SAC and 18 for MPC) and reducing active-power losses to 89 kW (compared with 102 kW for SAC and 111 kW for MPC). abstract: Abstract Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters such as ν-DABNA have enabled highly efficient deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, their device performance is strongly governed by the electronic structure of the host matrix. Here, we demonstrate that ν-DABNA displays a distinct host-dependent reversal of charge-trapping polarity in three representative host matrices—mSiTrz, mCBP, and PhCzBCz in an identical device architecture. Specifically, ν-DABNA behaves as a hole trap in mSiTrz, an electron trap in PhCzBCz, and a bipolar trap in mCBP according to its energy level. The electroluminescence (EL) spectra of ν-DABNA-based devices exhibit nearly identical peak positions around 470 nm, and the mCBP-based device delivers the highest peak EQE at low current density, a relatively serious efficiency roll-off at high current density, and a long device lifetime, indicating the bipolar carrier-buffering effect of doping ν-DABNA. Transient EL measurements reveal a clear decoupling between charge formation and emissive decay processes. The rise dynamics strongly depend on host-dependent trap polarity, leading to a significant variation in turn-on time, while the decay dynamics remain invariant across all devices, confirming that delayed fluorescence is exclusively governed by intrinsic ν-DABNA reverse intersystem crossing (RISC). title: A social entrepreneur’s journey to heal the world: uncertainty the only certainty?
abstract: Learning outcomes At the end of this discussion, students will be able to apply key theoretical frameworks – tensions of hybridity, institutional logics and hybrid organizing archetypes – to analyze Centre for Health and Development (CHD) Group India’s strategic challenges and emerging market context; evaluate whether CHD should accept, reject or seek to modify the donor’s hybrid condition, considering the trade-offs among financial resilience, mission integrity, stakeholder legitimacy and organizational capacity; develop and justify an organizational and governance arrangement appropriate to the recommended strategic pathway. Where the recommendation includes earned-income activities, students should explain how those activities can be structured and governed without undermining CHD’s mission; and assess the role of partnerships and stakeholder engagement in supporting CHD’s chosen sustainability pathway while protecting community access, organizational legitimacy and long-term impact. Case overview/synopsis This case examines the strategic dilemma faced by Dr Edmond Fernandes, founder of CHD Group India – a public health nonprofit organization operating in underserved communities in India. Despite reporting program reached of over four million people through health-care delivery, disaster preparedness and climate-health advocacy, CHD is encountering financial stagnation. As g…

title: Multiobjective Optimization of Integrated Green Hydrogen and Biomass Supply Networks for Vacuum Gas Oil and Bio–Oil Coprocessing in Refinery Hydrocracking Units
abstract: Abstract A multiobjective optimization framework is developed for the integrated green hydrogen and biomass supply network design of vacuum gas oil and bio–oil coprocessing in hydrocracking units, to support the low-carbon transformation of refinery hydrogenation processes. A mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model is established with dual objectives of minimizing total annual cost (TAC) and total carbon emission (TCE). The ε-constraint method is adopted to generate the Pareto optimal frontier, and the evaluation function method is used to screen the optimal compromise solution balancing economic and environmental performance. Results show that the system achieves a maximum carbon emission reduction of 43.99% with only a 6.91% increase in TAC. The optimal compromise solution realizes a 39.74% TCE reduction with a negligible 0.16% TAC increase compared with the cost-optimal scenario. Green hydrogen related costs account for more than 74% of TAC, which is the dominant factor affecting the supply chain economy, while biomass transportation contributes over 60% of total emissions as the core emission reduction handle. In sensitivity analysis, the optimal supply chain configuration remains stable under fluctuations of green hydrogen price, and the effective implementation interval of carbon tax is 0–75 CNY/t CO2-eq. The proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for …

title: Unsorted Antithetic RQMC for Relaxed Barrier Optimization: Enhanced Stability and Variance Reduction
Formulation optimization, flavor formation, and quality characteristics of a seasoning paste containing a Maillard-derived flavor base
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop and characterize a compound seasoning paste containing a Maillard-derived flavor base prepared from quinoa hydrolysate and bovine bone collagen peptides. Methods The flavor base was prepared through the Maillard reaction and subsequently incorporated with beef tallow and other auxiliary ingredients. Using sensory score as the evaluation index, the formulation was optimized through single-factor experiments and an optimal mixture design. The product was characterized by amino acid analysis, multivariate statistical analysis, volatile flavor profiling, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and physicochemical and microbiological analyses. Results The optimal formulation consisted of 37% flavor base, 33% beef tallow, 12% maltodextrin, 9% corn starch, 6% sucrose, and 3% salt. The experimental sensory score was 8.75 ± 0.11, showing a relative error of 0.13% from the predicted value. A total of 17 hydrolyzed amino acids were identified in the optimized compound seasoning paste, with Pro (0.60 g/100 g), Ala (0.38 g/100 g), and Glu (0.27 g/100 g) among the most abundant. Principal component analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis revealed that Pro, Ala, Arg, Glu, Asp, and Gly were the key differential amino acids contributing to sample discrimination. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry …

title: Balancing DOF margin and stochastic failure in high-NA EUV process
abstract: BackgroundHigh-numerical aperture (NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography delivers superior resolution, but it severely restricts the depth of focus (DOF) window. To expand this margin, the detrimental impact of stray photons leaking into unexposed areas must be mitigated. Crucially, we confirmed that increasing the photo contrast to decrease stochastic failure conversely increases sensitivity to this leakage light, thereby degrading the DOF margin.AimWe aim to maximize the functional DOF window in the High-NA EUV process by understanding the effects of the photoresist material configurations and post-exposure bake (PEB) process conditions.ApproachBased on lithographic simulations, we employed a low-contrast resist environment that exhibits low sensitivity to optical leakage in defocused condition.ResultThe DOF window was expanded by elevating the PEB temperature, reducing the polymer molecular weight, decreasing the protecting group (PG) ratio, or applying a PG with high activation energy (Ea) for deprotection. These adjustments reduced profile degradation and pattern collapse by systematically lowering the photosensitivity of the resist matrix against optical leakage in High-NA process.ConclusionThese findings expose a fundamental problem of High-NA process. Widening the DOF margin requires an insensitive resist environment, which can inherently degrade pattern uniformity.…

title: Implicit differentiation for measurement-efficient bilevel quantum-classical optimization
abstract: Quantum optimization has shown promising results for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Real-world applications, however, often involve polynomial coefficients that depend on tunable external factors—such as demand forecasts or risk preferences—giving rise to bilevel optimization structures. We show how variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) can efficiently handle such parametric problems, thus making three contributions. First, we propose a bilevel optimization model for diagonal cost Hamiltonians where coefficients depend on a tunable outer parameter: an outer loop adjusts this parameter—reshaping the cost landscape—while an inner VQA optimizes circuit variables. Second, since derivative-free probing methods incur multiplicative overhead when each outer evaluation requires a complete inner solve, we develop correlator-reuse implicit differentiation (CR-ID), which obtains outer gradients by reusing quantum measurements already collected during inner energy estimation, thus requiring essentially no additional circuit executions. Experiments across three coefficient families show that CR-ID consistently improves budget-normalized efficiency by 4% in 1D and over 14% in multi-dimensional settings, showing a significant performance advantage compared to finite-difference methods. Third, we show that this property is architecture-dependent: the Variational Q…

title: Optimization of Proximal Balloon Edge Dilation Technique for Link-Connect Type of Stent in Coronary Bifurcation Interventions
Sustainable multi-objective topology optimization of composite hybrid tubular trusses
abstract: Purpose The construction sector significantly contributes to global CO2 emissions, underscoring the need for structural optimization methods that explicitly integrate mechanical performance, cost, and environmental criteria. However, existing composite-truss optimization studies do not simultaneously couple truss topology and member sizing with composite slab geometry and reinforcement while considering these competing criteria. This work addresses the gap by developing an integrated multi-objective formulation for hybrid composite concrete–high-strength steel trusses, featuring a concrete-filled upper chord and simultaneous optimization of slab geometry with reinforcement. Design/methodology/approach Two assessment stages were conducted: (1) single-objective optimization across spans of 8–24?m to quantify the structural and environmental benefits of pairing hybrid trusses with optimized slabs; and (2) multi-objective optimization for the best-performing span from (1), including slab capacity as an explicit objective. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithms were used to solve the single- and multi-objective problems, respectively. Findings Results show that hybrid trusses combined with optimized slabs reduce emissions by up to 24% relative to the corresponding homogeneous trusses combined with catalog-based slabs, con…

title: Multistage MP-DRA optimization across C+L and S+C+L MB-WDM transmission systems
abstract: Abstract This paper introduces an optimized multistage design approach for multipump distributed Raman amplifiers (MP-DRAs) in future multiband wavelength division multiplexing (MB-WDM) systems. Wideband system increases transmission capacity of the transmission but results in extreme nonuniformity of gain and asymmetric noise accumulation. To limit these impairments, three single-stage configurations are systematically explored in the C+L band: copropagating, counterpropagating, and bidirectional. The bidirectional configuration provides the optimum C+L performance. It has a peak gain of 17.57 dB, a minimal gain ripple of 1.97 dB, an average noise figure of 7.077 dB (average), and a transmission reach of 206 km. This was the starting point for the implementation of a dual-stage cascaded bidirectional DRA in the same system of 8 channels C+L. This configuration increased the maximum common transmission reach to 274 km, an extra 68 km. The optimization framework is then extended to 110 nm S+C+L band (1,515–1,625 nm). Two different configurations are assessed; single-stage gain-flatting filter (SS-GFF)- and dual-stage (DS-GFF)-based DRA. The SS-GFF yields a 14.12 dB peak gain, a 4.125 dB ripple, and 188 km reach. Importantly, the DS-GFF architecture extends the range of transmission reach to be 236 km, an improvement of 25.5 %. The results provided a strong, simple path toward op…

Modeling the moral account: a system dynamics framework for brand-induced moral licensing and behavioral rebound in sustainable consumption
abstract: Introduction Quantitative models of sustainable consumption typically treat consumption as exogenous, assuming that every green purchase improves environmental outcomes. Behavioral research on moral licensing, however, suggests that purchases perceived as virtuous can license compensatory indulgence that erodes some of the benefit. Recent formal work treats licensing as an environmental rebound mechanism in static consumer models; this study contributes the first dynamic stock-and-flow formalization, developed from a recent conceptual framework of brand-induced moral licensing. Methods Four communication pathways (virtue attribution, identity conferral, effort signaling, and absolution framing) feed two moral accounts with opposite mechanics: credits, which deplete when spent, and credentials, which license behavior without being consumed. The model yields closed-form steady states and a licensing-resistance condition on the rebound ratio ρ> (backfire at ρ> 1). Communication parameters were calibrated through a preregistered content analysis of 120 verbatim-archived units from eight sustainable brands, with perfect dual-coder agreement on the reliability subsample; identity internalization was calibrated from a two-country survey of 3,293 adults. The behavioral conversion parameters are literature-anchored or illustrative, so all rebound magnitudes are model-derived, orde…

title: Estimation of minimum inflow time series under reservoir system operation
abstract: ABSTRACT Frequent and severe droughts driven by climate change highlight the need for reliable reservoir operation strategies. While most studies evaluate firm yield at the scale of individual reservoirs, few explicitly consider reservoir system operation of multiple reservoirs, despite its potential to enhance downstream supply reliability. The main objectives are to develop a method to estimate the firm yield of the Seomjingang and Juam Reservoirs in South Korea under reservoir system operation and to define and estimate the minimum inflow time series for each reservoir as a basis for assessing water supply reliability during extreme droughts. Results show that reservoir system operation increases firm yield by about seven percent (+1.24 cubic meters per second [CMS]), from 17.92 CMS under independent operation to 19.16 CMS under reservoir system operation, and delays reservoir depletion, thereby enhancing water supply stability during droughts. The novelty of this study lies in developing a firm-yield estimation method that incorporates reservoir system operation and establishing the concept of a minimum inflow time series. The proposed methodology establishes a quantitative framework for minimum inflow time-series estimation and highlights how reservoir system operation can enhance the resilience and reliability of long-term water supply.

title: Financial Culture as a Legal Phenomenon and a Crucial Component in the Development of the Financial System of the Russian Federation
abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and legal significance of financial culture and its correlation with financial literacy. An analysis of strategic planning documents adopted in the financial sector from 2008 to the present day reveals a legal transition: the focus has shifted from regulating how citizens are informed and how they acquire relevant knowledge (i.e., financial literacy) toward fostering specific values and cultivating desired behavioral practices (i.e., financial culture). It is acknowledged that, from the perspective of jurisprudence, and, more specifically, the theory of financial law, the term "financial and legal culture" is more precise and better suited to the scientific and terminological framework of financial law. In conclusion, the importance of financial literacy for the development of a state’s financial system and the strengthening of its financial sovereignty is also emphasized.

title: Error de prohibición y diversidad cultural: el pluralismo jurídico en el sistema penal ecuatoriano
abstract: En un Estado intercultural, una persona puede actuar conforme a las normas de su comunidad y, sin saberlo, infringir la ley penal ordinaria. El artículo analizó cómo el error de prohibición, regulado en el artículo 35.1 del Código Orgánico Integral Penal, se relaciona con el pluralismo jurídico y la jurisdicción indígena en Ecuador. Se realizó una revisión documental de la Constitución, el Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial, el Convenio 169, jurisprudencia constitucional y doctrina penal y de pluralismo jurídico arbitrada. El análisis distinguió tres supuestos: conductas dentro de la competencia indígena, conductas fuera de ella con error culturalmente condicionado y conductas sin relación con la cultura. Se concluye que la valoración de la vencibilidad del error debe incorporar el contexto cultural, mientras la ley no ofrece criterios expresos. No se recogieron datos primarios.
venue: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales

title: Cross-model validation of large language models in English-to-Chinese consecutive interpreting assessment: a multi-dimensional comparison with trained human ratings
Long-range spectral entanglement and quantum correlations in highly nondegenerate multi-comb and ultrafast systems
abstract: Abstract Frequency combs are multimode photonic systems that underlie countless precision sensing and metrology applications. Since their invention over two decades ago, numerous efforts have pushed frequency combs to broader bandwidths and more stable operation. More recently, quantum squeezing and entanglement have been explored in single-comb systems for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum-enhanced spectroscopy. However, the production of bright quantum light across multiple nondegenerate pulses or frequency combs, a key technology for multispectral applications, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we explore a mechanism that generates a series of nonlinearly coupled bright frequency combs through cascaded three-wave upconversion and downconversion processes mediated by a single idler comb. We consider both discrete combs and broadband ultrafast pulse systems, showing how these systems generate inter- and intracomb two-mode squeezing and entanglement directly in the frequency basis, spanning a large spectral range. Furthermore, we demonstrate how these systems can be engineered to produce target cluster states and concentrated two-mode squeezing through covariance matrix optimization. Our findings uncover a new multimode quantum regime enabled by hierarchical nonlinear interactions in two frequency dimensions, unlocking applications such as entanglement-a…

title: Concurrent Multi-Level Policy Implementation and the Technology Transfer Performance of Chinese Universities
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of concurrent multi-level policy implementation on university technology transfer performance. It clarifies the moderating roles of government financial support and regional research and development (R&D) conditions. It further examines heterogeneous policy effects across university disciplinary characteristics, geographical locations, regional technology intermediary density, and industrial structure. The findings offer a refined empirical perspective for evaluating multi-level policy effectiveness and optimizing university technology transfer practices. They also provide guidance for strengthening basic research capacity and better integrating of basic and applied research in universities. Design/methodology/approach Panel data from 61 universities directly under the Ministry of Education spanning 2011–2019 were analyzed. We employed the Difference-in-Differences (DID) method to empirically test the specific impact of the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies on university technology transfer. Additionally, moderating effect models and grouped regression are adopted to explore the underlying mechanisms. Findings The empirical results show that the concurrent implementation of local and university-level policies exerts a significantly positive impact on university technology transfer. Second, gover…

title: Bee venom bioactive compounds as multi-target anti-inflammatory therapeutics: a comprehensive review of molecular mechanisms, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and nano-formulated delivery
abstract: Abstract Inflammation is one of the main underlying causes of many diseases. Despite the fact that existing anti-inflammatory treatments like NSAIDs and corticosteroids can effectively treat inflammation, the use of these medicines clinically poses several problems due to serious side effects and poor specificity. Bee venom (BV) has emerged as a promising natural treatment for its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties due to the presence of biologically active compounds such as melittin and phospholipase A2 (PLA2). BV modulates multiple inflammatory signaling pathways by inhibiting NF-κB activation, suppressing MAPK signaling, downregulating inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase−2 (COX-2), promoting regulatory T-cell (Treg) polarization, and activating the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathways. Furthermore, BV enhances wound healing by macrophage polarization, regulation of NF-κB, MAPK, Nrf2/HO-1, and ROS signaling, inhibition of PI3K/Akt signaling, suppression of TGF-β-induced pro-fibrotic gene expression, and cytokine modulation to promote tissue regeneration. The therapeutic efficacy of BV constituents has been increased due to the recent advancement in the field of nanotechnology by improving the stability, bioavailability, targeted delivery, and toxicity. In the context of parallel network pharmacology, PPI network analysis, GO enrichment, KEGG pat…

title: Multi-strain SIS dynamics with coinfection across heterogeneous patches
Topology-guided lightweight multi-scale network for component recognition and defect detection in overhead distribution lines
abstract: Introduction Accurate defect detection in overhead distribution-line imagery requires both local visual evidence and structural information about the associated electrical components. This study proposes TG-LMNet, a lightweight multi-scale network for component recognition and defect localization. Methods TG-LMNet incorporates predicted component locations, categories, and confidence scores into defect detection through spatial compatibility fields. An anisotropic backbone preserves directional features, weighted multi-scale fusion integrates local and contextual information, and a topology-consistency objective constrains component-defect relationships. Local boundary supervision is additionally applied when mask annotations are available. Results On the synthetic SD-ODLD benchmark containing 7,200 images, nine component classes, and eight defect classes, TG-LMNet achieves 85.6% small-defect recall and a 5.8% image-level false-alarm rate, with 9.6 million parameters and 23.8 GFLOPs. On a label-aligned subset of real UAV inspection imagery, the model obtains 72.8% mAP@0.5 under zero-shot transfer and 81.3% after few-shot adaptation. The reported overall host-component association accuracy is 92.4%. Discussion The results indicate the potential of component-conditioned representations for defect detection while revealing a measurable gap between synthetic and real inspection ima…

title: Multi-source analysis identifies an NPC2-associated macrophage transcriptional program in ulcerative colitis
abstract: Background Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves extensive remodeling of intestinal macrophage states, but the molecular programs linking inflammation, lysosomal function, and lipid handling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify macrophage-associated molecules and cellular states linked to UC. Methods We integrated UC single-cell RNA sequencing, bone marrow-derived macrophage polarization transcriptomes, UK Biobank OLINK proteomic associations, external bulk transcriptomic datasets, and spatial transcriptomics. Candidate molecules were further examined in dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis and macrophage activation models. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, receiver operating characteristic, and Spearman correlation analyses were performed as appropriate. Results Twelve genes were shared among UC-associated macrophage differentially expressed genes, macrophage polarization-related genes, and UC-associated circulating protein signals. NPC2 was prioritized based on its macrophage enrichment, external transcriptomic performance, and established lysosomal function. Single-cell reclustering identified an NPC2+MMP12+ macrophage subset with heterogeneous abundance across donors. Donor-level analysis showed a numerically higher median proportion of NPC2+MMP12+ macrophages in UC than in controls, but the difference was not statistically significant (17.7%…

title: Multi-omics characterization of fibroblast subpopulations involved in osteogenic differentiation in periodontitis
abstract: Background Fibroblasts are the predominant stromal cells in periodontal tissues and are involved in inflammation and repair. However, their heterogeneity and molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Our study is to identify fibroblast subpopulations driving osteogenesis in periodontitis and their molecular markers. Methods We integrated bulk RNA sequencing with public datasets to select osteogenesis-related genes in periodontal ligament fibroblasts. Single-cell RNA sequencing resolved fibroblast heterogeneity; pseudotime trajectory inference (Slingshot and Monocle 2) and tradeSeq explored differentiation dynamics and hub genes. In silico knockout analysis predicted effects of marker loss-of-function. Functional enrichment explored cell subpopulation functions and perturbation gene effects. CellChat analyzed intercellular crosstalk. Spatial transcriptomics mapped subpopulations’ spatial enrichment within the tissue. Marker expression was validated by RT-qPCR and immunostaining in cultured cells and mouse models. Results 14 core osteogenesis-related genes were identified, with CCN4 and DPT being specifically identified as markers of fibroblast subsets, along with three other populations. Pseudotime analysis revealed divergent differentiation trajectories of CCN4 + fibroblasts in health v.s. periodontitis: in health they gave rise to immune-functional Fibroblasts 2, whereas in …

title: Multi-Omics Gut Microbiome Species Communities and Functional Modules Linking Metal Exposures to Children’s Neurodevelopmental Health in a Canadian Birth Cohort
abstract: Abstract Early life metal exposure has been associated with adverse neurodevelopment, with gut microbiome disruption proposed as a potential pathway. However, most studies have focused on individual taxa or pathways, despite microbes functioning within ecological communities and coordinated functional networks. Here, we integrated stool metal measurements, shotgun metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and neurodevelopmental assessments in 116 children aged 8–12 years from the GESTE birth cohort in Sherbrooke, Canada. Nineteen metals were quantified in stool samples, and neurodevelopment was assessed using parent-reported behavioral scales, attention performance testing, and resting-state fMRI. Using network-based community detection, we identified 10 co-occurring species communities (SCs) from metagenomic data and 16 coexpressed functional modules (FMs) from metatranscriptomic data and evaluated their associations with metal exposures and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Higher levels of lead, cadmium, aluminum, zinc, copper, and magnesium were associated with lower abundance of Streptococcus- and Veillonella-dominated SCs, while multiple metals were associated with lower abundance of amino acid metabolism and carbohydrate degradation FMs. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested potential indirect associations between stool metals and parent-reported ADHD-related traits througha meth…

title: Pengaruh Green Operations Terhadap Kinerja Operasional UMKM Melalui Green Supply Chain Management di Kota Ambon
abstract: Penelitian ini menguji hubungan Green Operations dengan kinerja operasional UMKM di Kota Ambon, dengan Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) sebagai variabel mediasi. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif eksplanatori dengan 60 responden yang dipilih melalui teknik sensus. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui SmartPLS 4. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa Green Operations berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap GSCM (β = 0,803; t = 17,167; p < 0,001) serta terhadap kinerja operasional (β = 0,378; t = 2,777; p = 0,006). GSCM juga berpengaruh positif terhadap kinerja operasional (β = 0,342; t = 2,376; p = 0,018). Pengaruh tidak langsung Green Operations terhadap kinerja operasional melalui GSCM signifikan (β = 0,275; t = 2,282; p = 0,023), sehingga hasilnya konsisten dengan mediasi parsial. Nilai R² sebesar 0,645 untuk GSCM dan 0,467 untuk kinerja operasional menunjukkan kemampuan penjelasan model pada kedua konstruk tersebut. Temuan ini menggarisbawahi pentingnya mengaitkan pembenahan proses internal dengan praktik rantai pasok yang mempertimbangkan lingkungan
venue: Jurnal Bisnis dan Manajemen West Science

title: Sensing through simulation: Alt-Text descriptive granularity and digital embodiment for visually impaired consumers
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how alternative text (Alt-text) descriptive granularity influences purchase intention among visually impaired consumers in digital restaurant environments. This study further investigates the roles of message framing, health consciousness, restaurant trust and perceived healthfulness through the lens of digital embodiment. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative pretest with 18 visually impaired participants informed stimulus development, followed by four between-subjects experiments (n = 868). The studies manipulated Alt-text descriptive granularity and promotion- versus prevention-focused framing, while health consciousness was measured in Studies 2–4. Studies 3 and 4 tested restaurant trust and perceived healthfulness as mediating mechanisms. Findings Highly descriptive Alt-text increases purchase intention. The effect is stronger under promotion-focused framing and becomes stronger as health consciousness increases. Restaurant trust and perceived healthfulness emerge as complementary relationship- and product-oriented mediating mechanisms. The overall pattern is consistent with an embodied-cognition account of accessible descriptive information. Originality/value This research extends digital accessibility beyond technical compliance by conceptualizing descriptive Alt-text as a basis for digital embodiment. It also shows that accessibili…

title: El Niño Events and Peruvian Fisheries: Multispecies Responses and Adaptive Management
abstract: The warm El Niño event alters the productivity, distribution, catchability, and management of Peruvian fishery resources. A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines was conducted, complemented by a descriptive synthesis of scientific publications and official documents covering the period 2015--2026. The results revealed heterogeneous ecological and fisheries responses to warm conditions. Peruvian anchoveta exhibited coastal concentration, deeper schooling distributions, and changes in size structure, whereas jumbo flying squid, jack mackerel, and Pacific bonito showed temporary availability to certain fishing fleets. Fishery landings simultaneously reflected environmental variability, resource accessibility, fishing effort, and regulatory measures; therefore, they cannot be considered direct estimates of abundance. Strengthening adaptive, climate-responsive, and multispecies fisheries management is recommended through integrated hydroacoustic and oceanographic monitoring, dynamic spatial closures, and differentiated forecasting for coastal and offshore environments to support timely and evidence-based fisheries management decisions. The 2026 El Niño event is considered an ongoing episode.

title: From engagement to loyalty: the mediating roles of brand trust and social media brand posts
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how social media brand engagement influences brand loyalty in the smartphone industry. Particular attention is given to the mediating roles of customer engagement with social media brand posts and brand trust, thereby clarifying the mechanisms through which engagement translates into enduring consumer–brand relationships. Design/methodology/approach The study collected survey data from 585 smartphone users in Jordan. Measurement validity was established through confirmatory factor analysis, and hypotheses were tested using a structural path model, providing robust statistical evidence of the relationships among the engagement, trust and loyalty constructs. Findings Social media brand engagement positively influences brand loyalty, both directly and indirectly through brand trust. Aggregated post-level engagement exerts a weaker effect, contributing modestly to loyalty. Disaggregated analyses reveal that engagement behaviors differ in impact: liking significantly influences trust and loyalty, whereas commenting and sharing do not. Serial mediation is not supported for aggregated post-level engagement; a significant sequential pathway emerges through liking, trust and loyalty. Originality/value Customer engagement theory is advanced by differentiating between brand-level and post-level engagement, revealing that visible engagement b…

title: When does AI capability improve sustainable performance? Strategic agility and the dark side of top management support
abstract: Purpose Returns on artificial intelligence (AI) capability vary widely. Most research links AI investment directly to performance without explaining what converts capability into results. This study positions strategic agility as that conversion process and tests how readiness, executive support and culture shape it. Design/methodology/approach The study integrates dynamic capabilities and sociotechnical theory into a process-based contingency model. It applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to two-wave survey data from 522 Fujian firms. Multigroup analyses test how effects differ by firm size and sector. Findings Strategic agility partially mediates the AI-sustainability link, and employee AI readiness strengthens this mediation. Top management support weakens it instead, a dark-side pattern tied to institutional decoupling. Green culture shows no moderating effect. AI capability harms small firms but benefits larger ones; the direct pathway holds only in industrial sectors. Practical implications AI creates sustainability value when firms treat it as a capability, not a self-executing asset. That capability needs agile routines and employee readiness to turn AI-generated insight into action. Distributed experimentation also merits protection: top-down endorsement can erode the innovation it aims to promote. Originality/value Prior research has la…

title: Growth in new technology-based firms: early partnerships and financial capital
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the associations between initial external partnerships, financial resource mobilisation, and the early growth of micro-sized new technology-based firms (NTBFs). Design/methodology/approach Drawing on survey data from Swedish micro-sized NTBFs, the study tests four hypotheses concerning market-oriented and institutional partnerships, as well as informal and formal sources of external financing. The empirical approach combines Pearson correlation analysis with multiple regression models. Findings The results indicate that partnerships with subcontractors and universities/research institutes are positively associated with early firm growth, whereas partnerships with local authorities are negatively associated with growth within the externally funded subsample. The negative association with local authority partnerships should be interpreted cautiously, as it may partly reflect selection effects or underlying firm characteristics rather than a direct adverse effect. Within the small subsample of externally funded firms, exploratory results indicate that crowdfunding is positively associated with growth, while funding from family and friends is negatively associated with growth. These financing-source findings should be interpreted as exploratory and conditional. Research limitations/implications The financing analyses are based on a relatively small s…

title: The competence-wage paradox among Islamic education management graduates: evidence from an Indonesian graduate cohort
abstract: Purpose This study examines the association between graduates' retrospective assessments of an experiential learning curriculum and their self-reported perceived competitiveness, while separately describing employment relevance and monthly income. The study treats the competence-wage paradox as a descriptive and interpretive pattern rather than an empirically tested wage relationship. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, cross-sectional ex post facto design was employed. Survey data from 55 graduates of an Islamic education management programme were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and descriptive statistics. PLS-SEM was used to assess the association between the experiential learning curriculum and perceived graduate competitiveness, while employment and income were analysed descriptively. Findings Graduates' assessments of the experiential learning curriculum were positively associated with their self-reported perceived competitiveness. Most respondents reported being employed and working in education-related fields, while 63.6% reported monthly income below IDR 1,000,000. The coexistence of perceived competitiveness, job relevance, and comparatively low reported income is described as a context-specific competence-wage paradox. This pattern is interpretive and descriptive; because income was not included in the structural mo…
venue: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education

title: Scope and process interdependencies: project portfolio management maturity
abstract: Purpose This study examines how inter-project interdependencies influence portfolio-level performance. Drawing on information processing theory (IPT), it distinguishes between scope interdependency (strategic alignment of deliverables) and process interdependency (executional and temporal linkages), and examines the moderating role of project portfolio management (PPM) maturity. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 219 project professionals in South Korea were analysed using structural equation modelling to test the effects of interdependencies on average project fulfilment and average economic project success, with multi-group analysis assessing moderation by PPM maturity. Findings The results show that scope interdependency positively affects average project fulfilment, indicating benefits from strategic alignment across projects. In contrast, process interdependency has a negative effect, suggesting increased coordination and information-processing burdens during execution. Furthermore, higher levels of PPM maturity mitigate the negative impact of process interdependency and strengthen the relationship between average project fulfilment and average economic project success. Originality/value This study advances PPM research by conceptually and empirically distinguishing strategic (scope) and executional (process) interdependencies and demonstrating their opposing eff…

title: Tunable optically-induced transmission grating via interacting dark resonances of microwave-driven Rydberg atoms
The Right to Be Born: Possibilities for Protection and Limits on Implementation in Russia and the USA
abstract: The article examines the substance of and mechanisms for safeguarding the right to be born in Russia and the United States. It addresses two dimensions of prenatal life: the disposition of in vitro embryos created through assisted reproductive technologies and the legal protection of the embryo (fetus) during pregnancy. Legislation and case law are used to compare parental reproductive autonomy, the interest in preserving prenatal life, and considerations relating to the future child’s health. Particular attention is paid to Davis v. Davis, Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization, LePage v. Center for Reproductive Medicine, and Russian cases concerning the transfer of cryopreserved embryos and compensation for harm caused by inadequate prenatal diagnosis. The article analyzes the influence of ethical concepts on the regulation of abortion and assisted reproductive technologies and considers the prospects of artificial-womb technology and whole-body gestational donation.

title: Relevant Issues of Classification of Currency Transactions in the Modern Conditions
abstract: The article discusses the need to classify currency transactions based on the subject of legal regulation. The differentiation of currency transactions established in the current Federal Law No. 173 of December 10, 2003 "On Currency Regulation and Currency Control" lacks a clear basis for division and is mixed in content, which does not reflect the specific features of individual types of transactions or the logic of associated currency restrictions. Сlarification of the theory of currency law on this issue, and simplification of the practice of applying currency legislation. At the same time, it is emphasized that the proposed classification of currency transactions is itself multi level, as it simultaneously incorporates both the subject based and territorial criteria for their differentiation.

title: The Constitutional Right to Healthcare in the Context of the Digital Transformation of Healthcare: Legal and Ethical Issues of Personal Data Protection
abstract: As part of the work, a comprehensive analysis of the legal and ethical issues related to the protection of personal data in the healthcare sector in the context of digital transformation was carried out; conclusions were drawn regarding the content and relationship between the concepts of «medical confidentiality» and «personal data». Judicial practice on the transfer and dissemination of medical data was analysed; proposals were formulated to expand the content of the constitutional right to health protection and medical care in the context of digital transformation, as well as to improve legislation taking into account bioethics and digital constitutionalism.

title: Legal Framework for Financial Control in Project Finance
abstract: The article examines issues of financial control when using the project finance method for investment projects. Particular attention is paid to the regulatory framework for project financing, including in the context of implementing public-private partnership projects.

title: Alternative Methods for Resolving Tax Disputes: The Genesis and International Experience
abstract: This article examines the historical background of alternative dispute resolution, the reasons for their popularity, and successful international experience in the use and implementation of alternative dispute resolution in tax disputes, including in the United States, Belgium, and the Netherlands. The author proposes: establishing the taxpayer's right to resort to mediation and (or) negotiations as an optional "pre-administrative" stage of pre-trial tax dispute resolution; establishing criteria for determining whether a tax dispute is mediatable; providing for the right to seek an initial consultation and/or an exploratory session on the mediatability of the dispute; create a registry of tax mediators and establish additional criteria for tax mediators.

title: Monetary Circulation within the System of Treasury Payments: Objects and Transfer Methods, the Start and the End of Monetary Circulation
abstract: The evolution of the cash structure of the budget system of the Russian Federation has led to the emergence of a complex multilevel system of treasury payments, which began to function fully in 2021, the monetary circulation within which is characterized by specific features manifested in its elements. The study of their content is aimed at improving the organization of monetary circulation in the treasury payment system, which is the basis for legal and methodological support for the mechanism of the treasury budget execution system, effective financial control and compliance with financial discipline.

title: Derecho a la educación en América Latina entre 2020 y 2024: revisión narrativa
abstract: El derecho a la educación está reconocido en los instrumentos internacionales y en las constituciones de la región, pero su ejercicio sigue desigual, sobre todo en zonas rurales y entre población vulnerable. El estudio analizó las reflexiones sobre el derecho a la educación en América Latina durante el período 2020-2024. Se realizó una revisión narrativa, con enfoque cualitativo, de artículos científicos y fuentes normativas, sin protocolo sistemático de búsqueda. Los trabajos revisados coinciden en que la pandemia de COVID-19 acentuó la brecha digital; que la formación docente en herramientas digitales fue irregular; que la inversión pública es insuficiente; y que la discontinuidad de las políticas educativas limita su efecto. Se concluye que garantizar el derecho exige conectividad, formación docente, financiamiento estable y políticas sostenidas, aunque los resultados de una revisión narrativa no permiten cuantificar su magnitud.
venue: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales

title: Automatic Jumper Length Extraction from Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) Point Cloud Data of Transmission Towers and Assessment of Wind Deflection Safety Margin
Financial Management Skills and Financial Decision Practices Among Microfinance Members in The Municipality of Maitum, Sarangani
abstract: This study examined the financial management skills and financial decision practices of microfinance members in Maitum, Sarangani, with the aim of developing a financial capability intervention. Utilizing a descriptive-correlational research design, the study assessed the relationship between the members' socio-demographic profiles and their financial management skills, specifically in fund management, spending management, and debt management. Additionally, it evaluated financial decision practices in income, spending, budgeting, savings, and investment. Findings revealed that the majority of microfinance members had low socio-economic status, with most falling below the poverty line and possessing only a high school education. Their financial management skills were generally rated as high, particularly in terms of fund and spending management, though challenges remained in systematic budgeting and distinguishing between essential and non-essential debt. Financial decision practices also scored high, with members demonstrating awareness in tracking income and expenses, though there were gaps in utilizing financial tools like budgeting applications and categorizing expenses effectively. Significant relationships were found between members' profiles and their financial management skills, as well as between financial management skills and financial decision practices. These findin…
venue: Journal of Health Research and Society

title: Navigating external conflicts, technological innovations, and financial risks for sustainable development: evidence from the EKC and ecological footprints in the next eleven
abstract: Abstract To achieve sustainable development, ongoing research needs further investigations in detail for stronger environmental protection. For this purpose, several studies have investigated the factors of ecological footprints (EF), but very few of them have taken external and internal conflicts with technological innovations in the context of EKC. Against this backdrop, this study applies some advanced techniques like wavelet plots and augmented mean group (AMG) methods over the panel data of 1984-2022 for the Next Eleven nations. The results find strong linkages among the variables. Moreover, reducing external conflicts can stimulate environmental quality. The results validate that the EKC, technological innovations, and financial risk are environmentally friendly. GDP is contributing to environmental degradation, while the population shows a mixed impact on environmental sustainability. The wavelet plots also show that there is a direct linkage between financial risk and ecological footprints.

title: A Tax Experiment: The Concept and Signs
abstract: The author summarizes the features of tax experiment proposed in the scientific literature. Then the author offers reasoned criticism. Based on the analysis, it is concluded that the focus on assessing the possibility of widespread implementation is a distinctive feature of tax experiments, allowing it to be compared with related institutions.

title: Derecho a la privacidad y protección de datos personales en Suramérica, 2020-2024
abstract: La digitalización acelerada por la pandemia aumentó la exposición de los datos personales en Suramérica y puso a prueba las leyes de protección. El estudio analizó el derecho a la privacidad y la protección de datos personales en Suramérica entre 2020 y 2024. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo con revisión documental de leyes y artículos científicos, y se examinaron cuatro trabajos recientes sobre armonización de derechos digitales, cooperación internacional, autonomía de las autoridades de protección y tutela penal de los datos. Se identificó una distancia entre las leyes aprobadas y su aplicación, la necesidad de autoridades de control con independencia y capacidad sancionadora, la influencia del Reglamento General de Protección de Datos europeo y un debate sobre el recurso al derecho penal. Se concluye que la protección efectiva exige supervisión, sanciones y educación digital, más que nuevas declaraciones normativas.
venue: Verdad y Derecho. Revista Arbitrada de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales

title: Regional Budgetary Control in the Federative Republic of Brazil: Organizational and Legal Support
abstract: This article provides a comprehensive study of the mechanisms, structure, and legal framework for regional budgetary control in the Federative Republic of Brazil. Given Brazil's complex federal system, characterized by the distribution of powers between the federal center, states, and municipalities, effective control over the use of budgetary funds is of strategic importance for ensuring financial stability and transparency in public administration. This paper provides a detailed analysis of the organizational model of budgetary control and examines the powers and functions of regional financial control bodies. Particular attention is paid to the legal framework for this activity, analyzing the hierarchy of legal acts governing budgetary control at the regional level. The author examines the legal status of regional audit chambers (Tribunal de Contas do Estado) as key institutions ensuring executive accountability. The article examines legal regulation mechanisms that allow for the adaptation of audit and control methods to the specifics of regional governance. The research's novelty lies in its systematization of approaches to understanding regional budgetary control in Brazilian legal doctrine and the identification of the relationship between the organizational structure of control bodies and the effectiveness of budgetary discipline in the federal subjects. The research fi…

title: The Right to Biological Identity: The Nature, Content, and Place in the System of Human Bio-Rights
abstract: The article examines doctrinal issues related to understanding the nature, content, and place of the human right to biological identity within the emerging system of bio‑rights. The relevance of introducing legal clarity into the definition of the right in question, identifying its main distinguishing features, and establishing its relationship with other types of bio‑rights is noted. The hybrid nature of the right to biological identity, which belongs simultaneously to personal and biological rights, is substantiated. The importance of legal regulation of this right at the international legal and national levels is emphasized in the context of addressing the tasks of unifying and codifying the system and content of bio‑rights as an independent group of human rights of the fourth generation.

title: BDMC2026: a groundbreaking conference on biomaterials, bio-design and manufacturing Predicting biofabrication sustainability based on 15 years of output
Perceived causes of construction disputes and the dispute-prevention potential of building information modelling and common data environments in Ghana
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the perceived causes of construction disputes and evaluate the dispute-prevention potential of building information modelling (BIM) and common data environments (CDE) among construction professionals in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 167 construction professionals using a structured questionnaire. The analysis used descriptive statistics, relative importance index, reliability analysis, Kruskal–Wallis and Mann–Whitney tests, Spearman correlation, Wilcoxon signed-rank test and robust regression modelling. Findings The results show that delayed payment and financial issues, communication gaps and unclear site instructions were the most important perceived causes of disputes. BIM was rated highly for digital audit trail, improved visualisation and stakeholder communication, while CDE was rated highly for better decision-making, trust and communication and transparency. All major scales showed excellent internal consistency. The findings further reveal strong positive associations between perceived dispute causes and the perceived preventive value of both BIM and CDE. No significant difference was found between BIM and CDE in their overall perceived dispute-prevention value. In the multivariable models, perceived dispute severity was the strongest predictor of b…

title: Special Issue on Design and Manufacturing for Environmental Sustainability
abstract: This is the eighth special issue on Design and Manufacturing for Environmental Sustainability. Since the first special issue published in 2009, this topic has been featured in this journal for 17 years. Even at that time, environmental sustainability was recognized as an important issue for manufacturing, which motivated the launch of this series of special issues. Since then, the importance and urgency of environmental sustainability have increased, not only in Europe but also in Japan and other countries. Currently, companies are increasingly expected to achieve both economic competitiveness and environmental and social sustainability. This evolution is redefining manufacturing by steering beyond the conventional model of mass production, mass sales, mass consumption, and mass disposal. Increasing concerns over resource security are further accelerating this transition. These developments highlight the necessity to reconsider how products are designed, manufactured, used, and circulated throughout their life cycles. This eighth special issue includes nine high-quality papers encompassing a broad range of topics related to environmental sustainability, including • Circular economy • Disassembly and assembly • Plastics recycling • Effects of consumer behavior on sustainability • Supply-chain management • Waste treatment Most of the papers were originally presented at EcoDesign …

title: Component Influence-Driven Fastener Reduction for Robotic Disassemblability-Aware Design Simplification
abstract: Robotic disassembly must be considered during the product design phase to accelerate automated remanufacturing. However, designers currently lack quantitative feedback for identifying the structural elements that hinder robotic operations. To address this, this study proposes an analytical framework that provides actionable redesign guidance focused on fastener reduction, because fasteners are numerous and ubiquitous components found in almost all manufactured products. Using a computer-aided design (CAD) model and its automatically generated contact-connection-constraint (CCC) graph, the framework translates the robotic disassembly sequence planning outcomes into component influence scores. These scores reflect the frequency with which a component causes structural constraint violations or evaluation objective deteriorations in a robotic disassembly sequence. To visually highlight structural hindrances, the framework projects these scores onto the CAD geometry as 3D heatmaps. The system then analytically simulates the removal of highly influential fasteners. It reports the expected reductions in structural constraints, tool changes, and robot travel distances while preventing structurally unsafe modifications by evaluating geometric stability metrics. Experiments on seven household appliances demonstrated that the framework successfully targeted redundant fasteners. Removing t…

title: A Gender-Disaggregated Analysis of Labour Market Performance and Economic Growth in Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the relationship between gender-disaggregated labour-market performance and economic growth in Nigeria, with emphasis on the quality of male and female labour-market participation rather than participation rates alone. The study was motivated by the concern that aggregate labour indicators often concealed gender-based differences in employment quality, productivity, informality, underemployment and access to growth-enhancing work. Using annual Nigerian data covering 1991 to 2025, the study constructed male and female labour-quality indices from labour force participation, employment-to-population ratio and unemployment indicators, while controlling for foreign direct investment and inflation. The empirical analysis employed descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, unit root testing, ARDL bounds testing and dynamic ARDL estimation. The findings showed that gender-disaggregated labour-market performance was relevant to Nigeria’s growth process. The ARDL bounds test confirmed the existence of a long-run relationship among economic growth, female labour-market quality, male labour-market quality, foreign direct investment and inflation. The results further showed that improvements in female labour-market quality were positively associated with economic growth, while inflation had a negative effect on growth. The implied long-run estimates indicated that fem…

title: Gcn5 and mTORC1 mediated regulation of autophagy controls Drosophila blood cell homeostasis
abstract: Blood progenitors are regulated by a variety of systemic and nutritional cues from their environment. In the Drosophila lymph gland (LG), the Posterior Signaling Center acts as a stem cell niche striking a balance between progenitors and differentiated blood cells. Autophagy is a vital cellular process that maintains homeostasis by removing unnecessary or dysfunctional cell components through autophagic degradation and recycling. Here, using genetic perturbation analysis, we show that autophagy plays a critical role in regulating LG blood cell homeostasis. General control non-derepressible 5 (Gcn5), a histone acetyltransferase, is expressed in the primary LG lobe, and modulation of Gcn5 levels perturbs LG homeostasis. Our results show that hemocyte-specific Gcn5 modulation controls autophagic flux in the hemocytes. Furthermore, we show that modulation of mTORC1 activity can perturb hematopoiesis. Our results indicate that organismal Gcn5 levels respond to dietary shifts and are modulated by mTORC1 signaling. Chemical intervention shows that mTORC1 overrides the effect exerted by Gcn5 in regulating LG hematopoiesis. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that Gcn5 and mTORC1 regulate autophagy to maintain blood cell homeostasis in Drosophila .

title: Synergistic Anion Regulation Inducing Fluoride‐Rich SEI and Defect‐Rich MnO 2 for Stable Dual Electrode‐Free Zn‐MnO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Dual electrode‐free (DEF) Zn─MnO 2 batteries based on dissolution‐deposition chemistry are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their lightweight architecture and high theoretical capacity (616 mAh g −1 ). However, poor interfacial reversibility and the accumulation of “dead manganese” significantly limit their lifespan. Here, we demonstrate a stable DEF battery enabled by an anion‐regulation strategy using a hybrid electrolyte (E‐OA) comprising trifluoromethanesulfonate (OTf − ) and acetate (Ac − ) ions. At the anode, OTf − facilitates the formation of a fluoride‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively suppressing dendrite growth and the hydrogen evolution reaction. At the cathode, the synergistic anionic environment elevates the MnO 2 nucleation overpotential, shifting the electrocrystallization pathway to an instantaneous nucleation mode. The kinetically driven growth process traps abundant structural defects, identified as proton‐compensated manganese vacancies (Ruetschi defects). These vacancies lower the thermodynamic energy barrier for Mn─O bond cleavage, thereby ensuring highly reversible dissolution. Consequently, the E‐OA‐based DEF battery achieves exceptional stability for over 7500 cycles at 0.5 mAh cm −2 and sustains 600 cycles at 2 mAh cm −2 (10 mA cm −2 ), demonstrating superior rate capability and versatility in both f…

title: The Mediator Complex Protein Vmg1 Plays a Central Role in the Regulation of Development and Pathogenicity in the Soil-Borne Pathogen Verticillium dahliae
abstract: Verticillium dahliae is a soil-borne pathogen that causes vascular wilts in a wide variety of agronomically important crops worldwide. The lack of host specificity and the systemic nature of the infection pose a challenge for the control of this pathogen. Furthermore, V. dahliae produces resistant structures, the microsclerotia, that can remain viable in the soil for long periods of time and are the main source of inoculum for new infections. In this work, using a forward genetic approach and targeted gene deletion we have identified Vmg1, a putative ortholog of the Mediator Complex protein Med15, as a major regulator of morphogenesis and essential for pathogenicity in V. dahliae . Mutants deleted for vmg1 do not sporulate, produce microsclerotia with an aberrant structure, show reduced aerial mycelium formation, and do not induce any Verticillium wilt symptoms. They also exhibit impaired glucose metabolism and altered stress responses. The developmental defects observed in Δ vmg1 strains are consistent with their inability to undergo processes that require cell budding. In planta analyses using confocal and scanning electron microscopy show that the Δ vmg1 strain goes through the prevascular phase of the infection but remains trapped outside the xylem vessels in the vascular tissue. We propose that as previously shown for the well-characterized Saccharomyces cerevisiae Med15 p…

title: Market chain analysis of myrrh in southeastern Ethiopia
abstract: Aim of the study: To investigate myrrh production and marketing channels in the El-Weyni district of Ethiopia’s Somali Region, identify the roles and relationships of market participants, analyze market structure and practices, and determine factors influencing household-level myrrh supply. Area of the study: The research was conducted in El-Weyni district, an area with substantial but underutilized potential for non-timber forest products (NTFP), particularly gums and resins. Material and methods: Data were collected through key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and a household survey of 117 randomly selected households. Qualitative data were summarized descriptively, while quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS version 20. Main results: The findings revealed that myrrh production is primarily motivated by cash income generation. Average annual income from myrrh was USD 209.97 per household, ranging from USD 53.39 to USD 772.31. Annual production varied between 7 kg and 90 kg, with an average of 23.6 kg per household. Three major oligopolistic marketing channels were identified. Family size, access to market information, and distance to market significantly influenced myrrh supply, while market information access was generally limited. Research highlights:The study recommends promoting cooperative formation, introducing improved tapping techniques, and strengt…

title: Desempeño comparativo de Holt-Winters y Prophet en la predicción de la demanda eléctrica en sistemas de distribución y alumbrado público
abstract: Accurate electricity demand forecasting supports operational planning and energy-efficiency decisions in distribution systems. This study compares the additive Holt-Winters and Prophet models applied to public lighting demand in Cotopaxi, Ecuador, using an institutional inventory of 52,365 luminaires from 2012 to 2020. The inventory was transformed into a monthly theoretical energy series through data cleaning, calendar-based energy calculation and a dynamic replacement rule for the transition from mercury and sodium lamps to LED technology. The models were implemented in Python and evaluated with MAPE, RMSE and R². Holt-Winters obtained lower short-term error, whereas Prophet better represented the 2019 LED structural change; therefore, both models are useful for complementary operational and strategic planning.
