title: Market Share Liability versus (Random) Strict Liability
abstract: Abstract I consider a model in which firms engage in Cournot competition in producing potentially harmful products. In addition to choosing output, they also choose safety precautions, which affect each product’s likelihood of harm to third parties. Under (individual) strict liability (SL), a firm whose product causes harm is found liable only if causation can be established in court. Under market share liability (MSL), all firms are held liable for a fraction of harms equaling their respective market shares. The model shows that, contrary to what many have suggested, proof-of-causation problems alone are insufficient to justify MSL. SL reduces the likelihood of liability, conditional on harm, while increasing the size of damages, relative to MSL. Because MSL ties liability to a firm’s production more closely than SL, it increases firms’ effective marginal cost of production more than SL, and thereby leads to less production than SL. Moreover, SL gives firms no worse incentives to take safety precautions than MSL, as long as the probability of holding the injuring firm liable is not smaller than that firm’s market share. Therefore, under these conditions, MSL leads to less welfare than SL, as long as SL does not lead to over-optimal production. An implication is that implementing SL in a symmetric equilibrium by randomly holding one of the firms in the market liable is superior…

title: A Critical Analysis of the Marketing Mix (4Ps) and Its Role in Market Development: A Case Study of Morerro Foods Pvt. Ltd., Baramati
abstract: This study examines the Product, Price, Place and Promotion (4Ps) of Morerro Foods Pvt. Ltd., Baramati, and looks at how these elements may work together to support market development. The study uses a descriptive case-study approach based mainly on observations recorded during the On-the-Job Training (OJT) period from May to August 2026. The field report records approximately 150 retailer interactions across Baramati, Baramati MIDC and nearby areas, and nearly 20 potential retailer opportunities passed to the senior sales team. The observed portfolio included a ₹5 chocolate bars of different flavors and ₹350 chocolate spreads. The bar received comparatively stronger acceptance during the observed visits, while the spread was more difficult to introduce; retailers reportedly indicated limited customer requests and low product awareness. These observations do not represent audited company-wide results and do not prove cause and effect. The analysis points to the need for different positioning and channel approaches: availability and visibility of bar, and use-based communication, targeted trials and closer evaluation of perceived value for the spread. The approximately 13.3% ratio of potential opportunities to interactions is treated only as a lead-generation indicator, not a sales conversion rate. Evidence gaps include the absence of verified product-wise sales, margins, consum…

title: Interdependence and Contagion Between Crude Oil Bubbles and Chinese Stock Market Bubbles
Macro- and Trace Elements in Fresh Fruits from the Reșița Agri-Food Market, Romania—Chemometric Analysis and Health Risk Assessment
abstract: Fruits are an important source of essential minerals, but can also contribute to the intake of potentially toxic elements. This study determined the moisture, macroelement (Na, K, Ca, Mg) and trace element (Cu, Mn, Fe, Cd, Pb, Zn, Cr) contents of 15 fruit species purchased from the agri-food market in Reșița, Romania, by flame and graphite furnace atomic absorption spectrometry. The data were evaluated by principal component analysis (PCA), k-means and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) and used to assess the health risk. Mean contents followed the orders K > Ca > Mg > Na and Fe > Zn > Mn > Cu > Cr > Pb > Cd, strawberry being the richest in most elements. The first three principal components explained over 93% of the variance and the samples clustered with literature data for the same species. Pb and Cd contents were well below EU and Codex Alimentarius limits. For daily intakes of 200 g (adults) and 175 g (children aged 6–9 years), all hazard quotients were below 1 and the margin of exposure indicated a low risk from Pb; thus, under the evaluated scenarios, the analysed fruits pose no health concern and are a valuable source of essential minerals.

title: Impact-Based Allocation of Common-Area Electricity Charges in Apartment Complexes
abstract: Under the single contract (SC) used in apartment complexes in the Republic of Korea, the total electricity consumption of an apartment complex is measured by a main electricity meter, and the residential high-voltage (HV) progressive tariff is applied to calculate the total electricity bill. The difference between the total electricity bill charged to the apartment complex and the sum of the electricity bills calculated for individual households constitutes the common-area electricity bill, which is generally allocated equally among households. However, because the residential progressive tariff is applied to the total electricity consumption, the common-area electricity bill depends not only on the electricity consumption of common-area facilities but also on the distribution of electricity consumption among individual households. Therefore, an allocation method that considers the impact of individual households on the common-area electricity bill is required. In this study, the impact value of each household on the common-area electricity bill is quantified by the change in the bill resulting from the inclusion of that household. Based on these impact values, proportional (PROP) and additive (ADD) allocation schemes are proposed, along with their nonnegative (NN) variants to prevent negative charges. A bounding method is also proposed to impose upper and lower bounds on the a…

title: From Static Risk Registers to Phase-Adaptive Risk Analytics: A Market-to-Credit Monitoring Framework for Renewable Energy Projects in Bulgaria
abstract: Static risk registers compiled at financial close do not follow the market conditions that determine the cash flows of merchant-exposed renewable projects. This study asks how far public day-ahead market data can support a phase-adaptive decision-support and monitoring framework for market-to-credit risk in solar-dominated renewable projects in Bulgaria. It uses 1096 daily observations (13 July 2023–12 July 2026) of day-ahead prices, renewable generation, and interpolated installed capacity. Across thirteen price specifications, the capacity coefficient is a conditional association that cannot be separated from time trends and has the sign opposite to the merit-order hypothesis, and same-day generation shows no stable negative association with the daily average price. In 730 rolling-origin forecasts, the capacity-and-trend model improves on a naive forecast by 5.9%, but not on an AR(1) benchmark, whereas calendar terms reduce the root-mean-squared error by about 25%. Days with a negative minimum price rise from 15 to 44 per sample year. Candidate monitoring indicators do not outperform a seasonal benchmark in the test sample and are not validated early-warning signals. A rolling debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) analysis of a stylized 1 MW PV asset rests on assumed capture rates, generation profiles, and financing terms, not on observed project data; under the base structure, …

title: Finding the ventilation sweet-spot: A validated CFD trade-off between airborne-infection risk, thermal comfort, and cooling energy in a tropical classroom
abstract: Post-pandemic high-occupancy classrooms renew concern over airborne pathogen transmission, yet in tropical climates ventilation for pathogen dilution competes with thermal comfort and latent cooling load. Existing studies typically optimise these objectives in isolation, largely for temperate climates. This study uses a Computational Fluid Dynamics model, verified by a grid-convergence analysis and validated, within measurement uncertainty, against field air-velocity and temperature measurements in a real Malaysian university classroom, to evaluate six air change rates (ACH 3.8 to 22.7) against three objectives: airborne-infection risk (Wells--Riley), thermal comfort (ISO 7730 draught rate and adaptive comfort temperature), and cooling-energy demand. Infection risk fell steeply up to ACH 11.3 to 15.1 (about a 75% reduction at ACH 15.1 relative to ACH 3.8) but only marginally thereafter (a further 8 percentage points by ACH 22.7, only 3 of them from the final step from ACH 18.9), while the cooling load rose 6.0-fold and local air speeds exceeded the ISO 7730 draught limit; near-occupant temperatures of about 24.3°C lay roughly 5°C below the local adaptive comfort temperature (29.3°C), indicating overcooling that is better addressed through the supply-air set-point. An air change window of approximately 11 to 15 per hour emerges as the cost-effective optimum, capturing near-maxim…

Market Competition, Pricing Strategy, and Firm Performance: An Economic Perspective
abstract: Market competition plays an important role in shaping firms’ pricing decisions and overall performance. This study examines the relationship between market competition, pricing strategy, and firm performance from an economic perspective. Drawing on theories of market structure, price elasticity of demand, and profit maximization, the study analyzes how different competitive conditions influence firms’ pricing behavior. It examines several major pricing approaches, including costbased pricing, competition-based pricing, value-based pricing, and dynamic pricing, and considers their implications for profitability, market share, and long-term competitive performance. The analysis further identifies product differentiation, consumer price sensitivity, market concentration, firm characteristics, and digital technologies as important factors affecting the relationship between competition, pricing, and performance. The findings suggest that pricing strategy does not have a uniform effect on firm performance. Lower prices may stimulate demand and market share but can reduce profit margins, whereas higher prices may improve margins while negatively affecting demand when consumers are price sensitive. Therefore, firms need to align pricing decisions with market structure, consumer demand, competitive conditions, and long-term strategic objectives. The study highlights the importance of in…

title: Development of a Vibrio natriegens -Based Plate-Clearing Assay for Rapid Screening of PET-Hydrolyzing Enzymes
abstract: Abstract Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a major contributor to plastic waste. Enzymatic PET degradation offers a sustainable recycling approach, but screening for effective enzymes remains challenging. Herein, we established an experimental plate-clearing assay using Vibrio natriegens, exploiting its protein secretion system to rapidly identify catalytic activity without time-consuming downstream processing. To validate the assay’s robustness, we tested variants of Fusarium solanipisi cutinase (FsC) and found that one variant, T45P, exhibited 3-fold higher PET-film degradation yield than the wild type and favored the production of terephthalic acid. As a further test case, we screened an error-prone polymerase chain reaction (PCR) library of FsC using the assay, obtaining a 25% hit rate after screening 150 colonies. This demonstrates the scalability of the method to large enzyme libraries.

title: Short-Term Probabilistic Forecasting of Irrigation Need Based on Relative Soil-Moisture-Deficit Persistence Using Copula Models
abstract: Soil-moisture deficits affect irrigation management in arid irrigated systems, yet their short-term persistence and uncertainty are difficult to quantify at the field scale. This study developed a spatially explicit probabilistic framework combining high-resolution root-zone soil-moisture estimation with Copula-based dependence modeling to quantify relative soil-moisture-deficit persistence in the Daheyanzi Irrigation District, Xinjiang, China. Using Google Earth Engine, the Enhanced Spatial and Temporal Adaptive Reflectance Fusion Model generated daily vegetation-index and land-surface-temperature products at 30 m resolution, while a Random Forest model estimated daily 0–40 cm soil moisture. A percentile-based relative soil-moisture-deficit index (RSDI) was constructed, and four Copula models were evaluated. The Frank Copula provided the best statistical fit. Kendall’s τ decreased from 0.505 at a 1-day lead to 0.085 at a 7-day lead, indicating that persistence information was concentrated mainly within 1–3 days. When current RSDI exceeded 0.80, the probabilities of future RSDI exceeding 0.90 were 28.0% and 19.0% at 1- and 3-day leads, respectively. Rolling-window validation showed the clearest predictive advantage at 1 day, with improved discrimination at 3 days. The framework provides spatially explicit deficit probabilities to support irrigation-need assessment and field pri…

title: The art of memes in feminist digital culture
Risk Regimes and Price Stability: Threshold Effects of Geopolitical Risk, Economic Policy Uncertainty, and Energy-Related Uncertainty on Inflation in G7 Economies
abstract: Heightened geopolitical tensions, policy shocks, and energy-market turbulence have renewed concerns about price stability in advanced economies. This paper examines whether geopolitical risk (GPR), economic policy uncertainty (EPU), and energy-related uncertainty (EUI) are associated with inflation linearly or through distinct risk regimes. Monthly data for Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States from 2013M2 to 2023M10 are analysed using second-generation panel methods accounting for cross-sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity. CS-ARDL, CCEMG, AMG, and CCEP estimates indicate positive inflation associations for GPR and, most robustly, EUI, while EPU exhibits only weak linear significance. Block-bootstrap tests identify significant thresholds for GPR and EUI, with weaker evidence for EPU. Dynamic CCE threshold estimates show that the long-run inflation association with EUI is several times stronger above its threshold, primarily during the 2022 energy crisis. This amplification survives alternative controls and specifications but loses significance when 2022 is excluded, indicating crisis-driven regime identification. Lagged estimates suggest delayed inflation responses to EPU, while quantile regression reveals stronger associations at higher inflation levels. Panel causality tests identify predictive content for GPR but not EPU or…

title: Conditional Scenario Forecasting of Children’s Health Indexes under Social Infrastructure Development: A Four-Outcome System and the Effect of Statistical Registration in the Regions of Uzbekistan
abstract: Purpose of research . Conditional scenario forecast is typically constructed for a single index of health usually infant mortality and cannot reveal the heterogeneous, sometimes opposite, response of different child-health indexes to social infrastructure development. This paper creates a multi-outcome conditional forecast of four child-health indexes under alternative infrastructure trajectories and assesses how far recorded indexes are fit for monitoring the results of such policy . Materials and methods. A balanced panel of fourteen regions of Uzbekistan over 2012–2024 (one hundred and eighty-two observations) is used. Four outcomes infant mortality, proportion of underweight children, incidence of bacterial dysentery and acute respiratory infections are modelled jointly by a system of externally unrelated regressions with regional fixed effects and logarithmic dependent variables. Infrastructure is presented by three composite indexes medical, utility, and educational. Scenario trajectories are specified as index increments calibrated to historical rates, and forecast uncertainty is estimated using the Monte Carlo simulation method. Results. A unified infrastructure-driven acceleration shifts the four indexes in different directions. By 2030, under the forced scenario, infant mortality decreases by 4.2 percent, the proportion of underweight children by 13.3 percent and dyse…

title: Progress but not on track: forecasting under-five mortality and the likelihood of achieving SDG target 3.2 in Southern Africa
MACHINE LEARNING, DEEP LEARNING, AND EXPLAINABLE AI FOR MULTI-SOURCE AIR POLLUTION FORECASTING: A REVIEW
abstract: Air pollution remains one of the most pressing environmental and public health challenges of the current decade, motivating sustained research into computational methods for forecasting pollutant concentrations. This review synthesizes recent literature on machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), hybrid ensemble architectures, multi-source data integration, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) as applied to air quality forecasting. Tree-based ensemble methods such as XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, alongside recurrent architectures such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and their convolutional and attention-augmented variants, dominate the recent literature, frequently combined into hybrid or stacked frameworks to balance short-term responsiveness with long-term temporal dependency modeling. A growing body of work integrates heterogeneous data streams, including ground-based sensor networks, meteorological records, traffic and emission inventories, and satellite-derived aerosol and trace-gas products, to improve spatial and temporal coverage. In parallel, explainability techniques, most notably SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), are increasingly incorporated to address the opacity of high-performing black-box models and to support policy-relevant decision-making. This review consolidates findings …

title: STRUCTURAL TREND, YIELD SHOCKS AND PRICE: THE DYNAMICS OF SECOND-CROP MAIZE IN DOURADOS, MATO GROSSO DO SUL, BRAZIL, 1994–2025
abstract: The expansion of second-crop maize has reshaped the agricultural base of Dourados, one of the leading farming hubs in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, yet little evidence exists on how output and price interact over a long horizon that includes the climate and market shocks of the 2020s. This study aimed to analyse the dynamic relationship between municipal maize output and the real price of the grain in the state from 1994 to 2025. It used 32 annual observations from the Municipal Agricultural Production survey of the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics, deflated by the national consumer price index, and applied unit root tests with and without structural breaks, the autoregressive distributed lag bounds test, Toda-Yamamoto causality, the Nerlovian partial adjustment model and a variance decomposition of output growth. All series were stationary around a deterministic trend, with breaks in 2010–2011 for output, area and yield and in 2019 for price. Output grew tenfold, but about 62% of its annual variance stemmed from yield swings linked to drought and frost. No temporal precedence was found between output and price; harvested area responded to the previous year's price with a short-run elasticity of 0.20, and price reacted to state-wide supply shocks but not to Dourados output, which characterises the municipality as a price taker. Local farm income therefore depends m…

title: Do Green Bonds Price Clean Power? Frequency and Quantile Evidence from Data-Center Load
DESENVOLVIMENTO DE UM PIPELINE DE DADOS INTEGRADO À PREVISÃO DE DEMANDA NO VAREJO DE COMÉRCIO ELETRÔNICO
abstract: Este trabalho desenvolve um pipeline de dados integrado à previsão de demanda no varejo de comércio eletrônico e avalia se modelos de aprendizado de máquina superam um baseline simples. Utilizou-se o Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist, organizado em camadas bronze, silver e gold no PostgreSQL, com a demanda definida como o número de itens vendidos em pedidos entregues, por categoria e mês. Regressão Linear, Random Forest e Gradient Boosting foram comparados ao Naive (demanda do mês anterior) por MAE, RMSE e WAPE, em dois cenários: sem e com agrupamento Pareto das categorias. No teste principal (junho a agosto de 2018), o Naive obteve o menor erro, com WAPE de 16,11% sem Pareto e 12,92% com Pareto, contra 22,61% a 25,94% e 19,55% a 20,11% dos demais modelos. Análises complementares (sensibilidade ao conjunto de variáveis, validação walk-forward com janela expansível e melhorias de modelagem) mantiveram o resultado: o Naive teve WAPE igual ou menor em todos os cenários e janelas avaliados, com empate prático em um único recorte. O comportamento é compatível com mudança de regime da demanda, histórico curto e baixa previsibilidade da variação mensal, hipóteses que não foram testadas formalmente. Conclui-se que, neste conjunto de dados, a maior complexidade dos algoritmos não trouxe ganho de precisão e que baselines devem ser referência obrigatória na seleção de modelos p…

title: Integrating local ecological knowledge from professional fishers with environmental observations can improve the understanding, forecasting, and management of climate-sensitive jellyfish hazards
abstract: Abstract Climate variability is increasing the frequency and impacts of marine hazards, yet early warning systems often lack mechanisms to translate environmental signals into timely governance responses. Here, we examine how local ecological knowledge can be operationalized within a national hazard monitoring framework using jellyfish blooms as a model marine hazard. We analyzed 15 years (2010–2024) of weekly, fisher-reported observations from Korean coastal waters, focusing on Aurelia coerulea and Nemopilema nomurai. From these weekly reports, we calculated occurrence rate, defined as the percentage of respondents reporting jellyfish presence, and aggregation frequency, defined as the percentage reporting jellyfish aggregations. These indices were interpreted as operational risk indicators rather than standardized abundance estimates. Their utility was evaluated by testing temporal alignment with official national jellyfish alerts and by quantifying species-specific lead–lag structures. Distinct bloom dynamics emerged: A. coerulea formed persistent aggregations peaking from late spring to summer, whereas N. nomurai exhibited low background occurrence punctuated by abrupt mass events in late summer to autumn. Monthly sea surface temperature (SST) showed positive associations with fisher-reported occurrence and aggregation frequencies for both species (p < 0.05). Generalized Ad…

title: A multi-method explainable AI for analyzing hybrid SARIMAX-GRU temperature forecasting in high-temperature data centers
abstract: Introduction Accurate temperature prediction is essential for improving energy efficiency and ensuring reliable operation in modern data centers. However, despite their high accuracy, deep learning forecasting models often lack interpretability, limiting their deployment in critical environments. This study extends a previously developed hybrid SARIMAX-GRU forecasting model by introducing an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework to analyze and validate its decision-making process under different operating conditions. Methods The proposed framework employs four XAI techniques, including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), Integrated Gradients, and Permutation Importance, to analyze the contribution of temporal residual features in temperature prediction. The analysis considers nine scenarios covering low, moderate, and high temperatures (24 °C, 27 °C, and 30 °C) with workload transitions between 50%, 75%, and 100%. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses are used to evaluate the agreement between explanation methods in terms of importance scores and feature rankings, respectively. Results The results show that the hybrid SARIMAX-GRU model mainly depends on recent residual features, particularly Residual_t1 to Residual_t4, while older residuals have limited influence. The dominant features vary according to…

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Driven Predictive Framework for Residential Energy Demand Forecasting in Smart Urban Environments
Forecasting residential water demand in Kuwait to 2050 and 2100 using the cellular automata Markov chain model
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate forecasting of residential water demand is essential for sustainable infrastructure planning in arid regions facing water scarcity. Kuwait, among the world's most water-stressed nations, depends almost entirely on desalinated water for domestic supply, yet spatially explicit, long-horizon demand forecasts remain scarce. This study applies the cellular automata Markov chain model (CA-MCM) to forecast residential water demand across Kuwait for 2050 and 2100. Three population density raster maps at 90-metre resolution (1975, 2000, 2025) were reclassified into five ordinal classes and used as inputs for CA-MCM transition analysis in TerrSet v20 (LiberaGIS). Model accuracy was validated by comparing the predicted 2025 class map to actual data, yielding an area under the curve of 0.980 via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and a Kstandard of 0.978 and Klocation of 0.989 through the multi-resolution VALIDATE procedure. Residential water demand was then computed at the pixel level using a per-capita consumption rate of 500 litres per person per day. Results show marked spatial intensification and expansion of high-demand zones, with total forecasted demand reaching approximately 3.25 million m3/day by 2050 and 4.53 million m3/day by 2100. These findings offer spatially explicit guidance for long-term water security investment planning in Kuwait.

abstract: В статье оценено влияние въездного туризма на национальную экономику на основе показателей вспомогательного счета туризма и разработан вероятностный прогноз на период до 2030 года. Обоснована необходимость разграничения валовой добавленной стоимости туристских отраслей и прямой туристской валовой добавленной стоимости: в 2024 году их соотношение составило 3,8. Предложена формула оценки эффекта увеличения продолжительности пребывания, согласно которой ее увеличение на одну ночь повышает потребление въездного туризма на 3,19 трлн сумов (9,4 %). Поскольку годовой республиканский ряд короток и имеет структурные разрывы, применена динамическая панельная гравитационная модель на основе 2 134 наблюдений по 194 странам. Вне выборки модель с ошибкой 1,0 % оказалась точнее моделей ARIMA (33,6 %) и случайного блуждания с дрейфом (5,4 %). Согласно прогнозу, в 2030 году число въездных туристов достигнет 18,9 млн человек, а вероятность достижения цели «20 млн туристов» составляет 47,6 %.

title: Cross-City Transfer Learning for Daily Rainfall Forecasting at Pune, India
abstract: Data-driven rainfall models normally need long local records, which many stations lack. This study asks whether a transformer pre-trained on data-rich coastal Mumbai can cut both the local data and the computation needed to forecast daily rainfall at Pune, a rain-shadow city 120 km inland. RainFormer, a transformer encoder-decoder, first trained on Pune’s full record, gave a reference test RMSE of 12.522 mm. It was then pre-trained on Mumbai, and only its last decoder block and output head, 52,481 of its 194,177 parameters, were fine-tuned on 10 to 100% of Pune’s record, against models trained from scratch on identical data. Transfer beat the scratch model at every share. With 10% of the local record its RMSE was within 0.43% of the reference, it equalled the reference at 50% and bettered it at 60% (12.441 mm), so full-data accuracy was reached with 40% less local data while training 73% fewer parameters. Beyond that point the advantage narrowed and the transfer RMSE rose slightly, to 12.479 mm at 100%, indicating over-fitting of the fine-tuned layers to Pune’s historical regime. Cross-city transfer can therefore replace much of a station’s record at a fraction of the training cost.

Equilibrium-Consistent Reservoir Prediction and Risk-Adaptive Model Predictive Control for Nonlinear Wing-Flutter Suppression
abstract: We investigate equilibrium-consistent reservoir-computing (RC) prediction and adaptively weighted model predictive control (MPC) for a nonlinear pitch–plunge flutter benchmark at Qf=8. A conditional residual-mean network compensates for RC prediction errors, and a post-training correction enforces the known zero equilibrium. The optimizer uses deterministic corrected-mean prediction; K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) residual-error covariance adjusts state and terminal penalties, without stochastic scenario propagation. Against separately tuned fixed weights, KNN-based weighting reduced normalized integral squared error (ISE) by 1.66% in a reference Gaussian-disturbance setting with five paired realizations. Four systematic noise conditions included independent and synthetic AR(1) disturbances. An additional exploratory comparison on two new paired Gaussian noise realizations used a fully KNN-independent state-feedback weight scheduler. This simpler scheduler lowered mean normalized ISE (0.151199 versus 0.155306 for KNN) but required more input effort (1.579680 versus 1.231068) and showed slightly larger late-stage normalized root mean square error (0.008832 versus 0.008410). Thus, the comparison exposes a regulation–effort trade-off but does not establish an incremental advantage specifically attributable to KNN covariance information. The KNN trace remains an empirical weighting signa…

title: Rapid prediction of peripheral axonal activation under multipolar stimulation using artificial intelligence methods
abstract: Abstract Objective: Computational models of nerve-stimulating electrodes enable the study of far more stimulation parameter sets than are feasible in situ, but analyzing nerve responses to thousands of stimulation sets requires rapid calculation of axonal responses to external voltage fields. Current methods involve a tradeoff between accuracy and computational efficiency: existing rapid predictors rely on activating-function thresholds across nodes of Ranvier, which cannot fully address nonlinear axonal dynamics such as anodal block or anodic break. Additionally, present rapid estimators do not accurately predict axonal responses to multipolar stimulation in which many voltage fields are applied to the same axon simultaneously. We aimed to develop a rapid predictor that captures these nonlinear behaviors and axonal responses to complex multipolar fields. Approach: We trained an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict axonal activation in peripheral nerve axons in response to multipolar stimuli from dense voltage sources around each nerve, as predicted by the MRG double-cable model. Main results: The implemented ANN achieves 98.59% ± 0.04% (95% C.I.) accuracy in axonal activation prediction over pulse widths from 10 to 200 μs, myelinated axon diameters from 5 to 20 μm, and stimulation amplitudes between −3 mA and 3 mA per contact in multipolar stimulation configurations. Density functional prediction of 2D spintronic materials: magnetic doping of semiconducting 1 T-GeO 2 monolayer
abstract: Abstract The search of new two-dimensional materials, for practical usage in the emergent field of spintronics, is a very active topic due to the exceptional properties of these systems compared to their corresponding bulk phases. In the present study, we use DFT calculations to investigate the electronic structure and magnetic ordering of 1 T-GeO 2 monolayer, doped with transition metal (TM) elements: V, Cr, and Mn; at 25% doping concentration. The undoped monolayer is predicted to be an ultrawide band gap semiconductor (with 5.34 eV indirect band gap). When the ferromagnetic ordering is considered, the V-doped system is found to be a half-metal; while the Cr- and Mn-doped ones exhibit a semiconducting character. The mechanism responsible for these predicted features is also examined. This suggests that TM-doped 1 T-GeO 2 could be advantageous for spintronic applications.

title: Beyond Disease Susceptibility: Genetics, Prediction, and the Limits of Inferring Human Potential
abstract: This narrative review examines the expansion of human genetics beyond disease susceptibility to variation in human function, development, and phenotypic outcomes. In this regard, we define human potential as genetically influenced variation in what individuals may develop or achieve under different biological and environmental conditions. Its genetic architecture is highly polygenic and shaped by pleiotropy, genetic background, developmental and regulatory context, gene–environment interplay, and genetic influences on response and adaptation. Similar observed phenotypes can arise through different genetic routes, while individuals with similar baseline function may differ in their responses to environmental conditions or interventions. Genetic prediction of these traits remains incomplete and strongly dependent on population and context. Polygenic scores developed in European-ancestry populations may show systematically different score distributions in populations underrepresented in genomic discovery datasets. Between-population differences in polygenic-score means cannot be interpreted as differences in intrinsic human capacity. Such differences can produce scientifically invalid comparisons and discriminatory use of genetic prediction. Genetic information concerning human potential should be used conscientiously, particularly in education, employment, insurance, reproduction…

title: Prediction of Molecular Physicochemical Properties Using Molecular Structure and Characteristics
abstract: The prediction of molecular physicochemical properties—such as solubility, hydration free energy, and lipophilicity—plays a crucial role in multiple fields, including drug discovery and materials science. Current prediction methods predominantly fall into two categories: machine learning methods based on molecular descriptors and deep learning methods that learn representations directly from molecular structures. However, when evaluated under rigorous scaffold splitting, these methods often exhibit limited generalization capability, resulting in unsatisfactory prediction accuracy. In this study, a method named PMPP is proposed to predict the physicochemical properties of molecules, which effectively utilizes enhanced graph representations that capture molecular motif structures and optimized selection of pharmacophore and physicochemical characteristics. The framework of PMPP contains three parts: molecular structure representation extraction, molecular characteristics extraction and optimized selection, and molecular physicochemical property prediction model construction. Experimental results demonstrate that PMPP achieves superior predictive accuracy, with lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) scores on three benchmark datasets: 0.787 (ESOL), 1.875 (FreeSolv), and 0.615 (Lipophilicity). These results outperform six state-of-the-art methods, including GROVER, MGSSL, MolCLR, KANO…

title: Multiscale homogenization-based finite-element modeling of fused filament fabrication (FFF)-printed polylactic acid (PLA) components for mechanical performance prediction
abstract: This study investigates the mechanical behavior of polylactic acid (PLA) components manufactured by fused filament fabrication (FFF) through a combined experimental and homogenization-based numerical approach. The effects of raster orientation (0°, 45°, and 90°) and strain rate (10 −4 –10 −2 s −1 ) on tensile properties were evaluated. Representative volume elements (RVEs) were used to determine the effective orthotropic elastic properties of the printed material, which were subsequently implemented in macroscale finite-element simulations. Experimental validation was performed using ISO 527-2 Type 1BA tensile specimens. The results showed that raster orientation and strain rate significantly influence the mechanical response of FFF-printed PLA. The 90° raster configuration exhibited the highest stiffness and strength, whereas the 0° configuration showed lower performance due to its greater dependence on interlayer bonding. The numerical model successfully reproduced the overall mechanical trends and anisotropic behavior of the printed structures, although discrepancies remained for Young's modulus and ultimate elongation because of the assumptions of perfect interlayer bonding and the absence of viscoelastic and damage mechanisms. The proposed framework provides an efficient tool for predicting the mechanical behavior of FFF-manufactured components while reducing experimental …

High-Precision Lumped-Parameter Thermal Modeling and CNN-LSTM-Based Temperature Prediction for Optical Interconnect Modules
abstract: The increasing power consumption and intensified thermal coupling in next-generation high-speed optical interconnect modules present severe thermal management challenges. To address these issues, we propose a high-precision lumped-parameter thermal modeling method for optical interconnect modules. Building upon the constructed lumped-parameter thermal model (LPTM), a real-time transient temperature prediction framework utilizing a hybrid convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture is developed. The LPTM achieves high-precision modeling while reducing computational complexity. Compared with the simulation results from COMSOL Multiphysics 6.3, the proposed LPTM model exhibits an average mean absolute error (MAE) of only 0.52 °C and an average root mean square error (RMSE) of only 0.69 °C for the transient temperatures of key components. Furthermore, the CNN-LSTM neural network, trained on the dataset generated by the LPTM, achieves an MAE of 0.34 °C and an RMSE of 0.78 °C on an independent transient temperature testset generated by COMSOL Multiphysics. The proposed methodology successfully achieves both high-precision modeling and real-time, accurate transient temperature prediction, providing a solid theoretical foundation for thermal management in next-generation optical interconnect systems.

title: Coupled Effects of Burial Depth and Surface Double Cracks on the Uplift Bearing Capacity of Strip Anchor Plates in Red Clay
abstract: Prolonged drought can induce shrinkage cracking in near-surface clay foundations, leaving persistent defects that may affect the uplift safety of underground structures before subsequent rainfall events. This study investigates how burial depth regulates the influence of two pre-existing surface cracks on the uplift bearing capacity and failure mechanism of a horizontal strip anchor plate in red clay. A two-dimensional plane-strain model was established in Optum G2 and validated against laboratory pull-out tests under crack-free conditions. Two burial-depth ratios, H/B = 3 and 8, were examined, and 360 cases were generated by varying normalized crack depth (h/B = 0.25–3), spacing (s/B = 0.25–3), and horizontal offset (d/B = 0–6). Under shallow burial, cracks readily intersect the potential sliding zone and the maximum capacity reduction reaches 81.6%, with pronounced transitions around s/B = 1 and d/B = 1. Under deep burial, the principal failure surface remains predominantly a deep elliptical arc and capacity reduction is generally below 15%. Burial depth therefore controls the spatial overlap between the environmentally damaged zone and the anchor-bearing zone. The results provide a mechanical basis for post-drought crack inspection, uplift-safety reassessment, and burial-depth selection. Hydraulic infiltration, suction, moisture evolution, and rainfall intensity are outside …

title: Soil pH primarily explains variation in clubroot disease potential, while exchangeable potassium and cation exchange capacity may also be involved
Building capacity for engagement: A scoping review of informal and formal research training for Indigenous youth
abstract: Abstract Community‐based research approaches, including community‐based participatory action research (CBPAR), are a research design that engages communities as active collaborators by offering training and support throughout the research process. These approaches, including CBPAR, have gained traction in work with Indigenous youth, as they build research capacity and foster equitable partnerships between community members and researchers. As an underrepresented population in CBPAR, Indigenous youth offer critical perspectives that can deepen understanding of community needs and inform culturally responsive approaches. To explore the uptake in community‐based research approaches and youth inclusion, this scoping review analyzed 37 research articles detailing 33 research training programs for Indigenous youth engaged in research in Canada, the United States, Aotearoa (New Zealand), and Australia. Training programs ranged from providing a brief overview of the research process (42%) to teaching youth specific research skills (27%). Youth involvement also varied across training programs, from being included as study participants (15%) to extensive youth co‐researcher partnerships (48%). Key themes were extracted from the articles to highlight the limitations and strengths of the research training programs. The programs demonstrated variability in delivery and youth involvement, wi…

title: Three-Dimensional Coupling Assessment of Eco-Geological Environment in Alpine Gorge Areas Integrating the Remote Sensing Ecological Index, Ecosystem Services, and Geological Environment Carrying Capacity
abstract: Alpine gorge areas are typical regions where ecological fragility and geological hazard risk overlap strongly. Existing eco-geological assessments remain largely single- or dual-dimensional: remotely sensed indices describe surface status, ecosystem-service indices describe functional supply, and geological models are usually applied separately from ecological assessment, so each approach misses the information carried by the others. To close this gap, this study proposes a three-dimensional coupling framework for Eco-Geological Environment Carrying Capacity (EGECC) that integrates the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI), the Ecosystem Services Index (ESI) and the Geological Environmental Carrying Capacity (GECC), and applies it in Lixian County, Sichuan Province. The three indices were coupled at pixel level, and their coupling and vertical differentiation were analysed along an altitudinal gradient. Three findings are highlighted. (1) RSEI and ESI are only moderately correlated, and their altitudinal peaks are separated, so neither can substitute for the other. (2) GECC contributes the largest share of the variation in EGECC, indicating that the geological dimension carries information that is not a linear combination of the two ecological dimensions. (3) Consequently, the geological dimension cannot be reproduced from the ecological ones: degrading the framework to RSEI +…

title: AI-Enabled Teaching Capability and Sustainable Education Practice among Teachers in Mountainous China: The Roles of OER-Enabled Pedagogical Capacity and Institutional Digital Support
abstract: This study examines how teachers' artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled teaching capability and open educational resources (OER)-enabled pedagogical capacity are associated with sustainable education practice in mountainous areas of China. It also assesses the indirect role of OER-enabled pedagogical capacity and the moderating role of institutional digital support.The study describes a cross-sectional quantitative survey of 462 teachers from 54 schools in 18 mountainous counties across Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Gansu, and Qinghai, using a 24-item questionnaire and partial least squares structural equation modelling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The analyzed results report positive associations between AI-enabled teaching capability and sustainable education practice (? = .331, p < .001), between AI capability and OER-enabled pedagogical capacity (? = .550, p < .001), and between OER capacity and sustainable practice (? = .390, p < .001). The indirect association is .215 and the interaction with institutional digital support is .134. The R² for sustainable practice is .475. The prediction claim is limited to predictive relevance within the cross-validation procedure, not demonstrated performance in new schools across different locations.This study integrates AI literacy, OER-enabled pedagogy, education for sustainable development, and socio-technical support in a teacher-centr…

title: Dietary Multivitamin Supplementation in Siganus fuscescens: Integrated Effects on Growth Performance, Antioxidant Capacity, and Mitigation of Darkening Syndrome Under High-Lipid Dietary Stress
abstract: Siganus fuscescens, an economically important species in southern China, is noted for its rapid growth and high nutritional value. Nonetheless, the prevalence of darkening syndrome, a condition marked by skin discoloration and significant mortality rates, presents a challenge to aquaculture practices, with its etiology remaining largely unexplored. This study aimed to examine the impacts of varying dietary lipid levels and multivitamin supplementation on the incidence of darkening syndrome in S. fuscescens. Five experimental diets were developed: a low-fat diet containing 10% lipids; a moderate-fat diet with 13% lipids; a moderate-fat diet with 13% lipids supplemented with multivitamins; a high-fat diet containing 16% lipids; and a high-fat diet with 16% lipids supplemented with multivitamins. A 55-day feeding trial was conducted on S. fuscescens specimens. The results indicate that, in this experiment, increasing dietary fat content led to a higher cumulative incidence of darkening syndrome in S. fuscescens. Serological and histological findings suggested that in the 16% lipid diet group, S. fuscescens exhibited liver injury and oxidative stress. Notably, supplementation with multivitamins alleviated these adverse effects. Overall, we recommend using an appropriate dietary fat level and further supplementing with antioxidant multivitamins, which may represent an effective stra…

title: Transmission mechanism and identification of power pulsation signals in sucker rod pumping wells
abstract: Abstract Traditional wellbore communication technologies for sucker-rod pumping wells suffer from severe signal attenuation and poor stability under deep-well and complex operating conditions. This study investigates the transmission mechanism and signal identification of power pulsation wireless communication. A three-dimensional full-scale fluid–structure coupling dynamic model incorporating the sucker rod, centering device, wellbore fluid, and tubing is established to characterize stress wave propagation from the downhole pump to the wellhead. The model reveals that the transmission channel exhibits typical high-impedance, low-pass characteristics, with fluid viscous damping, rod–tubing friction, and material damping governing signal attenuation, while low-frequency stress waves retain superior long-distance transmission capability. The model is validated using field-measured loading data, achieving prediction errors below 10% across the full operating condition range. Based on the validated model, a joint time- and frequency-domain identification algorithm is developed by combining characteristic spectral peak recognition with time-domain waveform verification, enabling detection of power pulsation signals under strong noise. The proposed model and identification method provide theoretical and technical support for wireless wellbore communication, downhole condition monitor…

title: Sovereign Risk Mitigation Mechanism in Emerging Markets
Tunable viscoelastic hydrogels for vascularization: mechanism, design and applications
abstract: Abstract Vascularization is crucial for fabricating large-scale functional artificial tissues and organs, and hydrogels are the most commonly used biomaterials for constructing microenvironments conducive to blood vessel formation. However, traditional static hydrogels lack the dynamic regulation of cell behavior similar to natural extracellular matrix (ECM) because they cannot replicate the viscoelasticity of ECM. Viscoelasticity is a key dynamic biomechanical signal for regulating the cell fate and is crucial for modulating vascular cell behavior. In recent years, tunable viscoelastic hydrogels (TVHs) based on reversible crosslinking have become highly promising biomaterials due to their capacity to mimic the viscoelasticity of ECM. Although some vascularization studies using TVHs have been conducted, and significant progress has been made, this emerging field lacks a systematic summary. Therefore, this review summarizes the recent advances of TVHs in vascularization, including the three major strategies for precisely controlling hydrogel viscoelasticity, the influence of hydrogel viscoelasticity on vascular cell fate, and the application of hydrogel viscoelasticity in regulating blood vessel formation. The prospects and challenges of TVHs are also discussed. This review aims to provide design principles for engineering TVHs capable of precisely controlling viscoelasticity an…

title: Digital Training Demand and Labor Market Alignment in Adult Continuing Education: Evidence from Slovakia
abstract: Rapid digitalization is reshaping occupational skill requirements and increasing the importance of flexible adult continuing education. This study examines expressed demand for digital and labor-market-oriented online training in Slovakia, identifies the skill domains represented in program choices, and compares the characteristics of packages selected by employed and unemployed participants. The analysis used 1,717 de-identified participant-program records from the Skills for the Labor Market project, collected between April 2024 and November 2025. Training packages were classified by thematic area and described using analytically constructed indicators of digital intensity, practical orientation, occupational market relevance, and labor-market alignment. Frequency distributions, descriptive statistics, Spearman rank correlations, and Mann-Whitney U tests with effect-size estimates were applied. Demand was concentrated in information technology, software development, data analytics, digital marketing, and related applied fields. Selected packages generally combined high digital intensity, practical orientation, and occupational relevance. Employed and unemployed participants showed broadly similar choice profiles. After Bonferroni adjustment, employed participants showed higher ranks for digital intensity and occupational market relevance. No statistically significant differen…

title: Nanomaterials in the Hydrogen Economy: A Narrative Review of Production, Storage, Carbon Capture and Commercialisation
abstract: Hydrogen is widely regarded as a key component of future low-carbon energy systems, and nanomaterials are central to improving the efficiency and performance of the technologies that will deliver it. Existing reviews typically treat hydrogen production, storage and carbon capture separately; this narrative review compares nanomaterials across these selected domains using qualitative evidence categories and, where the data permit, indicative cost benchmarks. Of the 22 classes assessed, 19 are classified on the maturity axis. Of those, 14 show laboratory evidence only, three reach prototype or pilot evidence and two reach field or commercial evidence in the reviewed application. The remaining three have industrial precedent only in other applications and are not classified on this axis. Across six unmatched storage examples, reported capacities vary substantially, but the data do not support an application-specific maturity relationship. Cost data for nanomaterial-based hydrogen storage are particularly scarce compared with production and carbon capture, where indicative but inconsistently reported benchmarks exist. Commercialisation pathways, hydrogen carrier technologies and environmental, health, safety and life-cycle considerations are also examined alongside the potential contribution to industrial decarbonisation. Key research priorities are identified, including a five-poi…

title: First-Principles Study of ScM2 (M = C and N) Monolayers as High-Performance Anode Materials for Potassium-Ion Storage
abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for sustainable energy storage technologies has driven the exploration of alternatives to lithium-ion batteries, with potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) emerging as promising candidates owing to the natural abundance and favorable electrochemical properties of potassium. Two-dimensional (2D) scandium carbide (ScC2) and scandium nitride (ScN2) monolayers were systematically investigated as potential anode materials for PIBs through first-principles density functional theory calculations performed using the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The absence of imaginary phonon modes and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations confirm the dynamical and thermal stability of both monolayers, while electron localization function analysis reveals mixed ionic-metallic bonding in ScC2 and ionic-dominant charge transfer in ScN2, with both satisfying the Born mechanical stability criteria. Electronic band structure calculations using GGA-PBE and hybrid HSE06 functionals confirm an intrinsic metallic character in both materials, ensuring efficient electron transport during charge/discharge cycling. The most favorable K adsorption occurs at the Sc top site with adsorption energies of −0.86 eV and −1.32 eV for ScC2 and ScN2, respectively, with Bader charge analysis confirming a K+-like ionic character through charge transfers of 0.85e and 0.86e. The K-ion dif…

title: A Transient Boundary Element Framework for Pressure Buildup, Injectivity Enhancement, and Reactive Permeability Evolution During CO₂ Storage in Heterogeneous Carbonate Reservoirs
abstract: Background Reactive CO₂ injection couples multiphase flow, aqueous chemistry, mineral alteration and permeability changes. Methods This paper develops a transient subdomain boundary element formulation for a reduced single-fluid pressure-diffusion model with phenomenological pressure-activated permeability feedback, and specifies a physically based two-phase compositional reactive-transport extension and a finite-radius well coupling that remain to be implemented. Results Previously reported scenario outputs and tables are preserved as illustrative legacy calculations. They do not provide matched experimental calibration, reproducible convergence or mass-balance evidence, or uniquely defined physical well injectivity. Conclusions The original model illustrates pressure–property feedback but cannot support field-scale reactive CO₂ storage or injectivity forecasting without further coupled physics and numerical validation.

title: Productive, profitable and energy-efficient Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based vegetable intercropping system under Northern Telangana zone
abstract: Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based intercropping systems offer considerable scope for improving productivity, profitability and resource-use efficiency (RUE) under sustainable agricultural production systems. An experiment was conducted in rabi season 2022 at the Agricultural Research Station, Adilabad, Telangana to test the efficiency of intercropping different vegetables in mustard with different row ratios. A total of 13 treatments comprising sole crops such as mustard, sole root vegetables (radish, beetroot, carrot and potato) and their combination under 2 : 2 and 3 : 3 row ratios were considered in the randomised block design (RBD) of the experiment. It was found that the highest total economic yield (24212 kg ha-1), mustard equivalent yield (5775 kg ha-1), gross returns (₹338968 ha-1), net returns (₹264526 ha-1) and benefit-cost ratio (B : C) ratio (4.55) were obtained from the monocropping of radish. While among intercropping combinations, mustard with radish under 3 : 3 row ratio yielded the highest total economic yield (13515 kg ha-1), mustard equivalent yield (3964 kg ha-1), mustard oil yield (351 kg ha-1), gross returns (₹216033 ha-1), net returns (₹160966) and B : C ratio (3.92). These results were statistically comparable with mustard with radish at ratio 2 : 2. An energetic efficiency analysis concluded that the performance of the mustard with radish (3 : 3 and 2 :…

title: Do CEO Characteristics Constrain Firm Growth? Evidence from the U.S. Energy Industry
abstract: Objectives Drawing on Upper Echelons Theory (UET), this study examines the relationship between CEO characteristics and firm growth among publicly listed U.S. energy firms. Specifically, it investigates the effects of CEO tenure, CEO compensation, financial expertise, financial education, technical education, and CEO age on firm growth, thereby extending the application of UET to firm growth in the context of the U.S. oil and gas sector. Material and Methods The study employs panel data from 26 publicly listed U.S. oil and gas companies over the period 2011–2024. Firm growth is proxied by firm size, while the explanatory variables capture selected CEO demographic, educational, experiential, and compensation characteristics. Panel-data econometric techniques are employed to examine the relationship between CEO characteristics and firm growth. Results The empirical findings indicate that CEO tenure has a negative and statistically significant effect on firm growth, suggesting that longer CEO tenure may be associated with reduced flexibility in responding to strategic change. CEO compensation is positively and significantly associated with firm growth, indicating that compensation incentives may encourage expansion-oriented managerial decisions. A Survey of Vehicle-Enabled Control of Traffic for Freeway Flow in Partially Connected Environments
abstract: Abstract Efficient freeway traffic control can alleviate congestion, improve operational efficiency, and enhance traffic safety. With the rapid development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and connectivity technologies, Connected Vehicles (CVs), including Connected Automated Vehicles (CAVs) and Connected Human-Driven Vehicles (C-HDVs), are expected to coexist with conventional Human-Driven Vehicles (HDVs) on freeways for a considerable period. In partially connected traffic environments, CVs can provide historical and real-time Vehicle Trajectory Data (VTD) as mobile sensing sources and can also influence surrounding traffic as mobile actuators through vehicle guidance and cooperative control, thereby enabling Vehicle-Enabled Control of Traffic (VECT) for freeway flow. This paper systematically reviews recent advances in VECT under partially connected environments. The literature is organized into four categories according to the functional role of CVs and the level at which information, decisions, or control actions are generated: (1) vehicle-trajectory-enabled traffic state analysis, (2) vehicle-trajectory-enabled traffic control, (3) vehicle-guidance-enabled traffic control, and (4) collaborative vehicle–flow control. The review covers traffic state estimation, traffic state prediction, traffic anomaly detection, Variable Speed Limit (VSL) control, Ramp Metering (…

الضوابط التي تحكم عملية تفتيش السيارات في القانون العراقي والقانون الكويتي

Analog‐Tunable Nonvolatile Memristors with Self‐Compliance Behavior via a MoS x ‐Interlayer Strategy for Neuromorphic Recognition and Zero‐Trust Image Encryption
abstract: ABSTRACT The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfO x memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self‐protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfO x /MoS x /HfO x trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self‐compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero‐trust XOR‐based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near‐optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoS x interlayer modification strategy to optimize hi…

title: Sustainability as a Mediating Construct: Connection, Evaluative Openness, and the Risk of Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Similar sustainability commitments can become organizationally consequential in markedly different ways, yet the relational architecture producing this variation remains under‐theorized. This conceptual paper theorizes sustainability as a mediating construct through representational, projective, and organizing forms. Recursive translation explains how changes within one form feed back into the others, generating varying degrees of connection. Because connection does not determine which sustainability claims retain capacity to challenge and revise mediation, the framework introduces evaluative openness as a second, analytically independent dimension. Their intersection yields four configurations: symbolic, exploratory, embedded, and captured sustainability. The embedded–captured distinction reveals the central implication: strongly connected mediation can sustain coordinated action while the range of values, actors, evidence, and possible futures capable of redirecting that mediation progressively narrows. By separating connection from evaluative openness, the framework extends research on decoupling, hybrid organizing, and performativity and explains why organizational incorporation alone does not establish transformative capacity.

title: Biopolymer-Based Biopriming Strategy with Trichoderma virens to Enhance Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) Establishment
abstract: Biopriming cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) seeds with beneficial fungi and biopolymer matrices offer a sustainable strategy to enhance crop establishment in smallholder agriculture. This study evaluated four biopolymers—sodium alginate (SA), guar gum (GG), arabic gum (AG), and maltodextrin (MAL)—as film-coating delivery systems for Trichoderma virens. We assessed biopolymer-bioagent compatibility, optimal imbibition kinetics, conidium loading efficiency via scanning electron microscopy (SEM), early seedling growth promotion, and inoculant survival over 30 days of cold storage. Results indicated that while all matrices preserved seed viability, their efficacy varied significantly. SA demonstrated the highest initial conidia entrapment capacity and provided superior protection of the conidia throughout storage, maintaining peak fungal viability and 100% seed germination. Conversely, AG exhibited a stimulatory effect on seedling development, resulting in the highest total plant and radicle elongation compared to unformulated T. virens and the untreated control. Microstructural analysis confirmed that matrix architecture directly dictates conidia binding and distribution. In conclusion, biopolymer-based seed coatings significantly modulate the biopriming efficacy of T. virens. Selecting an optimal carrier requires balancing physical loading efficiency and shelf-life viability with plant…

Distributed Fresnel Lens–Fiber System for Solar Light Collection and Transmission: Comparable Output Power with Reduced Thermal Loading
abstract: Concentrated solar radiation can be transported through optical fibers to remote locations; however, the high thermal load at the concentrator–fiber interface can limit the operation of systems using polymer optical fibers. This work investigates whether distributing a fixed solar collection area among multiple Fresnel lens–fiber channels can mitigate localized heating while maintaining comparable transmitted optical power. Two PMMA Fresnel lens–fiber configurations with the same nominal solar collection area were numerically and experimentally evaluated: a single-channel system and a four-channel system. Non-sequential ray-tracing simulations were used to analyze the optical performance and determine the lens–fiber coupling distances, while outdoor experiments and thermographic measurements were conducted to evaluate the thermal response. The numerical model predicted total output powers of 29.24 W and 31.39 W for the single- and four-channel configurations, respectively. Experimentally, visible melting occurred at the single-fiber entrance after approximately 40 s, whereas the four-channel system operated for more than 5 min without visible fiber deformation. These results indicate that distributing the solar collection area among multiple lens–fiber channels can reduce localized thermal loading while maintaining comparable total transmitted optical power.

title: An Analytical Transient Model for Three-Phase Transformer Reclosing Considering Hysteresis Residual Magnetism and Recovery Control of Cascading Failures in Cyber-Physical Power Systems
abstract: In cyber-physical power systems (CPPS), the inrush current generated during transformer reclosing can easily cause misjudgment of protection devices and thus serves as an important trigger for cascading failure propagation. Existing studies mostly rely on black-box electromagnetic transient simulations or simplified magnetization models, lacking analytical approaches that account for hysteresis and residual magnetism, and therefore fail to accurately characterize the coupling mechanism between physical transients and information-layer dynamics. To address this issue, an analytical transient model for three-phase transformer reclosing is established based on the Jiles–Atherton theory, in which the hysteresis loop and residual magnetism are embedded into the electromagnetic transient process as a differential–algebraic equation (DAE) set, and the semi-analytical dependence of the inrush peak, harmonic characteristics, and decay law on the residual flux and closing angle is derived. On this basis, an inrush-feature-driven probability model of protection misjudgment is constructed, a CPPS cascading failure propagation model incorporating physical–information state transitions is developed, and an adaptive reclosing recovery control strategy based on the node fault-state reachability is proposed. Simulations on the IEEE 39-bus system show that the proposed model accurately reproduce…

Subjective Age Discrepancy Associates With Sleep Quality in a Large Longitudinal Sample of Middle‐Aged and Older Adults
abstract: ABSTRACT While age is typically measured in chronological terms, subjective age has also been shown to be clinically relevant. Given the clinical importance of subjective age discrepancy (the distinction between chronological and subjective age), we aimed to examine whether it was associated with another important aspect of health, sleep quality, among middle‐aged and older British adults. Data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing was analysed. We used a longitudinal approach involving a primary test sample ( N = 11,050) and an independent replication sample ( N = 1800). Subjective sleep quality, sleep duration and frequency of difficulties falling asleep, staying asleep or experiencing unrefreshing sleep were self‐reported and subjective age discrepancy was derived from items regarding chronological age and subjective age. Regression analysis was conducted cross‐sectionally within a wave of data collection and longitudinally between two data waves separated by 4 years. Better sleep quality ( β = −0.11) and longer sleep duration ( β = −0.03) were associated cross‐sectionally with ‘younger’ subjective age discrepancy and unrefreshing sleep ( β = −0.12) emerged as the sleep factor most strongly associated with subjective age discrepancy. In the test sample, but not the replication sample, sleep quality had interactions with chronological age, sex and the presence of long…

title: EVOLUTION OF TURKISH GEOPOLITICAL STRATEGY: HISTORICAL AND ECONOMIC INSIGHTS
abstract: This paper reveals the basic stages of the transformation that Turkish geopolitical strategy and foreign policy have undergone in the 20th century by analyzing Türkiye’s position in the international system. The article mainly analyzes the framework of foreign policy built around a realist perspective that was followed during the founding period of the Republic of Türkiye, evaluates the challenges that Türkiye faced when it abandoned the basic philosophy of the founding period, and explains how the Republic’s geopolitical vision can guide the challenges that Türkiye faces in the environment of global fragilities. It argues that the need to redefine the elements of the geopolitical balance between Türkiye and the global powers, as was done one hundred years ago, is the key to Türkiye’s ability to overcome the possible political and economic difficulties in the contemporary era.

title: BRANDING CORPORATIVO, ESTRUTURAÇÃO ORGANIZACIONAL, ESTRATÉGIA DE MARCA E ASSESSORIA: UMA REVISÃO BIBLIOGRÁFICA E PROPOSIÇÃO DE UM MODELO PARA A INTERNACIONALIZAÇÃO DE PEQUENAS E MÉDIAS EMPRESAS NOS MERCADOS INTERNACIONAIS
abstract: Este artigo analisa como o branding corporativo, a estruturação organizacional e a estratégia de marca podem apoiar a internacionalização de pequenas e médias empresas, propondo um modelo de assessoria orientado à construção de reputação, adaptação e competitividade em mercados internacionais. Realiza-se uma revisão bibliográfica integrativa, de natureza analítico-conceitual, com protocolo transparente de busca e seleção de estudos publicados entre 2021 e 2026. Foram consideradas publicações localizáveis em Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Emerald, SciELO e Google Scholar, combinando descritores relacionados a branding corporativo, orientação de marca, estratégia, capacidades de marketing, internacionalização, reputação, processos empresariais, redes e pequenas e médias empresas. A síntese articula branding corporativo, visão baseada em recursos, capacidades dinâmicas, internacionalização e aprendizagem, orientação para o mercado, adaptação versus padronização, estruturação de processos, redes empresariais e governança. Os resultados indicam que a marca pode funcionar como capacidade estratégica quando é traduzida em identidade, posicionamento, promessa, cultura, processos, experiências e evidências reconhecíveis nos mercados-alvo. title: Biopsy-free versus biopsy-confirmed robot-assisted radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of an investigational strategy
abstract: Background Routine prostate biopsy before radical prostatectomy (RP) provides histopathological confirmation and information for risk stratification but is associated with procedure-related morbidity. Advances in multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA PET) have prompted interest in highly selected biopsy-free pathways. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026 for randomized or non-randomized comparative studies of biopsy-free RP (BF-RP) versus biopsy-confirmed RP (BC-RP). Analyses were stratified by study design, and fixed-effect models were used for design-specific subgroup estimates when at least two studies were available. Results Three comparative studies (one randomized trial and two non-randomized cohorts) contributed 532 analyzed participants. In the randomized trial, BF-RP was associated with shorter operative time (MD −15.06 min, 95% CI −22.11 to −8.01) and lower estimated blood loss (MD −29.80 mL, 95% CI −43.77 to −15.83). In the two non-randomized studies, BF-RP was also associated with shorter operative time (MD −9.89 min, 95% CI −12.29 to −7.49; I²=0%) and lower estimated blood loss (MD −20.56 mL, 95% CI −27.03 to −14.08; I²=47%). Non-randomized evidence favoured BF-RP for study-defined continence at 3 months (RR …

title: Sustainable Innovation Management: From Knowledge Creation to Resource Efficiency
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to uncover the internal organizational mechanisms driving sustainable innovation and to develop a unified conceptual framework. To address the theoretical fragmentation in current research, a systematic review of 128 recent empirical articles was conducted, combining conceptual mapping of keyword co‐occurrences with qualitative thematic synthesis. The findings reveal a sequential organizational architecture comprising four interdependent pillars: cognitive foundations, strategic orchestration (driven by dynamic capabilities and strategic agility), technological amplification, and sustainable materialization, all supported by a transversal human and relational substrate. Based on these insights, the study proposes the capability‐based sustainable innovation (CBSI) framework. By integrating the resource‐based view, the knowledge‐based view, and the dynamic capabilities framework, the model explicates the operational sequence required to execute the twin transformation and achieve verifiable circular economy and environmental performance. The framework provides a structured agenda for future research and offers managers a practical blueprint for appropriately aligning human capital with digital investments.

title: Development of Potent METTL1 Inhibitors Using a Nanoscale Direct-To-Biology Strategy
abstract: Abstract The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report the development of a potent series of METTL1 inhibitors by combining conventional structure−activity relationship (SAR) studies with a tandem direct-to-biology (D2B) approach. Lead compound VK238 inhibited METTL1 enzymatic activity at nanomolar concentrations and exhibited selectivity across a panel of methyltransferases and kinases. In a cellular context, pharmacological METTL1 inhibition reduced m7G levels in tRNAs, leading to apoptosis-mediated cell death in several acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines. Mechanistic studies combining biophysical experiments, photoaffinity labeling (PAL), and molecular docking suggested that this inhibitor series occupies the (S)-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding pocket of METTL1. Collectively, these findings highlight METTL1 as a tractable and pharmacologically relevant target for therapeutic intervention in AML.

title: Fairness perceptions in marketing strategy and across the marketing mix: An integrative review and call to action
abstract: Abstract Fairness is a foundational and highly consequential construct in marketing, shaping purchase intentions, brand attitudes, complaints, boycotts, and word‐of‐mouth. Yet extant consumer research has largely concentrated on price fairness, leaving fairness across the rest of marketing strategy and the marketing mix comparatively underexplored. This review makes three contributions. First, we review and integrate the field's three theoretical foundations: dual entitlement, inequity aversion, and moralized cognition. Second, we organize recent findings in the fairness literature around two managerial frameworks: strategy (segmentation, targeting, and positioning) and tactics (promotion, place, and product, in addition to price). Third, we highlight understudied areas and topics across the full range of marketing activities and issue a call to action for future research.

Concealed Groundwater Day Zero: An Uncertainty–Scarcity–Vulnerability Framework for Assessing Groundwater Unsustainability and Hydro-Social Risk in Bangladesh
abstract: Groundwater depletion is a major environmental and socio-economic challenge in Bangladesh. This study evaluates the spatiotemporal dynamics of groundwater depletion and hydro-social vulnerability using 400 Bangladesh Water Development Board monitoring wells for 1990–2019. The conceptual basis is the Reliability–Resiliency–Vulnerability (RRV) framework; operationally, it is adapted into three normalized groundwater-stress components: Uncertainty (U, the frequency of threshold exceedance and therefore a proxy for unreliability), Scarcity (S, persistence or non-recovery after a drought episode), and Vulnerability (V, severity of groundwater-level deficit). These components are combined into a Groundwater Day Zero Index (DZI), while population and irrigation layers are used separately to characterize exposure. Drought episodes are defined when standardized groundwater level falls below −1 standard deviation of the long-term mean. Results indicate widespread depletion, with reported rates of about 0.15–0.21 m yr−1 in stressed northwestern and central regions. Dhaka has a severe DZI (≈0.91; >0.75), while much of the Barind Tract falls within high-to-severe conditions (≈0.72–0.78). National mean component values (U = 0.46, S = 0.52, V = 0.57) indicate predominantly moderate-to-high stress. Financial Aspects in the Field of Activation and Prevention Aimed at the Elderly Based on the Nysa Daily Care Centre and Nysa Senior+ Clubs
abstract: Aim: The article addresses the growing problem of the ageing population, as well as the role of the state in preventing and counteracting the negative effects of this process, by activating a range of measures to improve the condition and well-being of older people. The study was based on an analysis of the Nysa Daily Care Centre (Dzienny Dom Pobytu w Nysie; Nysa DCC) and its activities in 2016−2025 and the newly established Nysa Senior+ Clubs, as an example of the implementation of measures for seniors in the region. The Nysa DCC is also taking initiatives to increase the value of its incomes by conducting additional economic activity. Senior+ Clubs, on the other hand, operate on the basis of funds obtained annually from participation in public tenders, as part of the Senior+ government programme. The aim of the study was to show how public institutions carry out preventive activities in this area, and how they raise and spend funds. Methodology: The research method used was a case study. The author employed basic methods of statistical description. Findings: The institutions in Nysa are operating properly and meeting the needs of seniors. A leading institution is the Nysa DCC which serves an average of more than 200 people per year, while three Nysa Senior+ Clubs cater for 60 people in total.
