title: A Modified Northern Goshawk Optimization Algorithm for Truss Design Problems
abstract: Northern goshawk optimization, one of the metaheuristic algorithms recently proposed for solving optimization problems, is an optimization algorithm inspired by the behavior of the northern goshawk in nature. In this study, a fitness distance balance (FDB) strategy was incorporated into the northern goshawk optimization algorithm to enhance its performance. This strategy strengthens the algorithm’s search capability and improves solution quality. Consequently, the algorithm developed with the fitness distance balance strategy has been named the modified northern goshawk optimization algorithm (MNGO). The performance of the proposed MNGO was analyzed using fifteen different benchmark functions, taking into account population size and the number of dimensions. The experimental results obtained are presented along with convergence plots. Furthermore, the proposed MNGO was compared with some other algorithms in the literature; convergence plots, box plots, and radar charts were used, and statistical analyses were also conducted. As a result of these analyses, it was observed that the performance of the MNGO improved as the number of dimensions increased. In addition, the performance of the proposed MNGO was examined statistically. Furthermore, the proposed MNGO algorithm was applied to challenging and complex 10-bar, 37-bar, 52-bar, 72-bar, and 200-bar truss problems, which are rea…

title: Beyond CRBN and VHL: DCAF16-Recruiting Degraders from Rational Design to Clinical Translation
abstract: Abstract Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has revolutionized modern drug discovery. However, the current clinical landscape remains predominantly reliant on CRBN and VHL, restricting the targetable proteome and increasing the risk of acquired resistance. Expanding the TPD toolbox with therapeutically tractable E3 ligases is imperative. Recently, DCAF16 has emerged as a frontrunner in this effort, underscored by the advancement of DCAF16-based monovalent degraders such as PLX-61639 and AMX-883 toward clinical evaluation. Unlike the historically serendipitous discovery of CRBN-based molecular glues, DCAF16 offers a versatile platform for the rational design of both bifunctional and monovalent degraders. In this timely perspective, we present the first comprehensive medicinal chemistry analysis of the DCAF16-mediated degradation landscape, focusing on delineating the expanding diversity of recruiting motifs and elucidating the design principles, structural basis, and SAR of representative degraders. Finally, we outline current challenges and offer insights into future design strategies and clinical translation of DCAF16-based degraders.

title: On the Kolmogorov constant explicit form in the theory of discrete-time stochastic branching systems – CORRIGENDUM
abstract: Abstract The explicit expression for the Kolmogorov constant given in Theorem 1.2 of [1] has a restricted range of validity: it gives the constant precisely for linear-fractional offspring generating functions, whereas for other subcritical offspring generating functions the constant may be strictly larger or strictly smaller than that expression. Within the class of embeddable offspring generating functions the expression is a sharp lower bound for the constant.

title: OpenGRF: prediction of ground reaction forces and moments during activities of daily living using OpenSim
abstract: Abstract OpenGRF is a new OpenSim-based tool that estimates ground reaction forces and moments (GRF&Ms) and centre of pressure (CoP) directly from joint kinematics, addressing an existing limitation of current OpenSim workflows. The approach combines calibrated foot–ground contact probes with an optimization framework derived from static optimization, and computes CoP by accounting for both kinematic and dynamic contributions. Its performance was validated against force-plate measurements. Validation involved 126 marker-based trials from seven healthy adults, each performing six trials of level walking, stair ascent and stair descent. Results showed the highest accuracy for vertical GRF, with normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) ≤ 1.5% and Pearson's correlation coefficient (ρ) ≥ 0.94, particularly during level walking. Anterior–posterior GRF was also satisfactorily predicted (nRMSE 4.4%–6.1%, ρ = 0.81–0.91). By contrast, medial–lateral GRF was less reliable, especially in stair tasks, with errors up to 11.2% and correlations as low as 0.48. Free moments were the hardest variable to estimate (nRMSE up to 28%), whereas ankle moments showed excellent agreement with force-plate data (nRMSE ≈ 1.7%, ρ ≈ 0.98). Median CoP error was 21–23 mm, with the largest discrepancies during double support. Overall, OpenGRF enables physics-consistent estimation of GRF-related variables, parti…
venue: Journal of the Royal Society Interface

title: Economic Fundamentals and Short-Run Exchange Rate Prediction: A Machine-Learning Perspective
abstract: Abstract The exchange rate predictability puzzle—that fundamentals fail to forecast short-horizon exchange rate movements out of sample—has long resisted resolution. We show that fundamentals do matter, but their effects vary with global financial conditions. Using a rich set of country characteristics interacted with global state variables and machine-learning techniques to handle the high-dimensional data, we document that interactions between country characteristics and foreign exchange market volatility are particularly important, consistent with a “flight to fundamentals” during periods of financial stress. Our forecasts deliver substantial economic value and offer new insight into the carry trade.
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis

title: GECKO-A v1.0: exploring VOC oxidation trajectories through comparison with the master chemical mechanism
abstract: Numerical models are crucial tools for understanding complex chemical systems such as the atmosphere, and their sensitivity across a range of conditions. In atmospheric chemistry models, reaction mechanisms are used to represent chemical transformations and define the underlying system of equations. Building highly explicit mechanisms that capture the full complexity of organic oxidation occurring in the atmosphere remains challenging owing to the large number of intermediates involved, the breadth of reaction pathways, and the limited availability of reliable kinetic and thermodynamic data. The Generator for Explicit Chemistry and Kinetics of Organics in the Atmosphere (GECKO-A) was developed to address these limitations by enabling the systematic construction of near-explicit mechanisms. Here, we present its first open-source release (v1.0), which incorporates updated chemical protocols and structure-activity relationships, together with its companion box model for mechanism integration. GECKO-A's performance is benchmarked through systematic comparisons with the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM v3.3.1), based on simulations of the oxidation of five representative hydrocarbons (butane, octane, dodecane, toluene, and α -pinene) under environmental conditions ranging from urban to remote. The two approaches yield similar oxidation pathways for small and structurally simple compou…

title: Transformation of Human Resource Management in Islamic Education: Problems, Global Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Human resource management in Islamic education has become a strategic issue in improving the quality, competitiveness, and sustainability of educational institutions in the modern era. This article aims to analyze the transformation of human resource management in Islamic education by focusing on major problems, global challenges, and future development prospects. This study employs a qualitative approach using library research methods through the collection of books, scientific journals, academic articles, and relevant documents related to Islamic educational management and human resource development. Data were analyzed using content analysis techniques to identify important themes and concepts associated with the transformation of human resource management in Islamic education. The findings indicate that Islamic educational institutions continue to face several major problems, including limited teacher professionalism, inadequate digital competence, weak organizational leadership, and insufficient welfare systems for educators. Global challenges such as digital transformation, educational competition, technological disruption, and changing student characteristics have intensified the need for strategic reform in educational management. However, Islamic education also possesses strong future prospects through the integration of Islamic values, digital innovation, continuous pr…
venue: AL GHAZALI: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Pemikiran Islam

title: Effects of air pollution on corporate charitable donations: evidence from China
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable giving by combining listing data from the China Stock Market and Accounting Research Database (CSMAR) and data on air pollution in Chinese cities. Using the instrumental variable method and regression discontinuity design, it explores the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable donations and further explores the impact of air pollution on state-owned enterprises and enterprises in high-pollution industries. Design/methodology/approach Using 2013–2019 data from Chinese listed firms and air quality indices, this study examines air pollution as a new influence factor. To address omitted variable bias, regressions include industry/year fixed effects, regional economic controls and corporate governance variables. Endogeneity concerns are mitigated via three tests: an instrumental variable (thermal inversion) for reverse causality, a regression discontinuity test and a Huai River policy placebo test – all yielding robust results. Findings Empirical results show air pollution significantly reduces corporate charitable donations: a 10% pollution increase correlates with an approximately 30% decrease in corporate charitable donations. These findings hold after robustness checks (excluding air quality index (AQI) manipulation, alternative measures and first-tier cities). Effects are heterogeneo…

title: Integrated early childhood development services in market and cross-border communities in Rwanda: a mixed-methods pre–post evaluation
abstract: Background Families working in markets and cross-border trade often have limited access to affordable and safe childcare. This study assessed the implementation, reach, and service quality of integrated early childhood development (ECD) centers established in market and cross-border communities in Rwanda. It also examined differences between baseline and endline samples in complementary feeding, nutritional status, child development, health and hygiene practices, caregiving, and child protection, while exploring stakeholder experiences, implementation constraints, and sustainability. Methods An embedded mixed-methods pre–post evaluation compared independent cross-sectional samples of child–caregiver pairs assessed at baseline ( n = 551) and endline ( n = 421). Survey-round differences were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression. Endline focus group discussions (FGDs), key-informant interviews (KIIs), and structured observations conducted at all eight centers documented service delivery, staffing, infrastructure, learning materials, safety, accessibility, and other implementation conditions. Results The eight centers provided integrated early learning, nutrition, health, hygiene, and child-protection services to 701 children. Endline survey participation was associated with higher adjusted odds of meeting minimum meal frequency (AOR = 2.66; 9…

title: [Retracted Article] อนุศักดิ ศิลาชัย และ สุริยา ประสมทอง. การประยุกต์ใช้วิธีทากูชิสําหรับกระบวนการเชื่อมเสียดทานกวนแบบจุด ระหว่างอะลูมิเนียมผสม Al6061-T6 กับเหล็กกล้าความแข็งแรงสูง โดยการศึกษาค่าพารามิเตอร์ที่ดีที่สุดของเครื่องจักรในการผลิต
abstract: การเพิกถอนบทความ วารสารวิชาการ มทร.สุวรรณภูมิ ขอเพิกถอนบทความ (Retracted Article) บทความเรื่อง การประยุกต์ใช้วิธีทากูชิสําหรับกระบวนการเชื่อมเสียดทานกวนแบบจุด ระหว่างอะลูมิเนียมผสม Al6061-T6 กับเหล็กกล้าความแข็งแรงสูง โดยการศึกษาค่าพารามิเตอร์ที่ดีที่สุดของเครื่องจักรในการผลิต (Silachai, A., & Prasomthong, S. 2021) ภายหลังการตีพิมพ์ ได้มีการแจ้งรายงานจากนักวิจัยมายังกองบรรณาธิการ เกี่ยวกับบทความดังกล่าวมีเนื้อหาซ้ำซ้อนกับผลงานที่ได้รับการเผยแพร่ในปี 2565 อย่างมีนัยสำคัญ ตามขั้นตอนการพิจารณาการรายงานจากนักวิจัย กองบรรณาธิการได้ดำเนินการตรวจสอบตามหลักเกณฑ์และแนวปฏิบัติด้านจริยธรรมการตีพิมพ์ของวารสาร และยินยันว่ามีความซ้ำซ้อนทางวิชาการ การตีพิมพ์ซ้ำซ้อน (Redundant Publication / Self-Plagiarism) รวมถึงการนำภาพถ่ายผลการทดลองมาใช้ซ้ำ ผลการตรวจสอบดังกล่าวทำให้กองบรรณาธิการมีมติให้เพิกถอนบทความ (Silachai, A., & Prasomthong, S. 2021) ฉบับนี้

title: The ‘invisible hands’ depicting early electricity: the careers of james mynde and john ingram at the royal society and the académie royale des sciences
abstract: Abstract While the historiography of eighteenth-century electricity has consolidated over the past fifty years, scholarly attention remains focused on natural philosophers, largely overlooking the hidden artisans behind early scientific imagery in this field. This paper addresses this gap by reconstructing the institutional trajectories of two British illustrators and engravers: James Mynde (1702–1770) and John Ingram (1721–ca 1776). Drawing upon extensive archival research at the Royal Society and the Académie Royale des Sciences, this study recovers their professional routines and institutional ties between the 1740s and 1760s, amid a rapid expansion in studies on electricity. As the primary engravers for the Philosophical Transactions and the Histoire et Mémoires, respectively, Mynde and Ingram produced virtually all electrical imagery published by these societies during this early stage of studies in electricity. This historical analysis reveals that producing these images involved diverse factors far removed from conceptual debates regarding what electricity was. Ultimately, it demonstrates how Mynde's and Ingram's work actively built a distinct iconography that underscored the empirical and captivating nature of electricity, highlighting the impact of these ‘invisible hands’ on the circulation of scientific knowledge.
venue: Notes and Records: the Royal Society journal of the history of science

title: Strategic reorientation under institutional volatility: a conceptual replication in an emerging-market fintech context
abstract: Purpose This study aims to conduct a bounded conceptual replication of McDonald and Gao’s (2019) strategic reorientation framework, examining what it retains, how stakeholder tension is contextually modified and which supporting interpretations become analytically useful in two Turkish fintech cases with varying regulatory salience. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative conceptual replication was conducted across two early-stage Turkish fintech ventures, Alpha and Beta, through nine in-depth founder interviews, documentary analysis and triangulation of secondary data. McDonald and Gao’s audience-management constructs, product framing, audience expectations and penalties and the anticipation, justification and staging of reorientation served as sensitizing concepts. Findings The framework’s broader audience-management problem remains recognizable in both cases but requires contextual qualification. Alpha provides the closer-transfer case, with predominantly market-related stakeholder tension. Beta provides the stronger contextual-modification case, where regulatory salience is more visible alongside customer-process, market and investor considerations. State-induced logic is therefore treated as an article-level interpretation most clearly evidenced in Beta, while founder-centric governance and situated legitimacy-building remain supporting interpretations. Practical implica…

title: Marketing Digitalization for Traditional MSMEs: Market Access, Digital Literacy, and Program Sustainability
abstract: Micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in Cikondang Village, Cianjur Regency, face marketing challenges, including dependence on intermediaries, limited digital literacy, and the lack of integration between product information and online market access. This article describes the marketing digitalization assistance process, identifies supporting and inhibiting factors, and outlines requirements for program sustainability. The community engagement program was conducted from 15 July to 23 August 2026 using a participatory qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured interviews, and activity documentation involving MSME owners and village officials. Activities included coordination and data collection, socialization, and assistance with Business Identification Numbers (NIB), QRIS, Google Maps/Google Business Profile, and a village product-catalog website. The findings indicate that a combination of direct assistance, village institutional support, and youth involvement helped establish a more structured foundation for digital presence. However, limited digital skills and internet connectivity remained obstacles. As the evaluation was conducted during the program period, increases in revenue, profit margins, and competitiveness cannot be concluded as measurable impacts. Program sustainability requires the appointment of a web…

title: QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THE GLOBAL HYDRAULIC MARKET DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The article provides an integrative quantitative and qualitative assessment of the global hydraulic equipment market, combining data from recent commercial reports, consulting studies and scientific publications. The analysis confirms that, despite methodological differences, all major sources predict sustained market expansion with an average compound annual growth rate of about 4% over the next decade, indicating favourable conditions for entering industrial and mobile hydraulics. Particular attention is paid to regional distribution, sectoral structure and component-level dynamics, showing the leading roles of Asia-Pacific, construction and mobile hydraulics, as well as the rising importance of energy-efficient pumps, smart systems and advanced actuators. The study identifies three key transformation drivers: electrification, digitalisation and smart hydraulics, and the green transition, which jointly shape future R&D priorities.

title: Imaging therapeutic response at brain neuroimmune interfaces in women with systemic lupus erythematosus
abstract: Purpose Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) frequently affects the central nervous system, likely via neuroimmune interfaces; how these interfaces respond longitudinally to standard therapy remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify these therapeutic dynamics. Methods This retrospective longitudinal study included 63 women with SLE who had brain MRI at baseline and after standard therapy. Enlarged perivascular spaces (ePVS), choroid plexus (CP), and gray matter (GM) volumes were segmented from 3D T1-weighted images; the diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index was computed from DTI scans. Paired t-tests compared baseline and post-therapy values. Patients were grouped into neuropsychiatric SLE (NPSLE) and non-NPSLE groups, and longitudinal deltas compared. Spearman correlations assessed associations of MRI changes with clinical measures. Results After standard therapy, all 63 patients showed clinical improvement (decreased SLEDAI-2K, increased MoCA scores). Left DTI-ALPS index increased (T = -2.475, P FDR = 0.048), and bilateral CP volumes decreased (left: T = 2.432, P FDR = 0.048; right: T = 3.330, P FDR = 0.006). ePVS volumes remained unchanged. No significant correlations emerged between MRI changes and clinical scores, and improvement did not differ between NPSLE and non-NPSLE subgroups. Conclusions Longitudinal MRI identified measurable altera…

A Supramolecular Symmetry-Breaking Strategy for Enhanced Circularly Polarized Luminescence, High-Temperature Phase Transition, and Piezoelectric Response in Chiral Manganese(II) Halides
abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) has attracted intense interest for applications in 3D displays, optical data storage, and quantum information processing. Chiral organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides (HOMHs) have emerged as promising CPL materials owing to their structural tunability, facile solution processability, and tunable photoluminescence, yet they often suffer from small luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum) and limited functionality. Herein, we report a pair of enantiomeric host–guest compounds, [18-crown-6]2[(R/S)-C3H12N2][MnCl4] (R-Mn and S-Mn; (R/S)-C3H12N2 = (R/S)-propane-1,2-diammonium), via a supramolecular assembly strategy. The resulting two-in-one structures feature strong N–H···O hydrogen bonds that lock the chiral cations and reduce the crystal symmetry from the C2 phase of the previously reported compound without 18-crown-6 to the lowest-symmetry P1 space group. R/S-Mn exhibits CPL with |glum| = 2.6 × 10–2, more than 10 times higher than the previously reported value of 2 × 10–3. Moreover, both compounds display a reversible high-temperature solid–solid phase transition at 405 K and a measurable piezoelectric coefficient of 11 pC/N. DFT calculations reveal that the band edges and emissive states are dominated by the [MnCl4]2– units. Meanwhile, the organic cations do not contribute to the electronic transitions, indicating that the CPL ari…

title: Perceptions of Trade Remedy Law and Firms’ Response Readiness in Vietnam: A Stimulus–Organism–Response Approach
abstract: This study examines the factors associated with firms’ response readiness to trade remedy measures among business owners and managers of import–export enterprises, with perceived legal effectiveness of trade remedy law and trust in the legal and enforcement system examined as mediating variables. The research model is grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework and empirically tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Data were collected from a survey of 425 business owners and managers of import–export enterprises in Vietnam, an emerging economy in Asia. The findings indicate that perceived legal fairness, legal information accessibility, and perceived government support are positively associated with firms’ response readiness through selected indirect pathways involving legal effectiveness and institutional trust. In contrast, perceived legal clarity and digital legal information quality are not significantly associated with firms’ response readiness. Furthermore, importance–performance map analysis (IPMA) identifies perceived legal effectiveness of trade remedy law and trust in the legal and enforcement system as priority factors for enhancing firms’ response readiness. The findings contribute to the empirical literature on trade remedies by extending the analysis to firms’ perceptions and behavioral readiness. They also prov…

title: Factors associated with treatment response to microwave ablation of benign thyroid nodules: a retrospective single-center study of nodule composition and vascularity
abstract: Background This study aimed to evaluate radiological and procedural factors associated with treatment response in benign thyroid nodules treated with microwave ablation (MWA). Methods Of 90 consecutive patients who underwent MWA for cytologically benign (Bethesda II) thyroid nodules, 80 who completed 12 months of follow-up were retrospectively analyzed. Pre-procedural ultrasonography was used to assess nodule volume, composition, and Doppler vascularity. All ablations were performed under ultrasound guidance using the moving-shot technique, and volume reduction ratio (VRR) was calculated during follow-up at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary outcome, treatment success, was defined as a VRR ≥75% at 12 months. Pearson correlation and multivariable logistic regression (forced-entry method) analyses were performed to determine factors influencing response. Results The mean patient age was 46.7 ± 16.6 years, and 66.3% were female. Mean baseline nodule volume was 11.75 ± 3.31 mL. Nodules were predominantly cystic in 38.8%, solid in 35%, and mixed in 26.3%. Mean VRR increased progressively during follow-up, from 26.2 ± 8.1% at 1 month to 72.5 ± 5.9% at 12 months, and treatment success (VRR ≥75%) was achieved in 35.0% of patients (28/80), whereas all nodules (100%) achieved a VRR ≥50%. Regrowth (any volume increase from the smallest recorded volume) occurred in 25.0% of patients, repe…

title: Immune Response to Hepatitis B Vaccination According to National EPI Schedule among Children Below 2 Years
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus infection is a public health burden globally. We incorporate Hep-B vaccine in our EPI schedule. There is no comprehensive data regarding the immune response of the HBV vaccine at one year in our country. The study was done to assess the immune response among HBV vaccinated children at this age group. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at EPI outdoor of Chittagong Medical College Hospital from January to December, 2022. Blood sample from 375 vaccinated children were tested for Anti-HBs titre by ELISA technique in between 9 months to 15 months. Statistical analyses were performed with Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 23.0. Results: This study shows that older children and male tend to have better immune responses after vaccination and malnutrition is a significant risk factor for low antibody titers. This study also shows that 79.2% of children had satisfactory or high levels of anti-HBs antibodies (≥10 mIU/mL). However, 20.8% of children had low antibody titers (<10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection. Conclusion: Most children vaccinated under the current EPI schedule develop protective immunity against hepatitis B; a small proportion remain vulnerable due to inadequate seroconversion. Key words: Anti HBs; EPI; Hep-B vaccination; One-year><10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection. Co…

title: Parent–teacher support congruence and adolescents’ academic well-being: a response surface analysis
abstract: Background Parental support and teacher support are usually studied as separate predictors of adolescents’ academic functioning, which leaves open whether the correspondence between these two resources carries its own significance. Drawing on ecological systems theory, developmental assets theory, and person–environment fit perspectives, this study examined how the joint configuration of parental and teacher support is associated with adolescents’ academic well-being, and whether expectancy-value motivation statistically accounts for part of this association. Methods Participants were 2,492 junior high school students (1,266 girls, 1,224 boys; M age = 13.04, SD = 0.88) nested within 101 classrooms in China. Multilevel polynomial regression with response surface analysis (RSA) was estimated in 20 multiply imputed datasets. The random-effects structure was selected by likelihood-ratio tests; the retained model, which included a random classroom intercept and a random slope for teacher support, was used for all surface parameters, figures, and mediation analyses. Surface parameters were tested directly, using standard errors from the pooled covariance matrix and a classroom-level cluster bootstrap. Results Motivation and well-being were higher when parental and teacher support were jointly high than when both were low (congruence-line slopes a 1 = 0.65 and 0.69). The direction of …

title: Intermittent Demand Forecasting and Inventory Service Level Evaluation Using The TSB Method and Machine Learning: A Case Study on PT X in The Document Solutions Industry
abstract: Intermittent demand presents significant challenges in demand forecasting and inventory management, particularly in the document solutions industry, where demand is driven by both rental and sales activities. Forecasting accuracy alone does not necessarily translate into improved inventory performance. This study evaluates the forecasting performance of the Teunter–Syntetos–Babai (TSB) method and machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM, across total, rental, and sales demand categories and examines their implications for inventory service levels. A quantitative analysis was conducted using supply demand data for 134 stock-keeping units (SKUs) of Brand Z at PT X from August 2023 to November 2025. Demand patterns were classified using the Average Demand Interval (ADI) and the squared coefficient of variation (CV²). Forecasting models incorporated historical demand, lead times, new printer installations, and new printer sales. Forecasting performance was evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE), while inventory performance was assessed using an order-up-to-level (S) policy based on the probability of no stockout (S1), fill rate (S2), and ready rate (S3). Random Forest demonstrated superior overall performance in terms of forecasting accuracy and inventory service levels, particularly for intermittent and lumpy dem…

title: Aggregating Demand and Standardizing Supply: Instrument Choice for U.S. Small Modular Reactor Deployment
abstract: The United States leads the world in small modular reactor (SMR) designs and has yet to complete a commercial deployment. Federal awards, hyperscaler agreements, and state funds are now underwriting first units for the leading projects, but serial factory production, the basis of the SMR value proposition, has begun nowhere, because the supply chain has neither a standard to tool against nor firm orders that justify tooling. This article asks what the minimal sufficient intervention is. Comparative analysis of SEMATECH, the French and Korean nuclear programs, and five decades of American standardization and cost-share attempts yields four diagnostic dimensions, and seven candidate instruments are rated against them on a five-point scale. None is sufficient alone. The design that prevails pairs two institutions for light-water SMRs and dominates a SEMATECH-style broad-membership consortium. In consensus standards work, ASME code cases carry vessel and component design rules, an ASTM International subcommittee writes the material, fabrication, and test specifications those rules cite, and the NRC accepts the result through its existing incorporation-by-reference process. A time-limited program in the DOE Office of Nuclear Energy, holding a no-year appropriation, makes fixed milestone payments and commits to buy the unsubscribed share of each qualifying unit’s output, up to a cap,…

title: Case Report: Durable response to lenalidomide rechallenge after azacitidine failure in myelodysplastic neoplasm with del(5q)
abstract: Lower-risk myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) with isolated del(5q) are particularly sensitive to lenalidomide, although most patients eventually lose their response and may experience disease progression. Hypomethylating agents (HMAs) are commonly used as salvage therapy after lenalidomide failure, but treatment options following subsequent HMA failure remain limited. Evidence regarding lenalidomide rechallenge after intervening HMA therapy is scarce. We report the long-term clinical course of a woman with MDS with del(5q) and multilineage dysplasia, diagnosed after prior cytotoxic therapy for colon adenocarcinoma. Lenalidomide was started for transfusion-dependent anemia (IPSS Intermediate-1; IPSS-R Intermediate) and resulted in transfusion independence and a complete cytogenetic response after four cycles. Hematologic remission was maintained for more than three years, but lenalidomide was discontinued after 41 cycles because of progressive cytopenias and cytogenetic evolution. The patient subsequently received 36 cycles of azacitidine, achieving transient hematologic improvement before disease progression with an increase in bone marrow blasts. Because the del(5q) clone persisted and no established salvage option was available, lenalidomide was reintroduced at the original starting dose and produced a rapid erythroid response together with a reduction in bone marrow blasts, wi…

title: Trap-Assisted Photoconductive Gain and Wavelength-Dependent Response of Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Heterojunction Ultraviolet Detectors
abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet photodetection is essential for secure optical communication, environmental monitoring and early warning systems, yet conventional GaN-based Schottky detectors rely on evaporated metal electrodes that introduce interfacial defects and limited UV transmittance. Here we report a solution-processed Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Schottky heterojunction UV photodetector formed by low-temperature drop-coating. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Raman analysis confirm the surface termination and structural integrity of the transferred MXene, and density-functional-theory calculations rationalize the tunable Schottky barrier. The device exhibits a low dark current of ~74 nA near zero bias, about 30% lower than that of conventional Ti/Au Schottky GaN detectors. Wavelength-resolved measurements at 300, 310 and 320 nm show a photocurrent ordering of 320 nm > 310 nm > 300 nm, governed by the interplay between photon penetration depth and near-surface recombination. Under 320 nm illumination at 1.91 W/cm 2 and -4 V, a responsivity of 0.58 A/W, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 212% and a specific detectivity of 3.35 × 10 11 Jones are obtained; the above-unity EQE indicates trap-mediated internal photoconductive gain in GaN. Periodic UV switching yields rise/fall times of 1.22/0.80 s with an on/off ratio of ~2.2 and <5% peak-to-peak variation over four c…

title: Understanding household food demand in Sri Lanka using a two-step budgeting framework
abstract: Purpose Sri Lanka has been affected by a severe economic crisis in recent years, which has changed food consumption behavior. Therefore, this study examines household demand for major food groups in Sri Lanka and provides evidence on how households respond to changes in food prices and expenditure. Design/methodology/approach A two-step budgeting framework combined with the quadratic almost ideal demand system (QUAIDS) was employed to estimate expenditure and price elasticities for major food groups, including cereals, pulses, vegetables, fruits, fish, meat, eggs and milk products, using data from the Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES). Findings The results show that cereals, pulses, eggs and vegetables all have an expenditure elasticity of less than one, while for fruits, fish, meat and milk products, the elasticity is greater than one. The estimated own-price elasticities suggest that households are more responsive to price changes for fruits, fish, eggs, meat and milk products than cereals, pulses and vegetables. Research limitations/implications This study's findings will help policymakers develop appropriate policies and targeted programs to mitigate the impact of the ongoing economic crisis and improve the overall well-being and nutrition of the Sri Lankan population. Originality/value This study provides a recent empirical evidence on household food demand in…
venue: Journal of Asian Business and Economic Studies

title: Incorporating authority perception, economic status and behavioural response in infectious disease control
abstract: Abstract We introduce a multi-population mean field game framework to examine how economic status and authority perception shape vaccination and social distancing decisions under different epidemic control policies. We conducted a survey to inform our model and stratify the population into six groups by income and perception of authority, capturing behavioural heterogeneity. Individuals choose socialization and vaccination levels to optimize objectives such as minimizing treatment costs, complying with social distancing guidelines if they are authority-followers, or reducing losses from decreased social interactions if they are authority-indifferents, alongside economic costs. Public health authorities influence behaviour through social distancing guidelines and vaccination costs. We characterize the Nash equilibrium via a forward–backward differential equation system, provide its mathematical analysis and numerically solve it. Our findings reveal a trade-off between social distancing and vaccination. Under stricter guidelines that target both susceptible and infected individuals, followers reduce both socialization and vaccination levels, while indifferents increase socialization owing to followers’ preventative measures. Adaptive guidelines targeting infected individuals effectively reduce infections and narrow the gap between low- and high-income groups, while lower vaccinat…

title: Hemingway to Mailer

title: Characteristic electric-field manipulation of the optical response in monolayer graphene oxide
abstract: The flourishing research on graphene oxide (GO)-based optical sensing platforms, laser media, and optoelectronic devices calls for efficient, reversible, and spatially resolved methods to acquire and control multimodal optical information from GO. Here, we demonstrate that the optical transmission and fluorescence of monolayer GO (mGO)—two complementary optical readouts—can be reversibly manipulated by an external electric field (EEF) as low as ±1 kV/mm; the dual-channel optical responses are monitored simultaneously by a home-built scanning confocal microscope with a spatial resolution of about 300 nm, yielding spatially resolved, real-time multimodal optical information from every probed spot. Domain-resolved dual-channel imaging reveals that the absorption and emission of mGO are spatially heterogeneous and, more strikingly, that adjacent domains on a single mGO flake respond to the EEF in opposite directions: the transmission of one domain increases by more than 25% while its fluorescence is quenched almost completely, whereas the neighboring domain exhibits a ∼25% decrease in transmission together with a twofold fluorescence enhancement. We further define, for each probing spot, a characteristic electric field E c —the smallest field at which the transmission or fluorescence departs from its zero-field baseline by more than three standard deviations of the baseline noise. …

title: Stem cell mobilization with G-CSF and on-demand plerixafor in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients treated with daratumumab: a single-center experience
abstract: Introduction Daratumumab-containing induction therapy improves treatment response in transplant-eligible patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma but may impair hematopoietic stem cell mobilization. We evaluated the effect of daratumumab exposure on stem cell mobilization and collection and assessed the effectiveness of on demand plerixafor in patients with inadequate mobilization. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 215 transplant-eligible patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated at a single center between January 2022 and February 2025. Patients underwent granulocyte colony-stimulating factor–based mobilization, with plerixafor administered on demand on the fourth day of mobilization. The primary endpoint was peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration on day 4 of mobilization. Secondary endpoints included plerixafor use, number of apheresis procedures, total CD34+ cells collected, and mobilization failure. Results Eighty-two patients received daratumumab-containing induction and 133 did not. The median peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration on day 4 of mobilization was significantly lower after daratumumab exposure than without (9.61 vs 20.0 × 10 6 cells/L; P < 0.001). Plerixafor was required in 74.4% versus 39.8% of patients, respectively (P < 0.001). Among patients who received plerixafor, the median peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration incr…

title: From urban digital embeddedness to management decisions: understanding innovative SMEs' digital orientation
abstract: Purpose Developed for management decision's “The Practice of Making Decisions” section, this study examines a concrete managerial dilemma: what can managers learn by considering how deeply digital technologies are embedded in the urban environment alongside their availability? We examine how urban digital embeddedness is associated with innovative small and medium-sized enterprise (SMEs') digital orientation (DO) and its four dimensions. Design/methodology/approach The study combines city- and firm-level information for 24 Italian cities and 243 innovative SMEs observed over 13 years. Urban digital embeddedness captures citizens' use of home banking, municipal applications and broadband services. SMEs' DO is derived from annual mission statements and assessed across digital technology scope, digital capabilities, digital ecosystem coordination and digital architecture configuration. Relationships are estimated using a two-way fixed-effects Spatial Durbin Panel Model. Findings The findings show that urban digital embeddedness is most consistently associated with firms' stated digital capabilities and digital ecosystem coordination, followed by digital architecture configuration, while evidence for digital technology scope is comparatively weak. Practical implications Managers should look beyond digital technologies when making digital-strategy decisions and consider how technolo…

title: Value co-creation pathways for construction waste reduction
abstract: Purpose This study aims to address the persistent challenges of fragmented collaboration and unclear value exchange in construction waste reduction (CWR). It seeks to develop a systematic understanding of how stakeholders collaborate by constructing a stakeholder value network (SVN) model. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was employed, integrating value co-creation and social exchange theory. The SVN model was developed and analyzed using data from a literature review, policy analysis and semi-structured expert interviews. The network analysis identified 45 value streams and 846 value loops, with robustness ensured through sensitivity analysis. Findings The results reveal that non-economic values, specifically knowledge sharing, policy support and social recognition, play a more critical structural role than financial incentives in sustaining collaborative networks. Furthermore, contractors, owners and designers form the triadic core of CWR governance, whereas suppliers and the public assume more peripheral roles than traditionally presumed. Originality/value This study contributes a novel, network-based analytical framework for examining multi-stakeholder cooperation in sustainability-oriented projects. It challenges the conventional overemphasis on economic drivers as the primary collaborative force and redefines core governance actors. Based on the findin…

title: The role of AI adoption in the relationship between digital self-efficacy and sustainable entrepreneurship intentions among university students in Jordan
abstract: Purpose This study investigates associations among digital self-efficacy (DSE), artificial intelligence (AI) adoption intention and sustainable entrepreneurship intentions (SEIs) among university students at a private university in Amman, Jordan – a context with high unemployment and national digital agendas. Design/methodology/approach A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was employed. Phase 1 involved semi-structured interviews with seven entrepreneurship faculty and an incubator director at a private university in Amman. Phase 2 comprised a survey of 150 students from the same institution. The technology acceptance model (TAM) and social cognitive theory (SCT) were integrated in a mediated model tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings DSE was positively associated with perceived usefulness (PU) (β = 0.570, p < 0.001) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) (β = 0.584, p < 0.001) of AI tools. AI adoption intention (AIAI) mediated the relationship between DSE and SEI. The total indirect effect of DSE on SEI through both serial mediation paths was 0.247 (p < 0.001). The specific serial indirect effects were 0.078 (DSE → PU → AIAI → SEI, p = 0.012) and 0.093 (DSE → PEOU → AIAI → SEI, p = 0.006). The model accounted for 42.8% and 25.3% of the variance in AIAI and SEI, respectively. These findings are limited to university students at …

title: Optimizing the Role of Internal Audit Through Effective Communication with Risk Management at PT Pegadaian (Persero)
abstract: This study examined the optimization of the Internal Audit Function (Satuan Pengawasan Intern, SPI), operating as the third line, through effective communication with the Risk Management Function, operating as the second line, at PT Pegadaian (Persero). The study was grounded in the Three Lines Model developed by The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), alongside Financial Services Authority Regulations (Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, POJK) No. 42 of 2024 concerning the Implementation of Risk Management for Financing Institutions, Venture Capital Companies, Microfinance Institutions, and Other Financial Services Institutions, and POJK No. 48 of 2024 concerning Good Governance for these institutions. Using a descriptive qualitative approach with a case study design, the research identified communication gaps that prevented internal audit findings from being systematically integrated with the organizational risk profile maintained by the second line. The findings revealed that coordination and communication between the two functions remained suboptimal. The Risk Management Function had not established a comprehensive risk register to support risk-based internal auditing, while SPI had identified 1,491 chart of accounts (CoA)-related conditions and 72 CoA-related causes that were not systematically consolidated into reports for the Board of Directors and senior management. The…

title: MANAJEMEN PEMBINAAN KEAGAMAAN DI UPT SMAN 1 BULUKUMBA MANAGEMENT OF RELIGIOUS DEVELOPMENT AT UPT SMAN 1 BULUKUMBA
abstract: Religious development in schools represents a strategic effort to cultivate student character grounded in noble morality and religious values. However, its practical implementation faces notable challenges, such as limited competent internal human resources and suboptimal motivation among educators, parents, and students. This study aims to analyze the management of religious development at UPT SMAN 1 Bulukumba examined through planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling (POAC) dimensions. A descriptive qualitative method utilizing phenomenological, psychological, and sociological approaches was conducted through in-depth interviews, participant observations, and documentation involving eight key informants. The findings reveal that UPT SMAN 1 Bulukumba administers eight structured religious development programs coordinated by Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teachers and external mentors. Planning is carried out through collaborative deliberation and program execution runs consistently, yet organizing lacks formal appointment decrees and parental monitoring at home remains limited. This study recommends sustaining the TAJDID program (Qur'anic Memorization, Congregational Zuhur Prayer, and Habituation of Dhuha Prayer), which has been officially endorsed by the principal to foster students' religious character. title: Stakeholder-Oriented Ecotourism Management and Marketing: A Sustainability Performance Evaluation of Chengyang Eight Villages in Guangxi, China
abstract: As ecotourism destinations face increasing market competition and growing sustainability pressures, destination managers must balance stakeholder interests while converting ecological, sociocultural, and economic resources into sustainable market value. Drawing on stakeholder theory, strategic management, and destination marketing perspectives, this study develops a stakeholder-oriented sustainability performance evaluation framework for ecotourism management. Fourteen indicators across economic, sociocultural, and environmental dimensions are constructed through a literature review and evaluated from the perspective of indigenous residents as core stakeholders. Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Likert-scale survey data, and Chengyang Eight Villages in Guangxi, China as the empirical setting, the study assesses the relative managerial priorities of sustainable ecotourism development. The reported dimension weights assign the highest priority to economic sustainability, followed by sociocultural sustainability, whereas environmental sustainability receives the lowest relative weight. Discrepancies between the displayed matrices and indicator weights require reconciliation before the indicator rankings can be treated as definitive. The reported weighting structure highlights differences in the relative emphasis assigned to livelihood, cultural, and environmental conside…

title: VLT/X-Shooter spectroscopic characterisation of the Didymos system, target of the ESA Hera mission
abstract: The Didymos--Dimorphos system was the target of the NASA Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission and is also the destination of the ESA Hera spacecraft. Ground-based spectroscopy provides an insight into its overall surface composition pre- and post-impact. We aim to characterise the Didymos system by analysing ultraviolet (down to 0.32 ) to near-infrared (up to 2.40 ) m m ground-based reflectance spectra obtained before and after the DART impact, expanding the pool of available Earth-based observations of the asteroid. We present the spectra of the Didymos system over four consecutive nights (September 26--29, 2022) acquired by the X-Shooter instrument of the Very Large Telescope. We taxonomically classified the spectra and analysed their main spectral features, evaluating the characteristic band parameters of the 1 and 2 broad absorption bands, as well as the spectral slopes. m We infer the following spectral properties: an average Band I centre at 0.944 , a Band II centre at 1.995 , and a band area ratio of 0.94 , we find that the surface exhibits a degree of space weathering comparable to that of main-belt asteroids. Furthermore, a meteorite-based ordinary chondrite classification method that isolates absorption band profiles from continuum reddening favours an H-chondrite affinity for the Didymos system. Post-impact spectra show no fundamental change in mineralogy.…

Mechanical design and experimental performance analysis of a hybrid single-axis photovoltaic tracking system under tropical climate conditions in Nigeria
abstract: Purpose The aim of this research is to determine if fixed-tilt photovoltaic (PV) systems have lower energy harvesting efficiency in tropical climates due to changing solar irradiation, cloud cover, and high operating temperatures. However, many modern tracking systems rely on complicated and expensive control design, which limits their use in underdeveloped countries. The aim of this research is to design, fabricate, and test a low-cost hybrid single-axis PV tracking system that combines light-dependent resistor (LDR)-based active tracking with real-time clock (RTC)-based astronomical control to improve PV energy harvesting in tropical environments. Design/methodology/approach A mechanically robust single-axis tracking system was designed and fabricated using locally available materials. The system utilizes a hybrid tracking method consisting of LDR active tracking and time-controlled astronomical calculation with an RTC. A fabricated mild-steel single-axis tracking structure and an ESP32 microcontroller were installed to enable real-time tracking and recording of PV system parameters PV voltages, PV currents and temperature) with battery status notification through an Internet of Things (IoT) system monitoring. A passive temperature regulation system was used to regulate high PV array temperature resistance within a tropical environment, which remains a key factor in improving…

title: From conflict to climate: dissecting external shocks to Islamic banking stability
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how foreign geopolitical risk (FGPR) and climate risk (CR) shape the stability of Islamic banks. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 56 publicly listed Islamic banks across 16 countries from 2010 to 2024, the authors assess bank stability through the Z-score and non-performing financing ratio. The authors estimate using fixed effects, generalized least squares and two-step system generalized method of moments models and conduct several robustness checks to address endogeneity and sample consistency. Findings FGPR from export partners significantly weakens Islamic bank stability and increases credit risk, whereas import-based risks show more mixed effects. The effects of CR on Islamic bank stability are heterogeneous across climate indicators and stability measures. Practical implications The findings suggest that Islamic banks and regulators should pay greater attention to cross-border geopolitical exposure, particularly export-market exposure, when assessing banking vulnerabilities. Given the heterogeneous climate-risk results, the study does not provide sufficient evidence for specific climate stress-testing requirements. Continued monitoring of external risks may support early identification of vulnerabilities, while specific hedging, diversification and early-warning measures require further empirical investigation. title: From Needs Assessment to Instructional Design: Empirical Requirements for a DIF-PBL Model in Inclusive Numeracy Learning
abstract: Inclusive elementary classrooms require instructional approaches that accommodate substantial variation in students’ numeracy readiness, learning characteristics, and support needs. This study examined teachers’ instructional needs and preliminary learner differences as an empirical basis for designing a Differentiation-Based Problem-Based Learning (DIF-PBL) model for inclusive numeracy learning. The study was conducted as a descriptive needs assessment within a broader research and development project. Participants included 20 classroom teachers and special education support teachers from three inclusive elementary schools in Bone Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Data were collected using a 13-item four-point Likert questionnaire and structured observations of three students representing different learner profiles. Questionnaire data were analyzed using item-level means, standard deviations, and response frequencies, while student observations were treated as illustrative contextual cases. Teachers reported substantial instructional challenges, including disparities in numeracy achievement, difficulty balancing instructional support, limitations in conventional Problem-Based Learning, and practical difficulties in implementing differentiated instruction. The strongest responses concerned the need for an integrated PBL and differentiation model (M = 3.95, SD = 0.22), an oper…

title: Data-driven well-resolved aggregate-capacity screening for brackish-blending management in Kuwait under pumping and total-dissolved-solids constraints
abstract: Brackish groundwater is a strategic supply buffer for arid states reliant on energy-intensive seawater desalination, yet the operational condition of legacy well fields and the distribution-side limits on dispatchable volume remain understudied. Both are addressed here for Kuwait, where desalination supplies ∼ 92% of municipal water. A ministry-level record of 393 wells across five production fields was assembled, and a well-resolved screening linear program was formulated to maximize brackish blending subject to the 1,000-ppm upper total-dissolved-solids (TDS) limit of the applicable Gulf drinking-water standard and an aggregate pumping bound. The model resolves individual wells but represents the distribution side as a single aggregate capacity scalar; it is a screening model, not a hydraulic network model, and its optimum is an upper bound on what a station-resolved network could deliver. Current operations support 62.24MIGD of blending; all rehabilitation scenarios saturate the pumping bound at 90.70MIGD, a 1.46 × (45.7%) uplift. The binding constraint is, therefore, distribution-side aggregate capacity, not upstream well availability. This finding is robust: a zone-partitioned re-solve yields 87.8 MIGD–90.70MIGD, and crediting the standby reserve shifts the binding constraint to the TDS limit; well availability never binds. title: Complete remission with single agent lorlatinib in children with ALK+ anaplastic large cell lymphoma and central nervous system involvement: a case report
abstract: Therapies targeting cancer-specific mutations can result in remarkable clinical responses while reducing adverse effects. We describe the use of lorlatinib, a potent oral inhibitor of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) that crosses the blood brain barrier (BBB), in a case report of two patients with refractory and relapsed ALK+ anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK+ ALCL) with central nervous system (CNS) involvement. In both cases, treatment with single agent lorlatinib led to rapid and durable complete remission with tolerable side effects. Furthermore, we also describe a novel application of next generation sequencing to characterize circulating immune receptor DNA sequences associated with ALCL, and tracked the molecular response to therapy with subsequent blood specimens. These cases demonstrate that utilization of an effective targeted therapy against cancer-specific driver mutations that penetrates the BBB can lead to a significant clinical response, and presents clonal tracking for molecular response assessment as a potential approach for further study.

title: Cost-effectiveness of disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab versus chemotherapy alone as first-line treatment for HER2-overexpressing advanced urothelial carcinoma: a cost-effectiveness analysis from the Chinese healthcare system perspective
abstract: Background The antibody-drug conjugate disitamab vedotin (DV) in combination with the programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor toripalimab has demonstrated favorable efficacy and a manageable safety profile in patients with HER2-expressing advanced urothelial carcinoma (AUC), as evidenced by the pivotal RC48–016 clinical trial. Nevertheless, the economic viability of this combination strategy relative to conventional chemotherapy remains inadequately characterized. This study sought to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the aforementioned combination regimen as first-line therapy for HER2-overexpressing AUC patients within the Chinese healthcare system. Methods Leveraging clinical data derived from the RC48–016 trial, a partitioned survival model (PSM) was developed to project long-term survival outcomes and healthcare resource consumption among HER2-overexpressing AUC patients receiving either DV plus toripalimab or chemotherapy alone. Primary outcome measures encompassed total costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER). The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was established at twice China’s 2024 per capita gross domestic product (GDP), amounting to $26,889.37 per QALY. Sensitivity analyses were undertaken to ascertain the robustness of the model findings. Results The chemotherapy-alone arm incurred total costs of $80,97…

Numerical Analysis of Five-Layer Ti–6Al–4V to Inconel 825 Functionally Graded Plate Using Power-Law Distribution, Voigt Homogenization, and Finite Element Method
abstract: This​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌ study uses numerical simulations to explore the mechanical behavior of a five-layer functionally graded plate. The setup features a unidirectional gradation that starts with Ti–6Al–4V on the top surface and gradually changes to Inconel 825 at the bottom. The purpose of this gradation is to allow a smooth transition between the two superalloys and thus reduce the number of abrupt material discontinuities. The study focuses on how the volume fraction in each layer affects the structure's mechanical response. The researchers use a layer-based modeling approach to conduct their investigation. In this method, the researchers adjust the metal proportions stepwise to alter the plate's composition. This gradual change results in continuous variation in key mechanical properties, such as stiffness, elastic modulus, and strength. A power-law function with a given power index represents the compositional gradation. The Voigt homogenization model is used to calculate the effective layer properties. After that, finite element analysis (FEA) is used to determine the plate’s behavior under static, modal, and buckling conditions. According to the simulations, functionally graded layering effectively relieves stress concentrations, thereby increasing structural durability. Optimized material distribution improves load-carrying capacity and resistance to mechanical failure. …

title: Evaluating the Interaction of Alzheimer Biomarker Burden and α-Synuclein Status on Cognitive Trajectories in Parkinson Disease: Methodological Challenges and Power Estimates
abstract: Background: Alzheimer disease (AD) and α-synuclein copathology frequently co-occur in Parkinson disease (PD), but whether their interaction accelerates longitudinal cognitive decline is unknown. Objective: To investigate whether the cross-sectional interaction between AD biomarker burden (CSF pTau181/Aβ42 ratio) and α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) status translates to accelerated cognitive decline, and to estimate sample sizes for future co-pathology studies. Methods: We studied 246 dementia-free PD participants from the Parkinson Precision Medicine Initiative, including genetically enriched subgroups, across seven cognitive domains over 12.9 years. Longitudinal trajectories were modeled using inverse probability of continuation weighted generalized estimating equations with Firth penalization, confirmed by linear mixed-effects and Bayesian joint models. Results: A cross-sectional AD×SAA visuospatial synergy was replicated ( P =0.022), but no longitudinal interaction survived false discovery rate correction (all q ≥0.180). However, a nominally significant AD×SAA interaction on verbal memory was detected by subject-specific models ( P =0.018 to 0.026). Power simulations indicated that 400 to 600 participants under enriched designs, or over 1000 under naturalistic conditions, are required for 80% power. title: Managing Informal Economic Activities at Sentani International Airport: An Organizational Safety Risk Management Perspective
abstract: Airport landside areas are open public spaces where passenger access, commercial services, and community activities overlap, yet little is known about how airports manage the operational risks that arise from informal economic activities there. This study examines how Sentani International Airport manages community-related operational risks associated with such activities from an organizational safety risk management perspective. A qualitative case study was conducted between January and March 2026. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with five airport personnel representing operations, safety management, aviation security, commercial management, and airport security management, and were analyzed thematically. The findings show that managing informal economic activities involved more than enforcement. Five interconnected organizational processes were identified: organizational risk recognition, risk-informed decision-making, cross-functional organizational capability, continuous operational monitoring, and safety promotion and organizational learning. Communication, local knowledge, coordination with external agencies, and continued supervision after intervention were central to these processes. Community-related operational risks in landside areas can therefore be managed as part of a continuous Airport Safety Risk Management process in which coordination an…

title: Corporate reputation in India: unveiling the role of board dimensions
abstract: Purpose The primary motive of this research is to quantify corporate reputation by developing a reputation index along with investigating the influence of governance mechanisms, specifically board characteristics, on the reputation of Indian firms. Design/methodology/approach Reputation of 249 manufacturing firms listed in the National Stock Exchange (NSE) 500 index has been analysed over the period 2015–2024 using a reputation index, and to further investigate its association with board dynamics, panel data analysis has been employed. Findings Results reveal that board dimensions at firms in India have a huge contribution in impacting their reputation. Specifically, larger boards negatively affect corporate reputation, adding credence to agency theory, while board independence enhances it. Research limitations/implications This study enriches the corporate governance literature by empirically linking board attributes with corporate reputation in the Indian context. Practical implications The findings suggest that firms should prioritise the appointment of independent directors while maintaining optimal board size to improve their reputational standing. Furthermore, the reputation index developed in this study offers investors an additional tool to evaluate potential investments by providing firms' reputation scores. title: Iterative Development and Functional Verification of GREENESA, a Sensor-based Smart Microgreen Cultivation System with IoT Monitoring and PLC–HMI Migration
abstract: Background Microgreen production in compact controlled environments requires timely irrigation and lighting, but many small-scale systems still rely on manual observation. This study developed GREENESA, a portable cultivation prototype integrating environmental sensing, local and remote monitoring, and manual and threshold-based actuator control, while documenting its migration from an ESP32–Blynk prototype to a more robust PLC–HMI architecture. Methods An iterative engineering design was applied. The initial prototype integrated an ESP32 controller, DHT11 temperature–humidity sensor, BH1750 illuminance sensor, analogue substrate-moisture sensor, 20 × 4 LCD, 4 × 4 keypad, relay module, two cultivation lamps, a 12-VDC pump, and Blynk connectivity. Functional verification assessed I2C communication, keypad response, moisture-sensor calibration in dry, moist, and wet media, local display, automatic and manual control, and remote monitoring. The redesign introduced an aluminium-profile frame, separated 24-, 12-, and 5-VDC power rails, PLC control, an eight-page HMI, and support for rockwool, cocopeat, and paper media. Evidence was synthesized from design records, test observations, and the project progress report. Drivers of supply chain resilience: the roles of artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, blockchain adoption and radical innovation capabilities
abstract: Purpose Global supply chain dynamics have undergone significant changes due to economic uncertainty, logistical disruptions and large-scale crises. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study examines the relationships among artificial intelligence, knowledge sharing, radical innovation capabilities, blockchain adoption and supply chain resilience. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 208 firms operating in Türkiye's foreign trade sector and analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings The results indicate that artificial intelligence facilitates knowledge sharing, which is positively associated with supply chain resilience. While knowledge sharing is significantly related to radical innovation capabilities, radical innovation capabilities do not exhibit a direct association with supply chain resilience. In addition, blockchain adoption strengthens the relationship between knowledge sharing and supply chain resilience, suggesting that blockchain enhances the effectiveness of knowledge-sharing mechanisms in fostering resilience. Originality/value This study contributes to the productivity and performance management literature by integrating digital technologies and knowledge-based capabilities within a unified framework to explain supply chain resilience from a dynamic capabilities perspective. title: A 3D robotic inspection framework for power quality monitoring in subterranean high-voltage transmission systems
abstract: The operation of underground power transmission systems is based on continuous monitoring to ensure reliable power transmission, maintain power quality, and avoid unexpected failures. However, most of the existing robotic inspection systems are mainly based on navigation and visual inspection, which have limited ability to integrate power quality monitoring and intelligent fault analysis. To overcome these drawbacks, this work proposes an intelligent robotic inspection framework that combines autonomous robotic monitoring, multimodal sensing, optimized deep learning and adaptive hyper-parameter optimization for power quality disturbance detection. The proposed framework uses a 101-layer Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Network (SE-ResNet-101x) to classify pre-processed one-dimensional voltage signals into normal and fault classes and hyperparameters are optimized through the Self-Adaptive Sea Lion Optimization (SA-SLnO) algorithm. A set of data is generated based on simulation to mimic an actual underground inspection scenario, including the electrical, environmental, and robotic operational factors. The LiDAR data is used in isolation to provide three-dimensional localization for the robot, while the thermal and camera data provide additional inspection data. Experimental results show that fault detection performance is very good, with 99.10% accuracy, 99.97% precision, 98.94% …

title: Proton beam therapy in the treatment of adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck: a single enterprise retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background and aims Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare salivary gland malignancy with high propensity for perineural invasion (PNI) and relative radioresistance. Proton beam therapy (PBT) may improve tumor control through improved target coverage, as well as higher physical and biologic dose while limiting dose to surrounding critical structures. This single-enterprise two-site study reports outcomes and toxicity in patients with ACC of the head and neck (HN) region treated with curative-intent PBT. Methods From 2015–2025, 89 patients with HN ACC were treated with curative-intent PBT. Patients with distant metastases or prior radiotherapy (RT) were excluded. Clinical outcomes were assessed retrospectively. Toxicities were recorded prospectively using CTCAE v5.0. The Kaplan–Meier method was used to estimate local tumor control (LC), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and overall survival (OS). Hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and test of association between tumor and treatment variables and outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Results Median follow-up was 3.1 years. Sixty-nine patients underwent surgery followed by postoperative PBT, while 20 received definitive PBT for unresectable disease. The 3-year LC rate was 98.3% following postoperative PBT and 82.6% following definitive PBT. Treatment approach was not signif…

title: Fair Walk-Forward Forecasting of ICE Robusta Futures: Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, Deep-Learning, and Hybrid Models
abstract: Distribution shifts can degrade nonlinear forecasting models trained on historical price levels, particularly relative to models that retain the most recently observed level. This study empirically compares 14 statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA)–recurrent hybrid specifications for the daily ICE Futures Europe Robusta Coffee benchmark, rather than proposing a new forecasting algorithm. The synchronized dataset comprises 4,603 observations from 14 January 2008 to 28 January 2026. Specifications are selected using a chronological pure-training/validation split and evaluated once on a 300-observation blind test set under a common one-step-ahead walk-forward protocol. The blind-test price distribution shifts sharply from gross training (Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic 0.955; standardized Wasserstein distance 4.274). Delta-Random Forest achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) at 83.59 USD per metric ton, whereas Khashei–Bijari ARIMA–Long Short‐Term Memory (LSTM) yields the lowest root mean squared error at 111.99. However, Delta-Random Forest improves MAE over Naive by only 0.27 USD per metric ton, and no selected pairwise comparison remains significant after Holm adjustment of the Diebold–Mariano tests. Grouped permutation importance shows that permuting lagged first-difference history increases Delta-Random-Forest MA…
