title: Enhancing Numeracy Skills through Animated Video-Based Learning Media Among Early Grade Elementary School Students: A Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: Developed numeracy skills are essential for students to understand mathematical ideas and apply them to everyday problems. This study investigated whether animated video-based learning media improved the numeracy skills of third-grade elementary school students. A quasi-experimental pre-test-post-test control group design was conducted with 48 students at SD Negeri 1 Tanjung Seneng, Bandar Lampung, Indonesia, comprising 24 students in the experimental class (IIIA) and 24 students in the control class (IIIB). Data were collected using a 20-item numeracy test; all items were valid (r = 0.461–0.698 > r-table = 0.413) and the instrument demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.892). The experimental group increased from a mean pre-test score of 58.13 (SD = 3.35) to 87.88 (SD = 3.30), whereas the control group increased from 57.29 (SD = 3.01) to 71.58 (SD = 2.98). Within-group paired-samples t-tests were significant for the experimental group, t(23) = 197.70, p < .001, and the control group, t(23) = 112.19, p < .001. The experimental group had a mean N-gain of 0.715 (high), and the control group had 0.336 (medium). ANCOVA indicated a significant effect of learning group on post-test numeracy scores after controlling for pre-test scores, F(1,45) = 6113.92, p < .001, partial η² = .993, with adjusted means of 87.47 and 71.98 for the experimental and control groups, …

title: Pelatihan Menulis Cerita Anak Bagi Siswa Kelas V MI PUI Santi Asromo Kabupaten Majalengka
abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan keterampilan menulis kreatif siswa kelas V MI PUI Santi Asromo Majalengka melalui pelatihan menulis cerita anak berbasis proyek buku kumpulan cerita anak. Permasalahan utama mitra meliputi rendahnya minat dan kepercayaan diri siswa dalam menulis, terbatasnya kesempatan siswa mengembangkan ide kreatif, serta praktik pembelajaran menulis yang masih didominasi tugas konvensional tanpa publikasi karya yang bermakna. Program ini menerapkan pendekatan Project-Based Learning melalui kegiatan pelatihan dan pendampingan intensif yang mencakup eksplorasi cerita, penyusunan story map, penulisan draf, umpan balik teman sebaya, revisi, hingga menghasilkan kumpulan cerita anak. Metode pelaksanaan meliputi tahap persiapan, sosialisasi, workshop interaktif, praktik menulis, pendampingan, dan evaluasi produk karya siswa. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa siswa sangat antusias dan terlibat aktif selama pelatihan berlangsung. Sebagian besar peserta mampu menghasilkan cerita anak dengan struktur naratif yang jelas, alur yang runtut, serta ide cerita yang lebih kontekstual berdasarkan pengalaman sehari-hari dan lingkungan sekitar. Luaran kegiatan ini berupa kumpulan cerita anak karya siswa MI PUI Santi Asromo, modul pelatihan, serta LKPD yang dapat direplikasi di sekolah dasar. Kegiatan ini berkontribusi terhadap penguatan budaya liter…

title: Detection of sacroiliitis in spondyloarthritis patients via deep learning from computed tomography scans
Free-Vibration Performance–Robustness Trade-Offs in Hybrid Composite Laminates under Manufacturing Uncertainty: A Probabilistic Decision Framework
abstract: Manufacturing variability introduces uncertainty in the vibration response of laminated composites, which can affect decision-making on laminate selection based on nominal parameters. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware methodology for free vibration evaluation and selection between Kevlar/Epoxy, Glass/Epoxy, and Kevlar-Glass hybrid plates. The first five natural frequencies were determined by propagating uncertainties in the material properties and manufacturing processes using a Mindlin-Reissner FSDT finite-element model in combination with Monte Carlo simulation. Published benchmark frequencies were matched with a maximum absolute relative error of 0.38%. Convergence of mesh and sampling was verified independently. The coefficients of variation for frequency ranged from about 2.8% to 3.3%. The local and global sensitivity analyzes showed that the ply thickness and the longitudinal elastic modulus were the main sources of uncertainty, followed closely by density. The Kevlar laminate had the maximum natural frequencies and Rank-1 probability (61.61%) and continues to be the leader under all nine decision assumptions. The KGGKs with Kevlar outer plies showed a favorable balance between cross-modal performance robustness and stable near-top ranking, while the glass laminate had the least variability in four of five modes, but at lower frequencies. These results indicate tha…

title: Social uncertainty and school disengagement: a theoretical framework of early school leaving in precarious family contexts
abstract: Romania has had the highest rate of early leaving from education and training in the European Union for several years, with the burden concentrated in rural areas and among Roma young people. Existing explanations attribute early school leaving to poverty, family disadvantage, institutional exclusion or individual disengagement, but they say little about why families with similar resources make different educational choices when their futures are unpredictable. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes that social uncertainty, defined as the reduced predictability of a household's material circumstances and of the returns to schooling, is analytically distinct from the level of deprivation and from neighbouring concepts such as precarity, vulnerability, risk and exclusion. Using a staged procedure for building conceptual frameworks, we derive a model in which uncertainty affects school engagement through four mechanisms: the contraction of temporal horizons, family stress, the reallocation of children's time to care and work, and the responsiveness of schools. We specify five moderators, including family resilience resources and student agency, set out eight testable propositions with their boundary conditions, and identify the evidence that would contradict them. We distinguish absenteeism, including its voluntary and involuntary forms, from disengagement, dropout and early …

title: An Intelligent Decision-Making Methodology Based on a New Fermatean Fuzzy Similarity Measure: A Case Study of Building Site Preference
abstract: Intelligent-driven decision-making through soft computing tools like Fermatean fuzzy sets has proven to be effective even in the presence of imprecision. The Fermatean fuzzy similarity measure is one of the avenues through which intelligent-based decision-making is made. Various methods of Fermatean fuzzy similarity measure have been fashioned; however, many of them are deficient in terms of formulation, precision, and compliance with the similarity conditions. These deficiencies can result in faulty decision-making with a concomitant effect during implementation. To this end, this paper presents a new approach of Fermatean fuzzy similarity measure, which outperformed the extant measures by comparison. Equally, the new approach evidently satisfies the similarity’s conditions. To test the application potential of the new similarity approach, it is used to discuss the complexity of locating a prefer location for an estate building based on TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution). In addition, a comparative analysis of the new approach in conjunction with the extant ones based on TOPSIS is presented, and the new approach unmistakably shows precision and reliability over the extant approaches. The flexibility of the new approach of intelligent-based decision-making qualifies its application in other complex decision-making scenarios.
venue: International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems

title: Heterogeneous impact of digital technology adoption on ambidextrous innovation: the moderating role of environmental uncertainty and industry competition
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore how digital technology adoption differentially affects the two dimensions of ambidextrous innovation. From the perspective of resource crowding-out and empowering effects, the authors analyze the impacts of digital technology adoption on exploratory and exploitative innovation, as well as the moderating effects of environmental uncertainty and industry competition. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a fixed-effects model with a sample of China’s Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed companies from 2008 to 2024. Findings There is a U-shaped relationship between digital technology adoption and exploratory innovation, while a positive linear relationship exists between digital technology adoption and exploitative innovation. The U-shaped relationship is flatter for firms under high environmental uncertainty and steeper for those facing fierce industry competition. Environmental uncertainty and industry competition weaken the positive relationship between digital technology adoption and exploitative innovation. Originality/value This study deepens the theoretical understanding of how digital technology adoption differently influences exploratory and exploitative innovation, thereby addressing ongoing debates in the literature.

title: Perpendicular transport in isotropic magnetic turbulence. The role of stochastic drifts
abstract: In the context of cosmic ray propagation in a turbulent magnetic field, transport perpendicular to the mean field plays an important role in a variety of situations of physical interest. Numerical simulations of test particles in isotropic turbulence with a guide field show that, for r_L<L_c, the parallel and perpendicular diffusion coefficients scale differently with energy, so that the corresponding ratio D_⊥/D_∥ increases with energy. Several attempts have been made to address this phenomenon, but no consensus theoretical understanding has yet been reached. We used test-particle numerical simulations of particle transport in synthetic turbulence over a broad energy range to establish a general trend of the perpendicular diffusion coefficient. We also provide a theoretical description of our findings based on an extension of the nonlinear guiding-center theory that includes stochastic drifts. The numerical simulations of isotropic turbulence are based on a wavelet method that allows us to reproduce turbulence over ∼ 6-7 orders of magnitude in wavenumber. This wide wavenumber range is reflected in a correspondingly wide energy range for test particles. The theoretical part presents a novel description of perpendicular transport based on autocorrelation functions of turbulent magnetic fields. It describes how particles diffuse perpendicular to the field lines through a combinat…

title: Multi-objective optimization of resource allocation and patrol routing for a maritime patrol and rescue system considering spatial risk distribution
abstract: Timely and effective search and rescue (SAR) services are crucial for ensuring maritime safety. Proactive patrol operations provide an effective means of improving the response capability and resource utilization efficiency of maritime patrol and rescue systems. However, existing maritime rescue systems mainly rely on fixed rescue bases and cannot fully account for spatial variations in maritime risk during resource allocation. To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-objective optimization approach for a maritime patrol and rescue system considering spatial risk distribution. Historical maritime accident data and AIS data are integrated, and a convolutional neural network–multilayer perceptron (CNN–MLP) model is developed to estimate the risk index of each service subarea. Based on this, a multi-objective optimization model is formulated for maritime patrol and rescue operations, integrating patrol-point location, SAR ship task allocation, and patrol routing into a unified framework. Considering the large continuous search space for patrol-point locations, the varying number of decision variables, and the complex combinatorial optimization characteristics, a hybrid optimization algorithm combining fuzzy C-means clustering and simulated annealing-based variable neighborhood search (FCM-SA-VNS) is proposed. Numerical experiments are conducted in the South China Sea, an…

title: Stochastic Mortality Modelling for Small and Data-Scarce Populations: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Stochastic mortality models developed for large national populations face challenges when applied to small populations with volatile death counts, short data series, and potentially biased parameter estimates. This systematic review synthesizes modelling strategies for small and data-scarce populations from an actuarial perspective, examining uncertainty quantification, model evaluation, and remaining research gaps. Following PRISMA 2020, records were identified through Semantic Scholar and citation snowballing. Of 40 unique records screened, 18 studies published between 2011 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria; included journal articles appeared in Scopus-indexed journals. Data were extracted using a structured form and synthesized thematically. Five categories emerged: reference-population and two-population models, credibility and Bayesian methods, analyses of small-population bias, subnational and small-area methods, and hybrids incorporating machine learning. Most approaches stabilized projections by borrowing information from larger, related populations. However, the reviewed machine-learning studies seldom reported forecast intervals, and none of the included studies used Southeast Asian data. The evidence supports selecting an appropriate reference population and reporting distinct sources of uncertainty separately when modelling mortality in small populations. By con…

title: Stress hyperglycemia ratio-integrated index and 28-day mortality in sepsis: a dual-cohort study
abstract: Background Stress hyperglycemia is common in sepsis, but admission glucose is influenced by antecedent glycemia. The stress hyperglycemia ratio-integrated index (SHRI) combines hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)-normalized glycemia with serum potassium. We examined the association between early SHRI and 28-day mortality in adults with sepsis. Methods This retrospective dual-cohort study included 4,495 adults with Sepsis-3-defined sepsis from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database and 320 patients from an independent hospital validation cohort. SHRI was calculated using HbA1c measured from 90 days before to 24 hours after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and glucose and potassium measured within 6 hours before or after ICU admission; the same exposure definition was applied in both cohorts. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, previously diagnosed diabetes, and day-1 Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, and restricted cubic splines characterized dose–response associations. Results Within 28 days, 903 patients (20.1%) died in MIMIC-IV and 64 (20.0%) died in the validation cohort. In MIMIC-IV, the adjusted hazard ratio per 0.1 increase in SHRI was 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04–1.11). The corresponding hazard ratio in the validation cohort was 2.00 (95% CI…

title: DIGITAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN AND INTEGRATED EVALUATION-CONSTRUCTION: PARADIGM RECONSTRUCTION AND PRACTICAL EXPLORATION OF "INTERCULTURAL COMMUNICATION" COURSES IN HIGHER EDUCATION
abstract: Addressing critical bottlenecks in traditional intercultural communication instruction—specifically, fabricated communicative contexts, the decoupling of teaching and assessment, and superficial technology integration—this study introduces a synergistic mechanism of "data-intelligence driving" and "evaluation–construction integration" to construct a data-driven precision teaching framework for college foreign language courses. Adopting a backward design approach, the study reconstructs a four-dimensional curricular objective matrix comprising language proficiency, digital-intelligence literacy, intercultural communicative competence, and comprehensive qualities. By deconstructing typical tasks in international professions, it develops a multimodal digital case repository and a three-phase, five-step virtual-real hybrid training chain ("Orient–Instruct–Practice–Explore–Evaluate"). Furthermore, a tripartite attainment assessment model integrating process evaluation, summative evaluation, and value-added evaluation is established. Drawing upon multiple rounds of pedagogical implementation at Zhejiang Yuexiu University, this paper summarizes the implementation pathways, core mechanisms, and preliminary observations of the proposed paradigm, while reflecting on its inherent constraints. This research aims to provide a transferable operational framework for the digital-intelligence t…

title: An integrated gut phage catalogue of nonhuman primates reveals functional adaptation to host ecology and evolutionary link to humans
abstract: Abstract Nonhuman primates (NHPs), the closest evolutionary relatives of humans, are pivotal models for biomedical and ecological research. Gut phage are recognized as critical modulators of gut microbial communities; however, comprehensive insight into gut phage of NHPs is lacking. We used gut metagenomes spanning 25 NHP species and constructed an integrated gut phage catalogue (IGPC) comprising 11 389 nonredundant phage genomes. Our results revealed that the composition and function of NHP gut phage were significantly influenced by host clade, dietary niche and lifestyle. Host clade exerted a stronger influence than dietary niche on gut phage diversity. The lifestyle of NHPs influenced gut phage diversity and altered auxiliary metabolic gene profiles for different NHP species. Comparatively, 78.5% of IGPC phages were detected in human guts, with higher prevalence in nonindustrialized human guts. crAss-like phage—the most prevalent human-associated phage—were abundant in NHP guts, while exhibiting distinct evolutionary differences from crAss-like phage of humans. These findings comprehensively characterize the gut phageome of NHPs, revealing NHP host-driven and environment-driven functional adaptations, and provide an evolutionary understanding of the gut phageome between NHPs and humans.
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: Social prescribing link worker voices through the lens of proportionate universalism
abstract: Purpose Drawing on testimony from frontline Social Prescribing Link workers (SPLWs) in England, this article analyses their perspectives and argues for increased resources at the community level, awareness of social determinants and stronger link worker identity. Design/methodology/approach This ethically approved small-scale qualitative study undertook interviews with eight SPLWs, employed in two different locations across the North of England, that encompassed both urban and rural locations. Findings The study produced rich testimony from their direct experience of SPLWs, which were mapped, against the regional determinants of health, incorporating Proportionate Universalism principles. Respondents felt that more could be done to support the development of a stronger identity for link workers. Importantly, the issue of resources, particularly in areas of deprivation where available services may be more limited, emerged as a strong theme. Originality/value The analysis suggests that resourcing is crucial for the success or otherwise of SPLWs input. The adoption of Proportionate Universalism (Marmot) in social prescribing and beyond could improve the resource allocation link workers have to support people in communities and raise awareness of working on the wider determinants of health and wellbeing, thus contributing to the sustainability of Social Prescribing and the SPLWs ro…

title: Drivers of zoonotic spillover at human–domestic animal–wildlife interfaces: a multi-species model incorporating wildlife chronic stress
abstract: Abstract Zoonotic disease emergence at the wildlife–domestic animal–human interface results from a complex interplay of ecological, physiological and anthropogenic factors. Here, we have developed a multi-environment, multi-host compartmental model to identify key drivers of spillover risk across urban, rural and natural environments. The framework incorporates heterogeneous host populations, inter-species contacts and host movement, and includes wildlife chronic stress as one factor influencing susceptibility, transmissibility and recovery. Sensitivity analyses show that domestic animal populations at agricultural interfaces strongly amplify spillover risk through their recovery dynamics and per-contact transmission probabilities, while within-wildlife transmission across environments also shapes system dynamics. Chronic stress effects can further increase spillover risk, and the model indicates that reducing wildlife stress alongside improving domestic animal health and management can markedly lower the likelihood of cross-species transmission. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that susta…

title: A multi-class anomaly signal classification method for fixed-point deformation combining PSO–VMD multiscale adaptive sample entropy and ALO–SOM model
abstract: To address the challenge of identifying five predefined categories of disturbance-related abnormal signals (lightning interference, artificial blasting, power-supply failure, collapse-related events, and meteorological anomalies) in fixed-point deformation monitoring, this paper proposes an identification framework integrating parameter-optimized variational mode decomposition (VMD), multiscale entropy analysis, and an intelligent classification model. Firstly, particle swarm optimization is adopted to adaptively determine the mode number and penalty factor for VMD to realize adaptive signal decomposition. Then, an adaptive sample entropy algorithm with self-adjustable similarity thresholds is applied to extract multiscale complexity-oriented features from each decomposed modal component. Finally, the ant lion optimizer optimizes the competitive-layer topology and training hyperparameters of a self-organizing map network to build the target classifier. Comparative experiments against 18 widely-used classification models (including AdaBoost ensemble learners, generalized regression neural networks, long short-term memory networks, and gated recurrent units) are carried out on the real-world observation dataset from the Yixian seismic station. The experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive classification performance for the five anomaly categories.…

title: A multi-database bibliometric study of cancer-related depression: hotspots and emerging trends
abstract: Background Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that affects cancer patients and survivors, exerting a persistent negative impact on their lives. This study aims to investigate the current status and potential trends of depression in cancer research from 2015 to June 2026. Methods The publications related to cancer-related depression were retrieved from the core database of Web of Science and Scopus, analyzed using CiteSpace and VOSviewer software, and a corresponding visual network diagram was generated for display. Results Annual output increased overall from 1,359 publications in 2015 to 3,275 in 2025, with fluctuations between years; the 1,588 publications for 2026 represent an incomplete year. The United States is the country with the largest number of publications and is at the center of international cooperation. Harvard Medical School in the United States has been the leading institution in terms of both the volume of published papers and the significance of its research contributions. Christine Miaskowski emerged as the author with the greatest output, while Jennifer S. Temel’s work achieved the highest average citation count. Among the journals, Supportive Care in Cancer published the most articles, whereas Psycho-Oncology garnered the greatest number of citations. Frequently occurring keywords in the research included “depression”, “quality of life”, and “anxiet…

title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk
abstract: Objective Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells. Methods Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R. Results BAFF-R on CD20 − (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797–0.926, P = 7.17 × 10 −5 ) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843–0.961, P = 1.57 × 10 −3 ) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs. Conclusion This multi-omics genetic-toxico…

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis deciphers the molecular mechanisms underlying the characteristic volatile flavor of Meishan pork
abstract: Abstract Background The Meishan pig is a celebrated indigenous Chinese swine breed renowned for its distinctive flavor profile. However, the specific signature flavor compounds and the molecular mechanisms underlying their formation remain largely uncharacterized. This study aimed to comprehensively profile the volatile flavor compounds across five pig breeds and decipher the molecular basis of the characteristic flavor of Meishan pork. Results Comparative analysis combining electronic nose, headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), and relative odor activity value calculations revealed that Meishan pork contained significantly higher levels of four key aroma compounds: hexanal, nonanal, 2-pentylfuran, and (E,E)-2,4-nonadienal. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses identified oleic acid and α-linolenic acid as critical precursors and highlighted the high expression of the arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase gene ( ALOX5 ) in Meishan pigs. Heating experiments confirmed that these fatty acids yield characteristic flavor compounds upon thermal oxidation. Furthermore, functional studies demonstrated that ALOX5 catalyzes the conversion of these precursors into flavor aldehydes. Conclusions The distinctive flavor of Meishan pork is associated with a dual mechanism: thermal oxidation of abundant precursors during cook…
venue: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology

title: Management Challenge in a Known case of Chronic Kidney Disease on Immuno-Suppressive Agents Now Presenting with Acute Viral Hepatitis
abstract: Background: Tubulo-Interstitial Nephritis (TIN) is a nonsuppurative inflammatory disease of the kidney interstitium and if chronic, almost always progresses to Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). Hemodialysis is frequently performed as renal replacement therapy. However, to treat the underlying cause of CKD, like in autoimmune cases immunosuppressive agents are needed in addition. Patients undergoing hemodialysis are at higher risk of developing blood borne infections such as HBV and HCV. Due to impaired immunity in CKD, TIN patients on immunosuppressive therapy becoming HBV infected, warrants a clear treatment limitation like withholding of immunosuppressants as the viral replication soars high, increasing the chances of developing chronicity and viral mutants. Anti-viral drugs are very helpful for HBV infection control in these patients. The purpose of this case report is to draw the clinicians' attention towards early diagnosis and management of HBV infection among such groups of CKD patients, as it can cause higher morbidity and mortality, if not appropriately addressed. Case Presentation: We report here a female of 37 years age suffering from CKD due to TIN, priorly on Maintenance Hemodialysis (MHD) for 3 months followed by immune-suppressive agents for next 3 months with evident clinical improvement. She suddenly developed silent deep jaundice and health deterioration with hepa…
venue: Chattagram Maa-O-Shishu Hospital Medical College Journal

title: The Role of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) Curriculum Management in Improving the Quality of Islamic Educational Institutions
abstract: Curriculum management in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) plays a strategic role in aligning academic achievement with students’ religious and moral development. This study examined its contribution to the quality of Islamic educational institutions through four management functions: planning, organization, implementation, and evaluation. A qualitative literature review was conducted, with relevant sources examined and analyzed descriptively to identify relationships between curriculum management functions and educational quality indicators. The synthesis indicated that planning aligned with students’ needs and institutional vision establishes clear instructional direction. Effective organization facilitates resource utilization and collaboration among educators, while innovative and contextualized instruction supports student engagement and the understanding and application of Islamic values. Systematic evaluation informs instructional improvement and continuous quality development. Together, these findings emphasize that curriculum management requires coordinated implementation across all four functions. The study contributes a synthesis of their complementary roles and provides a basis for strengthening instructional quality, cultivating students’ moral character, and developing adaptive Islamic educational institutions committed to continuous improvement.

title: Designing employee wellness programs in hotels: a prioritized resource framework
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how employee wellness programs (EWPs) function in high-demand service environments, addressing the limitation that prior research assumes wellness resources automatically improve employee well-being. Design/methodology/approach A four-stage mixed-methods design was adopted, including literature review, expert content validation, Fuzzy Delphi analysis with 28 experts and a survey of 507 hotel employees analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings A six-dimensional EWP framework comprising 26 validated indicators was confirmed. The results show that EWP dimensions are not functionally equivalent but operate within a structured system. Organizational resources, particularly healthcare support and health management policies, play a foundational role, while other dimensions contribute to recovery and longer-term development. The findings suggest that the effectiveness of wellness initiatives depends on employees’ capacity to use available resources. Research limitations/implications By integrating conservation of resources theory with the well-being-as-capability perspective, this study reframes EWPs as a capability-enabling system that emphasizes resource usability rather than mere provision. Practically, hotels should prioritize foundational organizational resources before expanding other wellness initiatives, using…
venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: The Effect of Instagram Social Media Marketing and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions of H'zhazu MSME Products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang
abstract: Social media marketing and product quality are important considerations in consumer purchasing decisions, particularly for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operating in competitive markets. However, further empirical investigation is needed to understand how these factors are associated with purchasing decisions in the context of traditional-snack MSMEs. This study examines the individual and joint associations of Instagram social media marketing and product quality with purchase decisions among consumers of H'Zhazu MSME products in East Ciputat, South Tangerang. A quantitative cross-sectional design with an associative approach was employed. The study population comprised 348 consumers, from which 78 respondents were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics version 29. The results revealed that Instagram social media marketing had a positive and statistically significant association with purchase decisions (B = 0.512; β = 0.437; t = 4.103; p < 0.001). Product quality also demonstrated a positive and statistically significant association (B = 0.541; β = 0.465; t = 4.371; p < 0.001). Furthermore, the regression model was statistically significant (F = 110.734; p < 0.001), with an R² of 0.747, indicating that the two predictors jointly accounted for 74.7% of t…
venue: International Journal of Management Science and Application

title: Beyond completeness
Regulatory fragmentation in bank–insurance conglomerates: a qualitative index for cross-regime supervision
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how differences across accounting, banking, insurance and group supervision affect the interpretation of capital strength and risk capacity in bank–insurance conglomerates. Regulatory fragmentation is treated as an interpretive and supervisory problem rather than proof of financial weakness. A structured method is developed through which observable differences can be identified from public evidence and compared across financial groups. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative documentary method is applied to laws, technical standards, supervisory guidance, consultation papers, enforcement reviews and corporate reports. A Regulatory Fragmentation Risk Index (RFRI) is developed across four pillars: measurement, capital aggregation, disclosure and supervisory coordination. Each pillar is classified through structured criteria and a common evidence hierarchy. The index is applied to 30 financial conglomerates across six regulatory environments and the results are examined through descriptive comparison and external plausibility assessment. Findings The greatest divergence is found where accounting and prudential valuations are compared, sector capital rules are combined at group level and related disclosures cannot be reconciled directly. Higher scores are also found where supervisory responsibility is divided across jurisdictions. L…

title: Financial Constraints and Perceived Bakery Operation Competency Among Public Senior High School Students
abstract: This study examined the financial constraints and perceived Bakery Operation competency of Grade 11 students at Tuy Senior High School during School Year 2026–2027. Using a descriptive-correlational quantitative design and total enumeration, the study involved 57 students. A researcher-made questionnaire assessed access to ingredients and baking materials, availability of baking tools and equipment, transportation and related school expenses, family financial support, and perceived competency in baking skills, equipment handling and operation, food safety and sanitation, and product preparation and presentation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson product–moment correlation. Financial constraints were generally manageable, although access to tools and equipment represented the most evident resource challenge and family support was strong. Students rated their competency highly in all four domains. Selected differences according to sex were significant, whereas differences by age, family income, and monthly allowance were generally nonsignificant. None of the financial-constraint dimensions showed a statistically significant relationship with perceived Bakery Operation competency. The proposed BAKE-SUPPORT Program addresses resource access and practical skills reinforcement. The findings concern self-reported c…
venue: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice

title: FinTech, transparency, governance and financial inclusion: channels to sustainable development goals in Gulf Cooperation Council banking
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how banking digitalization and FinTech development advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) banks, focusing on transparency, governance and financial inclusion as the channels linking FinTech to sustainability. Design/methodology/approach To explore the relationship between digitalization and SDGs in GCC banks, the authors construct a FinTech Engagement Index (FEI) and a Sustainability Engagement Index (SEI) for 69 GCC banks over 2020–2023. A GLS regression model estimates this relationship, controlling for bank-specific characteristics and macroeconomic conditions. Findings The results of this study reveal a significant positive relationship between FinTech adoption and banking sector sustainability, demonstrating that advanced digitalization enhances transparency, governance and financial inclusion while accelerating progress toward SDGs. Institutional characteristics play a meaningful role in this relationship. These results are valuable for policymakers and regulators aiming to leverage FinTech for sustainable banking development. Practical implications Policymakers should foster FinTech innovation while ensuring risk management and consumer protection. Bank leaders should use FinTech as a strategic sustainability tool, prioritizing digital platforms for green products, automated reporting and envi…

title: Out-of-pocket expenditure for neurosurgical care in Uganda: quantifying financial catastrophe and identifying policy pathways to universal health coverage
abstract: Background Out-of-pocket payments remain the primary source of healthcare financing in many low- and middle-income countries, frequently resulting in catastrophic and impoverishing expenditures. Neurosurgical care is particularly costly due to substantial direct and indirect expenses borne by patients and caregivers, typically with little or no financial protection. This study quantifies these OOP costs, estimates the prevalence of catastrophic and impoverishing health expenditures, and examines their socioeconomic impact to inform equitable surgical financing policies. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study at the two main Ugandan public neurosurgical centers - Mulago National Referral Hospital, Kampala, and Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital, Mbarara. Consecutive patients with confirmed neurosurgical diagnoses were enrolled at discharge or within two weeks post-discharge. Structured surveys captured sociodemographic, clinical and cost data. OOP health payments were direct medical plus direct non-medical payments; total economic burden added indirect costs. Catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) was OOP payments exceeding 10% of annual household consumption expenditure (World Bank) or 40% of it after food costs (WHO). Impoverishment was the change in poverty headcount against the $3.00/person/day line (2021 purchasing power parity). Data was analyzed using R 4.4.2. Ethica…

title: Sharia financial technology organizations and ethical responsibility for sustainable development: a moral economy perspective
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine whether the ethical responsibility of Sharia financial technology (Sharia fintech) can be normatively justified rather than assumed on the basis of its religious identity or developmental claims. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a normative–conceptual ethical analysis that evaluates Sharia fintech as a morally accountable financial system using two normative benchmarks: the objectives of Sharia (maqasid al-Sharia) and the ethical vision embedded in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Findings The analysis develops a conceptual evaluation framework structured around four ethical tension fields: inclusion versus digital exclusion, social objectives versus profit orientation, technological efficiency versus data ethics and accountability and sustainability commitments versus symbolic alignment. These tensions show that ethical legitimacy in Sharia fintech is neither inherent nor guaranteed by formal compliance, but conditionally achieved through continuous moral negotiation between innovation, market pressures and social responsibility. Research limitations/implications This study is conceptual in nature and does not empirically assess specific fintech platforms or governance practices. Future research may operationalise the proposed framework through qualitative case studies or institutional analysis to examine how Sharia fintec…
venue: International Journal of Ethics and Systems

title: How financial constraints influence the preferences for tourism destinations
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how financial constraints influence preferences for natural (vs cultural) destinations. It further investigates the mediating role of psychological distress and the moderating role of perceived economic mobility in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential multistudy design comprising eight studies (n = 1,874), including three main studies and five supplementary studies, was used to examine the effect of financial constraints on destination preferences and to test the underlying mechanism and boundary condition. Findings Financial constraints shape preferences for natural (vs cultural) destinations through psychological distress. Perceived economic mobility determines the direction of this self-regulatory response: financial constraints increase preferences for natural (vs cultural) destinations when perceived economic mobility is high but increase preferences for cultural (vs natural) destinations when perceived economic mobility is low. Originality/value This research advances the literature on financial conditions and destination decision-making by shifting attention from objective financial conditions to subjective financial perceptions. It identifies psychological distress as the mechanism linking financial constraints to destination preferences and perceived economic mobility as a boundary condition that determines the …

title: Financial stress and mental well-being among older adults: an extended conceptual framework of financial vulnerability, self-efficacy and social support
abstract: Purpose Population ageing has emerged as an important social and economic phenomenon, creating increasing challenges for the financial and psychological well-being of older adults. Although ageing is generally associated with retirement, declining earning capacity and increasing healthcare requirements, the financial consequences of these changes are not experienced uniformly. Existing literature has examined financial stress, healthcare expenditure, financial dependence, social support and mental well-being among older adults independently; however, the theoretical mechanisms explaining why some older adults experience stronger psychological consequences of financial stress than others remain under-theorised. This study aims to propose an integrated framework outlining various factors of financial stress and mental well being of older adults. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper combines Life Course Theory, Hobfoll theory, the Stress Process Model, Social Cognitive Theory and conservation of resources (COR) theory to propose a moderated-mediation model connecting financial vulnerability with financial stress and mental well-being with psychological and protective resources as moderators. Findings The proposed framework incorporates healthcare expenditure, retirement-income insecurity, financial dependence, debt and digital financial challenges as core sources of f…

title: Social support, financial threat, psychological distress, burnout and nursing clinical competence in mental health courses: self-efficacy and professional identity moderators
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the psychosocial factors related to burnout and perceived clinical competence among undergraduate nursing students, with particular attention to perceived social support, psychological distress and financial threat, and whether self-efficacy and professional identity moderated key associations. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 351 third- and fourth-year nursing students at Jerash University, Jordan. Perceived social support, psychological distress, financial threat, self-efficacy, professional identity, burnout and perceived clinical competence were assessed using established self-report measures. Four moderated regression models were estimated, adjusting for age, years of nursing experience, GPA, sleep and internet use. Predictors and moderators were mean-centered, interaction terms were tested and simple slopes were examined. Findings Perceived social support was negatively associated with burnout and positively associated with perceived clinical competence. Psychological distress was positively associated with burnout and negatively associated with clinical competence, while financial threat was positively associated with burnout. Four interaction terms were statistically significant. Financial threat × self-efficacy (B = 0.055, p < 0.001) and financial threat × professional identity (B =…

title: Constructing a Diversified Medical Insurance Financing System from the Perspective of Health Industry Transformation
abstract: Health industry transformation is changing the socioeconomic conditions under which medical insurance systems operate. This study examines the relationship between established financing mechanisms and evolving health service models, including digital health integration, value-based care, and the expansion of preventive and personalized interventions. A systems analysis of institutional design, fiscal sustainability, and stakeholder alignment identifies structural tensions between existing insurance arrangements and emerging health system priorities. On this basis, the study proposes a diversified financing framework that combines innovations in risk pooling, dynamic contribution mechanisms, and cross-sectoral funding instruments to strengthen equity, adaptability, and long-term sustainability. The analysis emphasizes that effective diversification requires changes in governance, accountability, and intertemporal resource allocation, as well as additional funding sources, to support health system transformation.

title: Housing Yields
abstract: Abstract We build a granular data set of residential property yields using rental and sale listings from a major German real estate platform. With more than 1.5 million property-level rent-to-price ratios, we document a novel heterogeneity puzzle. About two-fifths of yield dispersion remains unexplained after controlling for extensive observable property characteristics and postal code-level time-varying factors using fixed effects. When we absorb finer neighborhood amenities through richer fixed effects, the unexplained share remains close to one-third. This evidence points to the importance of investors’ beliefs and preferences—rather than several alternative explanations we test—as sources of heterogeneity in risk premia.

title: Digital twins for health and safety management in construction: a systematic review
abstract: Purpose Despite regulatory and technological advances, construction health and safety (H&S) management remains hindered by poor hazard visibility, fragmented information and reactive decision-making. Digital twins (DTs) offer a proactive, integrated and data-driven approach by connecting physical construction environments with continuously updated virtual representations. However, evidence remains fragmented regarding how DT applications, enabling conditions and implementation challenges interact to improve H&S outcomes. This study aims to systematically review and synthesise evidence on DT-enabled H&S management during the construction stage. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, identifying 26 peer-reviewed journal articles from the Scopus and Web of Science databases. Bibliometric analysis and qualitative content synthesis were used to examine research trends, DT applications, implementation enablers, challenges and future research directions. Findings DTs are mainly applied to workforce monitoring, hazard detection, safety training, risk prediction and decision support. Implementation success relies on technological, organisational, human and institutional enablers, but is hindered by interoperability issues, data governance gaps, skill shortages, …

Hapten Design, Antibody Engineering, and Immunochromatographic Application: A Rapid Fluorescent Strip for Acephate Residue Detection
abstract: Abstract Acephate (AP) is one of the most extensively used organophosphorus insecticides worldwide. Its high water solubility and environmental mobility result in frequent residue detection in agricultural products, posing health risks to consumers. In this study, a specific monoclonal antibody (mAb) against AP was generated through computer technology-assisted hapten design. A recombinant monoclonal antibody (R-mAb) was further obtained by gene sequencing and recombinant expression, exhibiting a higher affinity constant (7.29 × 109 L/mol) than the parental mAb (5.60 × 109 L/mol). Using R-mAb as the recognition reagent, a fluorescent immunochromatographic assay (FICA) strip was established. Matrix matched calibration curves for lettuce, orange, Flammulina filiformis, and soybean yielded IC50 values of 2.5, 2.3, 2.0, and 24.0 μg/kg, respectively. Recoveries at 5 and 50 μg/kg were 84.9%–102.5%, agreeing well with liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. The strip provides a convenient, efficient, and reliable tool for rapid screening of AP residues in agricultural products.

title: THE INFLUENCE OF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND SELF-EFFICACY OF TEACHERS ON UNIVERSAL DESIGN FOR LEARNING PRACTICES IN THE ENHANCED K TO 12 CURRICULUM
abstract: This study examined the influence of teachers’ professional development and self-efficacy on the implementation of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) practices under the Enhanced K to 12 Curriculum. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were gathered from 112 public school teachers in the Division of Panabo City, Davao del Norte, who had participated in the Revised K to 12 Curriculum seminar. Adapted survey instruments measured professional development, teacher self-efficacy, and UDL practices. Data were analyzed using weighted means, Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple regression. Teachers rated professional development as high across student variability (M = 3.80), peer support (M = 4.25), administrative support (M = 3.75), collaboration (M = 3.67), and training (M = 3.81). Self-efficacy was very high in student engagement (M = 4.33), instructional strategies (M = 4.38), and classroom management (M = 4.36). UDL practices were also very high in engagement (M = 4.23), representation (M = 4.25), and action and expression (M = 4.25). Professional development was significantly related to UDL practices (r = .643, p < .001), as was self-efficacy (r = .706, p < .001). Regression results showed that collaboration and peer support were significant predictors among professional development domains, while classroom-management efficacy was the significa…

title: Perceived mobility affordability and welfare vulnerability among Malaysia’s B40 households during targeted diesel subsidy reform
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how perceived mobility affordability and adequacy, community participation and housing affordability are associated with subjective welfare among Malaysia’s B40 households during targeted diesel subsidy reform. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional convenience sample of 400 respondents from B40 households in the Greater Klang Valley was analysed using reliability and factor analyses, Pearson correlations, ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors, demographic adjustment and vulnerability-profile comparisons. Findings The joint low/neutral mobility–low/neutral community profile represented 35.3 % of respondents and had the lowest observed mean subjective welfare. Its mean was significantly lower than those of the two profiles with favourable community participation and did not differ significantly from that of the profile combining favourable mobility with low/neutral community participation. Practical implications Mobility and community-participation indicators can complement administrative, income, transport-expenditure, compensation and accessibility records in welfare assessment and policy targeting. Originality/value The study brings perceived transport adequacy, housing affordability and community participation into a single welfare-vulnerability framework for Malaysian B40 households.

title: China’s revised Maritime Code and vessel-source oil pollution liability: innovations, gaps, and reform pathways
abstract: Vessel-source oil pollution remains a central concern in marine environmental governance because oil spills may spread rapidly, persist in the marine environment, and cause serious ecological and socio-economic harm. China has traditionally regulated vessel-source oil pollution through rules dispersed across civil, environmental, maritime, insurance, and administrative law. The revised Maritime Code of the People’s Republic of China, adopted in 2025 and effective from 1 May 2026, introduces China’s first dedicated chapter on Liability for Oil Pollution Damage from Ships. Distinct from prior scholarship that primarily analyzed draft proposals or focused narrowly on specific compensation mechanisms like the CLC vs. domestic fund models, this article offers an incremental contribution by conducting a comprehensive assessment based on the final promulgated text. It proposes a phased reform pathway to address emerging uncertainties and provides forward-looking risk assessments regarding non-spilling vessels in collisions, alternative fuels, and ecological damage valuation. By evaluating the finalized chapter against the 1992 Civil Liability Convention, as amended, the 2001 Bunkers Convention, and China’s pre-existing domestic framework, it argues that the revised Code advances systematic integration by clarifying liable parties and defences, establishing strict liability, placing co…

title: Effect of the Stock Market on Standard of Living in Nigeria. An ARDL Analysis
abstract: This study examines the effect of stock market performance on Nigeria’s standard of living over the period 1993–2023. The HDI served as a proxy for the standard of living, while Market Capitalization, Number of Listed Companies, Turnover Ratio, and Traded Value represented indicators of stock market performance. Annual time-series data were obtained from the World Development Indicators (WDI) and UNDP. The analytical techniques included descriptive statistics, Augmented Dickey–Fuller (ADF) unit root tests, Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds cointegration tests, ARDL estimation, and post-estimation diagnostics. The ADF results revealed a mixture of stationary and non-stationary variables, integrated at I(0) and I(1). The ARDL bounds test confirmed the existence of a long-run relationship between HDI and stock market performance indicators. The long-run ARDL estimates showed that Market Capitalization and Turnover Ratio had positive but statistically insignificant effects on HDI, while Traded Value exhibited a negative but insignificant effect. Conversely, the Number of Listed Companies demonstrated a statistically significant negative effect on HDI in the long run. The study concluded that the development of the Nigerian stock market has not yet translated into tangible improvements in human development, and recommended policy reforms aimed at tax incentives and procur…

title: P-80: Role of an education nurse in a low-resource health care service: challenges and observations
abstract: Abstract Introduction In low-resource health care settings, patients education is often limited due to heavy workload, staff shortages, and lack of educational tools leading to poor understanding of disease and treatment adherence. Objectives To explore the role of an education nurse in a low-resource healthcare service. Methods An observational study with purposive sampling was conducted over one month at the Mother and Child Center of the Chantal Biya Foundation. The study involved the educational nurse and type 1 diabetes patients with their families. Data was collected through direct observation of the nurse’s daily educational activities. Results The education nurse played both in-hospital and community roles. In the hospital, she provided simplified explanations of diseases, promoted preventive practices and treatment adherence, offered psychological support and trained healthcare staff. community activities focused on outreach and health education. Positive factors included the availability of educational videos, regular patient attendance, increasing participation in training, and improved health information systems. However, challenges included the lack of community health workers, community insecurity, limited time due to high patient load, staff shortages and difficulties in insulin supply. Conclusions Education nurse plays a crucial role in improving patient knowled…

title: P-165: Transforming youth diabetes care: the role of Tellmi in providing digital mental health support in Somerset National Health Service, United Kingdom
abstract: Abstract Introduction Youth with diabetes experience substantial physical and mental health challenges. Tellmi is a novel mental health app providing unlimited, anonymous, peer support moderated by AI and human oversight, with real-time counsellor intervention for high-risk content. The app was adapted to include diabetes-specific support, including direct access to the Somerset NHS Children’s Diabetes Nurses’ Helpline. Objectives To explore the lived experiences of youth with diabetes using Tellmi. Methods A mixed-methods sequential design was used. First, a diabetes-specific Tellmi survey was disseminated through Somerset paediatric diabetes clinicians, general practitioners, and local support services, resulting in responses from 32 youth with diabetes. Participants were invited to take part in interviews, with seven interviews conducted until data saturation was reached. Quantitative data were stratified by median age and analysed using chi-square and t-tests. Qualitative data were thematically analysed using Gibbs’s framework. Results Quantitative findings demonstrated high rates of mental health difficulties, including anxiety (68.8%), depression (40.6%), panic attacks (43.8%), sleep problems (43.8%), and suicidal thoughts (34.4%). Less than half (42.9%) had informed their diabetes clinic about mental health impacts. While 53.6% had attempted to access support, others had…

title: One Market, Twenty-Seven VAT Systems and Counting: Europe Simplifies Everything but Its Biggest Tax
abstract: In this Column, the author argues that VAT fragmentation remains a major obstacle to the EU single market, particularly for SMEs, which face high compliance costs from dealing with different VAT rules, registrations and digital reporting systems across Member States. She calls for much deeper VAT harmonization, ultimately proposing one EU VAT system with a single VAT number, common rules and administration, and a unified tax court, especially as the EU prepares for further enlargement.

title: The Interest Rate and Stock Market Performance in Nigeria (1981- 2024)
abstract: The study investigated the interest rate and stock market performance in Nigeria for the Period 1981- 2024. The specific objectives of the study were to analyze the impact of real interest rate on stock market performance in Nigeria, to ascertain the impact of nominal interest rate on stock market performance in Nigeria, and to examine the impact of monetary policy rate on stock market performance in Nigeria. The study adopted ex-post facto design and employed the Auto Regressive Distributed (ARDL) to estimate the model. The major finding of the study Real Interest Rate (RIR) at 5% level of significance has highly negative impact on stock market performance in Nigeria; Nominal Interest Rate (NIR) at 5% level of significance has negative impact on stock market performance in Nigeria; Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 5% level of significance has positive impact on stock market performance in Nigeria. While at 70% level of confidence we conclude that the effect is negative and significant. The policy recommendations based on the findings are; where the simple act of raising or lowering the MPR is insufficient; policymakers must manage the expectations and real economic environment that influence the RIR and NIR to ensure capital market stability. Given the substantial negative impact of RIR on SMP, the Central Bank should intensify efforts towards effective inflation targeting and ma…

Market and Labour Opportunities as a Driving Factor? Explaining the Gendered Literacy Disparities in the Eighteenth-Century Antwerp Countryside
abstract: Abstract This article investigates regional and gender disparities in literacy in the eighteenth-century countryside of the Southern Low Countries, comparing the Campine area and the Scheldt Polder region. We explore the socioeconomic drivers behind divergent literacy rates by drawing on a rich combination of quantitative and qualitative sources – including marriage certificates, probate inventories, and school enrolment data. Contrary to prevailing narratives of widespread illiteracy in Catholic rural regions, the Campine area displayed unexpectedly high levels of literacy, particularly among women. The analysis reveals that this disparity cannot be attributed solely to the presence of schools but must also be understood through the lens of labour market structures and gendered economic roles. The study shows that in the Campine region, smallholder farming and especially dairy production created commercial incentives for women to invest in basic literacy skills, unlike the more unequal, arable farming-based economy of the Scheldt polders. By integrating both macro-level data and micro-historical insights, the article challenges traditional assumptions about rural education and highlights the critical role of gendered economic agency in shaping literacy outcomes.

title: Price Premiums for Sustainability Claims: Evidence From U.S. Food and Beverage Markets
abstract: ABSTRACT As sustainability claims proliferate on food packaging, understanding their implicit market value is important for effective policy design and competitive firm strategy. This study quantifies the price premiums of sustainability attributes in the U.S. market using product‐level data. We analyze 210,515 food and beverage product launches from the Mintel Global New Products Database (2012–2024) and document a near‐doubling in the prevalence of sustainability claims, rising from 18% of new products in 2012 to 37% in 2024. Using a hedonic price model, we present significant price premiums for both environmental (7.9%) and social (3.5%) claims. Further decomposition reveals substantial heterogeneity, with “downstream” attributes related to disposal (e.g., biodegradable) generating the highest premiums, outperforming “upstream” production claims. Additionally, premiums vary widely across product categories, with large premiums in beverages, but zero or negative premiums in several utilitarian categories such as Sauces and Seasonings. These findings inform ongoing policy discussions on third‐party certification, standardized claim definitions, and disclosure requirements for sustainability claims.

Professional by Assumption, Consumer by Behaviour: The Microentrepreneur in the Retail Electricity Market in the Light of Behavioural Economics[1]
abstract: Civil law presumes that an entrepreneur acts as a professional, while the rules protecting electricity customers rely largely on disclosure. Drawing on behavioural economics, the article argues that both assumptions fail with respect to microentrepreneurs. It evaluates statutory classification (Germany), a default rule with standardised bills (Italy), and disclosure with ex post qualification (Poland). A CATI survey of 602 customers of one supplier (402 households, 200 businesses) shows that information on switching and on the comparison tool belongs to the least-read layer of the bill, that age and financial situation are associated with self-assessed knowledge but not the perceived comprehensibility of the bill, and that microentrepreneurs do not report understanding the bill better than households. The article formulates de lege lata conclusions concerning Annex I to Directive 2019/944, Article 31g of the Polish Energy Law, and Article 385⁵ of the Polish Civil Code, and de lege ferenda proposals favouring protection that does not depend on the addressee’s own initiative.

title: Voxel-Level Forecasting of Apparent Vertebral Bone Loss from Routine CT Using a 3D Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Existing computed tomography (CT) fracture-risk models typically output one scalar score per vertebra without localising the predicted change. We built and internally validated a three-dimensional (3D) convolutional network forecasting, from one baseline acquisition, a per-voxel map of apparent inter-scan bone-mask loss per lumbar vertebra. Paired CT studies from 65 patients yielded 298 baseline-unfractured vertebra patches (L1 to L5); every patient sustained at least one reader-adjudicated incident fracture, so the cohort is outcome-enriched. The endpoint was apparent vertebral-body mask loss between scans after rigid alignment of automated masks. A multi-task 3D residual U-Net with vertebral-level conditioning was compared with a gradient-boosted classifier on the same features and folds, under five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation with clustered bootstrap intervals. Pooled precision-recall area was 0.445 vs. 0.439 for the reference (+0.005, 95% confidence interval −0.018 to +0.028) and pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.815. At matched predicted volume, the network map was less fragmented (2.3 vs. 5.3 components per 1000 voxels), and the endpoint separated incident fractures (AUC 0.865). Voxel-level forecasting of apparent inter-scan vertebral change is feasible on routine CT; the contribution is the paired-scan forecasting framework and the spatial-profile differe…

title: Volatility Risk Spillovers Across China’s Electricity Spot, Carbon and Financial Markets: Implications for Low-Carbon Transition with Evidence from BEKK–GARCH and Nonlinear Granger Causality Tests
abstract: To support coordinated risk management of electricity and carbon markets under the new power system, this paper clarifies the volatility transmission mechanism between Guangdong electricity spot prices and Guangdong carbon allowance prices, and investigates risk spillover effects among the Guangdong electricity spot market, Guangdong carbon market and power-related financial market. The results help identify regional systemic risks in the low-carbon energy transition and provide references for regional energy security and financial stability. This paper adopts the logarithmic return of day-ahead average prices in the Guangdong electricity spot market (RE), the logarithmic return of Guangdong carbon emission allowance prices (RC), and the logarithmic return of the FTSE China A600 Electricity Index (RF). A VAR(2)-BEKK-GARCH(1,1) framework is constructed to analyze risk linkages from mean and volatility dimensions. News impact surfaces, volatility impulse response functions, the Diebold–Yilmaz volatility spillover index and the Diks–Panchenko nonlinear causality test are further applied for comprehensive inference. The results show that the electricity market has significant inherent baseline volatility stemming from real-time supply-demand balance and the non-storability of electricity. Volatility persistence ranks as financial market > carbon market > electricity market. In term…

title: GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonism does not directly drive skeletal muscle atrophy or impair myogenesis in primary human myotubes
abstract: Abstract GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists produce substantial weight loss in clinical trials but significant loss of lean body mass is reported. Whether this reflects a direct pharmacological effect on skeletal muscle or an indirect consequence of caloric restriction and reduced mechanical loading is unknown. Primary myoblasts were isolated from skeletal muscle of older adults with obesity undergoing orthopaedic surgery. GIPR and GLP-1R expression was characterised by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. Differentiated myotubes were treated with semaglutide or GIP peptide and assessed for atrophy-related gene expression (qPCR), secretome perturbation (Olink Reveal), mitochondrial and glycolytic bioenergetics (Seahorse XF Real-Time ATP Rate Assay, glucose uptake, lactate secretion) and myotube morphology and myogenesis (immunofluorescence). GIPR mRNA was consistently detected across all donors; GLP-1R mRNA was undetectable by PCR, though LUXendin645 flow cytometry in a subset of three donors identified low-level surface GLP-1R protein in 51–66% of myoblasts. Neither semaglutide nor GIP altered atrophy-related gene expression or the secretome, with no proteins reaching significance. Semaglutide reduced glycolytic and total ATP production rates, accompanied by reduced lactate secretion, suggesting modest suppression of glycolytic flux; mitochondrial parameters were unaffected. Neither…

title: Applicability of a modified weather research and forecasting (WRF) model to heavy rainfall information
abstract: Abstract The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) issues “Forecast Information on Linear Rainbands” (FILR; translated by the authors) approximately half a day before the expected formation of linear rainbands. A linear rainband is identified according to a set of operational criteria. A modified Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model was applied to sixteen heavy rainfall events associated with erroneous FILR decisions. Ten of these events had no FILR issued but subsequently experienced linear rainbands (missed issuance). Model results were compared with radar/rain-gauge analyzed precipitation data, with a primary focus on maximum rainfall, one of the criteria. The model reasonably simulated the occurrence of heavy rainfall in eight of the ten events and the rainfall intensity in six of those eight events. Conversely, six of the sixteen events had FILRs issued but ultimately experienced no linear rainbands (false alarm). In five of these events, the model reasonably reproduced the observed rainfall that did not satisfy the linear-rainband criteria. These results suggest that, despite several remaining challenges, the modified WRF model has the potential to complement JMA FILR decisions and contribute to reducing both missed issuances and false alarms.

title: Phagocytosis of Acanthamoeba by macrophages and neutrophils and “kiss and run” evasion by Entamoeba histolytica
abstract: ABSTRACT Phagocytosis was discovered in the 19th century and is a cornerstone of innate immunity. Although amoebae species cause over 100 million cases of severe infections annually, one long-standing dogma remained unchallenged: that eukaryotic amoebae are too large to be phagocytosed. Here, we overturn this entrenched dogma and show that human macrophages and neutrophils efficiently phagocytose Acanthamoeba polyphaga and Vermamoeba vermiformis , in a phosphoinositide 3-kinase-dependent manner. In contrast, Entamoeba histolytica utilizes a “kiss and run” evasion strategy of phagocytosis. However, formalin-killed and UV-irradiated E. histolytica are efficiently phagocytosed. Macrophages respond to E. histolytica by formation of striking F-actin fibrillar projections, in contrast to the bona fide phagocytic cups that engulf killed E. histolytica , A. polyphaga , and V. vermiformis . Remarkably, neutrophils harboring phagocytosed amoebae are efferocytosed by macrophages. These findings redefine innate immunity to amoebae, the physical and biological limits of phagocytosis, and uncover divergent evolution among pathogenic amoebae to subvert phagocytosis. IMPORTANCE Eukaryotic amoebae have been presumed to be too large to be phagocytosed. We demonstrate that human macrophages and neutrophils can efficiently phagocytose diverse amoebae species, while Entamoeba histolytica evades pha…

title: Forecasting Non-Fungible Token (NFT) Market Volatility Through Hybrid GARCH–LSTM Models
abstract: This study forecasts price volatility in the non-fungible token (NFT) digital asset market. We develop a hybrid forecasting framework that integrates long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with a set of generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH)-type models. Using daily data, we conduct a comparative evaluation of nine competing forecasting models across five representative NFT submarkets (i.e., OpenSea, Atomic, CryptoKitties, Gods Unchained, and Decentraland). Employing standard error metrics (RMSE, MSE, MAE, and RAE), a robust loss QLIKE function, and the Diebold–Mariano (DM) statistical test, our empirical results show that the hybrid GARCH-TGARCH-LSTM model achieves the lowest error metrics. Compared with the baseline LSTM model, it achieves RMSE reductions of approximately 14% for Atomic, 49% for CryptoKitties, 13% for Decentraland, 8% for Gods Unchained, and 29% for OpenSea. Furthermore, the EGARCH conditional variance specification underperforms the TGARCH counterpart in the most NFT submarkets. This finding suggests that combining the volatility clustering characteristics captured by standard GARCH models with the asymmetric volatility features captured by TGARCH models improves forecasting performance. This study contributes to research on hybrid deep learning approaches to volatility forecasting in emerging digital asset markets.

title: Understanding Barriers to Surgical Care: A Qualitative Study of Black Individuals With Hand Dysfunction
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To identify barriers influencing treatment decision‐making among Black individuals with carpal tunnel syndrome and to explore mechanisms contributing to disparities in hand surgery utilisation. Summary Background Data Racial disparities exist in a variety of surgical subspecialties, including hand surgery. Little information on why these disparities exist or how to improve disparities from the patient's perspective is known. Methods We conducted a study utilising virtual semi‐structured interviews, focusing on participants’ interactions with healthcare providers, the impact of hand dysfunction, and participants’ experiences with racism and discrimination. Using an interpretive description approach, we captured major themes in the coded data. Results The sample included 28 Black individuals with carpal tunnel syndrome. We identified three key themes: (1) Racism predisposes Black participants to inequitable care: participants experienced intergenerational drag, microaggressions, discrimination, and mistrust related to historical injustices. Participants engaged in code‐switching to navigate biases and have their symptoms validated. (2) Social and systemic factors enable access to care: participants experienced economic instability, limited paid leave, unreliable transportation, inequitable workplace policies, and lack of social support. title: Isoconversional kinetics, mechanical property loss and quantum computing prediction of kinetic parameters for naturally aged NBR
abstract: Nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) stored for 2 years under natural ambient conditions (28 ± 3°C, 55 ± 10% RH) was compared with fresh NBR by thermogravimetry at 5, 10 and 15°C min ‒1 under nitrogen and by tensile, hardness and density measurements. After separating the main backbone-decomposition stage from overlapping processes, Friedman and Vyazovkin analyses gave mean activation energies (α = 0.40–0.90) of 274 and 242 kJ mol ‒1 for fresh and aged NBR, and the Kissinger method gave 251 ± 12 and 201 ± 3 kJ mol ‒1 . The best-fit reaction model changed from three-dimensional diffusion (D3) to first order (F1), and tensile strength and modulus decreased by 41–46%. Quantum amplitude estimation, quantum kernel ridge regression and a quantum neural network, trained on the two measured states, were used to forecast the kinetic parameters at 1, 3 and 5 yr and compared with linear interpolation. All methods agree at 1 yr (257–258 kJ mol ‒1 ) but diverge beyond 2 yr (195–263 kJ mol ‒1 ) within propagated uncertainties of ± 62–110 kJ mol ‒1 .
