Thermodynamic Analysis of Liquidus Prediction Differences Between Redlich–Kister and MQMQA Descriptions for the NaCl–MgCl2 System
abstract: Accurate prediction of melting behavior is essential for defining the operating window of molten chloride salts. This study compares the adopted Redlich–Kister (RK) and Modified Quasichemical Model in the Quadruplet Approximation (MQMQA) liquid-phase descriptions for NaCl–MgCl2 using common pure-liquid reference Gibbs energies and solid-phase descriptions. Five previously measured DSC onset temperatures and 25 literature mixed-salt liquidus points were evaluated separately without parameter fitting or empirical temperature correction. Relative to the five DSC onset temperatures, the mean absolute deviations were 28.21 °C for MQMQA and 56.48 °C for RK. Agreement with the literature liquidus data varied among datasets, with neither description consistently yielding smaller deviations. Calculated minimum-liquidus temperatures were 459.22 °C for MQMQA and 487.11 °C for RK, both above the selected reported eutectic central values of 430–451 °C. At the five DSC conditions, MQMQA predicted liquid Gibbs free energies 0.74–0.79 kJ/mol salt lower, primarily through a more negative mixing contribution. These results characterize differences between the adopted descriptions and their agreement with specific datasets rather than establish the general superiority of either model formalism.

title: From prediction to design rules: explainable machine learning analysis of cryoprotectant effects in GelMA-based cryobioprinting bioinks
abstract: Abstract Machine learning has been used to predict cryoprotective-agent (CPA) effects in cryobioprinting, but prediction accuracy alone does not yield experimentally usable formulation rules. Here, we performed a secondary explainable analysis of Qiao et al ’s GelMA-HUVEC dataset using formulation-grouped validation, SHAP interpretation, stability metrics, and multi-objective ranking. A compact Random Forest model using permeable CPA identity, sugar CPA identity, permeable CPA concentration, sugar concentration, and storage day achieved MAE = 4.842%, RMSE = 6.106%, and R 2 = 0.649, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of 4.418–5.274% for MAE and 0.585–0.710 for R 2 . SHAP analysis identified permeable CPA concentration and storage day as the strongest viability drivers, with directional patterns favoring balanced 15% permeable CPA and 15% sugar CPA rather than simple concentration maximization. Multi-objective ranking identified GL_15_RA_15 as the strongest individual formulation, whereas EG + trehalose showed the highest average CPA-family performance. Cross-domain tests showed limited transfer between EG and GL formulations, indicating that the extracted rules should be treated as local, data-supported design hypotheses rather than universal cryoprotectant principles. Together, these results show that explainable secondary analysis can convert small cryobioprinting dataset…

Data-Driven Prediction-Route Coupling Optimization for Cold Chain Logistics
abstract: Fresh-product cold-chain logistics suffers high commodity losses and poor cross-link dynamic coordination, since demand prediction and vehicle routing are often decoupled in practice. This study developed a data-driven prediction-route coupling optimization framework for proactive intelligent distribution scheduling. A convolutional neural network–long short-term memory–attention model captured spatiotemporal demand dependencies to boost prediction accuracy under nonlinear, volatile conditions. Using the Arrhenius equation for freshness decay, the study formulated a dynamic vehicle routing model to minimize generalized total cost, covering transportation, refrigeration, cargo-damage costs, and time-window penalties. Tested on real enterprise operational data, the experiments suggested that the hybrid prediction model reduced forecast errors. Under the stated experimental settings, the coupled framework cut operational cost and mitigated cargo loss. It improved distribution resilience against high-temperature disruptions and provided a feasible reference for information-driven cold-chain intelligent decision-support systems.

title: Physics-guided deep residual learning for sound absorption prediction of micro-perforated panels
abstract: Abstract To address the limited accuracy of analytical models, the high computational cost of finite element method (FEM) simulations, and the sample dependence of purely data-driven approaches for micro-perforated panel (MPP) sound absorption prediction, this study proposes a physics-guided deep residual network (PGDRN). A paired analytical-FEM dataset is constructed under identical structural parameters and frequency sampling points. Instead of directly fitting the complete FEM absorption curve, the FEM response is decomposed into an analytical baseline and an analytical-FEM residual correction. The network is trained to learn this residual discrepancy, while the analytical absorption coefficient and resonance mismatch are introduced as physics-guided features to enhance the representation of resonance-related frequency regions. Experiments on 1000 paired analytical-FEM samples show that PGDRN achieves an MAE of 0.0012, an RMSE of 0.0021, an R 2 of 0.9999, and a mean peak absorption coefficient error of 0.0022 on the test set. Compared with Mambular, the strongest data-driven baseline, PGDRN reduces MAE, RMSE, and peak error by 94.76%, 95.14%, and 95.53%, respectively. Ablation and limited-sample analyses confirm the contributions of residual learning and physics-guided features to prediction accuracy, peak-region stability, and sample efficiency. FEM sound-field visualizatio…

title: Structure-borne noise of a steel box railway bridge: Unified FEM–BEM prediction, field validation, and the speed-dependent transition of acoustic radiation patterns
abstract: The rapid expansion of railway systems has intensified concerns regarding the structure-borne noise (SBN) of bridges, which is governed by the coupled train–track–bridge interaction. Conventional prediction approaches typically rely on two or more separate software platforms, in most of which the structural response is computed in a finite-element package and then exported into an independent acoustic solver, introducing a data-mapping error. This study developed a unified single-platform FEM–BEM framework, in which the structural and acoustic domains are solved within the same explicit transient environment, avoiding intermediate mesh remapping and preserving the time-resolved excitation associated with moving wheel–rail loads. The framework was validated against steel-plate vibration and sound radiation experiments in an anechoic chamber, yielding a mesh design guideline of 12 elements per bending wavelength, with relative errors below 1.7% in the dominant structural frequencies and below 6% in the corresponding acoustic eigenfrequencies. A full-scale model of a 180-m steel box-girder bridge was then developed, and its predictions matched the field-measured dominant acoustic peaks at 50–63 Hz to within approximately 2 dB. title: Conditional Multi-Step Prediction for Distributed Photovoltaic Clusters Using Implicit Neural Motion Field with Wind-Modulated Fourier Layer Under Limited Local Meteorological Sensing
abstract: Regional meteorological information does not fully resolve local microclimatic variability, while moving clouds over varied terrain cause dynamic spatial heterogeneity in distributed photovoltaic (PV) power output. This study performs retrospective evaluation adopting observed future period meteorology as known inputs. This study proposes an implicit neural motion field (INMF) for multi-step conditional prediction of distributed PV power under limited local meteorological sensing. Learnable site coordinates, site embeddings, and radial basis function interpolation map discrete site states onto a regular latent grid. A neural ordinary differential equation evolves this field through a wind-modulated Fourier layer, in which wind speed conditions spectral amplitudes and wind direction conditions spectral phases. An auxiliary irradiance-consistency term regularizes the temporal relationship between predicted outputs and irradiance. The model is evaluated on 20 rooftop PV sites in Hong Kong using observed target-period meteorology. Joint wind modulation reduces RMSE by 8.9–18.5% across the four evaluated step horizons. In the ablation experiments, phase modulation and the irradiance-consistency term yield reductions in aggregated-series RMSE. Governance, leadership and organisational capacity for decentralised medical training: insights from a South African medical school
abstract: Introduction Decentralised medical training has become a strategic approach for strengthening primary healthcare, expanding clinical training capacity and addressing health workforce shortages in South Africa. Despite its growing adoption, limited research has examined the governance, leadership and organisational conditions required for its successful implementation. Guided by Transformational Leadership Theory and Servant Leadership Theory, this study explores the governance structures, leadership practices and institutional readiness necessary to support sustainable decentralised medical training within a South African medical school. Methods An exploratory qualitative research design was adopted employing semi-structured interviews with 16 participants from a university and affiliated Department of Health clinical training sites in KwaZulu-Natal. Purposive and snowball sampling techniques were used to recruit participants and data were analysed thematically using NVivo 12. Results The findings demonstrate that effective implementation of decentralised medical training depends on collaborative governance, transparent communication, stakeholder engagement and distributed leadership. The results further highlighted the need for curriculum transformation, faculty development, adequate infrastructure, sustainable funding and strong partnerships between universities and the Depar…

Omega-3 DHA Targets P53-Mutant CRC Stem-like Cells via Membrane Disruption, Modulation of Differential Marker Genes, and Suppression of Self-Renewal Capacity
abstract: P53-mutant colorectal cancer stem cells (CRCSCs) are characterized by multidrug-resistance, high self-renewal, and limited differentiation potential, which necessitates the development of novel compounds capable of targeting the molecular drivers of differentiation and stemness maintenance in CRCSCs, independent of p 53 status. Given this, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) was selected as a promising therapeutic candidate and its ability to modulate differentiation marker genes and stemness maintenance in CRC stem-like cells was evaluated. P53-mutant (E204X) Caco2 cells, serving as a well-established model of CRCSCs, were treated with 50-150 μM DHA for 48 h. We then evaluated multiple parameters including cell number, metabolic activity, proliferation rates, and LDH release. Additionally, the expression of stemness (CD133) and intestinal differentiation marker genes (Muc-2 and CK-20) as well as clonogenic capacity were assessed. Bioinformatic analysis was performed to predict p 53-binding sites within the promoters of CD133, Muc-2, and CK-20 for wild-type p 53 and its mutant form. DHA significantly decreased cell numbers, metabolic activities, and proliferation rates after 48 h of treatment. Concurrently, DHA treatment disrupted cell membrane integrity, as evidenced by a marked increase in LDH release into the supernatant. The initially low expression levels of Muc-2 and CK-20 increas…

Business survival strategies: evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate business survival strategies in an emerging market to address the economic challenges faced by firms in the region. The primary objectives are to assess the strategies adopted by firms to survive, determine the extent to which these strategies contribute to business success and identify the sectors that perform best in the region. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative snapshot investigation was conducted using a structured questionnaire administered to business firms. Findings The results of this study reveal that the most significant adopted survival strategies include introducing new and unique products or services (69.5%), decision-makers increasing their academic knowledge of business growth (67.1%), deploying sensitization methods (61.0%) and reducing product prices to boost sales (54.5%). Regarding the effectiveness of these strategies, an average success rate of 42.3% was reported as the highest attained by the firms. Furthermore, analysis of dominating business sectors highlights agriculture (26.2%), health (5.7%), provision stores (5.2%) and construction materials (3.3%) as the top-performing industries in the region. Research limitations/implications While this study gives useful empirical insights into corporate survival strategies within an emerging industry, many notable limitations must be addressed. title: P-271: Intersectoral policy and capacity-building strategies to improve access to type 1 diabetes care for children and adolescents in Brazil
abstract: Abstract Introduction Gaps in diabetes care contribute to avoidable complications and inequities for children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D). The Intersectoral Forum of Noncommunicable Conditions (ForumCCNTs), established in 2017, convenes over 250 institutions to influence policy through multistakeholder action. Objectives To assess the contribution of intersectoral policy and capacity-building strategies (2017–2026) to improving access to T1D care in children and adolescents in Brazil. Methods A descriptive policy analysis of ForumCCNTs’ actions was conducted. Strategies included: (1) advocating for expanded access to insulin analogues, glucose monitoring, and point-of-care HbA1c through recommendations and letters to the Ministry of Health; (2) participating in public consultations for clinical guideline updates; (3) contributing to the National Health Plan 2024–2027; (4) multi-year capacity-building for civil society and advocates; and (5) developing a 2026 national T1D recommendation document. Institutional and policy documents were reviewed to assess outputs and uptake. Results Contributions to national guideline consultations supported clinical protocol updates. Recommendations, including insulin analogue expansion, were integrated into the National Health Plan 2024–2027. Capacity-building initiatives trained over 100 representatives from health organizations…

title: Institutional Capacity and Capital Inflows in Selected Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
abstract: This paper examined how governance quality affects capital inflows to the selected ECOWAS countries (Côte d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Liberia, Mali, Nigeria, Senegal, and Togo) between 2002 and 2024. The specific objectives are to determine the effects of government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, control of corruption, and political stability on foreign loan inflows. Given the nature of this study, panel datasets were obtained from the World and IMF Financial Statistics. Descriptive statistics, cross-sectional dependence test, panel unit root and cointegration tests, as well as heterogenous panel model estimation, comprising mean group (MG) and pooled mean group (PMG) were used for the data analysis. The cross-sectional dependence test indicates that there is no cross-sectional dependence across the panels. The panel unit root test results showed evidence of mixed integration in the series. The panel regression estimates indicate that government effectiveness has a significant positive effect on foreign loan inflows in the long run. The results also showed that regulatory quality has a significant negative effect on loan inflows in the long run. Evidence of a significant effect of the rule of law on foreign loan inflows was established in the long run. Discovery of Bioactive N-Substituted-3-methylbut-2-enamides: Synthesis, Crystal Structures, Antifungal Activity, Mechanism of Action, and Zebrafish Toxicity Evaluation
abstract: Plant pathogenic fungi pose a serious threat to agricultural and forestry production. Long- term reliance on chemical fungicides has led to rising pathogen resistance and ecological risks, making the discovery and development of novel, safe, and highly effective antifungal compounds of great practical significance. Three N-substituted-3-methylbut-2-enamide derivatives (compounds I–III) were synthesized and structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, infrared spectroscopy, and elemental analysis. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values of the three compounds were determined against six common plant pathogenic fungi, and the antifungal activity was found to be governed by the N-substituent structure. Compound III (3-methyl-N-(4-phenoxybenzyl) but-2-enamide) was the most active, with an MIC of 25–100 mg/mL, representing a 3-fold increase over the rigid fused-ring analogs I and II, which suggests that increased molecular flexibility favors antifungal activity. Preliminary mechanistic investigation of compound III revealed that it induces intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, compensatory upregulation of reduced glutathione, and elevated malondialdehyde levels in fungi, thereby inhibiting fungal growth through oxidative stress-mediated damage. Zebrafish embryo toxicity assays showed that compound III exhibited concentration- and time…

title: Dietary Capsaicin Protects Against Obesity via a Microbiome-Dependent Mechanism Independent of Host TRPV1 Signalling
abstract: Background/Objectives: Dietary compounds simultaneously act on host tissue and gut microbiota, complicating efforts to distinguish direct host–receptor mechanisms from microbiome-mediated effects. Using a common food ingredient as proof-of-principle, this study aims to disentangle capsaicin host receptor signalling from capsaicin–microbiome interactions to determine the role of the gut microbiome in capsaicin-mediated metabolic protection. Methods: We employed a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity model with or without capsaicin supplementation in TRPV1 knockout mice to determine the role of the host receptor. We also depleted the gut microbiota with antibiotics to determine the role of the microbiome. Host metabolic phenotypes were monitored, and microbiome 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics were analysed and extended with functional prediction and machine learning algorithms, followed by functional validation in vivo. Results: Capsaicin supplementation significantly protected against HFD-induced obesity, even capsaicin receptor knockout hosts. Crucially, depletion of the microbiota abolished this metabolic protection, demonstrating the microbiome’s obligatory role. While capsaicin supplementation did not alter hosts’ cumulative food intake, dietary preferences, or energy expenditure, it induced significant shifts in gut microbial diversity and function and triggered extensi…

Design of a Shipboard Sewage Treatment Plant Control and Monitoring System Using Microcontroller
abstract: This study focuses on the design and simulation of a microcontroller-based control and monitoring system for a shipboard sewage treatment plant aimed at improving operational reliability and automation. The system employs a dual microcontroller configuration using PIC16F84A devices to manage the operation of essential components, including the inlet pump, aerator, discharge pump, and dosing pump under both automatic and manual modes. A timing-based control approach is implemented to ensure proper sequencing of system operations and maintain stable wastewater flow between treatment stages. In addition to control functions, the system incorporates monitoring features that continuously track operating conditions and provide immediate feedback on system status. Abnormal conditions, such as overflow, are detected through sensor inputs and indicated by an alarm system with buzzer notification. A liquid crystal display (LCD) is integrated to present operating modes, system status, and fault indications for effective user interaction. The designed system is modelled and tested using Proteus Design Suite to evaluate its performance under normal and fault conditions. Simulation results indicate stable operation, accurate response to control inputs, and effective detection of system abnormalities. Overall, the designed system offers a practical and cost-effective solution suitable for shi…

Analysis of Power Performance and Wake Interference in a Three-Turbine Tandem Array of Offshore Wind Turbines
abstract: This study investigates multiple-wake interactions and downstream power losses in a heterogeneous tandem array comprising DTU 10-MW and NREL 5-MW offshore wind turbines. TurbSim is used to generate turbulent inflow fields, and a three-turbine tandem array is simulated in FAST. Farm using the Dynamic Wake Meandering model. Seven turbine configurations and 57 simulation scenarios are considered to systematically examine the effects of streamwise spacing, inflow turbulence intensity, turbine-type combination, and turbine-type arrangement on power output and wake evolution. The results show that increasing the streamwise spacing generally improves the power output and wake power retention ratios of the intermediate and downstream turbines. Compared with uniform inflow, turbulent inflow with a prescribed turbulence intensity of 15% generally enhances momentum exchange across the wake shear layers, accelerates wake recovery, and reduces downstream power losses, although its effect on total array power depends on the turbine configuration. Turbine-type arrangement affects downstream performance by changing the spatial extent of the wake generated by the intermediate turbine and its vertical overlap with the rotor-swept area of the downstream turbine. title: Desigualdades de gênero no mercado de trabalho brasileiro: Evolução, determinantes e desafios para o setor público
abstract: O presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar, por meio de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, a evolução das desigualdades de gênero no mercado de trabalho, os fatores associados à sua persistência, as particularidades observadas no emprego público e as respostas institucionais relacionadas ao seu enfrentamento no Brasil. A busca foi realizada na base Scopus, considerando artigos publicados entre 2016 e 2025, em português, inglês ou espanhol. Após etapas sucessivas de triagem por títulos, resumos e aderência dos estudos à questão de pesquisa, foram selecionados 25 artigos, posteriormente examinados por meio de análise de conteúdo. Os resultados indicam que, embora algumas desigualdades tenham diminuído ao longo do tempo, permanecem diferenças relacionadas à remuneração, à segregação ocupacional e vertical, à progressão profissional e ao acesso a posições de liderança. A maternidade e as responsabilidades de cuidado também aparecem de forma recorrente associadas à participação, à qualidade da inserção laboral e às trajetórias profissionais. No setor público, regras formais de ingresso, estruturas remuneratórias e mecanismos de carreira podem reduzir parte das diferenças observadas no setor privado, mas não eliminam desigualdades relacionadas à progressão, à hierarquia e ao acesso a determinadas oportunidades. Conclui-se que o enfrentamento dessas desigualdades requer atenção …

title: Market Perception of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Rollbacks of U.S Public Firms
abstract: Purpose: The rollback of diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives among publicly traded United States firms has raised concerns regarding investor confidence and corporate valuation. This study examined stock market perceptions of DEI rollbacks and their implications for shareholder wealth. Methodology: The study employed a quantitative event study methodology involving 20 publicly traded United States firms that announced DEI policy rollbacks. Daily stock returns were analyzed using a mean-adjusted model, with expected returns estimated from 250 preceding trading days. Cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) were calculated over a seven-day event window (-3, +3) surrounding each announcement. Findings: The findings revealed negative average cumulative abnormal returns throughout the event window, ranging from -1.02% to -1.98%, with an average CAR of -1.66% by day +3. These findings suggest an unfavorable market reaction to DEI rollbacks, although broader market movements and pre-announcement effects cannot be excluded. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study recommends that corporate managers carefully evaluate the financial and reputational implications of reversing DEI commitments, strengthen stakeholder communication, and incorporate investor expectations into governance decisions. Future research should employ market-adjusted benchmarks and larger…

title: Green finance market development and carbon emissions trading: evidence on corporate environmental responsibility in China
abstract: From the perspective of institutional–financial synergy, this paper integrates environmental regulation theory with financial development theory to construct a theoretical framework for analyzing the effects of carbon emissions trading (CET) and green finance market development (GF) on corporate environmental responsibility (CER). Based on panel data of listed firms in high-carbon industries on China's Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share markets from 2010 to 2025, we employ staggered difference-in-differences (DID), moderating effect models, mediation effect models, and a moderated serial mediation model to examine their interaction and potential transmission channels. The findings are as follows. First, during the local carbon market pilot stage, treated firms' CER increased by 0.0214 on average, or 5.43% relative to the sample mean. When extended to the post-2021 period, the national carbon market estimates are consistent with a positive governance effect. Second, regional green finance development is significantly and positively associated with CER, and the CET × GF interaction is significantly positive, consistent with a synergistic complementarity interpretation. Conditional marginal effects show that the estimated CET effect is stronger when green finance support is higher. Third, the Bootstrap indirect effects of financing constraints, environmental information disclosure, and…

title: Digital Leverage in Business Ecosystems: How AI and E-Commerce Enable Market Capabilities in Resource-Constrained Entrepreneurship
abstract: This systematic literature review investigates the methods by which resource-limited entrepreneurs leverage artificial intelligence (AI), e-commerce platforms, and various digital technologies to enhance market capabilities amidst resource constraints. Anchored on the viewpoints of platform ecosystems and dynamic capacities, the research employs a PRISMA-based review of scholarly articles released from 2015 to 2025. A cumulative total of 195 items were incorporated into the final collection. The results suggest that digital platforms and AI-driven tools can enhance access to clients, information, digital infrastructure, analytics, and distribution services, whereas their impact on the development of firm-level capabilities relies on how entrepreneurs utilise, integrate, and reorganise these externally sourced resources. The literature examined places more emphasis on customer acquisition and digital distribution than on pricing optimisation and market sensing. The evaluation also highlights a continual disparity between digital accessibility and the advancement of capabilities, with scant longitudinal data elucidating how the habitual utilisation of digital resources integrates into entrepreneurial practices. Utilising the synthesis, the research formulates a conceptual framework that situates digital leverage as a conduit linking ecosystem resources and digital affordances wit…

title: An Experiment Investigating the Interaction of Feedback Framing and Self-Perception in the Labor Market
abstract: Abstract: Performance feedback is a critical driver of motivation, development, and advancement, yet gender differences in how feedback is internalized remain underexplored. Across an experimental vignette study with 280 full-time employees, we investigate gender differences in expected disappointment after critical feedback and whether the tone of delivery effects men and women asymmetrically. Results show that women report higher disappointment than men following negative hypothetical evaluations. This gender disparity disappears when feedback is communicated in a communal tone as men increase in their self-disappointment. These findings suggest that communal framing differentially shapes men’s and women’s emotional responses to feedback, eliminating the gender gap in disappointment. Implications include rethinking managerial communication, training supervisors in inclusive feedback delivery, and recognizing the impact of feedback tone on employee self-perception, motivation, and career trajectories.

title: The labour market in Indonesia, 2001-2024
abstract: Indonesia’s labour market absorbed over 50 million additional workers between 2001 and 2024, while unemployment fell from 8% to under 5%. Yet job quality has not kept pace. Structural transformation, the movement of workers out of agriculture, has largely bypassed manufacturing and channeled labour into low-value-added services; 58% of workers remain informal; median earnings stand roughly 40% below the average minimum wage, even though more than a quarter of the workforce works over 48 hours per week; and female labour force participation trails male participation by 28 percentage points. These four interconnected features define Indonesia’s labour market challenge.

title: Accommodation-Based Tourism Demand and Rural Labour-Market Dynamics in Kazakhstan: Evidence from a Regional Panel
abstract: Tourism-related opportunities may be unevenly distributed within regions where visitor activity and economic linkages are spatially concentrated. This study examines associations between regionwide accommodation-visitor growth and rural labour-market changes in Kazakhstan. Using a harmonised panel of 14 regions over 2003–2025, we estimate first-difference regressions with year fixed effects, region-clustered standard errors, and wild-cluster bootstrap inference. The principal sample contains 293 observations (290 with regional economic and agricultural controls). Neither rural employment intensity nor rural unemployment shows a statistically significant contemporaneous association with accommodation-visitor growth. Distributed-lag models fail to reject joint null hypotheses for current and lagged tourism-demand coefficients at the 5% level. Targeted temporal, territorial, and control-based checks likewise yield no statistically significant contemporaneous associations at the 5% level. However, exploratory specifications reveal statistically significant negative associations with rural employment intensity and, in restricted annual samples, rural unemployment. These findings are sensitive to sample selection and measurement horizon and do not establish causal effects. Accommodation visitors are measured regionwide, including urban destinations, while labour-market indicators cov…

title: Exploration of the application of biomimetic design in improving the energy absorption effect of corrugated tubes
abstract: Abstract Thin-walled structures are widely used as lightweight energy absorbers, but conventional corrugated tubes still suffer from limited deformation controllability and high peak crushing force (PCF). Inspired by the periodic joints of natural bamboo, this study proposes a bionic bamboo-joint corrugated tube (BBCT) to improve crashworthiness. Quasi-static compression experiments and finite element simulations are conducted to reveal its deformation mechanism and validate the numerical model. Parametric analyses show that the bamboo-joint design promotes stable progressive folding and improves specific energy absorbed (SEA), mean crushing force (MCF) and crushing force efficiency compared with traditional corrugated and circular tubes under identical geometric and loading conditions. A theoretical model based on the simplified super folding element theory is established to predict the MCF, showing good agreement with numerical results. Furthermore, Kriging-based multi-objective optimization combined with Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II is performed to maximize SEA and minimize PCF. Engineering-scale high-speed rail collision simulations demonstrate that the BBCT-based anti-climbing device achieves a 76.3–217.0% higher SEA than representative railway energy-absorbing structures reported in the literature, confirming its potential for lightweight impact energy manag…

title: Decoupling Oxygen Reduction From Hydrogen Oxidation on Platinum via Phosphorus Coordination for Reversal‐Tolerant and Durable PEM Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT During the start‐up/shut‐down (SU/SD) processes of proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), anode reversal generates an excessively high voltage that accelerates corrosion of the cathode Pt/C catalyst. Conventional approaches focus on blocking the delivery of oxygen or electrons to the anode, but fail to address the intrinsic activity coupling of Pt/C for both hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Here, we report a strategy that can selectively tailor the catalytic function of Pt nanoparticles. We used phosphorus to modulate the electronic structure of low‐loading Pt clusters on a carbon support, forming a Pt/P‐BP catalyst. The P‐coordination downshifts the d ‐band center of Pt cluster, as evidenced by in situ ATR‑FTIR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, thereby widening the activity gap between HOR and ORR. Specifically, compared to Pt/C, Pt/P‐BP enhances HOR mass activity by fivefold while substantially suppressing ORR, transforming Pt from a bifunctional catalyst into a highly selective HOR catalyst. Consequently, Pt/P‐BP achieves a 10.8‐fold higher HOR/ORR selectivity than Pt/C. In SU/SD experiments, the Pt/P‐BP anode significantly reduces carbon corrosion of the cathode catalyst layer, maintaining the fuel cell performance better than Pt/C. This work paves a new avenue toward durable PEMFCs and inspires the selectivity design f…

title: Chronic Energy Drink Consumption and Subclinical Myocardial Injury Among Healthy Young Adults: Evidence From Cardiac Biomarkers
abstract: Energy drinks (EDs) are popular among young adults, but their multi-organ toxicity is still a concern. In this study, the effect of chronic ED use on cardiac biomarkers (troponin I, myoglobin, CK MB) and complete blood count (CBC) parameters was investigated. Thirty healthy males (18–35 years) with chronic EDs (3 or more cans/day for ≥6 months) and 10 healthy males without EDs (no EDs for ≥6 months) were included in a cross-sectional study. Troponin I was measured by Mindray CL900 chemiluminescence analyzer, myoglobin and CK-MB were measured by Ichroma immunofluorescence assays, and CBC parameters were measured by a Mindray BC30. Independent t tests and Mann–Whitney U tests (p<0.05, Bonferroni-corrected where appropriate) were used for the statistical comparisons. ED consumers had significantly higher troponin I (28.4±8.2 vs. 12.3±3.1 pg/mL, p<0.001), myoglobin (68.5±15.3 vs. 42.1±9.8 ng/mL, p<0.001), and CK MB (4.8±1.2 vs. 2.9±0.7 ng/mL, p<0.001). CBC revealed higher WBC (8.4±1.6 vs. 6.2±1.1×10³/μL, p<0.001), neutrophils (5.4±1.3 vs. 3.4±0.9×10³/μL, p<0.001), NLR (2.8±0.9 vs. 1.9±0.5, p=0.003), and platelets (285.6±42.3 vs. 242.8±35.1×10³/μL, p=0.004). Cardiac biomarker concentrations were higher in heavy consumers (>5 cans/day) than in moderate consumers (troponin I, p<0.001; myoglobin, p=0.003; CK-MB, p=0.015). Daily ED volume correlated positively with myoglobin concentrati…

title: Effect of inner DT gas-density on energy gain accounting for a simple modeling of the instabilities growth at the hot-spot surface
abstract: Abstract In a classical Inertial Confinement Fusion capsule a shell of solid Deuterium-Tritium fuel encloses an inner sphere of gas at vapor pressure. The temperature of the cryogenic fuel determines the vapor pressure and thus the density of the DT gas which decreases proportionally to the temperature. Typically, temperatures of the cryogenic DT shell and densities of the inner gas are around ≈ 18 K and 0.3 mg/cm 3 , respectively. A parametric study was conducted to analyze the effect of gas density on the final energy gain, assuming a simplified model for the evolution of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability at the hot spot surface. It is found that small gas densities (< 0.1 mg/cm 3 ) avoid the formation of a sufficiently large hot-spot mass, preventing high-energy gains. On the other hand, high-densities (> 1.0 mg/cm 3 ) are associated to larger deceleration times that allow for thicker mixing-layers surrounding the hot spot that quench the propagation of the fusion reactions reducing the final gain. This implies that there is an optimal gas density window between 0.1 to 1 mg/cm 3 that maximizes the capsule performance.

title: The Nexus Between Green Finance, Renewable Energy Consumption and Technological Innovation: Evidence From G20 Economies
abstract: ABSTRACT Green finance is intended to support decarbonisation, yet an average emissions relationship may conceal differences across financing instruments and the conditional emissions distribution. This study examines these differences in G20 economies during 2012–2018, alongside renewable energy consumption (RE) and research and development expenditure (RD). A Green Finance Index (GFI) combines green credit, green securities and green investment using principal component analysis. Fixed‐ and random‐effects models provide mean benchmarks; panel quantile regression examines distributional heterogeneity; and continuously updated fully modified and bias‐corrected estimators assess long‐run associations in a common‐factor framework. Panel Granger tests examine predictive feedback. GFI is negatively associated with CO 2 emissions in the fixed‐effects model (−0.0410) and the two long‐run models (−0.025 and −0.023). Its quantile coefficients, however, are negative at Q10–Q20 and Q60–Q95 and positive at Q30–Q50. RD is negatively associated with emissions throughout the reported quantiles, whereas RE changes from positive coefficients at Q10–Q40 to negative coefficients at Q50–Q95. Component estimates further distinguish consistently negative green‐securities coefficients from sign reversals in green credit and investment. Thus, a favourable average association does not establish unifor…

title: From the Rock Floor to the Cloud: A Systematic Review of State-of-the-Art NLP in Battery Life Cycle
abstract: This work presents a systematic review of the application of natural language processing (NLP) along the entire battery life cycle, instead of reviewing one stage or method, and introduces a novel conceptual technical language processing (TLP) framework for the European Union (EU)’s proposed digital battery passport (DBP) and other general battery predictions, as the main objective. It follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method and employs three reputable databases or search engines, including Google Scholar, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Xplore (IEEE Xplore), and Scopus, searched in October, 2025. The search criteria are ’text’, ’language processing’, and ’battery’, while the exclusion criteria are non-relevant papers and those published before 2017, which were applied to all databases, except IEEE Xplore because it turned up fewer results. Consequently, it assesses 274 scientific papers before the critical review of the final 66 relevant papers. We publicly provide artifacts of the review for validation and possible reproducibility. The findings show that new NLP tasks are emerging in the battery domain, which facilitate materials discovery and other stages of the life cycle. Notwithstanding, challenges remain, such as the lack of standard benchmarks. The proposed TLP framework, which incorporates agentic…

title: P-240: Case report:when hypoglycemia meets autoimmunity: a challenging intersection of glycogen storage disease type ix and type 1 diabetes in early childhood
abstract: Abstract Introduction GSD IX is a hepatic glycogenolysis defect causing hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly, whereas T1DM causes insulin deficiency and hyperglycemia. Their coexistence creates a rare metabolic paradox. Objectives To describe the clinical course and management challenges of combined GSD IX and T1DM. Methods A 4-year-old girl with PHKG2-related GSD IX was followed longitudinally. Results She presented with hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases. Genetic testing confirmed GSD IX by identifying a homozygous likely pathogenic variant in the PHKG2 gene, consistent with hepatic phosphorylase kinase deficiency and impaired glycogenolysis. This variant affects enzyme activity involved in glycogen breakdown, explaining the patient’s predisposition to fasting hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly. During follow-up, she developed T1DM at age of 3 years, confirmed by positive GAD65 (185 IU/mL), IA-2 (72 IU/mL), low C-peptide (0.18 ng/mL), and insulin requirement. Conclusions This rare coexistence causes extreme glycemic variability. CGM-guided insulin and permissive hyperglycemia are essential, while glucagon is unreliable.

title: An Improved SegRNN-Based Hierarchical Warning Method for Power Battery Thermal Runaway
abstract: Early detection of thermal runaway in electric vehicle batteries remains challenging, and warning lead times during real-world operation are often limited. This paper proposes a hierarchical thermal runaway warning method based on an improved SegRNN model. A cross-variable self-attention module and a one-dimensional convolutional channel fusion layer are integrated into the SegRNN encoder to improve voltage prediction accuracy. One year of operational data from 23 electric vehicles of the same model, including 17 normal vehicles and 6 vehicles with confirmed thermal runaway events, is used for validation. Pearson correlation analysis is applied to select five input variables for charging and discharging conditions separately. A three-level warning strategy is developed based on voltage prediction residuals, with thresholds of 0.05, 0.12, and 0.24 V. On the test set, the proposed model achieves MAE and RMSE values of 0.48624 × 10−3 and 0.64961 × 10−3 during charging, and 3.76869 × 10−3 and 8.2487 × 10−3 during discharging, respectively. Retrospective validation on the six thermal runaway vehicles shows average warning lead times of 87.3 days for Level 1 and 2.3 days for Level 3. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method for early thermal runaway risk identification under real-world operating conditions.

title: Pengaruh DER terhadap Revenue Growth dengan ROA sebagai Mediasi
abstract: Perusahaan sektor transportasi dan logistik memiliki peran penting dalam mendukung aktivitas perekonomian . Berdasarkan data Badan Pusat Statistik (BPS) rata-rata Revenue growth perusahaan sektor transportasi dan logistik menunjukkan kecenderungan menurun selama periode 2023–2025. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menganalisis Pengaruh Debt To Equity Ratio (DER) terhadap Revenue growth dengan Return On Assets (ROA) sebagai variabel mediasi pada perusahaan Sektor Transportasi dan Logistik yang terdaftar di BEI periode 2023–2025. Metode penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan asosiatif kausal. Data penelitian ini merupakan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan tahunan dan publikasi resmi perusahaan serta sumber resmi Bursa Efek Indonesia. Hasil penelitian menunjukan bahwa DER tidak berpengaruh secara langsung dan signifikan terhadap Revenue growth, tetapi memiliki pengaruh tidak langsung melalui ROA. Artinya, penggunaan utang yang tercermin dalam DER berkaitan dengan kemampuan perusahaan menghasilkan laba melalui aset yang dimiliki, sedangkan kemampuan menghasilkan laba tersebut berkaitan dengan pertumbuhan pendapatan perusahaan. Dengan demikian, ROA menjadi perantara yang menjelaskan hubungan antara DER dan Revenue growth. Perusahaan sektor Transportasi dan Logistik diharapkan dapat mengevaluasi penggunaan utang dan mengalokasikan dana secar…

title: From Technical Value to Storage Revenue: An Evolutionary Game Analysis of Energy Storage Deployment in Highway Service Areas
abstract: Deploying photovoltaic generation, energy storage, and electric-vehicle charging in highway service areas requires alignment between storage’s technical benefits and the incentives of implementing organizations. This study develops a tripartite evolutionary game involving highway operators, local governments, and the central government to examine how storage-attributable revenue, conditional subsidies, implementation costs, and supervision shape deployment decisions. The results reveal that stable coordination depends on the alignment of operator investment incentives and local government implementation incentives. Subsidy allocation is therefore subject to a two-sided constraint: increasing support for operators can encourage storage investment but may undermine local implementation when insufficient resources remain for coordination. Central supervision plays a complementary role, with intensive intervention influencing strategic adjustment and routine oversight becoming compatible with stable coordination once participation incentives are aligned. Extended simulations further reveal that apparent short-term coordination can conceal unstable incentive structures, while locally stable outcomes may remain sensitive to initial strategic conditions. These findings highlight the importance of coordinating financial returns, implementation resources, and supervisory arrangements, p…

title: Porphyrin Integration Enhances Bipolar Redox Accessibility for High‐Rate Sodium‐Based Dual‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closing the gap between theoretical multielectron capacity and practical accessibility remains the central bottleneck for high‐energy organic batteries. Herein, we report a molecular design strategy that integrates a porphyrin motif into a sulfur‐rich conjugated polymer (BTTP) to align electronic structure, state‐dependent ion interactions, and electrochemical kinetics across the bipolar window. Despite possessing a lower theoretical capacity than its reference counterpart (BTB), BTTP achieves an exceptional theoretical capacity utilization of 94.2% (delivering 477 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , compared to only 53.5% and 351 mAh g −1 for BTB). Electrokinetic analyses, including GITT and DRT, confirm accelerated apparent ion diffusion and reduced polarization limitations, enabling BTTP to retain 166 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g −1 over 25 000 cycles. Operando/ex situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations elucidate that the dual pyrrolic/imino nitrogen sites in porphyrin and the sulfur‐rich backbone cooperatively provide potential‐dependent coordination environments for PF 6 − anions and Na + cations. This work suggests that molecular regulation of complementary ion‐interaction environments within multi‐active‐unit frameworks, rather than simply increasing the number of redox units, is important for enhancing rate capability and capacity utilization.

title: PFAS Fate and Transport During Aquifer Storage and Recovery: Effects of Aquifer Mineralogy and Conditioning
abstract: Abstract Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are increasingly detected in groundwater and may affect aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) operations. This study evaluated PFAS fate and transport during ASR with emphasis on the effects of aquifer mineralogy and conditioning on recovered water quality. A mineral‐component adsorption database was developed that used log K OC for organic matter, empirical chain‐length regressions for clays, and a CD‐MUSIC surface complexation model for iron oxyhydroxides. The database was coupled to a reactive transport model (RTM) to simulate 18 PFAS over repeated ASR cycles. When PFAS were assumed to be initially present in native groundwater, the model predicted that clay minerals were the primary sorbing component for many short‐chain PFAS, with iron oxyhydroxides providing a secondary contribution. By contrast, organic matter was more important for long‐chain PFAS. During successive ASR cycles, sediment‐associated PFAS in the near‐well aquifer became progressively depleted through aquifer conditioning, causing recovered water concentrations to decline over time. For initial groundwater concentrations of 10 ng/L or less, the model predicted that recovered perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) concentrations decreased to near or below the federal maximum contaminant level (MCL) within two ASR cycles. By contr…

title: Development of a sustainable moringa oleifera seed-shell-derived activated carbon for reactive black 5 abatement
The Silk Nebula: A Newly Discovered Giant [O iii ] Emission Filament
abstract: Abstract We report [O iii ] narrowband imaging of an extremely large-scale nebula, the Silk Nebula, discovered by the Super Wide-Field [O iii] Narrow-band Survey (SWONS), together with multifiber medium-resolution spectroscopic data covering the H α , [N ii ], [S ii ], and [O iii ] emission lines, acquired with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) as part of the Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N). Based on 2684 high-quality spectra, we measured its physical parameters, including relative line intensities, radial velocities, and full widths at half-maximum. The [S ii ]/H α ratio of the nebula significantly exceeds the shock-excitation threshold of 0.4. Its location in BPT diagnostic diagrams and spatial morphology of [O iii ] both support the optical emission is dominated by shock-heated gas. The oxygen abundance is near solar and spatially uniform, consistent with a shock propagating into the ambient interstellar medium. Because [O iii ] is the only emission line that clearly traces the nebular morphology, we base our distance estimate exclusively on the [O iii ] kinematics, obtaining a fiducial distance of ∼160 pc. At this distance, the nebula has a physical extent of ∼28 pc along the north–south direction. We suggest that the Silk Nebula is a large [O iii ] filament possibly associated with a supernova remnant, although…

title: Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
Centrosymmetric Coupling Strategy Enabling High‐Color‐Purity Green Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters With 40.84% EQE and CIE y > 0.70
abstract: ABSTRACT Extending the narrow emission characteristics of multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) to all three‐primary‐color emitters is of great significance for next‐generation ultra‐high definition (UHD) displays. Herein, we propose a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy to construct two MR‐TADF isomeric molecules ( 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO ) by covalent dimerization. Both molecules achieve ultra‐narrow green emission in toluene solutions with full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) values of 17 nm (0.086 eV) and 18 nm (0.085 eV), respectively. By combining experimental and theoretical investigations, the spectral narrowing mechanism was elucidated based on this centrosymmetric topological structure through the symmetry dilution of charge variations upon electronic excitation. Non‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on these two isomers exhibit outstanding maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 37.90% ( 2pBZT‐2BNO ) and 38.00% ( 2mBZT‐2BNO , CIE y = 0.71). Notably, with the assistance of sensitizer, ternary‐doped devices of 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO push EQEs to nearly 40% (39.86% and 40.84%) while maintaining well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs. These performances represent the state of the art for narrow‐band MR‐TADF green OLEDs. Overall, this work not only provides a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy for designin…

title: P-316: Dried blood spot C-peptide as a home monitoring tool for β-cell function in early-stage type 1 diabetes
abstract: Abstract Introduction Screening programmes for Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) are expanding, helping to identify presymptomatic individuals. Monitoring changes in β-cell function is crucial for recognising stage 3 progression. Objectives To evaluate serial home-measured dried blood spot (DBS) fasting C-peptide as a tool for monitoring β-cell function and predicting T1D progression in the INNODIA paediatric cohort of first-degree relatives (FDR). Methods FDRs aged 1–18 years with ≥2 autoantibodies (IAb) were followed for up to 4 years with assessments including 6-monthly oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTTs) and monthly home DBS fasting C-peptide measurements. Linear mixed-effect models were fitted to evaluate DBS C-peptide over time. Results Seventy-one children (median [interquartile range] age 10.0 [6.5-12.8] years) collected 735 DBS (average of 6 cards per person [3.0-17.0]). Twenty (28.2%) progressed to stage 3 after a median of 18.6 (9.6-22.3) months. Baseline DBS C-peptide was lower in participants <10 years (n=35) compared to those 10-18 years-old (n=36): 213.5 (184.2-301.0) vs 398.0 (347.5-569.5) pmol/L, p<0.001, but C-peptide trajectories did not differ by age. Linear effects models adjusted for age, BMI, glucose, and sex demonstrated a significant positive association between ln(DBS fasting C-peptide) and ln(OGTT C-peptide area under the curve) (β= 0.25, p=0.025). DBS C-p…

title: Crossing boundaries: learn to spot the warning signs
Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras as Clearing Agents for Pretargeted ImmunoSPECT
abstract: Abstract In vivo pretargeting based on the inverse electron-demand Diels−Alder reaction between a trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-modified monoclonal antibody (mAb) and a radiolabeled tetrazine (Tz) is a highly effective approach for reducing radiation burden in nuclear imaging and therapy. However, the large size and slow pharmacokinetics of full-length immunoglobulins greatly hinder their bloodstream clearance. To circumvent this limitation of pretargeting, much effort has been put towards developing masking or clearing agents: molecules designed to be injected prior to the radioligand to rid the bloodstream of excess circulating TCO-mAbs via clearance organs. Yet even with the use of previously established clearing agents, high levels of TCO-mAb still remain in circulation. Moreover, some of these agents could lead to aggregate formation in the lungs or clogs in the bloodstream. Recently, a novel class of cell−surface protein degraders called lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) have been reported to simultaneously bind hepatocytic-expressed asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) and a harmful, disease-relevant protein, internalizing the latter for lysosomal degradation. Herein, we present a novel ASGPR-targeted tetrazine-bearing LYTAC  TriGalNAc-Tz (LYTAC-Tz)  as a clearing agent for pretargeting. First, the essential components of the pretargeted system were synthesized: LYTAC-Tz, …

title: Optimal allocation of electric vehicle charging stations and renewable energy resources using a modified version of walrus optimizer
abstract: Abstract Decarbonization policies aim to electrify the transportation sector by increasing the use of Electric Vehicles (EVs); consequently, Electric Vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) are widely integrated into distribution systems (DSs). EVCSs can be considered a significant additional electrical load on DSs, leading to negative effects such as increased system power losses and reduced voltage profile and voltage stability. In this regard, the negative effects of adding EVCSs can be mitigated through optimal integration of EVCSs and renewable energy resources (RERs), such as wind turbines (WTs), photovoltaics (PVs), and biomass units. This paper aims to optimize the planning of integrating the EVCSs and RERs into multi-microgrid-based DSs (IEEE 33-bus, 69-bus, and 94-bus) to reduce the total voltage deviations (VDs), the total costs, and improve the total voltage stability index (VSI). A modified version of Walrus Optimizer (MWO) is proposed and applied to solve this problem. MWO is based on enhancing the search capability of the conventional WO algorithm and avoiding its stagnation at local optima using three approaches, including a hybrid chaotic mutation (HCM), Fitness Distance Balance (FDB), and Quasi-opposition-based learning (QOBL). The performance and capability of the MWO are tested and verified using standard benchmark functions, and the obtained results are compared …

title: Frequency and Waveform Effects on Bath-Surface Heat Input from an AC Arc in a Titanium Slag Electric Arc Furnace
Prior Knowledge Enhanced-Velocity Guided Chirplet Transform for Nonstationary Feature Estimation with Application to Bearing Fault Diagnosis in Vehicle Electric Drive Systems
abstract: Effective diagnosis of electric bearing faults, especially weak early-stage faults, remains challenging due to complex rotational-speed conditions and external noise. Although the velocity-guided chirplet transform (VGCT) can effectively characterize nonstationary components, it requires synchronized rotational-speed information, which is often difficult to obtain in practice. To this end, this paper proposes a prior-knowledge-enhanced velocity-guided chirplet transform (PKVGCT) for fault diagnosis without prior rotational-speed information. PKVGCT includes two stages. In the first stage, multiple candidate instantaneous frequencies (IFs) are obtained via peak searching and are smoothed by a second-order difference operator to support obtaining a reliable guideline. In the second stage, the manually selected guideline is further used in the analysis of VGCT, and simultaneously a weak-noise energy filtering mechanism is applied to ultimately yield a high-quality time-frequency (TF) representation (TFR). In numerical analysis, the qualitative analysis of the TFR results, the mean relative error (MRE)-based quantitative analysis, and the robustness analysis under different noise levels all demonstrate the superior performance of PKVGCT. With two experimental cases, the effectiveness of PKVGCT in practical applications is fully demonstrated.

title: Optimized Operating Strategy for the Thermal Management of a Battery Electric City Bus Using Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Electrified propulsion systems offer the potential to reduce global CO2 emissions in the transportation sector, particularly in the field of urban mobility. Electric city buses combine the benefits of public transport systems with locally emission-free mobility. To ensure sufficient range for daily duty cycles, energy efficiency is crucial. Thermal management has a significant impact on the energy demand of battery electric vehicles. Therefore, efficiency can be improved by employing an integrated thermal management architecture that interconnects the individual coolant circuits and enables system-wide optimization. This study proposes an approach to optimize the operating strategy for the thermal management of a battery electric city bus. The important thermal components, including the drive system, battery system and HVAC system, are investigated. Experiments were carried out using a test setup of the system to identify the thermal behavior of the components. The study develops a simulation model of the thermal system of a BEV bus and subsequently uses this model to optimize the operating strategy by means of Bayesian optimization. The goal is to minimize energy demand under representative driving and environmental conditions in the city of Hamburg. The simulation-based analyses highlight potential gains resulting from the optimization of coolant temperatures and the flow rat…

title: Uncertainty-aware overturning stability and operating boundaries of a compact transport vehicle-mounted crane boom
Digital Pedagogies for Entrepreneurship Education in South Africa: Opportunities and Limitations
abstract: This research is situated in the field of entrepreneurship education in the South African higher education context. The analysis is conducted through a systematic literature review with qualitative thematic synthesis, grounded in constructivist and connectivist learning theory. Digital pedagogies provide clear opportunities for application in this field. These approaches may improve learning accessibility, flexibility and student engagement, and promote experiential and interactive learning based on constructivist principles by using tools such as learning management systems, simulations, and online collaboration platforms. Yet, the implementation of these pedagogies is still encountering numerous challenges: the persistent local digital divide, disparities in digital literacy between teachers and students, inadequate technological infrastructure, insufficient funding, and institutional barriers stemming from the lack of a comprehensive digital strategy have impeded their widespread adoption.Furthermore, while digital platforms support learning, they may not fully replicate the complexity of real-world entrepreneurial experiences, underscoring the importance of blended learning approaches. The central argument advanced in this paper is that digital technology alone cannot transform entrepreneurship education; its effectiveness depends on pedagogical integration, institutional c…

title: A circular economy strategy to optimize textile waste collection under a bilevel optimization approach
The Emergence of Sustainability Reporting in a Family Firm: A Case Study in the Luxury Fashion Industry
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the emergence of sustainability reporting in a family‐owned luxury fashion firm. Using a qualitative case study and drawing on socioemotional wealth theory, it focuses on the preparation of a firm's first sustainability report. Findings show that reporting is not initiated as a technical compliance exercise but as a sustainability conceptualization process involving the translation of longstanding values and practices into a communicable, formal structure. This process unfolds through interrelated stages, with a specific configuration of socioemotional wealth dimensions shaping its development. The family influences this development through concerns for authenticity, control, and continuity. Sustainability reporting evolves through negotiation between internal identity and external expectations, supported by a governance core and cross‐functional collaboration. Rather than using disclosure instrumentally, the firm adopts a cautious and value‐driven approach, gradually moving toward selective transparency. In a context dominated by quantitative research, this study offers qualitative, process‐based insights into the micro‐dynamics through which sustainability reporting emerges in a family firm.

title: Digital Marketplace Participation as a Configurational Capability System: Evidence from Township Entrepreneurs in South Africa
abstract: Digital marketplaces are increasingly viewed as critical infrastructures for enabling inclusive entrepreneurial participation in developing economies. However, township entrepreneurs in South Africa continue to experience uneven and structurally constrained engagement despite widespread digital platform diffusion. This study examines Digital Marketplace Participation (DMP) as a configurational capability system shaped by the interaction of technological embedding and structural conversion conditions. Drawing on Domestication Theory and the Capability Approach, the study conceptualises DMP as a multidimensional construct comprising engagement intensity, transactional participation, market reach expansion, platform integration, and customer responsiveness. The explanatory framework integrates platform design and digital literacy (domestication conditions) with affordability, agency, and access to resources (capability conditions). A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, using survey data collected from 152 township SME owner-managers in the Ngaka Modiri Molema District Municipality, South Africa. Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) was used to examine the multivariate relationship between the predictor system and the multidimensional participation outcome system. The results indicate a strong and statistically significant canonical relationship (Rc = 0.81), explainin…

title: Innovative Management Strategies for Enhancing the Sustainability and Profitability of SMMEs in the Western Cape Province in South Africa
abstract: This research examines the novel management techniques utilised by Small, Medium, and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs) in the Western Cape Province of South Africa to improve their sustainability and profitability. Although small and medium-sized enterprises are crucial for economic development and job generation, they encounter several obstacles jeopardising their existence. Employing a qualitative research methodology and a case study framework, semi-structured interviews were carried out with 12 owners and managers of small, medium, and micro enterprises. Thematic examination with ATLAS.ti revealed five principal strategy themes and numerous significant difficulties. The results indicate that small and medium-sized enterprises exhibit resilience and ingenuity when confronted with challenges, utilising digital resources, customer-centric strategies, and localised partnerships. Suggestions encompass enhanced policy backing, readily available financing, and focused skill enhancement

title: Digital Inequality, School Climate and Creative Thinking among Fifteen-Year-Olds in Morocco
abstract: Digital resources may widen students’ opportunities to generate and refine ideas, but access does not guarantee productive educational use. This study examines how digital resources, use patterns and school climate are associated with creative-thinking performance among Moroccan fifteen-year-olds. We analyse the official PISA 2022 student, school and creative-thinking public-use files, comprising 6,867 students in 178 schools. All ten creative-thinking plausible values, the final student weight and 80 Fay-BRR replicate weights are propagated through survey-weighted contextual models. The extraction reproduces Morocco’s published creative-thinking mean (15.48; published rounded value 15) and Level 3-or-higher share (23.31%; published 23%). Greater ICT resource breadth was positively associated with performance after background and school adjustment. By contrast, the adjusted coefficient for perceived access quality was negative. Subject-related and enquiry-based ICT use also had negative adjusted gradients, whereas ICT use for school activities outside class was positive. Sense of belonging was consistently positive; disciplinary climate and mathematics teacher support were imprecisely estimated in the fully adjusted models. Socioeconomic interactions were not supported. Results therefore distinguish digital possession, setting and purpose. Morocco’s challenge extends beyond exp…

title: Infrastructure and Inclusive Growth in West Africa: Dynamic Threshold Evidence with a Focus on Nigeria
abstract: At what level does infrastructure allow economic growth to translate into human development? A Nigeria-only annual threshold model is not statistically feasible because open national data provide only 24 Human Development Index observations, six poverty observations and six inequality observations over 2000–2023. We therefore estimate a Nigeria-centred dynamic threshold model in a 16-country West African panel. The composite infrastructure index is the first principal component of electricity access, internet use, basic water and sanitation; it explains 78.4% of their joint variation. The complete dynamic sample contains 338 country-year observations. Country and year fixed effects, clustered inference and a 399-replication wild-cluster threshold test are used. A candidate breakpoint occurs at 0.544 standard deviations, near the 71st percentile. Above it, the contemporaneous growth–HDI slope appears larger. However, the threshold confidence set is wide and the bootstrap test does not reject linearity (p=0.545). The data therefore does not identify a defensible infrastructure level at which growth begins to improve human development. Average GDP-per-capita growth and institutional quality are positively associated with HDI, while Nigeria’s apparent high-infrastructure differential is weaker than the regional pattern and remains exploratory because the threshold itself is unsuppo…

title: Integral Sliding Mode Control Enhanced by an Adaptive Double-Power Reaching Law for UAV Systems
abstract: This study proposes a robust flight control framework for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory tracking based on Integral Sliding Mode Control (ISMC) enhanced by an Adaptive Double-Power Reaching Law (ADPRL). The proposed controller is designed to improve robustness against lumped uncertainties, external disturbances, and nonlinear UAV dynamics while reducing chattering commonly associated with conventional Sliding Mode Control (SMC). To prevent unnecessary gain escalation near the sliding manifold, a practically bounded adaptive reaching mechanism incorporating sigma-modification, dead-zone regulation, and saturation-based switching regularization is introduced. The controller is formulated within a dual-loop position–attitude control architecture, and its stability properties are examined using a Lyapunov-based approach. Comparative MATLAB simulations are conducted against representative baseline controllers, including SMC, ISMC, STSMC, and ADRC. The results show that the proposed ISMC-ADPRL controller achieves the lowest thrust RMS value of 9.5297 N while maintaining competitive trajectory-tracking performance, indicating a practical balance between tracking accuracy, control-effort reduction, and smoother actuation.

title: Hubungan Power Otot Lengan dengan Kecepatan Jodan Tsuki pada Atlet Shorinji Kempo Unpatti Kota Ambon
abstract: Power otot lengan merupakan komponen kondisi fisik yang berperan dalam mendukung kemampuan pukulan pada olahraga bela diri Shorinji Kempo. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan power otot lengan dengan kecepatan pukulan Jodan Tsuki pada atlet Shorinji Kempo Universitas Pattimura, Kota Ambon. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional. Sampel terdiri atas 20 atlet yang dipilih melalui teknik total sampling. Power otot lengan diukur menggunakan tes two hand medicine ball put, sedangkan kecepatan pukulan diukur berdasarkan jumlah pukulan Jodan Tsuki selama 10 detik. Data dianalisis menggunakan korelasi Pearson Product Moment. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,788 dengan nilai signifikansi p < 0,001 dan koefisien determinasi sebesar 62,15%. Temuan tersebut menunjukkan hubungan positif yang kuat antara power otot lengan dan frekuensi pukulan Jodan Tsuki. Secara biomekanis, kemampuan menghasilkan tenaga eksplosif berpotensi mendukung pelaksanaan pukulan secara cepat dan berulang. Namun, performa pukulan juga dapat dipengaruhi koordinasi gerak dan penguasaan teknik. Penelitian menyimpulkan bahwa power otot lengan berkorelasi signifikan dengan kecepatan pukulan Jodan Tsuki. Hasil ini memberikan dasar bagi pelatih untuk mempertimbangkan pengembangan power otot lengan dalam program latihan.

Pengaruh Intraktivitas Influencer dan Keaslian Influencer Terhadap Loyalitas Melalui Keterikatan Emosional dan Kepercayaan Merek Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of influencer interactivity and influencer authenticity on customer loyalty, with brand trust and emotional attachment serving as mediating variables, in the context of the "Bekas Pantas" thrift shop in Sukabumi City. A quantitative approach utilizing a survey method was employed. Data were collected via questionnaires distributed to customers of the "Bekas Pantas" thrift shop, selected through purposive sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS software. The results indicate that influencer interactivity has a positive and significant effect on brand trust but does not significantly affect emotional attachment. Influencer authenticity has a positive and significant effect on both brand trust and emotional attachment. Furthermore, brand trust and emotional attachment were found to have a positive and significant impact on customer loyalty. These findings suggest that influencer authenticity is a more dominant factor in building emotional connections and consumer trust, whereas influencer interactivity plays a greater role in enhancing brand trust. The study offers implications for thrift shop business owners to be more selective in choosing influencers who are authentic and credible, and capable of fostering long-term relationships with consumers to boost customer loyalty.

title: The Emerging Strategies for Longevity, Succession, and Sustainability of Rural Family-Owned Retail Businesses (RFORBs) in Developing Countries
abstract: Despite a growing body of literature on family business, succession, and intergenerational transition challenges, few studies have addressed the same family businesses in a rural-sector context. Yet, they play critical socio-economic roles- enhancing social integration, serving as commercial hubs that supply essential goods and services, and supporting vulnerable households, including facilitating trade in the most remote market. The study investigates emerging strategies for business endurance and sustainability in rural retail family enterprises in developing economies. A PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of 27 journal papers focusing on developing countries was conducted, and a thematic synthesis was conducted alongside a bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer version 1.6.20, focusing on keyword analysis, thematic mapping, and clustering to identify emerging themes in rural family-owned businesses transitioning to long-term survival across generations. The findings uncovered key emerging innovation strategies: digitalisation, financial inclusion, and consumer-oriented innovation that enhances resilience and long-term sustainability. Also, the study concludes that vision trap, entrepreneurial traits, occult beliefs or supernatural power, resource availability and capacity are the major barriers to longevity of rural family-owned retail businesses. Evaluating the effectiveness of infrastructure development projects in Mnquma Local Municipality
abstract: Infrastructure development is central to improving service delivery and supporting socio-economic development in local municipalities. However, the effectiveness of municipal infrastructure projects depends not only on their physical completion but also on the quality of planning, implementation, governance, community participation, and post-handover maintenance. This study evaluated the effectiveness of infrastructure development projects in Mnquma Local Municipality in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa. Guided by Systems Theory and Participatory Development Theory, the study adopted a qualitative case-study design. Data were collected from 56 participants, comprising six municipal officials who participated in semi-structured interviews and 50 community participants organised into five focus group discussions across Wards 3–7. Municipal documents and limited field observations were used to complement participant accounts. Data were analysed thematically, resulting in five themes: planning and alignment, execution challenges, accountability and transparency, participation and consultation, and sustainability and maintenance. The findings indicate that infrastructure development projects in Mnquma Local Municipality are partially effective. Although formal planning mechanisms are established and completed projects have improved access to some services, their effectiveness…

title: Corruption Perception and Firm Performance: Evidence from High-Polluting Listed Companies in South Africa
abstract: The corruption remains a persistent challenge that distort firm financial performance by increasing operational costs, distorting resource allocation and weakening investor confidence. However, limited studies have been conducted to examine the impact of corruption on financial performance of companies listed in Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa. Limited empirical evidence on the impact of corruption on financial performance in firms listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange many result in policy and governance frameworks that are not evidence-based, limiting the interventions aimed at improving curbing corruption and improving financial performance with JSE-listed companies. This study explores how corruption perception impacts the financial performance of high-polluting companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) for the period 2015 to 2025. The corruption perception index was obtained from the transparency international corruption perception. The financial data and corporate governance data were companies’ annual financial reports/integrated reports. Corruption perception is measured using the Corruption Perception Index (CPI), while firm performance is proxied by return on assets (ROA) and Tobin’s Q. Board independence and board gender diversity are included as governance control variables. The study then utilises the System Generalised Method of Mom…

title: Characteristics of Innovative Digital Technology Entrepreneurship in South Africa: Case of KwaZulu-Natal
abstract: This study examines entrepreneurial characteristics of innovative digital technology entrepreneurship in Kwa-Zulu Natal, for survival and growth. These characteristics are in two folds: personal traits and entrepreneurial behaviour. The purpose of these objective is to address innovative digital SMEs in South Africa who often either struggle to effectively use digital systems such as computers and software’s, or they completely lack adequate skills to exploit the benefits of the digital technology. A quantitative research approach was adopted, while using a non-probability sampling technique to achieve a sample size of 179 excluding 10 participants for pilot study. Data were collected using a self-administered, closed-ended questionnaire, with predetermined answers scaled using a 5-point Likert scale, while data analysis was conducted using SPSS (version 29.0). Innovative digital technology entrepreneurship is becoming recognised worldwide for its significant positive impact on the economic and social growth of a country. It is an important driver for economic growth and development in South Africa. Nevertheless, the study found that digital SMEs in undeveloped and small communities in South Africa have significant constraints that affect both the survival and growth in these regions.
