Association of Intraoperative End-tidal Carbon Dioxide, Ventilation, and Hypotension with Postoperative Mortality in Noncardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Low intraoperative end-tidal carbon dioxide (ET co 2 ) has been associated with increased postoperative mortality in retrospective studies. However, whether this association is independent of intraoperative hypotension, a strong predictor of mortality, and minute ventilation, a primary determinant of ET co 2 , remains uncertain. The authors hypothesized that low intraoperative ET co 2 is independently associated with postoperative mortality after adjustment for both intraoperative hypotension and minute ventilation. Methods: The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing noncardiac surgery during general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation between 2010 and 2020 at a tertiary care center. Primary exposures were intraoperative mean ET co 2 , minute ventilation, and hypotension (severity and duration). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression estimated the independent association between ET co 2 and mortality after adjustment for predefined confounders. An interaction between ET co 2 and hypotension was tested. Results: Among 185,455 patients (in-hospital mortality, 0.85%), lower intraoperative ET co 2 was nonlinearly associated with increased mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 5-mmHg decrease from the median, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.36 to 1.86) independent of minute ventilation and hypotension. Dual Activation and C–N Coupling of CO 2 and N 2 Mediated by Small Fe n + Clusters
abstract: Abstract We present a combined experimental and theoretical study on how small iron clusters activate dinitrogen (N2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) under ambient conditions. Mass spectrometry shows these clusters can cleave the N≡N triple bond, producing a range of odd-nitrogen species, with Fe3N7+ and Fe4N7+ appearing as major products. Introducing CO2 into the downstream flow-tube reactor yields distinct FenNmCO+ and FenNmO+ species, indicating that the CO2 also undergoes C═O bond dissociation under this condition. Thermodynamics and kinetics analyses reveal that the formation of Fe3,4N5CO+ proceeds via C–N coupling pathways and generates a stable N2O molecule. The empty d orbitals of Fe atoms facilitate the coordination of N2 and CO2; meanwhile, not only Fen+ but also the Fe3,4N7+ clusters exhibit delocalized electrons and superatomic states. This allows the half-filled superatomic P orbital to engage in superatom–atom bonding with carbon and oxygen atoms, thereby modifying the covalent coordination and active sites for reactions with N2 and CO2. These findings advance mechanistic insight into nitrogen fixation by iron clusters─highlighting the role of electron delocalization─and point to a promising route of plasma-assisted catalytic conversion of atmospheric CO2 and N2 into value-added products under mild conditions.

Study on the coupling effect characteristics of multiple RFID sensors for crack monitoring in aluminum alloy structure
abstract: Purpose The aircraft skins are prone to fracturing, leading to serious safety hazards, due to manufacturing defects, overstress, fatigue and harsh environments. Therefore, a method with high reliability, low cost and simple networking was needed to achieve structural life evaluation through continuous monitoring. This paper aims to investigate using a sensing system consisting of densely arranged multiple tags for crack monitoring in aluminum alloy structures. Design/methodology/approach In this paper, a sensing system was composed of four tag arrangements, and the variation of gain and impedance caused by the coupling effect among tags was analyzed via simulation. The reliability of sensor systems for crack detection was studied by constructing a test platform. Findings The simulation results showed that as the crack depth in the coverage area of Tag 1 increased, the real part of the impedance of Tag 1 remained constant. In contrast, the value of the imaginary part tended to increase, while the impedance values of other tags remained unchanged. The gain of Tag 1 decreased, while the gains of the different tags remained unchanged. The test results indicated that the backscattered power tended to decrease as the crack depth increased when a single tag was placed on the surface of the aluminum alloy structure. title: Produced-Gas (PG) Versus CO2 Foam in Carbonate Porous Media: Residual-Oil Sensitivity
abstract: Abstract Foam is commonly evaluated with pure CO2 for gas mobility control, yet field operations may inject a CO2-rich produced-gas stream containing methane and nitrogen. This study compares the transport behavior of foam stabilized by the branched nonionic surfactant G12 in pure CO2 and produced gas (PG) in Indiana limestone under reservoir conditions. Foam apparent viscosity was evaluated as a function of the superficial velocity, foam quality, residual oil, and surfactant concentration. Both CO2 and PG generated strong foam and substantial mobility control. Under oil-free conditions, the PG foam generally exhibited higher apparent viscosity than the CO2 foam over the tested velocity and foam-quality ranges. However, residual oil reduced the PG foam strength more strongly than the CO2 foam strength. The CO2 foam showed similar velocity-dependent behavior with and without residual oil, whereas the PG foam exhibited lower apparent viscosity and a changed shear-thinning response in the oil-bearing core. Power-law fits showed similar velocity dependence for CO2 foam with and without residual oil, whereas the PG system showed a larger difference between oil-free and residual-oil conditions. Foam-quality scans similarly showed that the PG foam was more strongly affected by residual oil, particularly at intermediate foam qualities. These results indicate that pure CO2 does not nece…

title: Intelligent Energy Consumption Model for a Smart Building
abstract: Background The increasing deployment of smart meters in buildings has created opportunities for data-driven energy management, but the detection of abnormal electricity consumption remains challenging because energy-use patterns vary with time, operational schedules, and environmental conditions. These smart meters and connected monitoring technologies continuously create electricity consumption data, which can be used for energy management, fault detection, operational monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Methods In order to monitor building electricity consumption, this study developed an intelligent anomaly detection system based on a Support Vector Machine (SVM) with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel. Electricity consumption data sourced from smart meters was used as the developed model achieved reliable anomaly detection, identifying irregular energy consumption with improved detection and achieved dependable anomaly detection. Results The overall performance metrics of the model was Accuracy of 97.79%, with a macro-averaged F1 Score of 0.8842, Precision of 0.925, and Recall of 0.8513 The results showed reduced false alarms and enhanced adaptability to changes in energy use patterns. Conclusion The study contributed to energy efficiency, cost reduction, and sustainable building management, while also providing a reliable framework for intelligent energy monitoring in…

title: Fire Bloom: Energy-Efficient Cluster-Based Routing Protocol for Scalable Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have been used in smart agriculture, industrial automation, and environmental monitoring applications, which require efficient and reliable routing with energy efficiency. Particularly the selection and operation of the cluster heads (CHs) play significant role in the performance of the network. In this work, we introduce a scalable, reliable and energy efficient cluster-based routing protocol (Fire Bloom), which combines adaptive CH selection and energy-aware routing. The cluster map and the packet flow intensity map even show the communication loads on the base station. The packet delivery ratio (PDR) of Fire Bloom is 97.2%, which is 6–10% better than the competing protocols. Fire Bloom achieved a PDR greater than 91% under a scalability test with 100–500 nodes, which means it can maintain good performance as the density of the network becomes denser. Energy usage is roughly proportional to the traffic volume but lower than previously reported values. Near-linear scalability at runtime is also proposed: increasing the number of nodes from 100 to 1,000 took from 1.2 s to 14.1 s. In general, Fire Bloom lowers overall end-to-end delay, increases load balancing across CHs, boosts energy efficiency, and it is resilient to changes in network conditions and maintains successful packet delivery. These results prove that it is capable of scalable and en…
venue: Journal of ICT Research and Applications

title: Wsn Cluster Head Selection for Energy Balancing Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model
abstract: Energy efficiency is a critical design consideration for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), particularly in heterogeneous environments. To optimize energy utilization and enhance network longevity, this study integrates deep learning models into the cluster head (CH) selection process. The proposed methodology employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze spatial attributes such as residual energy, node density, and proximity to sinks, and a Recurrent Neural Network with Long Short-Term Memory (RNN-LSTM) to capture temporal variations in energy depletion and workload distribution. The outputs of these models are combined through a hierarchical decision framework, enabling dynamic and adaptive CH selection. Comparative analysis with I-SEP and OptGACHE demonstrates that the proposed methodology maintains a residual energy of 9.89 J at a node density of 150, surpassing I-SEP and OptGACHE by 1.34% and 1.33%, respectively. Cluster lifetime is extended to 0.63 ms for 20 clusters, reflecting improvements of 16.7% over OptGACHE and 57.5% over I-SEP. Additionally, the packet delivery rate (PDR) reaches 450,000 kbps at a node density of 150, representing enhancements of 28.6% over OptGACHE and 50% over I-SEP. These findings validate the proposed methodology as a robust solution for energy-efficient CH selection, improving the sustainability and performance of WSNs in diverse oper…
venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)

title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network
abstract: Abstract Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment–protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic–vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pigment compositions of CP29 and Lhcb1, a monomeric subunit of the major LHCII trimer, reshape excitonic connectivity and energy transfer pathways in the complexes. Compared to Lhcb1, energy transfer pathways in CP29 are more spatially connected and reversible, suggesting that CP29 evolved to distribute excitation between the core and periphery of the PSII antenna. We find that small structural modifications from a common framework tune CP29 and Lhcb1 to complementary roles in the PSII supercomplex.
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

title: Integrasi Teknologi Digital Dalam Pembelajaran Tematik Terpadu Model Webbed Untuk Mengatasi Kesulitan Belajar Siswa Di Sekolah Dasar: Kajian Sistematis
abstract: Tujuan – Penelitian ini mensintesis bukti mengenai kesulitan belajar dalam pembelajaran tematik terpadu di sekolah dasar, menelaah penggunaan teknologi digital, dan mengusulkan kerangka integrasinya dalam model Webbed. Penelusuran laman penerbit dan jurnal pada 25 Oktober 2026 mencakup publikasi periode 2021–2026. Satu penilai menyaring 70 rekaman unik dan menetapkan 13 studi inti: tiga mengenai kesulitan belajar, tujuh mengenai teknologi digital, dan tiga mengenai model Webbed. title: Replacing CTAB with Renewable-Origin Surfactants for the Synthesis of Mesoporous 8YSZ: Structural Integrity, Functional Validation, and Sustainability Assessment
abstract: Abstract Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB), a conventional structure-directing agent for mesoporous materials, is a petroleum-derived toxic compound whose removal requires energy-intensive multistep purification, increasing the environmental impact of the process. This study presents the sustainable synthesis of mesoporous 8 mol % yttria-stabilized zirconia (8YSZ) by replacing CTAB with glycerol (GLY) and glycerol monostearate (GMS), low-cost, renewable agents derived from the oleochemical industry. Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and N2 physisorption confirm the formation of fully cubic fluorite 8YSZ with mesoporous frameworks of interconnected nanocrystals, which exhibit appropriate macroporosity after high-temperature sintering. Ionic conductivity measurements, corrected for porosity, tortuosity, and constrictivity, demonstrate that scaffolds derived from renewable surfactants retain intrinsic oxygen-ion conduction equivalent to the CTAB reference and consistent with literature values for dense 8YSZ. A quantitative sustainability assessment shows that the renewable route reduces process mass intensity by up to 89% (from ∼710 to 78–81), energy intensity by 73% (from 3.87 to 1.03 kWh g–1), and production costs by up to 60%, while maintaining structural integrity in batches up to 10 g. These findings establish renewable surfactant substitution as…

title: Phenology and surface energy balance changes across northern lands
abstract: Plant phenological shifts – notably earlier start (SOS) and later end (EOS) of the growing season – affect surface albedo, latent and sensible heat fluxes, and ultimately the surface temperature. The magnitude and spatial variability of these effects remain uncertain. Using Earth observation and reanalysis data (2001–2021), we quantify the sensitivity of surface energy fluxes to SOS and EOS changes across northern lands (> 30° N), and we report uncertainties and convergence across multiple independent datasets. Spatially-aggregated results show that an earlier SOS is generally associated with decreased albedo by up to 0.003 d −1 (needleleaf forests and tundra), and increased latent heat fluxes by 0.47 Wm-2d-1 (spatial median), ranging from 0.15 Wm-2d-1 (croplands) to 0.68 Wm-2d-1 (mixed forests). Delays in EOS are also associated with decreases in albedo, though much smaller in magnitude, and with increases in latent heat flux – up to ∼0.14 Wm-2d-1 in mixed forests – with weaker and more variable responses across other land-cover types. Datasets reveal large spatial variability and discrepancies in the responses of the sensible heat fluxes and thus evaporative fraction. Across datasets, earlier SOS is consistently associated with increased latent heat flux, and the concurrent evidence from evaporative fraction suggests a shift towards enhanced latent cooling. These findings are…

title: Machine Learning for Predicting Dielectric Energy-Storage Properties of Perovskite Oxides
abstract: Perovskite oxides with the ABO₃ structure are core candidates for dielectric energy-storage capacitors, whose recoverable energy density is governed by the dielectric constant, the breakdown field strength, and the nonlinear polarization response. This review surveys recent machine-learning studies on predicting these properties of oxide perovskites, covering three representative quantities—the dielectric constant, the breakdown field strength, and the ferroelectric Curie temperature—together with direct performance indicators such as recoverable energy density and efficiency. The works are compared along the evolution of methods, from manual descriptors and ensemble learning to graph neural networks, small-sample strategies, and generative inverse design, with dataset size, verification level, and accuracy documented. Three insights emerge: physical descriptor models remain competitive and interpretable under small-sample conditions; equivariant graph neural networks offer advantages for tensorial and finite-temperature tasks at higher data and computational cost; and generative inverse design is emerging, with preliminary success at the ferroelectric mesoscopic scale, but remains limited by scarce multimodal data and incomplete experimental-validation loops, which constitute the main challenges ahead.

title: Pore-Scale Oil Mobilization during CO2 Water-Alternating-Gas Flooding in a Low-Permeability Medium-Viscosity Oil Reservoir
abstract: Abstract Water-alternating-gas (WAG) flooding has been widely applied for enhanced oil recovery. However, how it mobilizes oil in pores of different sizes remains poorly understood in low-permeability reservoirs with medium-viscosity oil. Core flooding experiments with online nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements compared water flooding, CO2 flooding, and WAG flooding using cores and fluids representative of the Niuquanhu block. A calibrated conversion between the transverse relaxation time T2 and the pore diameter, with its uncertainty propagated, related the class boundaries of 10 and 100 ms to 0.5 and 5 μm. A segmentation algorithm showed that these boundaries lie within the two pooled transition bands of the mobilization profiles, which shift with the pore-size modes of each core. The mobilization degree of each pore class was quantified by validated trapezoidal integration of the T2 spectra. Shifting the residual-oil spectra by 0.05 decade, which bounds the effect of dissolved CO2, changed the class-wise values by at most 8.45 percentage points. A shift of 0.10 decade changed the values of WAG flooding on Core 1 by at most 4.70 percentage points, and the ranking remained unchanged. On the metered basis, WAG flooding recovered 88.82% of the oil, 1.32 times that of CO2 flooding, and 3.60 times that of water flooding. On the NMR basis, its ratio to water flooding was …

title: Strategic integration of business intelligence tools to enhance business management efficiency
abstract: Purpose This study examines how data and business intelligence (BI) systems support procurement decisions and strategic execution. It aims to improve the efficiency of business management. Design/methodology/approach A five-stage implementation framework is proposed for integrating BI into strategic business execution. The methodology includes technical validation and a case study that assesses the impact of digital transformation and BI adoption on tracking strategic execution and key performance indicators (KPIs). We frame BI adoption within the broader digital transformation (DT) agenda, aligning data, processes and governance to strategic objectives. Findings Research shows that aligning digital transformation initiatives with an organization’s specific operational needs is the most cost-effective path to achieving efficiency. Analysis suggests that a successful digital transformation must be closely linked to the management requirements. Selecting appropriate BI tools is critical to delivering substantial business value. Research limitations/implications The proposed framework offers managers a structured approach to implementing BI systems aligned with strategic goals. The case study provides actionable insights for professionals aiming to improve operational and management performance through data-driven strategies and digital transformation. title: Physical Origins of Anion Recognition in Rationally Designed Receptors: Balancing Interaction Energy and Drug Score
abstract: Abstract The rational design of synthetic anion receptors requires a detailed understanding of how different noncovalent interactions govern molecular recognition while maintaining physicochemical properties compatible with biological applications. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to investigate the recognition of biologically relevant anions (acetate, chloride, and dihydrogen phosphate) by seven structurally distinct receptors. The analyses reveal that classical N–H···anion hydrogen bonds constitute the dominant contribution to the calculated interaction energy, whereas halogen bonding, C–H···anion contacts, and anion−π interactions provide secondary or cooperative stabilization depending on the receptor architecture. Complementary in silico ADMET, drug score, and toxicity analyses, integrated through a composite multicriteria ranking, identify receptor 7 as the system that best combines strong anion-binding affinities, predominantly arising from classical N–H···anion hydrogen bonding, with an excellent pharmacokinetic profile, full compliance with Lipinski’s criteria, and the absence of predicted mutagenic, tumorigenic, irritant, or reproductive risks. These findings establish quantitative relationships linking electronic structure, noncovalent interaction mechanisms, and pharmacological descriptors, providing mechanistic principles for…

The High Energy Photon Source: A 6 GeV and Fourth-Generation Synchrotron Light Source in Beijing
abstract: Abstract The high-energy photon source (HEPS) is a 6 GeV, fourth-generation synchrotron light source. As a greenfield light source, the project has spanned more than seven years to complete the design, procurement, assembly, installation, commissioning, and pilot operation. The accelerator complex features a hybrid 7-bend achromat lattice and a 1360 m circumference storage ring. A natural emittance of 55.6 pm·rad has been achieved at a 120 mA beam current with brightness exceeding 1 × 1022 phs/s/mm2/mrad2/0.1% BW. In Phase I, 15 beamlines have been constructed, three of them long beamlines. The first light from an insertion device was delivered downstream to an endstation 350 m away at the ID21 Imaging beamline in October 2024. HEPS had met all of the key performance parameters in October 2025. HEPS is characterized by its high-energy, high-brightness, and high-coherence X-ray capabilities. Following four runs of pilot operations since December 2025, the HEPS formally opens to global users in the second half of 2026.

title: Impact of local roughness gradients on laminar flow within granite fractures
abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting fluid dynamics in crystalline rock remains fundamental to deep geothermal reservoir management. In particular, within the wider pressure-stimulated zones of geothermal reservoirs, high fluid pressures drive low effective normal stress conditions, often resulting in normal opening or shear displacement with minimal abrasion. This study investigates the relationship between granitic fracture roughness and the resulting flow behavior under these conditions. While global surface statistics are frequently used to characterize fractures, this study investigates whether local topography fluctuations are a more critical factor. We conducted high-resolution topography measurements of granite fracture samples from three locations next to the geothermal anomaly of the Rhine Graben. Our analysis reveals that local fluctuations in the roughness height gradient dominate the evolution of the fracture aperture during shear. The resulting fracture voids exhibit mean apertures up to 2 mm larger than conventional models suggest, leading to a decreased normalized local aperture distribution, widening with shear distance. To quantify the fluid dynamic impact of these geometric shifts, we employed a dual-modeling approach applying laminar flow at low Reynolds numbers: a 1D model was used to isolate how the width of the aperture distribution affects the fracture hydraul…

title: The Role of Civil Engineering in Renewable Energy Storage: Contributions and Challenges
abstract: Renewable energy generation is characterized by intermittency; consequently, energy storage is a prerequisite for its large-scale utilization. Existing research primarily focuses on power systems and electrochemical materials, often overlooking the civil engineering aspects of energy storage projects. This paper employs a literature review approach to examine the engineering characteristics of four mainstream technologies, namely pumped hydro storage, compressed air energy storage, battery energy storage stations, and hydrogen energy storage, and summarizes the roles of civil engineering and the typical issues involved. The study reveals that civil engineering encompasses the entire lifecycle of energy storage projects from site selection and design to construction, and that the extent of civil engineering involvement directly impacts project feasibility and long-term operational safety. Specific challenges include lining cracking and hydraulic fracturing risks in pumped hydro storage; surrounding rock degradation and sealing performance in lined-cavern compressed air energy storage; caprock integrity and fault avoidance in salt-cavern hydrogen storage; pollution containment following thermal runaway in battery storage; and the prevention of hydrogen embrittlement in pipelines for hydrogen transport. This study demonstrates that the engineering constraints associated with energ…

Variable Step-Size LMS-Based Anti-Jamming Algorithm for Industrial IoT Communications over 2.4 GHz ISM Band
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems deployed in factory environments face severe narrowband interference in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, where ZigBee-based sensor networks coexist with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices operating under strong electromagnetic interference from industrial machinery. Conventional adaptive filters employing fixed step-size Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithms fail under high Jammer-to-Noise Ratio (JNR) conditions, exhibiting numerical instability and bit error rates (BER) approaching 0.5. This paper proposes a Variable Step-Size LMS (VS-LMS) algorithm integrated with Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) modulation to address this limitation. The proposed step-size update rule adaptively scales the learning rate according to instantaneous filter error: μ(n)=μ min +(μ max -μ min ) · exp(-α·e 2 (n)) , enabling large step-sizes during convergence and small step-sizes under strong interference to maintain numerical stability. Python-based simulations under AWGN plus sinusoidal narrowband interference (JNR=25 dB) demonstrate that the proposed VS-LMS scheme reduces BER by 76.1% compared to conventional fixed-step LMS, recovering communication quality (BER=0.12) in scenarios where fixed-step LMS completely fails. The results confirm that the proposed software-layer approach provides a practical, hardware-agnostic solution for reliable IIoT communications in el…

Biodiversity, conservation and design thinking: an AI-driven, geodesign framework for determining habitat quality
abstract: Abstract Species Distribution Modeling (SDM) is central to biodiversity assessment, yet its diagnostic outputs rarely translate into spatially explicit conservation strategies. We present an AI-driven Geodesign framework that embeds Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modeling in an iterative refinement cycle to produce phased conservation priorities. Applied to Illinois, we compiled 826,989 occurrence records for 10,029 species across 11 taxonomic classes (fungi, invertebrates, vertebrates, and plants) modeling class-level habitat suitability against 27 environmental predictors at 600 m resolution. Iterative refinement improved mean apparent Area Under the Curve (AUC) from 0.684 to 0.764 (mean True Skill Statistic 0.439). Comparison with 542 Critical Trends Assessment Program (CTAP) field sites showed statistically significant but modest concordance between the modeled plant component and observed plant richness (Spearman ρ = 0.275, p < 0.001). Protected area covers only 4.42% of state lands, misaligned with modeled conservation priorities along the Mississippi River corridor and Shawnee Hills. Four conservation tiers quantify protection gaps: the most conservative (95th percentile, 7.25% of area) requires 1.6-fold expansion, while meeting 30×30 goals (75th percentile, 36.25%) demands an additional 4.64 million hectares. A Biodiversity Efficiency Index showed deciduous forests support 12…

title: Failure-Aware Explainable Decision Support for Circular Sulfate Adsorbent Design under Hydrochemical Domain Shift
abstract: This study develops a failure-aware, explainable environmental decision-support framework for circular sulfate adsorbent design and asks whether predictive transportability and engineering usefulness remain aligned under hydrochemical domain shift. A 58-sample Semarang groundwater dataset served as the development domain. Random forest achieved internal AUROC 0.710 ± 0.165, and a target-free matrix-complexity index (MCI) combined EC, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Cl⁻, and HCO₃⁻ into four treatment regimes. Using the fixed Semarang model, discrimination was retained in the 25-sample Bayat basin (AUROC 0.794; balanced accuracy 0.762) but was lost in a larger cross-country Mekong challenge (n = 118; AUROC 0.491; 95% CI 0.367–0.617). In contrast, the fixed-reference MCI remained strongly associated with sulfate in Mekong (rs = 0.699; 95% CI 0.587–0.782), with 73 of 78 high-sulfate events in the complex-matrix domain. To assess consistency between the engineering interpretation and independent material evidence, open-access sulfate-adsorption studies were synthesized at study level. Zirconium modification increased reported pomelo-peel-biochar qmax from 1.02 to 35.21 mg/g (34.5-fold), while CaCl₂-modified kelp carbon retained substantial reported kinetic uptake in lake water (569.37 mg/g versus 624.39 mg/g in simulated water). The combined evidence supports a workflow in which external model validity…

title: Integrated Computational Design and Discovery of Novel Indole-Linked Guanidine Derivatives as BACE-1 Inhibitors for Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a chronic, progressive neurodegenerative disorder predominantly affecting 47 million people worldwide. Dysregulation of BACE-1, the initiating enzyme in the amyloidogenic cascade, plays a pivotal role in AD pathogenesis. Conventional anticholinesterase inhibitors can only provide symptomatic relief without stopping disease progression. In this study, we employed an integrated computational approach to rationally design novel indole-based BACE-1 inhibitors through pharmacophore modeling, 3D-QSAR analysis, ligand–protein docking, pharmacophore-guided virtual screening, MD simulation, and ADME studies. DDHRR_1 was identified as the best pharmacophore model with a survival score of 5.7767. Statistically significant 3D-QSAR models were obtained, wherein the atom-based model demonstrated high predictive reliability ([Formula: see text]), while the field-based model exhibited acceptable predictive ability ([Formula: see text]). Among the dataset compounds, compound B38 (3i) displayed the optimal binding affinity (−6.567 kcal/mol; PDB ID: 4DJU), with key interactions at GLY95, TYR132, and PHE169. [Formula: see text]-group enumeration generated 2408 derivatives, among which [Formula: see text]1 and [Formula: see text]2 exhibited strong binding affinity (−10.339 kcal/mol and −9.611 kcal/mol). A comparative analysis of the referenced ligand, the two best-perfor…

title: Key considerations in the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of observational studies in dialysis
abstract: Purpose of review In this review, key considerations in the design, conduct, and analysis of observational studies in dialysis research are explored in a unique patient population for which interventional trials are challenging and limited. Recent findings The use of target trial emulation is increasing and provides a conceptual framework for the design of observational studies. A target trial is a hypothetical trial that would be conducted to answer a research question. It requires investigators to ask a clinically relevant question and then specify eligibility criteria, the treatment strategies that will be compared, the follow-up period, outcomes of interest, and the causal contrast (intention-to-treat vs. per-protocol analysis). The protocol for an observational study is then created to mirror the target trial. In doing so, the question is clear, bias is reduced, and underlying assumptions are made transparent. Illustrative examples are used to highlight common pitfalls in dialysis research. Summary In conclusion, randomized controlled trials are not always feasible or even the ideal approach for answering certain questions. However, observational studies are challenging and require careful planning and execution to ensure robust, unbiased results. Target trial emulation provides a blueprint to improve the quality of observational study design.

title: Innovation Direction of Intelligent Products - Research on Personalized Product Design System Based on Generative AI
abstract: In the context of consumption upgrade and intelligent manufacturing, personalized customization has become a core trend in product innovation. Generative AI (AIGC) is gradually a new tool, for the automation product design. This paper puts forward an AI-driven personalized product design system, that integrates engineering constraints and business dimensions. This is built on a diffusion generation model combined with a dual-cycle generative-evaluation architecture, and we use the smart lunch box as an empirical case to verify its feasibility. Through our research, workflow reengineering and quantitative evaluation, our study implecates that the system achieves an engineering feasibility for generated solutions, compared to unconstrained AIGC generation. The design cycle is reduced greatly, representing an efficiency gain. This research not only provides new tools and for product design but also offers a feasible path to achieve mass customization.

title: Where access meets sustainability: a qualitative multi-city reading of accessibility and green disclosure in peer-to-peer short-term rental platforms
abstract: Purpose This paper examines whether accessibility and sustainability are pursued together or separately in peer-to-peer short-term rental accommodation, and what this implies for platforms, hosts and destinations advancing Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 8.9 and SDG 10. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative comparative content analysis covered all 624,581 public listings in twenty-two developed and emerging short-term rental markets. One set of coding rules, with word lists in the main local languages, separated access provision from access barriers and environmental equipment from everyday practice. Guest reviews from Albany and New York City served as depth cases. Findings The platform's amenity vocabulary contains environmental terminology but no accessibility terminology. Hosts mention access barriers far more often than provision, and the two topics rarely appear together. Developed markets mention access about three times as often as emerging markets, which mention environmental equipment twice as often. Disclosure concentrates among professionalized operators without commercial penalty. In both depth cases, guest reviews reported obstacles that listings had not disclosed. Practical implications The binding constraint on inclusive short-term rental accommodation is informational rather than physical, and inexpensive to relieve. An action agenda is offered for platf…

title: What is The Relationship Between Peer Pressure to Follow Entertainment Trends and High School Students' Peer Relationships?
abstract: The entertainment trend is increasingly integrated into the daily social life of teenagers. Popular music, online videos, games, movies and other forms of entertainment can provide common topics and influence the way high school students interact with their peers. At the same time, teenagers may feel pressured and want to keep up with these trends to participate in group dialogue and maintain a sense of belonging. This study explores the relationship between peer pressure, trend-chasing behaviour and peer relationships among high school students who follow entertainment trends. Therefore, we have collected relevant data through online questionnaires, covering these three aspects. After data screening, a total of 54 replies were obtained, of which 47 valid data were retained. Pearson correlation analysis shows that peer pressure is positively correlated with social relationship score, r = 0.485, p < 0.001; wind-chasing behaviour is also positively correlated with social relationship score, r = 0.464, p = 0.001. However, there is no significant correlation between peer pressure and wind-chasing behaviour, r = 0.182, p = 0.221. The multivariate regression model has statistical significance, F(2, 44) = 13.53, p < 0.001, and the adjusted R² is 0.353. Peer pressure and trend-following behaviour are still significant independent predictors of social relationship scores. In general, th…

title: Strategic value of peer-driven ESG practices: decomposing ESG into its core components
abstract: Purpose Firms do not make environmental, social and governance (ESG) decisions in isolation; they operate within industries where competitors’ sustainability practices can shape strategic choices. However, despite growing evidence of peer effects on corporate policies, little is known about whether and how peer firms influence a firm’s ESG engagement. This study aims to examine peer-driven ESG behavior and investigates whether these effects differ across the ESG dimensions. Design/methodology/approach Using a comprehensive sample of US publicly listed firms from 2005 to 2021, the authors examine how industry peers’ ESG performance influences a firm’s own ESG practices. Rather than treating ESG as a single measure, the authors decompose it into its ESG components to identify differences in peer effects across ESG dimensions. Findings The authors find strong evidence that firms adjust their ESG practices in response to their industry peers. Peer effects are particularly pronounced for environmental and social practices, while the effect for governance is weaker. Further analysis suggests that firms respond to peer ESG practices partly to remain competitive and improve access to external financing. The results are robust to alternative specifications and tests. Research limitations/implications The US-focused analysis points to several directions for future research. Although the …

Economic and institutional drivers of renewable energy adoption: A cross-country panel analysis
abstract: This article identifies the economic and institutional factors driving cross-country differences in renewable energy adoption, focusing on solar and wind power. Unlike previous studies that either compare the share of renewable energy sources or analyze individual support policies, we propose the Renewable Deployment Gap Index (RDGI), an indicator which captures the gap between actual renewable deployment and the level expected under given resource, macroeconomic, and regulatory conditions. The empirical analysis is based on a panel dataset of countries spanning 2010–2023. The methodology includes country- and year-fixed effects models, a dynamic specification with a lagged dependent variable, and a counterfactual scenario in which regulatory quality is improved to the level of leading countries. The results indicate that the most persistent barrier is fossil fuel inertia in the electricity sector: a higher share of fossil-fuel-based generation is statistically associated with a lower share of renewables (excluding hydropower) and a lower share of solar and wind generation specifically. The Regulatory Indicators for Sustainable Energy (RISE) tool exhibits stronger explanatory power across countries than within-country short-term dynamics. The counterfactual analysis suggests that if countries below the 90th percentile of the RISE distribution were to raise their regulatory qual…

title: How Does the Relationship Between Elite Youth Sports Participation and Post-Secondary Enrollment Vary Across Different Races and Ethnicities in Canada?
abstract: Elite youth sport is often described as a pathway to university, scholarships, and future opportunity, but access to that pathway is not equal for every athlete. This paper asks: How do race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic factors shape the relationship between elite youth sport participation and post-secondary opportunities in Canada? To investigate this question, this paper employs a qualitative case study using two in-depth, one-on-one interviews with elite youth athletes from soccer and hockey. Their experiences were compared with existing Canadian research on sport participation, financial barriers, discrimination, family support, and recruitment knowledge. The interviews suggest that race was not the most visible barrier in either athlete's personal experience, although both accounts leave open the possibility of less obvious forms of racial bias. Instead, socioeconomic status, family resources, recruitment knowledge, and personal connections appeared to have a stronger direct influence on access to elite development and post-secondary opportunities. In short, elite sport can create educational opportunities, but access to and benefit from those opportunities depend on more than athletic talent alone.

title: Determinants of Cloud Storage Adoption in Indonesia: Integrating Positive Valence, Security, and Trust
abstract: Cloud storage adoption in Indonesia remains under-researched, and prevailing technology-adoption models generally assume that user trust is a robust antecedent of adoption intention. Drawing on the positive Valence Framework, this study integrates two positive utility constructs—perceived ubiquity and perceived benefits—with security and trust to explain behavioral intention to adopt cloud storage. Survey data from 202 digitally literate Indonesian internet users were collected through Google Forms and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM); common method bias was assessed using Harman’s single-factor test and a full collinearity (VIF) assessment. Perceived benefits exerted the strongest effect on behavioral intention, followed by security and perceived ubiquity, whereas trust had no significant effect. Theoretically, the non-significance of trust indicates that, in an ecosystem dominated by a few globally legitimate providers embedded in users’ device platforms, trust operates as an assumed baseline rather than a differentiating criterion. This reframes trust from a direct antecedent to a boundary-conditioned, hygiene-type factor and refines the applicability of Valence- and TAM/UTAUT-based adoption models to developing digital markets.

title: Household work participation is associated with adolescent mental health through parent-child relationship and resilience
abstract: Adolescent mental health is a central concern in educational psychology and youth development. This study used data from a school-based survey on 1,152 junior middle school students in Xi’an, China and examined whether and how participation in household work was associated with adolescent mental health. We assessed a serial mediation model in which parent-child relationship and adolescent resilience were specified as potential mediators. Results revealed that household work participation was positively correlated with adolescent mental health, parent-child relationship, and resilience. Furthermore, household work participation was significantly associated with greater perceived closeness with parents and higher resilience, after adjusting for gender, grade, only-child status, academic performance, hukou status, school type, family structure, and parental education. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that the association between household work participation and mental health was consistent with an indirect-effects pattern that involved parent-child relationship, resilience, and their serial pathway. Among the indirect pathways, the resilience pathway accounted for the largest proportion of the total indirect effect. These findings suggest that household work may represent a meaningful family-based context associated with adolescent psychological well-being, greater perceived…

title: Women’s Participation, Human Resource Management, and Local Natural Resource Governance: A Conceptual Analysis of Panchayati Raj Institutions in Una District, Himachal Pradesh, India
abstract: Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) have become increasingly significant for decentralised local governance and may be relevant for the management of natural resources, including forest, grazing and water. With the adoption of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, the women’s quota in PRIs has increased their representation in local governance formally. Nevertheless, numerical representation does not always mean effective participation and influence on natural resource governance. The objective of this study is to analyse theoretically the relationship between women’s participation, human resource management (HRM), and local natural resource governance, especially in the case of Una district, Himachal Pradesh. Based on literature on decentralised governance, gender, common pool resources, reservation policy, and public sector HRM, a theoretical framework is developed. This study underlines the significance of taking into account the institutional conditions along with representation, keeping in mind that the impacts vary based on the context. The conceptual analysis highlights that formal representation is not sufficient to achieve effective participation, and that capacity development, role clarification, and institutional support may possibly explain this relationship. Its main contribution lies in bringing into consideration public sector HRM issues in the analysis of …

REVENUE GROWTH AND EXPENDITURE PRIORITIES IN KARNATAKA: TRENDS IN STATE FINANCES AND IMPLICATIONS FOR INCLUSIVE GROWTH
abstract: The fiscal capacity of state governments plays a crucial role in promoting economic growth, social development and inclusive welfare. Karnataka has experienced substantial changes in revenue mobilisation, capital receipts and public expenditure over the period 2011–12 to 2025–26. This paper examines the trends in the state’s revenue and capital receipts and the composition of developmental and non-developmental expenditure using secondary data published in the Karnataka Economic Survey 2025–26. The paper argues that strengthening revenue mobilisation, improving expenditure efficiency and protecting growth-enhancing investments are essential for sustainable and inclusive development. The study also identifies inconsistencies in selected expenditure-table totals that require verification before definitive fiscal conclusions can be drawn.

title: Research on Route Optimization for Electric Vehicles Leveraging 5G-Enabled Vehicular Networks
abstract: With the deep deployment of 5G in intelligent transportation, 5G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has become an important carrier for vehicle-road collaboration, smart mobility and intelligent transportation development. Taking into account the differentiated travel behaviors of electric vehicles, the incomplete spatiotemporal traffic parameters and the limited collaborative perception and decision-making, this paper presents a systematic 5G-IoV traffic model for complex urban scenarios. Electric vehicles are classified as taxis, commuter private cars, and other functional vehicles based on global traffic statistics and industry norms, excluding pure electric busses with fixed charging patterns. In this study, the parameters of vehicle state and multi-type travel chains are defined by mathematical models, including normal distributions to describe the patterns of vehicle departure and return for different travel chains. The 5G-IoV model integrates 5G-V2X vehicle-road collaboration, smart mobility, and digital automotive supply chain management, and integrates with vehicle-road-cloud to support comprehensive modeling of vehicle perception, information interaction, traffic scheduling, and operation and maintenance. The results show that the model can effectively reflect the differentiated spatiotemporal travel characteristics, and is helpful for traffic simulation and collaborative sch…

Beyond cost and sustainability: a strategic value creation framework for mobility investments in SMEs
abstract: Purpose The purpose and goals of the proposed research are to design and demonstrate a strategic decision-support system for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) evaluating investments in sustainable mobility under conditions of uncertainty. While the emphasis of existing studies primarily lies on vehicle attractiveness and technical capabilities, the proposed study will adopt a strategic management approach, highlighting the value-creation potential of electric mobility, especially in combination with renewable energy production within the local environment, in uncertain circumstances. Design/methodology/approach The proposed framework is based on the fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making approach, which is based on the Fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution (Fuzzy TOPSIS) approach. A Strategic Value Creation Index is proposed, which is fuzzy in nature and acts as a fuzzy economic indicator of the value-creating potential of sustainable mobility solutions that cannot be measured using economic parameters such as cost and performance. The framework integrates economic, environmental, and energy-related criteria. It is applied to an illustrative case study involving an SME evaluating alternative sustainable mobility investment options, including electric vehicles with and without photovoltaic energy support. Fuzzy logic is employed to repre…

title: Biochar as a sustainable strategy for greenhouse gas remediation and climate change mitigation
abstract: Abstract The continuous rise in global greenhouse gases (GHGs) emission over the past decade has created an urgent need for cost-effective and environmentally sustainable technologies to mitigate GHG emissions and enhance carbon sequestration. Biochar (BC), a renewable carbon-rich material produced through the pyrolysis of biomass has attracted increasing attention because of its superior physico-chemical characteristics like porous structure, large surface area as well as long-term carbon stability. These characteristics position BC as a promising tool for achieving net-zero emissions. This review critically examines BC application in GHGs mitigation, factors influencing BC effectiveness to combat GHG emissions, limitations and SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats) analysis are also discussed to stimulate investment in the BC industry, while supporting circular economy principles and sustainable carbon sequestration at a global scale. Overall, this review analyses BC as a scalable negative-emission technology with significant potential to support carbon reduction targets in alignment with the sustainable development goals. It has also been highlighted that BC exhibits significant potential for mitigating GHG emissions from soil. However, long-term studies are required to establish optimal BC application practices in agroecosystem. Furthermore, comprehensive …

title: A generalized model predictive fault-tolerant control strategy for hybrid multilevel converter under arbitrary open-circuit failures
Deliberate metaphor as a rhetorical strategy for corporate identity construction
abstract: Abstract Using Deliberate Metaphor Theory and metaphor scenario analysis, this study compares the corporate identities constructed by Huawei before and after the imposition of US sanctions. The results show both convergence and divergence in deliberate metaphors and corporate identities. Although Huawei has long been portrayed as partnership-focused, innovation-driven, talent-valued and law-abiding, the specific identities it has constructed change markedly. In the pre-sanction period, Huawei is portrayed as a confident navigator, a military-style agile organization, a discerning talent gardener, and a vigilant sentinel against organizational decay. In the post-sanction period, it is framed as a resilient and steadfast traveler, a forward-looking strategic force mobilizer in the intelligence era, a storm survivor, and a down-to-earth ecosystem cultivator, reorienting its communication focus from internal optimization to addressing external challenges and accomplishing digital-era missions. This study indicates that corporate identity is a dynamic, context-sensitive cognitive construct which enables corporations to build trust across diverse contexts.

Impact of Electrolyte Feeding Strategy on Bubble Dynamics and Performance in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
abstract: Electrolyte feeding strategy critically influences hydrogen production performance of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs), yet the mechanistic influence of electrolyte feeding strategy on bubble transport inside the electrolyzer remains unclear. In this work, an optical bubble visualization platform was employed to compare bubble evolution under anode-feeding and cathode-feeding strategies, revealing totally different bubble evolution phenomena. The anode-feeding strategy promotes oxygen bubble departure at diameters below 200 μm, dominated by the internal bubble growth and departure mode, which presents low transport resistance. In contrast, the cathode-feeding strategy limits hydrogen bubble adhering onto the electrode at diameters above 1 mm, dominated by bubble wicking and gas-filled modes, leading to severe bubble transport issues. This transition in bubble evolution originates from differences in electrode structure, surface wettability, and Marangoni forces. The smoother oxygen bubble transport in the anode-fed electrolyzer further reduces mass transport resistance and enhances hydrogen production performance. These findings clarify how electrolyte feeding strategy affects bubble evolution and provide practical guidance for optimizing AEMWE operation to improve energy efficiency. Highlights 1. Bariatric Surgery as a Rescue Strategy After Semaglutide or Tirzepatide
abstract: Objective: To evaluate 2-year weight loss after bariatric surgery among adults with intolerable adverse effects or inadequate weight loss with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Summary Background Data: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are effective obesity medications, but intolerance and inadequate weight loss are common, creating uncertainty about next-step therapy. Methods: This retrospective cohort included adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m² undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) or sleeve gastrectomy (SG) at Cleveland Clinic hospitals from 2018 to 2024. Electronic health record and dispensing data classified preoperative semaglutide or tirzepatide exposure and response. The primary outcome was estimated 2-year total body weight loss (TBWL), stratified by procedure and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) status. Results: Among 4929 patients, 4661 had no prior exposure (comparator group), 61 discontinued semaglutide or tirzepatide because of intolerable adverse effects, and 207 had inadequate weight-loss response. Before surgery, estimated 2-year medication-associated weight change was a 1.4% gain in the intolerance group and 1.5% TBWL in the inadequate-response group. After surgery, 2-year TBWL in the intolerance group was 27.9% and 22.7% after RYGB and 20.1% and 21.6% after SG among patients without and with T2DM, respectively. Corresponding estimates in the inadequate-response group were 35.8%, 27.4%…

title: Religious Guidance Strategy through Majelis Taklim for Employees of the Koja Container Terminal, Jakarta
abstract: Workplace religious education must operate within organizational constraints that differ from community-based learning, particularly in continuous operations with rotating shifts. This study examined how Majelis Taklim functions as nonformal Islamic education for employees at Koja Container Terminal, Jakarta, and how its strategies, value internalization, participant experiences, and organizational conditions are interpreted. A constructivist qualitative case-study design was used. Six substantive semi-structured interviews were analyzed purposively: one manager, one Islamic spiritual-development organizer, two active participants, and two less-active participants. Data were coded in two cycles, compared across informant positions, and interpreted through social construction, knowing-feeling-acting, and workplace-spirituality lenses. The findings show an adaptive strategy characterized by needs mapping, contextual religious content, flexible scheduling, blended access, repeated materials, humanistic facilitators, and social activities. Internalization appeared through increased religious understanding, affective calmness, and reported everyday practice, but the pathway was not uniform. Less-active participants still valued the program while reporting barriers related to time, fatigue, location, transportation, digital limitations, and work priorities. Organizational support was…

title: An advanced control strategy for matrix converters in unbalanced grid voltage conditions
abstract: Purpose A novel control technique for the matrix converter (MC) under unbalanced grid voltage conditions is proposed in this paper. Compared to conventional direct AC–AC power conversion systems that require an intermediate DC link, matrix converters provide direct AC–AC conversion between sources with different phases and frequencies, and are compact and efficient. But maintaining balanced output voltage and current remains a significant challenge under grid voltage imbalance. This paper aims to propose a novel control technique for the matrix converter (MC) under unbalanced grid voltage (UGV) conditions. Design/methodology/approach To address this challenge, the proposed control algorithm uses a voltage imbalance compensation technique, a reference-frame transformation and space-vector modulation to achieve stable, balanced MC operation. Moreover, a new Matrix Converter Control-Deep Reinforcement framework is designed, comprising fundamental control features and processing steps for maximum adaptability and robustness under dynamic grid conditions. Findings The suggested method successfully maintains output voltage and current balance, even with a significant voltage imbalance in the grid, as demonstrated by extensive MATLAB simulations. Waveform regulation, output voltage control and speed response analysis are used to further validate the system’s performance. Originality/v…

title: Managing critical raw materials supply chains: aligning capabilities and strategic levers for effective strategy formation under uncertainty
abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms should design supply chain strategies to secure Critical Raw Materials (CRM), which are scarce, geographically concentrated, and exposed to geopolitical and institutional interference. These features generate structural uncertainty that amplifies normative and mimetic pressures on strategic decision-making, exposing firms to strategic isomorphic bias and leading organizations to replicate legitimized sourcing templates rather than formulate strategies calibrated to their specific dependence structure. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Resource Dependence Theory, the study links key strategic levers (Supplier Substitutability, Discretion over the Resource, and Importance of the Resource) to underlying supply chain capabilities (resilience, agility, flexibility, sustainability, efficiency). A rank-ordered logit choice experiment with supply chain managers elicits preferred capability configurations in CRM supply scenarios, allowing the inference of the associated strategic levers while reducing strategic isomorphic bias in self-reported strategies. Findings Results show that Supplier Substitutability emerges as the dominant strategic lever for CRM-intensive supply chains. Resilience and sustainability are identified as the core capabilities underpinning this lever, supporting rapid reconfiguration of the supply base and the maintenance o…

title: Risk-taking orientation and entrepreneurial strategy as drivers of business performance: evidence from private childcare centres in Indonesia
abstract: Purpose Entrepreneurial orientation (EO) is a recognised driver of firm performance, yet findings remain inconsistent and the mechanisms linking entrepreneurial behaviour to performance are underexplored in socially sensitive service sectors. This study examines whether risk-taking orientation affects business performance in private childcare centres in Indonesia via entrepreneurial strategy as a mediator. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey of 338 owners and managers of registered private childcare centres was conducted via cluster sampling from a population of 2,775 centres. 315 valid responses (93.2%) were analysed using partial least squares–structural equation Modelling with 5,000-resample bootstrapping. Findings Risk-taking orientation is positively associated with business performance, although this direct effect is comparatively modest. Entrepreneurial strategy shows a substantially stronger association with performance and partially mediates the risk-taking–performance relationship, suggesting that formalised strategic action represents a crucial structural path through which risk-taking orientation is associated with performance gains. Together, the two constructs account for a large share of the variance in business performance, and the measurement model demonstrates adequate discriminant validity and predictive relevance. Improving Accuracy and Interpretability of Educational App Recommendations via Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Abstract— As the usage of mobile apps in digital education is growing, it has become more critical to provide accurate and personalised recommendation systems that can enhance user engagement and learning effectiveness. The difficulty of collaborative filtering techniques is caused by the sparseness, dynamism and time dependence of crowdsourcing educational information. As a means of solving these problems, a mobile app recommendation framework is created with the help of a crowdsourced educational feedback dataset from Kaggle. It was methodologically preprocessed using timestamp creation, discard of irrelevant attributes, label encoding, and feature engineering (pivoting) and 80/20 train-test split. A number of machine and deep learning models are used including SVD, SVD++, NMF, SlopeOne, variations of KNN, CoClustering, BaselineOnly, NormalPredictor, GRU, LSTM, Stacked Autoencoder, Gated Autoencoder and hybrid LSTM-GRU. Explainable variance, MAE and RMSE are used to assess the model performance. The experimental results show that the hybrid LSTM-GRU consistently gives the minimum mean RMSE value of 0.267332 and mean MAE value of 0.118370 with the largest individual performance at k = 16 (RMSE = 0.005066, MAE = 0.003821). LIME and SHAP enhance the explainability, and user interface with Flask enables practical applicability. This technique increases the accuracy, robustness an…

title: Perceived Student Workload in English-Medium Instruction: Evidence from a Large-Scale Study in Business Education
abstract: This study examines differences in perceived academic workload between students enrolled in English-Medium Instruction (EMI) and non-EMI programs, contributing to the broader discussion on student experience in higher education. Drawing on a large sample of 11,427 course evaluations from a Business Administration degree at a Spanish university (2016–2019), we compare self-reported workload scores across groups. Results indicate that EMI students report slightly higher workloads, particularly in the first year and in subject areas such as Economics and Quantitative Methods. However, these differences diminish in subsequent years, and effect sizes are generally small or negligible. The findings suggest that while EMI students initially invest more effort, likely due to adapting to instruction in a non-native language, this additional workload is temporary. These results reinforce the viability of EMI programs and highlight the value of targeted first-year support to optimize the student learning experience.

title: Machine learning driven analysis and development of LD sludge-polypropylene composites for industrial tribo-components
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effect of Linz–Donawitz (LD) sludge reinforcement on the microhardness and abrasive wear behavior of polypropylene (PP) composites, and to optimize and predict the specific wear rate (SWR) using Taguchi design and an artificial neural network (ANN) model for improved performance and sustainable utilization of industrial waste. Design/methodology/approach PP composites reinforced with 0–20 Wt.% LD sludge were fabricated by compression molding. Microhardness was measured using a micro-indentation test. Three-body abrasive wear tests were conducted according to ASTM standards and analyzed using Taguchi L25 design. An ANN model was developed to predict the SWR. Findings The incorporation of LD sludge significantly enhanced the microhardness and abrasive wear resistance of PP composites. Microhardness increased from 0.059 GPa for neat PP to 0.639 GPa at 20 Wt.% filler content. SWR decreased considerably with increasing LD sludge, indicating improved abrasion resistance. Taguchi analysis identified sliding velocity and filler content as the most influential parameters affecting wear behavior. The ANN model accurately predicted SWR with errors below 9%, confirming its effectiveness for reliable wear performance prediction. Originality/value This study demonstrates the effective utilization of industrial LD sludge as a reinforcement in PP comp…

title: TyG-CVAI for identifying hyperuricemia: geographical external validation, model updating, and explainable machine learning
abstract: Background TyG-CVAI can be calculated from routine metabolic and anthropometric measurements, but evidence for same-visit identification of prevalent hyperuricemia across regions, its incremental value beyond conventional variables, and its advantage over the constituent variables themselves remains limited. Objective To assess the geographical transportability of the triglyceride-glucose Chinese visceral adiposity index (TyG-CVAI) for identifying prevalent hyperuricemia and to determine whether model updating or more complex machine-learning methods materially improve externally validated performance. Methods We analyzed prospectively collected, single-visit health-examination and questionnaire data from 2,119 adults and performed a cross-sectional analysis. The Shandong center was used for model development (n=1,288) and the Jiangsu center for geographical external validation (n=831). Associations were estimated with multivariable logistic regression and robust Poisson regression, with restricted cubic splines for dose-response assessment. Single-index discrimination, transferred thresholds, calibration, decision-curve analysis, five prespecified logistic model formulations, recalibration, reverse validation, and dataset shift were evaluated. Machine-learning models were tuned by nested resampling in Shandong and evaluated once in Jiangsu; serum urate and all outcome-derived …

title: Visualizing use of generative artificial intelligence in higher education
abstract: Purpose Higher education students are engaged with academic learning and research using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) applications. A major shift in pedagogical approach surfaces many challenges to academic integrity that urging to redefining assessment model and ethical literacy. This study aims to investigate impact of the GenAI apps among the students using survey of technical and non-technical disciplines. Survey is mainly focused on: use of GenAI apps, variations in observed effectiveness and student’s usage pattern, level of adoption and acceptance of GenAI apps. Reviews of existing literature on the implications of GenAI and emerging need for systemic changes are discussed with reference to result. Design/methodology/approach Survey was developed to assess the integration of GenAI apps in the higher education. It was conducted with undergraduate and postgraduate students so as to find the adoption and acceptance rate of GenAI apps among the students; it has been partitioned into two categories: non-technical disciplines and technical disciplines. Students from the social science and pure sciences are in the non-technical disciplines, while students from computer science and engineering students are in the technical discipline. The questionnaire included a mix of multiple-choice questions, scale items and open-ended responses. Findings This research is classi…

title: The no mesh breast reconstruction evaluation (No-BRA) study: protocol for a national prospective audit and shared learning study of pre-pectoral implant-based breast reconstruction with no mesh
abstract: Introduction: Implant-based breast reconstruction (IBBR) is the most common reconstructive modality for women undergoing mastectomy in the United Kingdom (UK). Practice has evolved from subpectoral to pre-pectoral implant placement, typically utilizing a mesh for implant support. A newer iteration of this technique, which omits the use of mesh entirely, is gaining popularity but lacks a robust evidence base regarding its safety, effectiveness, and optimal application. This study is positioned within phases 2a/2b of the Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment, Long-term study (IDEAL) framework to formally evaluate this surgical innovation. The No-BRA study aims to conduct a national audit to explore the safety and effectiveness of immediate pre-pectoral IBBR without mesh to inform the delivery of best care. Methods and analysis: This is a national, multicenter, prospective audit aiming to recruit 350 patients from 15 to 20 UK centers. The study employs a dual-component design. The first component is a quantitative audit of clinical and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) for women undergoing immediate pre-pectoral IBBR with no mesh. The primary outcome is implant loss at 3 months post-surgery. Secondary outcomes include other key complications (e.g., infection, unplanned re-operation, and readmission) and PROMs (preoperatively, at 1.5 and 5 years), which will be benchma…

title: Large Language Model Driven Reinforcement Learning based Intelligent Control Method for Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Controllers which can interpret and react to high-dimensional process state and perturbations without loss of stability are needed for industrial cyber-physical systems. In this paper, we propose a large language model driven reinforcement learning approach based on semantic state augmentation using the Llama-3-8B model and a Proximal Policy Optimization controller. Process numerical values are converted to structured operation descriptions and concatenated with normalized feature vectors from sensors to provide the policy with both dynamics of the process and relationships between its components. We create an environment for experiments using Siemens Process Simulate software and Python 3.11 with Tennessee Eastman Process data. As a result, we demonstrate that the proposed controller achieves the normalized control RMSE of 0.158 ± 0.014 versus 0.223 ± 0.018 for classical PPO and a settling time of 8.47 ± 0.71 s versus 11.36 ± 0.94 s. Under combined disturbances, the proposed controller achieves a recovery time of 12.8 ± 1.1 s and a cumulative reward of 846.7 ± 25.8, demonstrating improved control accuracy and disturbance adaptability while maintaining computational feasibility.

title: Application of a problem-based learning teaching method based on mini-CEX and DOPS assessments in the teaching of clinical molecular biology testing in higher vocational colleges
abstract: Objective To develop a problem-based learning (PBL) teaching method incorporating Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX) and Direct Observation of Procedural Skills (DOPS) assessments, and to investigate its application effect in the teaching of Clinical Molecular Biology Testing in higher vocational colleges. Methods This study adopted a quasi-experimental design involving two intact classes of students majoring in Medical Laboratory Technology at a higher vocational college. The two classes were assigned to the control group (traditional teaching method) and the experimental group (PBL combined with Mini-CEX/DOPS assessments), respectively. The experimental group adopted a teaching approach driven by authentic clinical cases, with Mini-CEX assessments incorporated into each round of PBL teaching to evaluate clinical reasoning ability and DOPS assessments to evaluate laboratory procedural skills, followed by immediate structured feedback. A total of five rounds were conducted. The control group received only traditional teaching. At the end of the course, the teaching outcomes of the two groups were compared using a theoretical knowledge examination, an independent Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), and a satisfaction questionnaire. Results After teaching, the total OSCE scores, clinical case analysis scores, core procedural skills assessment scores, and l…

title: Implementing lesson study as teacher professional development in English schools: exploring the role of the leader through an implementation science lens
abstract: Purpose Lesson study (LS) is a Japanese teacher professional development (PD) approach which has been adopted globally to emulate Japan's high student achievement. In Japan, three leadership roles ensure the high-quality implementation of LS: a school Research Steering Committee, in-school facilitators and external experts. Teachers can develop leadership expertise through their participation in LS. This study uses implementation science as a framework to investigate leadership functions that enabled and hindered LS implementation in English schools that voluntarily adopted LS, frequently without funding, policy guidance or systemic opportunities for LS leadership development. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a case study methodology, exploring data from six purposefully recruited schools that implemented and used LS for at least two years, four of which subsequently abandoned it. We analysed interview data from LS leaders and participants, alongside documents detailing LS policy and practice, to assess the extent to which leaders fulfilled the three Japanese leadership roles and to reveal the characteristics and behaviours of implementation leaders. Findings What distinguishes sustained from abandoned cases is the propensity of LS leaders to “champion” LS. These knowledgeable yet humble leaders led implementation with passion, solved problems, allocated funding and …

title: PENINGKATAN KETERAMPILAN MENULIS PUISI MELALUI MEDIA POP UP BOOK DIGITAL BERBASIS ASSEMBLR EDU
abstract: The low level of poetry writing skills among elementary school students remains a challenge in Indonesian language learning, particularly in generating ideas, selecting appropriate diction, developing imagery, and composing meaningful poems. This study aimed to improve students' poetry writing skills and describe teacher and student activities through the implementation of a digital pop-up book based on Assemblr Edu. This study employed Classroom Action Research (CAR), conducted in two cycles consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The participants were 35 fifth-grade students of SDN 2 Tambakrigadung. Data were collected through observation, performance tests, and documentation, then analyzed using quantitative descriptive techniques. The results showed that teacher activity increased from 55% in Cycle I to 88% in Cycle II, while student activity increased from 53% to 88%. The average poetry writing score also improved from 67 to 79, with learning mastery increasing from 40% to 83%. These improvements indicate that three-dimensional visualizations provided through the learning media helped students generate inspiration, develop imagination, and select appropriate diction. Therefore, implementing a digital pop-up book based on Assemblr Edu can serve as an alternative approach to improving elementary school students' poetry writing skills. ABSTRAK Rendahnya k…

title: Reimagining adolescent education with ephegogy: generative AI and active learning in practice
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces ephegogy, a theory addressing the gap between traditional educational models and adolescents' developmental needs in artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented societies. Blending constructivism, connectivism and generativism, it explores how integrating generative AI (GenAI) and active learning can scaffold motivation, autonomy, and relevance for adolescent learners. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods case study conducted in a single secondary-school geography course during 2024–2025. Quantitative data came from matched pre- and post-intervention surveys measuring motivation and self-efficacy (N = 17; N = 11 for the self-efficacy composite) and locus of control (N = 12), using instruments adapted for an under-14, predominantly English-as-an-additional-language cohort. A separate matched engagement survey (N = 24) and an end-of-course co-creation survey (N = 33) provided further data. Qualitative data comprised 74 individual student reflections analysed thematically using the cultural-historical activity theory (CHAT) framework, alongside open-text survey responses from 74 students. The study was designed using three frameworks (self-determination theory, ephegogy and CHAT). Findings Findings are associational and exploratory, specific to this pilot.
