Psychosocial Impact of the Vehicle-Ramming Attack on the Magdeburg Christmas Market in Germany: Protocol for the MD-Care Longitudinal Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background On December 20, 2024, a vehicle-ramming attack occurred at the Magdeburg Christmas market, resulting in 6 fatalities and more than 300 injuries. Mass violence incidents have the potential to cause long-lasting psychosocial consequences for directly and indirectly affected individuals. However, the outcomes can vary depending on relevant risk and protective factors. To improve the psychosocial aftercare of mass violence incidents in Germany, more research is essential. Objective The MD-Care study strives to examine the psychosocial impact of the vehicle-ramming attack on the Magdeburg Christmas market by investigating the levels, longitudinal trajectories, and associated factors and predictors regarding (1) psychosocial, mental health, and somatic burdens; (2) individual resources and protective factors; and (3) mental health service use and support needs. Methods The MD-Care study is a prospective longitudinal epidemiological study with 3 measurement time points. Data were collected pseudonymously via the online platform LimeSurvey. The baseline survey (t1; 3-month follow-up to the incident) was completed from March to April 2025. The 6-month follow-up (t2) was completed from June to July 2025. Finally, the 15-month follow-up survey (t3) was filled out by participants from March to April 2026. The surveys comprise standardized as well as self-developed ad ho…

title: Climate Risk and Insurance Market Development in Nigeria
abstract: This study examines the relationship between climate risk and insurance market development in Nigeria, focusing on how climate-related losses, government disaster risk management (DRM) spending, and reinsurance capacity influence insurance penetration and density. The research adopts a quantitative approach using secondary data spanning 2000 to 2024, sourced from the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM), the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), and the World Bank Climate Data. Econometric techniques, including descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root test, Johansen cointegration, the Error Correction Model (ECM), and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, were employed to analyse the data. The results reveal that climate-related losses have a negative and statistically significant impact on insurance market development, indicating that increasing climate events such as floods and droughts reduce insurers’ capacity to underwrite new risks. In contrast, government DRM spending and reinsurance capacity exert positive and significant effects, suggesting that proactive fiscal intervention and strong financial resilience enhance the sector’s growth and stability. GDP growth was found to positively influence insurance development, while inflation showed a weak negative effect. The …

title: Robust Design of Wide-Area Damping Controllers Against Permanent Communication Failures Using LQR-Based Optimization
abstract: Low-frequency oscillation modes (LFOMs) with insufficient damping can compromise power system stability following disturbances. The increasing interconnection of large-scale power systems has resulted in a greater number of poorly damped low-frequency oscillation modes, thereby motivating the development of advanced damping control techniques, such as Wide-Area Damping Controllers (WADCs). Since WADCs rely on remote measurements, communication failures and cyberattacks can impair their operation and adversely affect system stability. This study proposed an optimization framework based on Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) theory for the robust design of WADCs, aiming to enhance system resilience against permanent communication failures. The WADC parameters were considered as optimization variables, and the objective function was formulated to maximize the damping ratios of the closed-loop system under both normal WADC operation and permanent communication failure conditions. Unlike conventional LQR-based approaches, the proposed methodology also considered the WADC poles as optimization variables, thereby providing additional degrees of freedom for controller design. Three metaheuristic optimization algorithms, Glider Snake Optimizer, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Sine Cosine Algorithm, were incorporated into the proposed framework, and their performance was comparatively eval…

title: Extracellular amylolytic activity in marine Croceibacter sp. 23-6: Cu 2+ response and optimized wheat starch hydrolysis
abstract: Background Marine bacteria are important sources of extracellular hydrolytic enzymes, but the amylolytic activity of many non-model marine bacterial lineages remains insufficiently characterized at the phenotype level. This study evaluated extracellular amylolytic activity in the marine isolate Croceibacter sp. 23-6 and examined its metal-ion response and wheat starch hydrolysis performance under defined laboratory conditions. Methods Strain 23-6 was isolated from mesopelagic seawater of the western Pacific Ocean and identified at the genus level using 16S rRNA gene sequence analysis. Extracellular amylolytic activity was first screened on starch agar. A partially purified extracellular amylolytic protein preparation was then used to determine the effects of temperature, pH, thermal and pH stability, metal ions, apparent kinetic parameters and hydrolysis of different starch substrates. Wheat starch hydrolysis was further evaluated using single-factor experiments and response surface methodology based on a Box–Behnken design. Results Strain 23-6 produced a clear starch-hydrolysis halo and was conservatively assigned to the genus Croceibacter . The partially purified extracellular protein fraction showed maximum amylolytic activity at 50 °C and pH 7.0 and retained comparatively higher activity under near-neutral conditions. Among the tested metal ions, Cu 2+ increased the measure…

title: Defining and understanding treatment non-completion and non-response in family based treatment, for anorexia nervosa or atypical anorexia nervosa in children and adolescents: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Background Family-Based Treatment (FBT) is a first-line treatment for anorexia nervosa in childhood and adolescence, however, remission rates following treatment remain modest. This systematic review aimed to examine definitions of, and identify factors that may influence, non-completion or non-response to FBT in children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa or atypical anorexia nervosa (AN/AAN). Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Three databases (APA PsycINFO, Embase, and Web of Knowledge) were searched from 2005 to 4th August 2025, supplemented by citation searching. Inclusion criteria were studies in any language examining FBT for AN/AAN, in participants aged 18 years or under, in outpatient settings. Quality assessment was completed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. The review was prospectively registered (PROSPERO CRD420251114023). Results Searches identified 1794 articles, 988 following removal of duplicates. Fifty-five papers examined treatment non-completion and/or non-response (25 primary studies; 30 secondary analytic studies; N = 2,820). Definitions of treatment non-completion and non-response varied significantly. Non-completion rates ranged from 2% to 55% but in more than half of papers, this group was not characterised further. Non-response rates ranged from 14% to 71%. Factors associated w…

title: Large Language Models for Forecasting of Electricity Price Spikes
abstract: Can market notices read by a large language model (LLM) improve short-horizon electricity price spike forecasts? We study five regions of Australia's National Electricity Market. A local LLM extracted features once per notice, only notices visible at the forecast origin were used, and a gradient-boosting model produced onset probabilities. In an out-of-sample development back-test (July 2022 to July 2024), notice features did not lower the 60-minute Brier score of a numeric model including the market operator's next-hour forecasts. At 24 hours they did, but rule-based features did so almost equally and attribution to notice content was not established. A locally frozen protocol, not publicly deposited, governed a retrospective single-use holdout from 15 August to 17 October 2026. At 60 minutes, the hypothesis that LLM features lower the numeric model's Brier score was not established (H1; relative Brier skill -0.09%), so the planned comparison with rule-based features was not tested (H2). At 24 hours, the hypothesis that LLM features lower the score against a text-free control was not established (H3; +0.37%, 95% CI [-9.74, 1.39], inconclusive). By the frozen wording rule the non-significant 24-hour improvement comes mainly from recalibration and cannot be attributed to notice content, although post hoc the decomposition could not separate recalibration from resolution. The 24-…

title: A Swin Transformer for Multiparameter Solar Wind Forecasting from MHD Simulations
abstract: Abstract Accurate forecasting of solar wind parameters is crucial for space weather forecasting and the protection of infrastructure. Existing physics-based magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) models are computationally expensive and often rely on assumptions. Most deep learning methods focus only on single-parameter predictions at spatial locations, making it difficult to characterize the multiparameter coupled dynamics that govern space weather effects. The model proposed in this study is based on the Transformer and adopts a Swin Transformer encoder–decoder architecture. It is trained on MHD simulation data and can predict eight solar wind parameters (number density, three velocity components, temperature, and three magnetic field components) on a two-dimensional polar coordinate grid of the solar equatorial plane. In order to handle the nonuniform spatial distribution of the grid in the polar coordinate system, this study introduces a position-dependent relative bias to encode the variation of physical spacing with heliocentric distance. The model was trained on MHD simulation data covering 631 Carrington rotations. In single-step (24 hr) predictions on the test set, the weighted correlation coefficients (wCC) exceed 0.98 for all parameters. In the autoregressive rolling prediction mode, the model maintains high accuracy for approximately 72 hr. When compared with OMNI observations c…

title: Solar-Irradiance Forecasting in Arid Climates: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Models and Probabilistic-Uncertainty Quantification Using Four Years of Riyadh Data
abstract: Precise short-horizon solar-irradiance forecasting is essential for grid-tied inverter control and battery scheduling in arid climates, yet model performance in regions with frequent dust remains under-characterized. This study benchmarks six machine-learning models—Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)—for 1-, 3-, and 6-h-ahead Global Horizontal Irradiance forecasting using 34,871 hourly records from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (2013–2016). All models were tuned with temporal cross-validation and evaluated on an independent 2016 test set. Two feature tracks were evaluated: a full twenty-five-feature set and a three-feature set (hour_sin, hour_cos, GHI_lag_1) selected by recursive feature elimination with 100% bootstrap stability. A four-feature SVR adding doy_cos is the empirical optimum at 1- and 3-h horizons, achieving an RMSE of 65.43 and 77.16 W/m2 (R2 0.956 and 0.948, skill scores 61.5% and 82.8%). At 6 h, Gradient Boosting with the full 25-feature set is best (RMSE 78.99 W/m2). The three-feature LSTM achieves 98.25, 148.84, and 233.47 W/m2. Split-conformal prediction achieves nominal 90% coverage (89.56%, 90.30%, 89.65%) with CRPS of 25.94, 31.36, and 32.42 W/m2, and intervals 7–21% narrower than quantile regression. A matched-condition dust analysis shows no statistically significant dif…

title: A Comparative Analysis of Volatility Predictions via EGARCH, Transformer and Hybrid EGARCH-Transformer Models: Changes in Forecasting Ability after Introducing Sentiment Factors
abstract: The application of cryptocurrency asset volatility forecasting is relevant for real‑world risk‑management procedures and derivatives pricing in the digital‑asset market. This paper assesses out-of-sample forecast performance for three model families: standalone EGARCH, vanilla Transformer, and an EGARCH‑Transformer combined hybrid architecture for forecasting Bitcoin volatility. Another goal is to measure whether there is any actual marginal forecasting benefit from investor sentiment obtained from the Reddit posts. We use information from Reddit with the subreddit r/Bitcoin from 25th March 2021 to 30th December 2024. We collaborate with the open-source ProsusAI/finbert language model that has been trained for financial text tasks to construct a daily sentiment score based on the number of upvotes given to the post‑comment. In the hybrid model we constructed, the one-step-ahead conditional-variance values produced by EGARCH are used as other features as input to the Transformer network. The results from controlled feature-ablation tests show that, in general, using structured volatility inputs (volatility realized from volatility inputs) and EGARCH conditional volatility outputs yield better forecasts. Social media sentiment data of investors, by comparison, has mixed results. Under specific combinations of features, sentiment boosts the accuracy of predictions, but in other ex…

title: Weekly sales forecasting using time series decomposition with irregular seasonality: A case study of Sony TV sales in the United States
abstract: In the practice of sales forecasting, alongside high accuracy, simplicity and interpretability are desirable qualities in a predictive model. Here, we use time series decomposition to construct a simple and interpretable forecasting method for weekly sales, taking as a case study the total weekly sales of Sony TV units in the United States. The main challenge is to properly address irregular seasonality arising from the way a year is divided into weeks and from floating holidays and events. As a solution, we propose the concept of ‘analogous weeks’, a general framework for grouping weeks that are similar according to some criteria, which encodes seasonality and already accounts for calendar effects. By incorporating this notion into the time series decomposition and forecasting, we achieved yearly average percentage errors of less than 10% for the 1-week-ahead forecast and less than 15% for forecast horizons of up to 26 weeks, accuracy levels comparable to or better than those of other established seasonal models, namely Prophet and SARIMAX, particularly at longer forecast horizons.
authors: Arthur Matsuo Yamashita Rios de Sousa

title: Richard Price (1723–1791), Scotland and the Scottish Enlightenment
abstract: The dissenting minister, philosopher, and mathematician Richard Price (1723-1791) is usually located within an Atlantic-republican or a Welsh context context. Those analytical frameworks have obscured connections within Scotland. A Welshman who lived in Newington Green, near London, and who styled himself an “Englishman”, Price is an unlikely candidate for a study of Scottish philosophy. Criticizing historiographical pigeonholing, and building on research on Price’s engagement with a David Hume essay, and Adam Ferguson's Remarks on Dr. Price's Observations on the nature of civil liberty (1776), this paper seeks to map out Price's contacts with Scots. It identifies points of convergence and common concerns with Ferguson, discusses contexts of discussion in Price’s immediate circles of sociability and through private correspondence. Though this is article discusses Price’s reception in Scotland, it is primarily concerned with Price’s view of Scotland and contacts with Scots.

title: The Altruism Paradox: How Retailer Concern for Consumer Welfare Shapes Supplier Encroachment and Price Matching
abstract: E-commerce enables suppliers to bypass traditional retailers and sell directly to consumers, but such encroachment intensifies channel competition. Although price matching commitments can mitigate this conflict, their strategic role has primarily been studied under the assumption of profit-maximizing retailers. We develop a game-theoretic model to examine how a retailer’s valuation of consumer surplus alongside accounting profit affects a supplier’s pricing choice and direct-channel sales. The supplier chooses whether to adopt an exact commitment to match the retailer’s price. We show that the supplier adopts price matching only when the retailer’s weight on consumer surplus is sufficiently large and the direct-selling cost falls within an intermediate range. Under supplier-preferred selection among retail-only pricing equilibria and without a fixed entry cost, the supplier opens the direct channel throughout the maintained cost range. Under this selection, the price matching option changes the pricing arrangement rather than the entry decision. Greater retailer altruism improves consumer surplus and social welfare within each conditional outcome yet can lower either measure in equilibrium by inducing the supplier to adopt matched pricing or stop direct sales while retaining unmatched pricing. This interaction can give rise to an altruism paradox. Numerical extensions show that…

title: Profitability and Share Price of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
abstract: Volatility of share prices (SPR) of listed Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Nigeria is a major concern to investors because they often suffer huge losses as against their expectations. Share prices volatility can result to low returns and increase uncertainty of future returns to investors. Thus, investors need information disclosed by management in the annual reports of DMBs to make investment decisions, therefore, this study investigated the impact of profitability on SPR of listed DMBs in Nigeria. The study utilised an ex post facto research design. The population of the study consists of all listed DMBs on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX). Purposive sampling technique was used to select 10 listed DMBs having the required data for the study from 2015 to 2024. The results of the Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS) analysis revealed that the influence of return on assets (ROA) on SPR was positive and significant, while return on equity (ROE) has an insignificant positive influence on SPR. The study concluded that Profitability, represented by ROE and ROA, altogether significantly affects the SPR of listed DMBs in Nigeria. The study recommended that management of DMBs in Nigeria should boister ROA by managing bank assets efficiently in other to generate more profits from assets which will reinforce investor trust and driving up share demand thereby resulting in share price …

title: Systemically delivered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron -derived bacterial extracellular vesicles inhibit primary and metastatic melanoma growth
abstract: ABSTRACT The gut microbiome can contribute to anti-tumor immunity and cancer therapy responses, but translating live microbe-based interventions remains challenging due to safety, controllability, and delivery constraints. Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are an attractive cell-free alternative, as they package bacterial cargo into a nanoscale format capable of host-cell engagement, immunological activation, and systemic distribution. Here, we investigated the anti-tumor potential of BEVs derived from the human gut commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (Bt). We show that the delivery route is a major determinant of efficacy. Intravenous, but not intraperitoneal, administration produced robust anti-tumor activity in a B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Intravenously delivered Bt BEVs suppressed primary tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner and reduced metastatic outgrowth in the lung. Bt BEVs did not reduce B16F10 metabolic viability during a 24-h in vitro exposure, but they activated NF-κB and Toll-like receptor signaling in human reporter systems, and NanoLuc-associated signal from labeled BEV preparations was detected in excised tumor tissue following systemic administration. Although the host pathways responsible for tumor control remain to be defined, these findings identify naturally produced commensal-derived Bt BEVs as a candidate cell-free microbial therapeutic moda…

title: From Predict-Then-Optimize to End-to-End: A Systematic Review of AI Architectures in Demand Forecasting–Inventory Management Integration
abstract: Demand forecasting and inventory management have evolved as parallel bodies of literature, despite their operational interdependence, and the resulting disconnect between prediction and decision has been diagnosed as a standing gap in operational research. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) protocol, this review systematically codes 46 studies published between 2010 and 2023 in journals listed by the Australian Business Deans Council, operationalizing an established prediction–inventory integration hierarchy to evaluate how modern artificial intelligence architectures couple prediction with decision-making. We find that predict-then-optimize (PtO) and end-to-end or joint learning (E2E) architectures co-evolve rather than succeed one another. Crucially, integration level is orthogonal to model class: seven of the seventeen E2E studies use no neural network, so decision-focused coupling does not inherently require the opacity of deep learning. Instead, architecture performance is highly contingent on a domain’s data regime and cost structure rather than algorithmic sophistication alone. We provide a contingency framework equipping academic researchers, analytics practitioners, and supply chain managers with actionable architecture-selection guidance, identifying hybrid PtO–E2E designs, which remain absent within this cor…

title: Budget Constraints, Price Shocks and Urban Rural Consumption Allocation: Cobb-Douglas Utility Framing for Food, Tobacco, Alcohol and Apparel
abstract: There is an obvious income gap between urban and rural residents in China; changes in income levels and commodity prices will jointly affect the distribution of household consumption budget and consumption structure. This paper takes food, tobacco, alcohol, and clothing as the research objects, constructs a Cobb-Douglas two-commodity consumption model based on utility maximization, and uses the statistical data of income and consumption expenditure of urban and rural residents from 2021 to 2025 to calibrate the preference parameters of the model, and sets up three scenarios of benchmark, income increase, and food price rise for analysis. The results show that both urban rural income and target category consumption generally grow. Rural residents witness faster consumption growth yet remain at lower absolute consumption levels. Rural households persistently allocate a larger budget share to food tobacco alcohol, with these two basic goods accounting for a higher proportion of their disposable income. Simulation suggests that income growth expands the consumption budget proportionally and lifts real consumption of both goods without changing budget shares. Given a fixed total budget, rising food tobacco alcohol prices reduce real consumption while leaving clothing consumption unaffected. This paper provides modeling insights for interpreting urban rural consumption disparities.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: PGCLN: A physics-guided approach for personalized optimal sitting posture prediction using pressure distribution
abstract: To bridge the gap between physiological data and engineering implementation, this study addressed the limitation of indirect mapping of sitting posture by establishing a direct predictive link between physiological information from pressure distribution and optimal sitting posture. A novel predicting framework named Physics-Guided and Contrastive Learning Network (PGCLN) was proposed to predict sitting posture using 12 pressure distribution features and seven anthropometric data, and designed to overcome small-sample and high-dimensional regression problems. Crucially, Contact Pressure Distribution Index (CPDI) was firstly introduced as a new biomechanical constraint to ensure the model’s physical consistency. By integrating CPDI-based physical prior constraint with contrastive learning, the PGCLN can accurately predict the optimal sitting posture for diverse occupants with a R 2 of 0.9711 and RMSE of 0.7649, significantly outperforming baseline models. Furthermore, SHAP analysis reveals that Waist Average Pressure and Shoulder and Back Contact Area are the primary determinants for PGCLN. Overall, this work offers a robust solution for an on-vehicle deployment of real-time, personalized seat adaptive adjustment, providing both a theoretical foundation and a practical pathway for intelligent seating systems in human factors engineering.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part D: Journal of Automobile Engineering

Prediction of Medical Students’ Performance in Summative Assessment Using Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Abstract Background: Early identification of medical students at risk of poor academic performance is essential for timely academic intervention and student support. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models to predict the performance of second-year MBBS students in summative assessments. Methods: This observational analytical study was conducted at All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Kalyani, using academic data from five consecutive MBBS batches (2019–2023). Variables included demographic information, attendance records, internal assessment scores, previous academic performance, and final summative examination results in microbiology, pathology, and pharmacology. Multiple machine learning algorithms including logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbors, Naïve Bayes, XGBoost, and LightGBM were implemented using R statistical software. The models were trained using data from four batches and validated using the fifth batch. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: Machine learning models demonstrated strong predictive performance across all three subjects. Among the algorithms evaluated, the SVM model showed the highest sensitivity (89%) in …

Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Steel–Recycled Aggregate Concrete Bond Stress: A Comparative Study of Artificial Neural Networks and Empirical Models
abstract: This study investigates the bond behavior between steel reinforcement and recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) using two predictive approaches: empirical formulations and artificial neural networks (ANN). A comprehensive dataset of pull-out experimental test compiled from previous research was utilized to develop four empirical equations, each tailored to a specific range of RAC compressive strength. The equations incorporate key parameters including: concrete compressive strength, the ratio of concrete cover to steel bar diameter, the ratio of steel bar diameter to bond length, the replacement ratio of coarse recycled aggregates, the water-to-cement ratio, and the product of steel bar area and yield strength. The ANN model was structured with an input layer reflecting the same parameters used in the empirical equations, a hidden layer containing 20 neurons, and an output layer representing bond stress. Training was conducted using the collected dataset, while validation was performed against experimental results from 30 experimental pull-out specimens performed in the present study. While the empirical models yielded reasonable predictions, the ANN demonstrated superior accuracy and robustness in replicating experimental bond stress values. These findings affirm the potential of ANN as a reliable tool for predicting steel-RAC bond behavior.
venue: Journal of Sustainable Architecture and Civil Engineering

title: Battery State of Health Early Prediction via a Generative Adversarial Network and a Hybrid Deep Learning Model
abstract: Early prediction of the State of Health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is crucial for battery manufacturing and management. However, battery aging is complex and nonlinear, and scarce early data challenges long-term prediction. To address this, a data-driven SOH prediction method based on transfer learning is proposed. As SOH degradation relates to various factors, an improved TimeGAN is first employed for data augmentation and style transfer to expand the training dataset. Additionally, a hybrid architecture, ATTCN-Mamba, integrating attention mechanisms, temporal convolutional networks, and state-space models, is constructed to improve prediction accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms traditional models in key metrics. Furthermore, with the TimeGAN-based transfer learning strategy, the model significantly enhances prediction accuracy and robustness even with substantially reduced target-domain data, with RMSE, MSE, and MAPE lower than those of the baselines without transfer learning. The method also demonstrates broad prospects for high-precision, full-life-cycle battery health management under edge-cloud architectures and cloud-based battery management systems.

title: Cross-Geometry Flow-Field Prediction in Irregular Wellbores Using Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: Irregular borehole enlargement alters annular flow structures and can create low-velocity regions that impair hole cleaning. However, conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) requires repeated geometric reconstruction and numerical simulations for each wellbore configuration, while existing physics-informed models have limited capability for cross-geometry extrapolation. This study develops transfer-learning-based parameterized physics-informed neural networks (TLP-PINNs) for the rapid three-dimensional prediction of Herschel–Bulkley drilling-fluid flow in locally enlarged irregular wellbores. A Gaussian enlargement ratio is introduced as an explicit geometric input, while mass and momentum conservation equations, boundary conditions, adaptive loss weighting, extrapolation-distance-driven physics-point allocation, and partial-layer transfer learning are integrated into a unified framework. The source model generally maintains good in-range interpolation accuracy for the velocity field within the 10–50% enlargement range, although the pressure error shows greater case-to-case variability for unseen intermediate geometries. For the unseen 80% enlargement case, transfer learning reduces the relative RMSEs of axial velocity, velocity magnitude, and pressure from 14.0%, 13.5%, and 3.5% to 9.42%, 9.50%, and 1.34%, respectively, with corresponding Rp2 of 0.9668, 0.9663, and 0.9…

title: LSTM and DeepONet Surrogate Models for Particle Trajectory and Bed Segregation Prediction in Magnetically Fluidized Beds
abstract: Abstract Particle-resolved prediction in magnetically fluidized beds (MFBs) is needed to link local particle motion with bed-scale segregation, yet repeated CFD-DEM simulations remain computationally expensive. This study develops and benchmarks two complementary deep-learning surrogates for Lagrangian trajectory prediction in a magnetic-last MFB: a particle-wise long short-term memory (LSTM) network and a deep operator network (DeepONet). Both models are trained on a common CFD-DEM data set of 9240 binary particles under a magnetic-field gradient increasing from 0 to 0.30 T m–1. The source code developed in this study is openly available to facilitate reproducibility and future research. In particle-wise forecasting, both architectures achieve R2 > 0.99 and recover the segregation-index evolution from predicted positions; DeepONet yields narrower ensemble error bounds, whereas LSTM incurs lower training cost. A shared DeepONet further generalizes across particle identities (R2 = 0.9991, 0.9984, and 0.9975 in X, Y, and Z) while preserving principal collective structures. Applied without retraining to an unseen inlet gas velocity, the DeepONet retains an R2 above 0.99 in all three directions (pooled R2 of 0.998) and the LSTM retains a pooled R2 of 0.991, and trained-surrogate inference reproduces the full 14 s trajectory of all particles roughly an order of magnitude faster i…

title: Channel attention-enabled deep learning for permeability prediction from 3D digital rock images
Enhanced Graph Representation Learning for Link Prediction in Human–Machine Collaborative Assembly Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Human–robot collaborative assembly relies on structured knowledge of components, assembly operations and process constraints. We propose a knowledge graph representation learning framework to predict missing links in assembly knowledge. A human–robot collaborative assembly knowledge graph is constructed through joint entity–relation extraction, entity alignment and manual verification. Two adaptive relational graph attention network encoders learn structural and semantic representations, which are fused through element-wise addition. A local–global mutual information objective guides structural representation learning, while a Fourier Kolmogorov–Arnold network decoder scores candidate triples. Link prediction experiments on WN18RR, FB15K-237 and the domain-specific HRKG examine the contributions of the model components through ablation. The complete model achieves mean reciprocal ranks of 0.498, 0.382 and 0.902, respectively. An assembly assistance system integrates visual recognition, link prediction, and robotic grasping and delivery. In 600 gearbox assembly subtasks, component requirement prediction was correct in 576 of 594 trials with correct target recognition (97.0%), and the complete workflow succeeded in 550 trials (91.7%). The stage-specific evaluation distinguishes prediction performance from system-level task completion.

title: When prediction is not explanation: AI and the ethical transformation of medicine
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving from a collection of discrete applications towards a technology increasingly embedded in the infrastructure of medicine. This development may improve diagnosis, prediction, monitoring, and the use of clinical information, but technological adoption is advancing faster than the governance structures needed to accompany it. At the level of the individual patient, this transformation creates a specific ethical problem. Patient information enters computational systems and emerges as probabilities, classifications, predictions, or recommendations that may influence care. The black box provides a metaphor for the intervening computational process when clinically relevant elements cannot be sufficiently examined. Yet opening the black box does not resolve the entire problem: an intelligible and validated prediction does not itself establish that a proposed intervention will benefit a particular patient. I propose a Patient-Level AI Code of Conduct governing the transition from AI output to clinical action. The Code requires examinability, validation, patient-level applicability, independent clinical justification, and meaningful human responsibility before an AI output materially influences care. Its purpose is to preserve a fundamental distinction as AI becomes increasingly infrastructural to medicine: computational capability can inf…

The Mediating Role of Consumer Satisfaction in The Influence of Trust and Service Quality on Streetwear Purchase Decisions on Shopee
abstract: Background: The rapid expansion of digital marketplaces has heightened the significance of consumer trust, service quality, and satisfaction in determining online purchase decisions, especially among Generation Z buyers who acquire streetwear products via Shopee. Objective: This research investigates the direct influence of consumer trust and service quality on purchase decisions and assesses the mediating function of consumer satisfaction among Generation Z consumers residing in Serang City. Methods: An explanatory quantitative survey involving 100 respondents chosen via purposive sampling was carried out. The data were gathered through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and processed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 20, encompassing validity and reliability examinations, classical assumption tests, simple and multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, coefficients of determination, and Sobel mediation analysis. Results: Both consumer trust and service quality exerted positive and significant direct effects on purchase decisions as well as on consumer satisfaction, whereas consumer satisfaction likewise positively and significantly influenced purchase decisions. The Sobel analyses verified significant mediation for trust (Z = 5.396) and for service quality (Z = 5.771). Within the simultaneous model, consumer satisfaction stayed significant, and the model accounted for…

title: Syllabus content on forces and interactions in pre-service primary teacher education: a Croatian case study in relation to the natural science curriculum
abstract: Introduction The introduction of the experimental programme “Primary School as a Full-Day School: A Balanced, Equitable, Efficient and Sustainable System of Education” in 2023 brought a new school subject, Natural Science, into Croatian primary schools. The curriculum for this subject includes educational outcomes that were not previously represented in the subject Nature and Society, raising the question of their representation in initial teacher education. Methods This study aimed to analyse the extent to which syllabi of science and teaching methodology courses within integrated teacher education programmes in Croatia explicitly include learning outcomes and content related to the effects of force, gravitational force, friction, and magnetic interaction, as defined by educational outcome PRI OŠ B.2.2 for the second grade of primary school, and how this content is distributed across courses and syllabi within the analysed study programmes. A qualitative document analysis was conducted on 56 publicly available syllabi selected from seven study programmes. Results The analysis showed that categories C1 -C4 were not explicitly represented in the learning outcomes of the analysed syllabi, whereas each of the four categories was explicitly represented in the course content of 2 of the 56 syllabi (3.57%). title: What I Wish I Knew Before Implementing School-Based Outdoor Experiential Education: Interviews with In-Service Teachers
abstract: Teacher preparation programs in the United States rarely integrate school-based outdoor experiential education (SBOEE), leaving many new teachers underprepared to use the outdoors as an instructional setting. This qualitative study examined how in-service teachers successfully implement SBOEE, what they wish they had learned about SBOEE before entering the classroom, and how their insights can inform teacher preparation. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 22 educators from across the United States who regularly facilitate SBOEE. Findings show that effective SBOEE implementation develops through mentorship, collaborative learning communities, hands-on practice, and supportive school environments. Teachers emphasized that their preparation programs offered little exposure to SBOEE, which they viewed as a significant oversight. Participants identified experiential learning, structured practice opportunities, access to practical resources, and faculty modeling as key supports they wished had been included in their preparation. These insights offer actionable guidance for incorporating SBOEE into teacher education.

Digital fashion product–service system: the reconfiguration of apparel design, user participation, and platform value
abstract: Digital fashion is reshaping clothing and apparel research by changing how garments are designed, represented, experienced, and circulated across physical–digital environments. Existing studies have examined digital fashion through technological innovation, virtual garments, consumer experience, sustainability, and platform branding, but these perspectives remain fragmented. This paper argues that digital fashion should be understood as an apparel product–service system (PSS) in which design processes, user participation, platform infrastructures, and mediated value creation are increasingly integrated. Drawing on an integrative conceptual review and a structured illustrative scan of selected fashion enterprises, the study develops a relational framework for interpreting digital fashion transformation. The analysis shows that digital technologies reconfigure apparel design into adaptive and feedback-driven practices; users participate as operant resources through styling, sharing, remixing, and feedback; and platforms coordinate garments, digital assets, interfaces, data, content, and commercial interaction. The paper contributes by reframing digital fashion as a platform-mediated apparel PSS.

title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Bilingual Interactive Citizenship Education Concept Module for Pre-Service Primary Teachers
abstract: Bilingual resources that integrate national civic content with global citizenship perspectives are essential in pre-service primary teacher education. This study developed and conducted a preliminary evaluation of an Indonesian–English interactive module for the Citizenship Education Concept course. The development process followed the Dick and Carey model, encompassing learner and context analysis, formulation of performance-based objectives, instructional strategy and material development, and formative evaluation. An initial questionnaire administered to 37 students assessed their perceptions of the quality of existing instructional media and their self-reported learner autonomy. After implementation, a post-use survey completed by the same cohort, consisting of 30 closed-ended statements and four open-ended questions, evaluated technical usability, content quality, bilingual presentation, interactive learning, and visual design. As the instruments measured distinct constructs and employed different response scales, data were analyzed separately using descriptive statistics, and written responses were summarised thematically. The initial assessment produced 86.42% of the maximum possible score for the perceived quality of existing instructional media and 77,97% for learner autonomy. The post-use evaluation yielded an overall score of 90,99%, with consistently high ratings fo…

title: Effects of out-of-pocket health expenditure on universal health service coverage: evidence from panel data from low-, middle-, and high-income countries
abstract: Abstract Background Achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by 2030, a key SDG target, requires progress in both service coverage and financial protection. Out-of-pocket (OOP) financing remains an important component of health-financing systems, but its association with UHC service coverage may differ across country income groups. Objective To investigate how OOP health expenditure as a share of current health expenditure is associated with UHC service coverage across low-income countries (LICs), middle-income countries (MICs), and high-income countries (HICs), while accounting for demographic, economic, governance and temporal factors. Methods We analyzed a balanced panel of 147 countries from 2015 to 2023. The outcome was the UHC service coverage index (UHCSCI) and the main exposure was OOP health expenditure as a percentage of current health expenditure, representing the composition of national health financing rather than household-level OOP burden or per-capita OOP expenditure. GDP per capita, population size, elderly population (65+), external health expenditure, and the Corruption Perception Index (CPI) were also used as covariates. The fractional logit generalized estimating equation (GEE) model with an AR(1) correlation structure was employed to estimate the population-averaged associations between OOP health spending and UHCSCI across LICs, MICs, and HICs. Frequency-domain energy transformation characteristics of nonlinear inertia in vibration isolation systems
abstract: Nonlinear inertia in vibrating systems redistributes incoming kinetic energy among multiple frequency components. This paper examines two coupled aspects: the frequency-domain transformation of nonlinear inertial kinetic energy and its influence on the response and harmonic kinetic-energy distribution of the system output. Two metrics—Energy Transformation Ratio ( R E . T . ) and Energy Distribution ( Dist e )—are proposed to quantify this spectral redistribution. For a general nonlinear inertia coupled to a single-degree-of-freedom isolator, the energy distribution is nearly independent of excitation frequency at high frequencies but strongly frequency-dependent in the low-to mid-frequency range. Higher excitation amplitudes increase the proportion of higher-frequency energy, while a smaller minimum value of the prescribed nonlinear inertia further amplifies this effect. The type of coupled isolator also reshapes the energy spectrum: the X-structure results in a lower high-frequency energy proportion than linear or nonlinear spring–damper isolators. Nonlinear inertia can significantly enhance the high-frequency components in the system output, and its effects vary across different coupled systems. title: Reciprocal links among gratitude, emotion regulation, and social media addiction: A positive psychology framework
abstract: Abstract Social media addiction (SMA) is prevalent across age groups and has attracted both public concern and scholarly attention. From a positive psychology perspective, this longitudinal study focused on gratitude and emotion regulation, examining the prospective effects of these two socio‐emotional strengths on SMA. Using an online survey platform, 660 participants (54.1% female) aged 19 to 69 years ( M = 32.99, SD = 7.63) completed the baseline and 6‐month follow‐up questionnaires in January and July 2024. As hypothesized, gratitude and emotion regulation were negatively correlated with SMA at both waves. The cross‐lagged panel model further demonstrated the bidirectional associations: higher baseline gratitude and emotion regulation predicted lower SMA at follow‐up, whereas baseline SMA predicted decreases in subsequent gratitude and emotion regulation. Moreover, baseline emotion regulation predicted higher gratitude at follow‐up, but the reverse pathway was not observed. These findings support positive psychology interventions that strengthen gratitude and emotion regulation as preventive strategies against SMA.

When Does a Self-Assessment Carry Information? Regional Variation in the Corroboration of Reported Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Capacity Across 182 Countries
abstract: International antimicrobial resistance (AMR) monitoring relies on the unverified Tracking AMR Country Self-Assessment Survey (TrACSS). Whether its ratings provide equivalent information across settings remains unclear. This cross-sectional analysis examined correspondence between self-rated surveillance capacity and laboratory capabilities in the 2025 public dataset, by WHO region and income. For 182 countries answering surveillance item 3.5, a corroboration score (0–4) incorporated reference-laboratory susceptibility testing for 12 priority bacteria, standardized testing guidelines and external quality assurance beyond reference laboratories, and reporting a laboratory count. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlations. Mean corroboration increased from 1.50 at rating A to 3.43 at rating D (overall ρ = 0.43; 95% CI 0.29–0.55; p < 0.001). Regional correlations ranged from 0.67 in the Eastern Mediterranean to 0.20 in the Western Pacific; confidence intervals excluded zero in three regions but included zero in Europe and the Western Pacific. Mean corroboration did not differ significantly between regions (Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.80). Across six regions, correlation strength was inversely rank-ordered with corroboration among low self-raters (ρ = −1.00; exact p = 0.003), consistent with ceiling effects. title: Investigation of cellular DNA repair capacity with an inhibitor-modified comet assay
abstract: Abstract DNA repair plays an important role in genomic integrity. Major DNA repair pathways for substance-induced DNA damage are base excision and nucleotide excision repair, as well as the repair of double strand breaks by homologous recombination and non-homologous end joining. However, the quantitative measurement of cellular DNA repair capacity remains a challenge. Here we applied a modified comet assay in which DNA repair capacity can be tracked using DNA repair inhibitors combined with selected DNA-damaging substances. The combinations of the alkylating agent methylmethansulfonate + olaparib, UV-C (causing pyrimidine dimers) + aphidicolin, and the topoisomerase II inhibitor etoposide + SCR7 were used to reflect base excision repair, nucleotide excision repair, and non-homologous end joining. Although neither the agents nor the inhibitors are by themselves completely selective for these DNA repair pathways, the combinations and also the missing reaction to other combinations of the same substances indicated a certain degree of preference. By using all of them within one experiment, a pattern of DNA repair activity of cell lines was established. A comparison of five cell lines/types differing in their sensitivity to the damaging agents demonstrated its applicability. title: Contract Management as a Mechanism Linking Stakeholder Pressure to Procurement Performance in a Ugandan Local Government
abstract: Public procurement performance depends not only on stakeholder demands but also on the administrative mechanisms through which those demands are translated into contract results. This study examined whether contract management mediates the relationship between stakeholder pressure and procurement performance in Bushenyi District Local Government, Uganda. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was adopted. The quantitative population comprised district personnel involved in procurement governance and contract implementation, including the accounting officer, contracts committee, procurement and disposal unit, and user departments. Of 103 questionnaires distributed, 82 usable responses were obtained, representing a 79.6% questionnaire response rate. Four of ten planned key-informant interviews were completed. Stakeholder pressure was operationalised through power, legitimacy and urgency; contract management through contract planning, monitoring and vendor appraisal; and procurement performance through competition, efficiency, effectiveness, economy and environmental considerations. Regression results showed that stakeholder pressure significantly predicted procurement performance, R² = .619, adjusted R² = .614, F (1, 80) = 129.760, p < .001, and contract management, R² = .710, adjusted R² = .706, F (1, 80) = 195.604, p < .001. Contract management also predicted procurement perfor…

title: Self-Assessed Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Capacity in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region: An Internal Validation of the Tracking AMR Country Self-Assessment Survey
abstract: Global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) monitoring relies heavily on the Tracking AMR Country Self-Assessment Survey (TrACSS), an unverified annual self-report instrument. This study examined whether Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) surveillance self-ratings corresponded with laboratory and programmatic capacities reported by the same respondents and characterized non-response. A cross-sectional analysis used the TrACSS 2025 public dataset, covering 184 responding countries. For 19 EMR respondents, we compared surveillance ratings against four criteria: reference-laboratory susceptibility testing for all 12 priority bacteria, standardized testing guidelines, external quality assurance beyond reference laboratories, and reporting a laboratory count. Ratings were also compared with national action plan (NAP) implementation. Nineteen of 22 EMR member states responded; non-responders, Libya, the Syrian Arab Republic, and the occupied Palestinian territory, were conflict-affected. EMR had the highest proportion reporting standardized national surveillance or better (73.7% versus 58.8% globally). Countries rated D–E met a mean of 3.5 corroborating criteria, compared with 1.6 among those rated A-C. However, only 7/14 countries claiming standardized national surveillance met all four criteria; 5/14 omitted laboratory counts, including three high-income countries. Furthermore, 11/14 rep…

title: Estimating Lithium-Ion Battery Capacity from Charging-Curve Health Indicators: How Far Does It Generalise to an Unseen Cell?
abstract: Accurate battery capacity estimation is important for evaluating the health of lithium-ion batteries. However, a complete discharge test is difficult to perform when a battery is already installed in a vehicle. This study investigates whether battery capacity can be estimated from health indicators extracted from a single charging curve and whether the prediction can generalise to an unseen cell. The NASA ageing data from four 18650 lithium-ion battery cells were used. After charge-discharge pairing and data cleaning, 628 charging samples were retained. Ten health indicators were extracted and divided into time, voltage and temperature groups. Linear Regression, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting were evaluated using a pooled random split and leave-one-cell-out validation. Under the pooled random split, Random Forest with all features achieved the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0119 Ah. However, the tree models showed clear performance reductions under leave-one-cell-out validation. Linear Regression with time and voltage features achieved the best cross-cell result, with an MAE of 0.0329 Ah and an R² of 0.9446. Adding voltage features reduced the cross-cell MAE by 38.6% compared with using time features alone, while temperature features did not provide a further improvement. B0006 was the most difficult cell to predict. The results show that charging-curve indicators c…

title: Cognitive Engagement as a Key Mechanism of Cognitive Sustainability in the Age of Generative AI: An Interdisciplinary Framework
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) systems can improve productivity, yet their long-term implications for human cognition remain contested. This article develops an interdisciplinary framework for explaining how different patterns in the distribution and support of cognitive operations between humans and GenAI may shape cognitive engagement and cognitive outcomes over time. The framework draws upon a Neuro-Information-Systems (NeuroIS)-informed approach by integrating cognitive, behavioral, self-report, and neurophysiological perspectives into a multilevel account of how GenAI use shapes human cognition. We argue that cognitive engagement—the depth, persistence, and strategic quality of human processing during AI-supported tasks—is a proposed central mechanism linking the distribution and support of cognitive operations between humans and GenAI to cognitive outcomes. Direct effects on outcomes may coexist with engagement-mediated effects on outcomes. The cognitive consequences depend particularly on whether cognitively consequential operations related to understanding, learning, critical evaluation, and independent judgment continue to involve meaningful human engagement. Specifically, the framework integrates five elements: (1) antecedent conditions (user, task, and GenAI/system characteristics); (2) regulatory processes (metacognition, trust calibration, and motivatio…

title: Circular Consumer Collectives as a Meso-Level Mechanism in Circular Economy Transition
abstract: Circular economy transition requires sustained changes in everyday consumption, yet household practices remain weakly connected to system-level change. This paper conceptualises circular consumer collectives as meso-level mechanisms that bridge this gap. Integrating systems theory and social practice theory, it identifies two functions: translation, which converts circular ambitions into actionable routines, and amplification, which aggregates individual actions into signals visible to institutions. These functions operate through three mechanisms: intrapersonal cultivation, which strengthens circular identity and competence; interpersonal scaffolding, which supports progression from observing to trying to teaching; and system signalling, which makes collective outcomes legible to firms, NGOs, and public authorities. Repair Cafe Wales provides an illustrative case of these mechanisms in practice. The framework also identifies potential failures, including exclusionary dynamics, volunteer and subsidy dependency, and rebound effects. It contributes to macromarketing by connecting individual behaviour change with broader provisioning-system transitions.

title: Enhanced Rock Weathering for Carbon Dioxide Removal: An Integrated Review of Potential, Challenges, and Pathways to Scalable and Sustainable Implementation
abstract: Abstract Enhanced rock weathering is an emerging CO2 removal strategy with considerable potential to mitigate climate change while providing additional agricultural and environmental benefits. By 2050, enhanced rock weathering has a global CO2 removal potential of 0.5–2 gigatons of CO2 annually and can increase crop yields on agricultural land by 7 to 20%. However, large-scale implementation encounters technical, environmental, economic, and regulatory challenges. In this review, we consolidate research from geochemistry, agronomy, economics, environmental science, and policy to present an integrated analysis. We outline novel analytical approaches, including reframing heavy-metal risk as an optimization challenge and critically evaluating the scalability–permanence trade-off in CO2 removal portfolios. In this review, we identify strategic future research needs to support enhanced rock weathering’s role as a transformative solution for climate and sustainability. Key research needs include optimizing particle size while minimizing comminution energy requirements; evaluating the long-term accumulation, mobility, and ecological effects of potentially toxic elements; developing spatially resolved techno-economic and life-cycle assessments; establishing standardized and scalable MRV frameworks; and implementing coordinated, long-term field trials across geographically and pedo-clim…

title: Experimental and Numerical Study on Mechanical Properties of Threaded-Sleeve-Type Disconnectable Coupling for Foundation Pit Engineering
abstract: To overcome the performance shortcomings of disconnectable couplings in foundation pit support systems, a threaded-sleeve-type disconnectable coupling was designed and developed in this study. An axial loading test was performed to investigate the bearing capacity of the coupling. Its yield load, initial compression stiffness, load–displacement curve, stress distribution, and failure mode were determined. A finite element analysis parametric study was performed and formulae for calculating the yield load and compressive stiffness proposed. The following conclusions were drawn from the results: (1) The coupling has good bearing performance. The yield load is 10,509.96 kN, the ultimate load is 12,980.2 kN, and the initial compression stiffness is 4215.17 kN·mm−1. The failure of the coupling is characterized by an outward bulging of the nut part and shearing of the thread. (2) The coupling has good ductility. Strain concentration occurs at the screw. (3) The bearing capacity of the coupling is positively correlated with the outer diameter of the nut, nut thickness, and screw thickness and linearly inversely related to the elongation and screw pitch. (4) The established calculation formulae can accurately estimate the yield load and initial compression stiffness of the coupling.

title: Bromeliad Brocchinia reducta , a rare carnivorous monocot, is a holocarnivorous plant secreting its own digestive enzymes
abstract: Abstract Carnivorous bromeliad Brocchinia reducta is a rare carnivorous plant. As a monocot, it is the youngest and most distantly related to the remaining ∼800 dicot carnivorous plant species. Although considered carnivorous for more than 40 years, it is believed that it does not secrete digestive enzymes and relies on microorganism-mediated digestion. Here we investigated the digestive physiology of B. reducta by measuring enzyme activity and using LC-ESI-MS/MS in response to feeding. We found prey-induced pH regulation and digestive capacity with secreted hydrolytic enzymes (e.g., aspartic protease, type I and III chitinase, GDSL hydrolase) similar to those found in other carnivorous lineages. Although the enzyme activity is rather low and comparable to the members of the carnivorous Sarraceniaceae family, the active prey response and presence of secreted enzymes placed B. reducta among truly holocarnivorous plants. Our results showed that a nutrient-poor environment exerts the same selective pressures on even distantly related plants and, through the process of convergent evolution, leads to the co-option of the same proteins for digestive function.

Dual knockout of susceptibility genes AtKRP6 and AtWRKY23 confers nematode resistance without affecting the host fitness
abstract: Abstract Background The root-knot nematode, Meloidogyne incognita , is responsible for significant yield losses worldwide. Breeding nematode-resistant crops has traditionally provided a sustainable management strategy. However, regulatory challenges associated with genetically modified crops and the emergence of nematode populations capable of overcoming resistance have limited the efficacy of resistance breeding. As an alternative strategy, CRISPR/Cas9 technology has been employed to confer nematode resistance by selectively knocking out host susceptibility ( S ) genes in various crop plants. Nevertheless, targeting a single S gene has often failed to reduce nematode populations below economically acceptable thresholds, likely due to functional redundancy among nematode-responsive S genes. Results Here, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept using multiplex genome editing (polycistronic tRNA–gRNA system) to simultaneously knock out two distinct nematode-responsive S genes, AtWRKY23 and AtKRP6 , which were specifically selected based on their strong and localized induction upon M. incognita infection. This expression pattern, confirmed by promoter: GUS reporter assays and RT-qPCR analyses, minimizes potential fitness costs associated with gene disruption. Compared to the wild-type, nematode multiplication per plant was reduced by 29.22%, 26.75% and 56.45% in AtKRP6 knockout (KO), At…

title: Soil engineering by an invasive ant reprograms plant growth–defense trade‐offs to entrench a tripartite mutualism
abstract: Summary Ants are ubiquitous ecosystem engineers, yet the mechanisms through which their nesting activity regulates mutualistic interactions remain elusive. Here, we provide evidence consistent with the hypothesis that ant nesting initiates a soil–plant–herbivore cascade that reinforces a tripartite mutualism. Using the invasive fire ant Solenopsis invicta as a model system in both laboratory and field settings, we show that ant nesting increases soil nitrate and ammonium concentrations, which are associated with enhanced plant growth. These nesting‐related changes coincide with shifts in the host plant's hormonal signaling network: auxin signaling is systemically elevated, whereas salicylic acid defense pathways and jasmonate signal transduction are suppressed. Plants associated with ant nests exhibit compromised defense responses to aphid herbivory. This shift toward a growth‐biased physiology supports larger aphid populations, which in turn provide increased carbohydrate rewards for ants, augmenting ant colony survival and brood biomass. Collectively, our findings suggest a potential terrestrial feedback loop in which ants indirectly enhance their own performance through nesting‐associated changes in soil nutrients and plant physiology, which ultimately benefit a mutualist herbivore. In doing so, this study establishes a tripartite ant–plant–herbivore mutualism that extends b…

Research on a Short-Circuit Current Suppression Strategy for Multi-DC Receiving-End Power Grids Integrating Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation and Coordinated Optimization of Grid Structure and Current-Limiting Devices
abstract: To address excessive short-circuit currents and the pronounced “strong DC, weak AC” characteristic caused by large-scale UHVDC infeed into receiving-end grids, this paper proposes a planning-oriented suppression strategy integrating coordinated optimization of grid structure and superconducting fault current limiters (SFCLs) with fuzzy comprehensive evaluation. A coordinated model is first established to jointly determine discrete branch states and continuous SFCL equivalent series resistances while accounting for line-disconnection costs, equipment-investment costs, short-circuit-current limits, and physical-logical coupling constraints. A sensitivity-assisted Benders-type iterative framework is then developed, in which a mixed-integer master problem generates candidate planning decisions and a BPA-based subproblem performs nonlinear physical verification. Local finite-difference sensitivities are used to construct feasibility-guidance cuts rather than globally valid analytical Benders cuts. Physically feasible schemes are subsequently evaluated in terms of current-limiting effectiveness, steady-state voltage deviation, equipment-investment cost, and network loss. The method is validated using the modified CSEE-VS-66 system under standard and high-load operating conditions, a representative single-line-to-ground fault scenario, and an additional CSEE-FS-47 system. title: Legal protection of Omani folklore (popular heritage) in the AI-driven virtual world: Preserving identity
abstract: Folklore and intangible cultural heritage reflect the folk traditions and identity of a specific society. States intervene to protect such heritage—both domestically and internationally—a practice adopted by the Sultanate of Oman through various legislative frameworks. These include laws concerning copyright and related rights, regulations governing cultural heritage, and penal provisions. Such heritage is considered state-owned intangible property; its distortion or commercial exploitation without official authorization from the competent authorities is prohibited and subject to specific legal penalties and enforcement measures. This study underscores the significance of cultural heritage and its intrinsic link to national identity, while highlighting the need to address legal gaps in intellectual property protection to keep pace with digital transformation and support the digital cultural economy. The study aims to identify the digital risks posed to folklore in the virtual realm—exacerbated by the widespread use of artificial intelligence—and to evaluate the adequacy of existing laws in addressing challenges related to digital platforms and AI. Ultimately, it seeks to propose legal and technical solutions that safeguard heritage and preserve identity by integrating digitalization and modern technologies, all in alignment with the "Oman Vision 2040."
venue: International Journal of Law Research and Studies

title: The Tartary Buckwheat FtMYB15 Coordinates Cadmium Uptake and Detoxification by Regulating FtZIP3 and FtGSTU19 Expression
abstract: ABSTRACT Tartary buckwheat ( Fagopyrum tataricum ) is a crop of significant value, yet its cultivation in cadmium (Cd)‐contaminated soils poses risks to food safety. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of Cd uptake is crucial for developing strategies to minimize its accumulation. Here, we demonstrate that the Tartary buckwheat transcription factor FtMYB15 promotes Cd 2+ influx and enhances Cd accumulation in transgenic hairy roots. Yeast one‐hybrid (Y1H) and electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) results indicate that FtMYB15 binds to the MYB‐binding sites (MBS) of the FtZIP3 promoter, thereby upregulating the expression of FtZIP3 , which encodes a zinc/iron‐regulated transporter‐like protein. Overexpression of FtZIP3 similarly enhances Cd 2+ influx and Cd accumulation in buckwheat hairy roots. Further analysis reveals that FtMYB15 binds to the MBS in the promoter of the tau glutathione S‐transferase gene FtGSTU19 and upregulates its expression in buckwheat hairy roots both before and after Cd exposure. Overexpression of FtGSTU19 in buckwheat hairy roots enhances Cd detoxification capacity via its glutathione transferase activity, thereby alleviating Cd‐induced oxidative stress. Heterologous expression of FtGSTU19 increases Cd tolerance in Arabidopsis . Expression of FtMYB15 , FtZIP3 , and FtGSTU19 is induced by Cd stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that FtMY…

title: Sulfur Locking and Chlorination Synergistically Enable Efficient Charge Transport and Low Nonradiative Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient charge transport while maintaining low nonradiative energy loss remains a key challenge in the molecular design of small‐molecule acceptors (SMAs) for organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a stepwise molecular engineering strategy based on sulfur locking and chlorination to regulate intermolecular packing and excited‐state properties simultaneously. Sulfur locking modifies molecular conformation and intermolecular packing, leading to enhanced exciton diffusion and charge transport. Subsequent chlorination further strengthens intermolecular interactions through additional Cl···S contacts, resulting in tighter π–π stacking and improved crystalline ordering. Binary OSCs based on D18:Qx2Ph‐SCl achieve an efficiency of 20.0% with a high open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.951 V, while maintaining a low nonradiative energy loss of ∼0.19 eV. Owing to its intrinsically lower reorganization energy and weaker electron–phonon coupling than L8‐BO, Qx2Ph‐SCl further serves as an effective third component in ternary OSCs, reducing nonradiative recombination and increasing the V OC . As a result, the ternary device delivers an efficiency of 21.3%. This work demonstrates that stepwise sulfur locking and chlorination provide an effective molecular design strategy for simultaneously optimizing charge transport and voltage loss in high‐performance OSCs.

SpellGlasses: An Augmented Reality Interface to Support Novice Players in Trading Card Games
abstract: Trading card games have grown significantly in popularity, with “Magic: The Gathering” ( Magic ) standing out as one of the most widely played examples. However, the increasing complexity of cards and mechanics presents a steep learning curve for new players, making it difficult to understand game mechanics and come up with game strategies. This paper addresses this challenge by introducing “ SpellGlasses ,” an augmented reality (AR) interface for smart glasses to support Magic players during gameplay by providing real-time explanations of game mechanics and supplementary information. The development process was guided by player feedback and iterative user studies. Participants perceived SpellGlasses as helpful for rule comprehension and onboarding support while largely preserving the physical gameplay experience. These results suggest that AR smart glasses have the potential to support learning and accessibility in complex physical games. We present design implications that are transferable to similar applications for smart glasses aimed at facilitating the onboarding in physical games.

title: Co-BDC metal organic framework and fluoride free process synthesized partially etched MXene composite for electrochemical energy storage applications
abstract: Abstract Poor electrical conductivity and sluggish charge transport often limit the electrochemical performance of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). Here, a cobalt- benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate-dimethylformamide, [Co(BDC)DMF] n MOF, was synthesized via a solvothermal route and integrated with alkali assisted partially etched MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ; T = -O, -OH, x = 1–4) to develop a high-performance composite electrode. Compared to conventional HF-based etching, alkali etching offers a relatively safer and environmentally benign approach while increasing interlayer spacing, thereby enhancing ion accessibility and interfacial interaction. Structural and morphological analysis confirm successful composite formation, while X-ray photoelectron and Raman spectroscopies reveal strong interfacial coupling and improved electronic properties. Electrochemical measurements show that the composite delivers a high specific capacitance of 704 F g − 1 at 1 A g − 1 , significantly exceeding that of pristine [Co(BDC)DMF] n MOF (417 F g − 1 ), along with improved power capability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis indicates reduced charge transfer resistance from 12.58 Ω (pristine) to 8.47 Ω (composite), confirming enhanced charge transport. Additionally, the [Co(BDC)DMF] n / partially etched MXene composite electrode exhibits 91% capacitance retention as compared to [Co(BDC)DMF] n , whi…

title: Energy Subsidies and the Climate Dilemma in Middle Eastern Petro-States: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: This study examines the association between fossil fuel subsidies and greenhouse gas emissions in five major Middle Eastern petro-states: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, which face a severe dilemma as they weigh the imperative of addressing climate change against their economic reliance on fossil fuels. Covering the period 2010–2023, the analysis estimates the within-country association between per-capita emissions and total and fuel-specific subsidy levels in a two-way fixed effects panel model. The results indicate a consistent and statistically significant positive association between subsidies and emissions, with a 10% lower level of total subsidies associated with a 1.2% lower level of emissions. Among fuel types, gas subsidies show the strongest and most consistent correlation with emissions, while oil and electricity subsidies exhibit weaker or statistically insignificant patterns. The findings highlight the policy relevance of fuel-specific subsidy measures and provide empirical evidence to inform reform strategies that balance fiscal sustainability, resource management, social welfare, and emission-reduction objectives in Middle Eastern petro-states.
venue: International Journal of Energy Economics and Policy

title: The AWAKEN wind farm benchmark – Part 1: Observed conditions
abstract: Wind turbine wakes significantly reduce downstream performance, yet accurately modeling their sensitivity to atmospheric stability and terrain remains a challenge. To address this, the International Energy Agency Wind Technology Collaboration Programme Task 57 launched a new wind farm wake benchmark leveraging high-resolution observations from the American WAKE experimeNt (AWAKEN). This paper, Part 1 of a two-part series, details the observational dataset and the selection of 24 August 2023 as the case study for the benchmark. This date was selected for its canonical diurnal cycle, which features a low-level jet with strong nocturnal stratification and high turbulence during the daytime. Analysis of the observational data reveals that despite the relatively simple terrain, interactions between the low-level jet and topography drove significant spatial variability in wind flow, leading to turbine power differences of up to 80 % across the considered wind farm. These findings demonstrate that a single vertical profile is insufficient to characterize wind plant inflow even in moderately complex terrain and that terrain-induced flow modifications can outweigh wake losses under stable stratification. The observed conditions documented here, together with the openly released dataset, constitute a unique multi-scale reference case for wake model validation at a large operating wind pl…

title: Thực trạng nhiễm độc chì nghề nghiệp và một số yếu tố liên quan ở công nhân sản xuất ắc quy tại Hải Phòng năm 2024
abstract: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang được thực hiện trên 89 công nhân sản xuất ắc quy tại Hải Phòng nhằm xácđịnh thực trạng nhiễm độc chì nghề nghiệp và một số yếu tố liên quan. Thông tin về đặc điểm nhân khẩu vànghề nghiệp được thu thập bằng phỏng vấn trực tiếp, nồng độ chì máu được xác định bằng phương phápquang phổ hấp thụ nguyên tử. Nhiễm độc chì nghề nghiệp được chẩn đoán khi nồng độ chì máu >40 µg/dL theo Thông tư 15/2016/TT-BYT. Kết quả cho thấy nồng độ chì máu của người lao động là 35,8 ± 14,7µg/dL; tỷ lệ nhiễm độc chì nghề nghiệp là 38,2%. Một số yếu tố liên quan tới nhiễm độc chì nghề nghiệpbao gồm: tuổi nghề, từ 10–20 năm và trên 20 năm (aOR=3,42; 95%CI: 1,12–10,41) và (aOR=4,15; 95%CI:1,08–15,94) so với tuổi nghề dưới 10 năm. Lao động trực tiếp sản xuất (aOR=4,92; 95%CI: 1,02–23,71) sovới nhóm không trực tiếp sản xuất. Nhiễm độc chì nghề nghiệp là vấn đề sức khỏe phổ biến ở công nhânsản xuất ắc quy, đặc biệt ở nhóm lao động có thời gian tiếp xúc nghề nghiệp kéo dài và trực tiếp tham giasản xuất. Cần ưu tiên giám sát phơi nhiễm chì và theo dõi sức khỏe định kỳ đối với các nhóm lao động cónguy cơ cao nhằm hạn chế các tác động bất lợi đối với sức khỏe.
