title: Research on Impurity Separation Behavior During Pre-Storage Paddy Cleaning with CFD-DPM
abstract: Paddy grains require impurity removal before storage, and cyclone air separation is the final stage for removing lightweight impurities. In this study, a three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics–discrete phase model (CFD–DPM) was established to investigate impurity separation in a cyclone air separation device. The Reynolds stress model (RSM) was used for the continuous air phase, and the discrete phase model (DPM) was used to track impurity particles. Simulations were performed at an inlet velocity of 9 m/s, corresponding to a Reynolds number (Re) of approximately 1.84 × 105 based on an inlet hydraulic diameter of 0.299 m. Three structural parameters were investigated: the dust outlet diameter (Ddo = 454–654 mm), conical section length (Lcs = 1476–1876 mm), and impurity capture diameter (Dic = 240–440 mm). Particle tracking showed four main stages: particle entry, downward spiral motion, size-dependent separation, and discharge. When Ddo increased from 454 to 654 mm, separation efficiency decreased from 88.75% to 55.46%, while the pressure drop decreased from 223.65 to 161.09 Pa. Increasing Lcs from 1476 to 1876 mm increased the separation efficiency from 44.46% to 82.87%, with the pressure drop increasing from 170.13 to 208.90 Pa. Increasing Dic from 240 to 440 mm reduced the separation efficiency from about 85% to 53%, while the pressure drop decreased from about 205 t…

title: Polymer-Engineered Ionogels for Lithium-Based Energy Storage: Interactions, Processing, and Electrode Interfaces
abstract: By immobilizing ionic liquids (ILs) within polymer networks, ionogels offer a route to quasi-solid-state electrolytes with liquid-like ion mobility and solid-like dimensional stability. Their practical performance, however, is not determined by IL content or total ionic conductivity alone. Frequently reported limitations include low Li+ transference numbers, polymer–IL demixing, creep, insufficient electrode wetting, and unstable interphases. This review develops a mechanistically informed framework that traces how polymer chemistry and polymer–IL–lithium salt interactions shape process-induced microstructures, which in turn influence ion transport, mechanical response, and electrode interfaces. We examine electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and competitive Li+ coordination across representative polymer–IL systems, and compare fabrication routes in terms of the confinement, phase connectivity, and electrode contact they generate. The routes considered include solution casting, phase inversion and scaffold impregnation, electrospinning, thermal or photoinitiated in situ polymerization, physical self-assembly, interpenetrating-network and multiple-network formation, hybrid sol–gel processing, and thin-film patterning. The review distinguishes structural evidence from Li+-specific transport evidence and considers differences in measurement and cell conditions. Load-beari…

title: CONTRIBUTION OF CITES APPENDIX II SNAKE EXPORTS TO INDONESIA'S NON-TAX REVENUE
abstract: The trade of snakes listed in CITES Appendix II plays a pivotal role in conservation and contributes to Indonesia's economy through non-tax state revenue. This study examines the volume and trends of Appendix II snake exports from 2020 to 2024, their contribution to non-tax state revenue, and how wildlife trade is monitored as part of conservation efforts. This study uses a mixed-methods approach, merging quantitative analysis of secondary data from the CITES trade database with qualitative interviews conducted at the Ministry of Forestry. Specifically, in-depth interviews were held with two key informants, both serving as Forest Ecosystem Management Officers (Pengendali Ekosistem Hutan/PEH) at the Directorate of Species and Genetic Conservation. The results indicate that the snake skin category has the largest total volume, amounting to 1,378,878 pieces, and generates the highest non-tax state revenue, reaching IDR 2,794,006,380.00. Meanwhile, live snakes, leather products, meat, gallbladders, and garments show declining export trends. Conversely, the export trend for skin pieces is increasing. Rather than a broad shift toward fully processed downstream products, this trend indicates a specific shift toward intermediate commodities, as the export of finished leather products has concurrently declined. Currently, trade management is conducted through a quota system and physical…

title: Benchmarking Extended and Unscented Kalman Filters for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Charge Estimation against a Physics-Based Virtual Cell: Effects of OCV Flatness, Initial Covariance and Temperature
abstract: Kalman-filter state-of-charge (SoC) estimators are usually compared in simulations where the same equivalent circuit model (ECM) generates the data and runs inside the filter, and where errors are computed after the measurement update. Both practices flatter the estimators. This paper benchmarks Coulomb counting (CC), the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) against a physics-based virtual cell: an experimentally parameterised Doyle–Fuller–Newman model of a 5 Ah LG M50 21700 cell with lumped thermal dynamics. A second-order RC ECM is identified from a simulated GITT/HPPC test (2.7 mV RMS fitting error) and then used, unchanged, by all estimators. The cell is driven by repeated UDDS and US06 cycles from 90 % to 10 % SoC at 10, 25 and 40 °C and in an aged state, with 10 mV voltage noise, 25 mA current noise and a 50 mA current offset. Errors are computed from the a priori estimate so that the initial error is always counted. With a correct initial SoC, both filters keep the RMSE between 0.39 % and 0.68 %, while CC drifts to 6.7 % over a 6.9 h UDDS test. A 300-run Monte Carlo study without SoC-limit effects shows that the two filters converge equally fast from under-estimated starts, but the EKF is markedly slower from over-estimated starts: with the recommended initial covariance its mean convergence time into a ±3 % band was 166 s (maximum 1110 s) a…

title: Influence of Suspension Stiffness and Vehicle Speed on Passenger Vehicle Ride Comfort over Random Road Profiles
abstract: Ride comfort is crucial to passenger vehicle design because it affects occupant comfort, stability, and suspension performance. We developed a 7-DOF (seven-degree-of-freedom) spatial full-vehicle dynamic model in MATLAB/Simulink to investigate a passenger car’s vibration response to ISO 8608:2016-classified random road profiles. The spatial model represents coupling effects among the four suspension corners by accounting for vehicle-body bounce, pitch, and roll motions, as well as the vertical motion of the unsprung masses, unlike quarter-car and half-car models. The model is compared with simplified vehicle vibration models, and its capabilities are discussed in relation to recent full-vehicle models reported in the literature. The vehicle response is evaluated for road classes B–E, vehicle speeds ranging from 20 to 80 km/h, and suspension stiffness values ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 times the nominal stiffness. Ride comfort is evaluated using Root mean square (RMS), body displacement and vertical acceleration based on ISO 2631-1. Results reveal that road roughness affects vibration response more than vehicle speed. Raising suspension stiffness from 0.5 K to 1.5 K at 80 km/h on a class E road decreases RMS body displacement by 32.8%, while increasing RMS vertical acceleration by 43.8% (from 0.680 to 0.978 m/s2). These results show the inevitable trade-off between vibration isolati…

title: Continuous Terminal–Vessel Routing for Automated Ro-Ro Finished-Vehicle Handling: An OSM-Based Three-Layer Network and Level-Aware Bidirectional A* Search
abstract: Finished vehicles are loaded onto and discharged from roll-on/roll-off (Ro-Ro) vessels by drivers who choose routes from experience. Automated handling requires continuous routes between storage-yard parking positions and on-deck stowage positions in both directions. This study represents the storage yard, the quay connection and the vessel decks as a single directed network built from OpenStreetMap (OSM) data. The route cost adds fixed penalties for turns, level transitions and ramp use to the travel time, which is reported separately. Because these penalties dominate the route cost, a lower bound on the level-transition penalties is incorporated into the A* heuristic, and routes are computed by bidirectional A* with an average potential and a sum-based stopping rule. On the Gwangyang Port testbed, the method returned the optimal route for all 15,000 origin–destination pairs and reduced the search effort by about one quarter relative to Dijkstra’s algorithm. Unidirectional A* with the same bound achieved a similar reduction, indicating that the gain derives from the heuristic rather than from the bidirectional structure. Compared with shortest-distance routes, the cost-based routes contained markedly fewer left turns at almost no additional travel time and remained stable over a wide range of penalty values.
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: Power grid topology control
abstract: Power grids are facing major challenges from growing renewable integration and worsening climate impacts. While flexibility on both the demand and generation sides has been widely explored to address these challenges, network-side flexibility, especially in network topology, remains highly underutilized. Advances in communication, power electronics, and circuit breakers have made network topology increasingly controllable. However, leveraging this topological flexibility poses substantial challenges, primarily due to the inherent non-convexity and hybrid dynamics in associated optimization and control problems. This monograph surveys the development of power grid topology control in both early and recent years. It begins by discussing the fundamental topological constraints involved in topology control problems. Subsequently, it introduces steady-state topology control for transmission and distribution networks separately, covering fundamentals, a state-of-the-art review, and representative recent advances. Additionally, the network topology transition problem, which addresses the implementation of optimal topology solutions and has garnered increasing attention in recent years, is further modeled and analyzed. Beyond utilizing the flexibility of steady-state network topology, controlling network topology during transients can also contribute to system stabilization. Traditiona…

title: Hybrid Ion Guide with Continuous Electric Field Transition from Dipole to Hexapole Fields for Wide m / z Bandwidth and High Transmission Efficiency
abstract: Abstract Boosting ion transmission efficiency in the rough vacuum region is an important issue in atmospheric pressure mass spectrometry (API-MS). In this work, a hybrid ion guide (HIG) is proposed to enhance ion transmission efficiency and suppress the mass discrimination effect within rough vacuum environments. The HIG is constructed with discrete double-helix electrodes and a segmented hexapole assembly. Benefiting from the smooth continuous transition from the dipole field to the hexapole field, the device exhibits weakened fringe electric fields and superior ion-focusing capability. The central axial potential well of the HIG is shallow, which facilitates efficient transmission of low m/z ions. Fabricated via printed circuit board (PCB) technology, the HIG was integrated into a nanoESI-TOF-MS platform for experimental characterization. Experimental results show that at an RF voltage of 220 Vpp, the signal intensity ratio of caffeine ions (m/z = 195) to reserpine ions (m/z = 609) increases from 1.2% with the ion funnel (IF) to 43.1% with the HIG, demonstrating that the HIG has a wider m/z bandwidth. Moreover, relative to the discrete-double-helix ion funnel (DDH-IF), the HIG achieves improved instrumental sensitivity: the signal intensities of caffeine ions and reserpine ions are maximally enhanced by 2.2 and 4×, respectively. By realizing a continuous electric field transi…

title: Shaping the Electric Field: Overcoming Geometric Inhomogeneities in the Electrochemical Fabrication of Mesoporous Materials
abstract: Abstract Integrating porous systems such as mesoporous silicon (pSi) into reliable macroscopic devices for sensing, photonics and energy storage requires stringent control over their structural homogeneity. While radial variations in layer thickness and porosity are frequently attributed to edge sealing effects or pinned gas, the macroscopic impact of the electrochemical cell’s internal geometry is largely overlooked. Using pSi as a model system, we demonstrate that the insulating cell body acts as a significant field-shaping component. Combining 2D axisymmetric finite element simulations of the current distribution with spatially resolved near-infrared (NIR) spectrometry, we investigate distortions caused by standard cell features. We reveal that the internal container widening step, commonly used to accommodate counter electrodes, strongly compresses the electric field and generates localized, ring-shaped zones of accelerated etching. Optimizing this step height reduced the radial thickness deviation of a pSi layer 6-fold to just 2%. Furthermore, predictive simulations demonstrate that internal obstacles, such as stirring rods, can be deliberately positioned to either prevent unwanted current shadows or actively manipulate the current distribution for precise three-dimensional structuring. Ultimately, mindful hardware design that prioritizes spatial current distribution is a …

title: A Linguistic Pythagorean Fuzzy Decision Framework for Patient Satisfaction Improvement Strategy Selection in Hospitals
abstract: Patient satisfaction has emerged as a pivotal indicator of healthcare quality, yet the selection of effective improvement strategies remains a complex decision problem characterized by conflicting criteria, imprecise expert judgments, and inherent uncertainty. This study develops a novel multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework for selecting optimal patient satisfaction improvement strategies in a Pythagorean fuzzy environment. Five alternatives are evaluated against six patient-centered criteria. Linguistic assessments are collected from seven domain experts—a hospital administrator, chief physician, head nurse, quality manager, patient representative, healthcare academic, and IT/systems manager—and converted into Pythagorean fuzzy numbers. Expert opinions are subsequently aggregated using a Pythagorean fuzzy Aczel-Alsina weighted aggregation operator, which offers superior flexibility in modeling varying degrees of uncertainty. Criterion weights are objectively determined via the CRITIC (Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation) method, capturing both contrast intensity and inter-criteria conflict. The decision problem is addressed using a TOPSIS method incorporating a spherical distance measure for Pythagorean fuzzy numbers, which mitigates the loss of information associated with conventional distance metrics. A sensitivity analysis is conducted across se…

title: Marketing Mix Strategy to Increase Wedding Package Sales at Six Senses Uluwatu, Bali
abstract: The wedding industry in Bali is developing as a strategic opportunity for hotels to increase wedding package sales, but Six Senses Uluwatu, Bali experienced a decline in sales from 100 events in 2024 to 87 events in 2025. This study aims to analyze the 7P marketing mix strategy to increase wedding package sales. The study used a descriptive qualitative method. The population and numerical sample were not determined because informants were selected by purposive sampling, namely the Assistant Director of Wedding & MICE as the key informant and the Assistant Manager of Wedding & MICE and Wedding & MICE Coordinator as supporting informants. Data were obtained through unstructured interviews, observation, and documentation, then analyzed thematically using NVivo 15 through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results showed that Product, Place, People, Process, and Physical Evidence were the main strengths, while Price and Promotion and several operational aspects still had weaknesses. In conclusion, increasing sales requires the development of intimate wedding packages, strengthening sales calls, consistent digital storytelling, cross-training, simplifying the approval process, and preventive maintenance.

title: A reinforcement learning-enhanced collision avoidance strategy integrating motion planning and control
abstract: Existing automotive collision avoidance (CA) systems typically adopt a multi-layer architecture, separating motion planning and control due to computational complexity and differing optimization horizons, leading to potential conflicts and compromised safety in complex collision avoidance scenarios. To this end, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement learning-enhanced CA strategy that integrates motion planning and control processes. A cascaded nonlinear model predictive control (CNMPC) approach is proposed, employing high-fidelity nonlinear dynamics for immediate control actions and simplified linear dynamics for long-term trajectory planning. Additionally, a horizon-decreasing risk-weighting (HDRW) strategy is introduced to prioritize imminent collision risks, addressing the limitations of traditional model predictive control (MPC) in multi-obstacle situations. Furthermore, reinforcement learning (RL)-based adaptive control agents are developed to dynamically adjust the coordination strategy between the longitudinal and lateral inputs based on real-time road adhesion, enhancing the system’s environmental adaptability and robustness. Simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments under multi-obstacle CA scenarios with low and varying road adhesion demonstrate the proposed strategy’s feasibility and superior performance, ensuring safe and stable collision avoidance u…

title: Research on Sensor Layout Strategy Based on Inverse Finite Element Deformation Reconstruction Using an Enhanced NSGA-III Algorithm
abstract: Strain sensor placement strongly influences the accuracy and cost of deformation reconstruction with the inverse finite element method (iFEM). This study develops a common sensor layout for several loading regimes by coupling the four-node inverse shell element with a Lichtenberg-inspired local search embedded in the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (LA-NSGA-III). At a prescribed sensor count, the layout is optimized by simultaneously minimizing reconstruction residuals for multiple training loads. The method is assessed using DTLZ benchmarks and a plate example under equal objective-evaluation budgets, with separate controls for the multi-load formulation and the local search operator. Across 20 paired plate runs with 23 sensor sites, the proposed search reduces the mean joint training residual by 18.65% relative to NSGA-III, with mean displacement errors of 0.73% and 0.77% for the two training loads. Additional pressure, torsional and off-center force cases, a withheld combined load, strain noise, and sensor loss are used to assess a fixed layout under changing conditions. A cantilever plate test demonstrates strain-based displacement reconstruction, with laser peak displacement measurements used to calibrate the FE reference model. The method supports the offline design of a single sensor layout for iFEM reconstruction under multiple anticipated loading conditions…

title: PRICING STRATEGY OPTIMIZATION FOR TRADITIONAL SCENTED CANDLE PRODUCTS IN DIFFERENTIATED LUXURY GOODS MARKETS
abstract: Pricing strategy was a factor of competitive advantage in the markets for luxury goods in which product value, brand and differentiation are determinants of consumer’s choices. The approach may allow premium positioning and competitive advantage. This research investigates Pricing Strategy Optimization (PSO) for traditional scented candles, focusing on Consumer Price Perception (CPP), Brand Equity (BE), Sales Volume (SV), Customer Retention (CR), and Overall Market Performance (OMP). The research was carried out with 285 respondents from various fields including marketing managers, executives, and managers working in luxury candle companies. 5-point Likert scale structured questionnaires were distributed through online and physical mediums. Quantitative data were analysed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) 27 through descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and reliability analysis. It examined production costs, scent complexity, packaging exclusivity, and brand positioning as key pricing determinants. Results revealed positive correlations between pricing strategy optimization and overall market performance (r = 0.66), consumer price perception (r = 0.62), and brand equity (r = 0.58). Regression analysis indicated positive relationships with consumer price perception (β = 0.68), overall market performance (β = 0.65), brand equity (β = 0.62), c…

title: ASSESSMENT OF FACTORS INFLUENCING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CREATIVE AND INNOVATIVE SYSTEMS MODELING IN RETAIL NETWORKS
abstract: The article examines the methodological foundations for assessing factors affecting the effectiveness of modelling creative and innovative systems in retail chains. The relevance of the study stems from the digital transformation of trade, intensifying competition, and the need to align innovation activities with changing consumer expectations and environmental responsibility requirements. Under these conditions, particular importance is attached to a comprehensive examination of factors influencing the selection of modelling tools and information support for managerial decisions. The study aims to explore methodological approaches to assessing these factors, considering their interrelationships and the operational characteristics of retail chains. Its scope encompasses technical and technological, economic and managerial, social and communication, and environmental and institutional aspects of modelling creative and innovative systems. The methodological framework includes systems and comparative analysis, indicator normalisation, weighting, and composite assessment. Attention is devoted to selecting indicators, establishing their correspondence with the factors under examination, ensuring the comparability of heterogeneous characteristics, and using open information sources. The quality of primary data is also considered. Particular attention is paid to indicator aggregation,…

title: APLICAÇÃO DO MÉTODO PROPPAGA NA CADEIA DE SUPRIMENTOS: UM ESTUDO DE CASO NA ESCOLHA DE FORNECEDORES PARA UM COMÉRCIO VAREJISTA
abstract: A seleção de fornecedores é uma das atividades mais críticas para se gerenciar na cadeia de suprimentos, com o reflexo direto no desempenho das organizações. O problema de avaliação de fornecedores é versado como uma decisão estratégica que agrega valor à cadeia, bem como vantagem competitiva. Neste contexto, o objetivo geral deste artigo é apresentar a aplicação de um modelo multicritério de tomada de decisão, a fim de auxiliar no processo de seleção de fornecedores, facilitando o processo de tomada de decisão de acordo com suas exigências e necessidades. Para isso, realizou-se um estudo de caso com caráter quantitativo em um comércio varejista com pseudônimo “Mercadinho da Bia”, situado no Distrito Federal, mais especificamente no bairro de Santa Maria Norte. Foram selecionados oito critérios e estes foram julgados por meio do método PrOPPAGA, para avaliar cinco fornecedores. Ao fim da análise dos resultados, concluiu-se que o fornecedor F04 era o que melhor atendia os requisitos do comércio em questão, com o critério decisivo de localização. Desta forma, este estudo pode ser útil para que o referido comércio varejista formalize critérios de avaliação de fornecedores, de acordo com a sua capacidade de atender a estratégia de aquisição corrente, como também de disseminar uma metodologia capaz de sinalizar aos decisores caminhos mais adequados às especificidades de cada caso.

title: Impact of Promotional Insert Campaigns on Retail Sales Performance: An Empirical Analysis of a Local Supermarket Chain
abstract: Today, the retail sector is in a state of constant transformation. Sales promotion activities play a critical role in an environment where it is increasingly difficult for brands to boost their sales and strengthen their market positions. Insert campaigns are one of the most common and traditional methods among these activities, which can directly influence consumers’ purchasing decisions. This study aims to reveal the distribution of periodic campaigns by year, the product variety within these campaigns, the status of product prices before and after the campaigns, the sales volumes and rates of products included in the campaigns, and whether the campaigns affect the retail sector’s overall sales volume. For this purpose, the campaign performances of 125 products from 6 main categories and 31 subcategories included in 13 two-day insert campaigns conducted in 2024 were analyzed using data obtained from 10 local supermarket branches. The distribution of campaigns throughout the year can be considered an indication that the retail sector strives to maintain active year-round communication with customers. Although there is general product variety, it was observed that campaigns conducted especially in the initial and final months of the year included a wider range of products compared to others. The emphasis on products perceived as essential, ongoing, and non-deferrable needs in c…

title: Narrative Factor Extraction Using Large Language Models and Its Implications for Asset Pricing
abstract: Drawing on Shiller's theory of narrative economics, this article puts forward the "narrative-sentiment-pricing" (NSP) transmission mechanism and divides the transmission process from narrative to asset pricing asset pricing into three stages, namely narrative germination, sentiment diffusion and expectation solidification. Then, through non-diversifiability and heterogeneity relative to classical factors, it is argued that the narrative constitutes an independent source of systematic risk. At the factor construction level, this paper proposes a narrative factor (NARR) extraction method based on large language models (LLMs). At the level of asset pricing testing, this paper designs three testing paths. Incorporate NARR into the Fama-French multi-factor model for incremental information testing; place NARR under Merton's ICAPM framework to distinguish between rational hedging demand and behavioral deviations; and finally, introduce NARR into the stochastic discount factor (SDF) framework for a no-arbitrage test. The above paths jointly build a complete evaluation system to verify the independent pricing power of narrative factors, and also provide practical reference for subsequent empirical research on narrative factors.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: A feed-forward and fractional-order feedback control strategy for integrating and unstable systems
abstract: A feed-forward fractional-order control strategy employing a feedback loop is developed for unstable and integrating types of processes. The suggested method combines the proactive disturbance rejection capability of the feed-forward concept with fractional-order control, which uses fractional calculus to provide greater flexibility and improved controller tuning. The primary goal is to reduce the disturbances’ effect before they influence the actual process variable, resulting in better control performance, improved stability and more effective operation than conventional control schemes. The forward path control is analytically designed in such a way that it is completely decoupled from the design of feedback control (proportional-integral or proportional-integral-derivative). The proposed methodology provides a sufficiently fast and smooth set-point tracking response even in the presence of noise, disturbance and process parameter perturbations. The results presented in this study further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in achieving significantly improved closed-loop performance (smaller integral square error and integral absolute error) compared to the previous arts under both the nominal and perturbed conditions.
venue: Transactions of the Institute of Measurement and Control

title: Biocatalytic Valorization of Used Soybean Cooking Oil for Furfuryl Esters Production: Effects of Alcohol Feeding Strategy and Water Removal on Immobilized Lipase Performance and Stability
abstract: Abstract This study describes an efficient biocatalytic process for the synthesis of furfuryl esters from used soybean cooking oil (USCO). The process involves the hydrolysis of USCO using free Candida rugosa lipase, followed by solvent-free esterification of the resulting free fatty acids (FFAs) with furfuryl alcohol (FA) catalyzed by immobilized lipase Eversa Transform 2.0 (ET2.0). Five supports, including acid-treated rice husks with fine (FRH) and coarse (CRH) particle sizes, commercial and rice husk-derived octyl-functionalized silica, and poly(styrene-divinylbenzene) (PSty-DVB), were evaluated for ET2.0 immobilization by physical adsorption. Among the evaluated supports, PSty-DVB provided the highest immobilized protein loading (31.3 ± 1.1 mg g–1) and the best overall catalytic performance in furfuryl esters synthesis. Using this biocatalyst, FFAs conversion reached approximately 94% within 60 min at 45 °C under solvent-free conditions and with a slight excess of FA (FFAs:FA molar ratio of 1:1.15). The combination of stepwise furfuryl alcohol feeding and molecular sieves for in situ water removal improved biocatalyst operational stability, allowing the retention of approximately 95% of the initial activity after 15 consecutive esterification cycles. These results show that ET2.0 immobilized on PSty-DVB is a suitable biocatalyst for the solvent-free conversion of waste-der…

title: A Dual-Mode Electrochemical Aptasensor for Ochratoxin A Detection in Red Wine Based on a Target-Induced Displacement Strategy
abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA) is a mycotoxin of concern in wine and food safety, highlighting the need for reliable detection in complex food matrices. In this study, a dual-mode electrochemical aptasensor was developed for OTA determination in red wine based on a target-induced displacement strategy. OTA binding to its aptamer induces dissociation of the aptamer from complementary DNA (cDNA) pre-immobilized on the electrode surface, thereby altering the interfacial environment and enabling detection by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV). The sensor showed a semi-logarithmic calibration relationship over the experimentally tested OTA concentration range of 0.05–10 ng/mL. The estimated EIS limit of detection (LOD) was 0.018 ng/mL; however, this value was below the lowest tested concentration and was not experimentally validated. For DPV, 0.05 ng/mL represents the lower limit of the tested range rather than an established LOD. In spiked red wine, recoveries ranged from 94.6% to 103.9%, with relative standard deviations below 10%. The dual-mode strategy provides two readouts of the same target-induced interfacial change and offers potential for preliminary OTA screening in red wine with simplified sample pretreatment.

title: Meaning-Based Leadership, Intergroup Leadership, and Team Strategy Implementation
abstract: The core role of leadership in organizations is to motivate contributions toward the pursuit of organizational purpose—the reason the organization exists. This role comes into particular focus for overarching organizational initiatives, such as implementing organizational strategy. Motivating strategy implementation is notoriously challenging, however, because how to contribute to the pursuit of strategic objectives differs from team to team, and teams may struggle to see how they can contribute to such big-picture pursuits. We draw on meaning-based leadership theory to outline how meaning-based leadership (i.e., leader advocacy of the meaning that organizational purpose gives to team efforts) can stimulate the development of strategy understanding (i.e., shared understanding of how the team can contribute to efforts to put the organizational strategy into practice) and thus motivate team efforts to contribute to organizational strategy implementation. Recognizing that even when teams differ in how they can contribute to strategy implementation, their efforts are interdependent with those of other teams, we further propose that the effectiveness of meaning-based leadership in stimulating team strategy understanding is contingent on team intergroup leadership (i.e., leader advocacy of a team's interrelatedness with other teams). Thus, the indirect effect of meaning-based leaders…

title: Sustainable and Degradable Thermoplastic Polyurethane Library Derived from Bio-Based Secondary Diols via Single-Feeding Strategy
abstract: Abstract Traditional polyurethanes (PUs) rely heavily on petroleum-based feedstocks and are often prepared by a two-step process. Here, bio-based dimethyl tartrate (DMT) and isosorbide (IS) were used as chain extenders to synthesize biomass-based thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) library with poly(tetramethylene ether) glycol (PTMG) and diisocyanates through a single-feeding strategy. The obtained TPUs with tunable properties showed high number-average molecular weights of up to 43400 g/mol. DMT-based TPUs exhibited a single glass transition at −26 to 38 °C, while IS-based TPUs showed two glass-transition regions at −68 to 48 °C and 73 to 98 °C. Their initial decomposition temperatures reached 261 °C. The mechanical properties ranged from flexible elastomers to rigid plastics. DMT-based TPUs achieved elongation at break up to 2325%, whereas IS-based TPUs showed tensile strength up to 32.4 MPa. In addition, the DMT-based TPUs were degradable under alkaline conditions. These bio-based TPUs offer a promising route toward sustainable PU materials.

title: Hacia una estrategia de accesibilidad y visibilidad del patrimonio contemporáneo: análisis y diagnóstico del sistema de gestión de la información de Andalucía
abstract: Esta investigación se centra en el patrimonio inmueble contemporáneo ofreciendo un protocolo para el análisis y diagnóstico de los Sistemas de Información de Patrimonio Cultural (SIPC) con el fin de mejorar la accesibilidad y visibilidad. Para ello, el estudio revisa las experiencias en la documentación del patrimonio contemporáneo a nivel estatal y andaluz, aportando su contextualización internacional; realiza un diagnóstico detallado del SIPC andaluz desde la experiencia del usuario; genera un protocolo de cara a identificar las limitaciones de los SIPC en materia de información y funciones, y, por último, aporta estrategias para mejorar la accesibilidad y visibilidad del patrimonio contemporáneo tanto en los SIPC existentes como para los futuros.

A Survey on Computational Efficiency Optimization for Graph Neural Networks on Large-Scale Graphs
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become a dominant paradigm for learning from graph-structured data, yet their application to large-scale graphs remains constrained by three coupled system bottlenecks: memory, computation, and communication. This paper organizes the literature around a bottleneck-centric taxonomy that maps representative techniques, including Cluster-GCN, GraphSAINT, GraphSAGE, SGC, DistDGL, and AliGraph, to the specific constraint each primarily relieves. Three representative systems, GraphSAGE, Cluster-GCN, and DistDGL, are further analyzed as case studies and consolidated into a practical decision matrix linking graph scale, hardware budget, and structural properties to an appropriate strategy. The paper also identifies a largely unaddressed challenge: the shift toward high-dimensional, LLM-encoded node features, which is beginning to move the dominant bottleneck from computation toward memory bandwidth and I/O. The review concludes that current sampling and partitioning techniques remain vulnerable to long-tail bias, that reported near-linear distributed speedups depend on network conditions rarely disclosed in published work, and that the most promising direction for future systems lies not in a new algorithm but in adaptive schedulers that reconfigure strategy at runtime.

Agrobiodiversity dynamics in traditional socioecological systems: An agent‐based model approach on the role of kinship systems and variety transmission
abstract: Abstract Context : Agrobiodiversity depends on multiple interconnected socioecological processes. The loss of crop diversity represents a critical challenge for global food security and for the resilience and adaptation of small‐scale farming communities to climate change. However, the role of kinship and the transmission of variety in the formation of agrobiodiversity have not been systematically addressed. Objectives : Our objective was to examine how kinship and transmission of varieties influence the dynamics of the diversity of cassava ( Manihot esculenta) in traditional socioecological systems. Methods : We employed an agent‐based model to simulate the vertical diffusion of cassava varieties by considering different postmarital residence norms, variety of transmission rules and two marriage norms (Endogamy and Dual Organization). Results : The model successfully captured the expected loss of diversity over time, while also demonstrating that social norms slow down this process. We further showed that the interaction between postmarital residence rules and variety transmission consistently impacts diversity patterns between groups and clans. Conclusions : By showing how the transmission of varieties' dynamics shapes ecological outcomes, this work underscores the central role of human social institutions in sustaining agrobiodiversity. Moreover, our study highlights the imp…

title: Analysis of the Role of Agricultural Technology Adoption and Access to Financial Inclusion on the Development of Rural Areas in Indonesia
abstract: Rural areas in Indonesia support approximately one-third of the national population but continue to face challenges related to productivity, welfare, and infrastructure. Although agricultural technology adoption and financial inclusion have independently been associated with improved rural welfare, empirical evidence integrating both factors remains limited in the Indonesian context. This study aims to analyze the effects of agricultural technology adoption and financial inclusion on rural development and to examine the mediating role of financial inclusion in the relationship between agricultural technology adoption and rural development. A quantitative approach was employed using a cross-sectional survey of 300 smallholder farmers in several rural provinces of Indonesia. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model was assessed through indicator reliability, composite reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity using the Fornell–Larcker criterion and HTMT. The structural model was evaluated using path coefficients, bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples, R², and Q². The results show that agricultural technology adoption has a positive and significant effect on rural development (? = 0.312; p < 0.001). Financial inclusion also has a positive and significant effect on rural development (? = 0.458; p < 0…

title: Financial Vulnerability Among Swedish Young Adults with Self-Reported ADHD: A Secondary Analysis of Cross-Sectional Survey Data
abstract: The increasing prevalence of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in Western countries highlights the need to better understand its impact on everyday functioning, including financial outcomes. This study examines financial vulnerability among Swedish young adults with self-reported ADHD diagnosis. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among young adults (N = 2057). Group differences were examined between individuals with self-reported ADHD diagnosis (n = 149) and those without a psychiatric diagnosis (n = 1380). Logistic regression analyses assessed associations between ADHD diagnosis, financial health variables (financial strain, financial self-control, and financial literacy), and indicators of financial vulnerability, controlling for age and gender. Individuals with self-reported ADHD exhibited significantly poorer outcomes across all financial health variables compared to controls. In the multivariable analyses, an ADHD diagnosis was significantly associated with two of the three indicators of financial vulnerability, with higher odds of taking out consumer loans without understanding the terms (OR = 2.4) and having informal debt to friends or relatives (OR = 1.8). ADHD was not significantly associated with outstanding consumer loan debt for more than 18 months (OR = 1.5). Young adults with ADHD may therefore be at increased risk of financial vulnerabili…

title: A systematic review of avian influenza virus transmission models: Gaps and opportunities
abstract: Abstract Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) increasingly threatens wild birds, poultry, non‐human mammals and humans, yet gaps and opportunities in avian influenza virus (AIV) transmission modelling have not been comprehensively synthesized. We reviewed 182 articles published through 2025, categorized dimensions, including modelling approaches, data, host types, biological levels, spatial scales, temporal scales and model objectives, examined associations among these dimensions, and synthesized author‐stated limitations and recommendations. Statistical and mechanistic models dominated. Model data centred on population dynamics and demography, disease surveillance, host epidemiology and competence, meteorology and land use and land cover. Most studies focused on poultry or wild birds at regional spatial scales, seasonal/annual and multi‐year temporal scales, population or multi‐population levels, and were retrospective. Machine learning and decision‐making models were less common. Immunity, behaviour and life history, community composition, morphology, viral genetics and viral persistence received less attention. Non‐human mammals, individual and community biological levels, local and broader spatial scales, daily temporal scales and prospective modelling were also less frequently modelled. The authors frequently reported limitations related to data availability, su…

title: Climatic Conditions, Macroeconomic and Financial Dynamics, and Agricultural Performance in South Africa: Implications for Sustainable Development from an ARDL Framework
abstract: Climate conditions affect the macroeconomic and financial environment, which in turn affects sustainable agricultural development in South Africa. In this study, the short- and long-run relationships between agricultural performance, temperature, economic activity, trade openness, Consumer Price Index and financial-sector development are investigated using annual South African time-series data for the period 1972 to 2022 in an ARDL (Autoregressive Distributed Lag) model. The ARDL bounds test confirms a long-run equilibrium relationship among the variables included in the final specification. Economic activity exhibits a negative and statistically significant long-run association with agricultural performance (β = −0.7985, p = 0.0009). Temperature also has a negative long-run coefficient (β = –0.1119), but this is not statistically significant at conventional levels (p = 0.1212). In addition, financial-sector development has a negative, but marginally significant association with agricultural performance (β = −0.0032, p = 0.0589), whereas the natural logarithm of the Consumer Price Index (β = 0.3994, p = 0.0537) and trade openness (β = 0.0080, p = 0.0873) have positive, but marginally significant associations. The sign of the error correction coefficient is negative and highly significant (−0.4742, p < 0.001), suggesting that around 47.4% of short-run disequilibria will be resol…

title: Family Management Control and Trade Credit Utilization: The Influence of Financial Constraints and Supplier Monitoring
abstract: We examine how family management control affects trade credit utilization. We find that firms with family management control use significantly lower trade credit, reflecting both lower financial constraints and a stronger preference to preserve control. More importantly, we show that the effect varies across family firms, becoming stronger with deeper family involvement and under first-generation control. We also note that institutional ownership and competitive environment encourage greater trade credit utilization, whereas independent directors and nonfamily Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) exert limited influence. Overall, our findings indicate that substantive family control matters more than formal governance structures in shaping family firms’ short-term financing decisions.

title: How it all began
Research on the Characteristics and Dissemination Effects of Short-Form Video Content: A Literature Review Based on Cover Design, Content Style, and Video Duration
abstract: As the user base for short videos continues to expand and their commercial value keeps growing, how thumbnail design, content style, and video length influence dissemination effectiveness has become a question that marketing and communication studies need to address systematically. This paper employs a literature review approach to synthesize several representative empirical studies conducted in recent years on platforms such as YouTube and TikTok. It examinies the relationship between the visual attributes of thumbnails, content style, video length, and metrics such as view count, engagement, and completion rate. The review reveals that the emotional intensity, color schemes, and character portrayal of thumbnails, as well as trending elements and the emotional tone within the content, all have a significant positive impact on dissemination effectiveness. The role of content style is partially mediated through social media engagement. However, no consistent conclusions have been reached regarding the role of video duration, results vary across different research contexts, suggesting that this relationship may be moderated by factors such as content verticals. Future research could expand to domestic platforms, incorporate experimental designs, and examine the interactive effects of cover visuals and content style. These findings can serve as a reference for content operators, s…

title: The Monsoon Revolution and Limitations of Police Reform in Bangladesh
abstract: This article examines police reform undertaken in the aftermath of Bangladesh’s Monsoon Revolution of 2024. Drawing on 20 semi-structured interviews with law enforcement officials, legal professionals, journalists, civil society actors and academics, the article analyses policing practices before, during and after the uprising. The findings show that policing during the uprising largely reflected entrenched authoritarian practices, including excessive use of force, politicisation and systematic human rights violations, rather than a temporary institutional breakdown. While the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus articulated a reform agenda and established a Police Reform Commission, initiatives remained constrained by structural legacies, weak accountability mechanisms and limited political consensus. These initiatives for reforms signal intent but ultimately fall short of substantive democratic transformation, highlighting the lack of democratic policing in Bangladesh.

title: Large Language Models for Forecasting of Electricity Price Spikes
abstract: Can market notices read by a large language model (LLM) improve short-horizon electricity price spike forecasts? We study five regions of Australia's National Electricity Market. A local LLM extracted features once per notice, only notices visible at the forecast origin were used, and a gradient-boosting model produced onset probabilities. In an out-of-sample development back-test (July 2022 to July 2024), notice features did not lower the 60-minute Brier score of a numeric model including the market operator's next-hour forecasts. At 24 hours they did, but rule-based features did so almost equally and attribution to notice content was not established. A locally frozen protocol, not publicly deposited, governed a retrospective single-use holdout from 15 August to 17 October 2026. At 60 minutes, the hypothesis that LLM features lower the numeric model's Brier score was not established (H1; relative Brier skill -0.09%), so the planned comparison with rule-based features was not tested (H2). At 24 hours, the hypothesis that LLM features lower the score against a text-free control was not established (H3; +0.37%, 95% CI [-9.74, 1.39], inconclusive). By the frozen wording rule the non-significant 24-hour improvement comes mainly from recalibration and cannot be attributed to notice content, although post hoc the decomposition could not separate recalibration from resolution. The 24-…

title: Enabling vehicle-grid interaction through carbon credit trading for renewable energy integration in China
Day-Ahead Techno-Economic Optimization of a Grid-Connected VPP Considering BESS and EV Degradation Costs
abstract: This study investigates a day-ahead technoeconomic optimization framework for a grid-connected Virtual Power Plant (VPP) comprising electrical loads, photovoltaic (PV) generation, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and an electric vehicle charging station (EVCS). It addresses the complementary objectives of technical virtual power plants (TVPPs), which prioritize grid support and operational performance, and commercial virtual power plants (CVPPs), which focus on economic efficiency, by integrating both perspectives within a unified energy management framework. Day-ahead load and PV forecasts generated using long shortterm memory (LSTM) networks are incorporated into the optimization framework. The proposed approach accounts for BESS and EV degradation costs across different operating scenarios, enabling the assessment of their impacts on operating costs, peak grid demand, and techno-economic performance. The optimization framework evaluates three operatingscenarios: cost minimization, cost minimization subject to peakshaving constraint, and multi-objective optimization, whileaccounting for BESS and EV degradation costs for every case. The results indicate that incorporating degradation costs reduces net daily operating costs from €11,966 to €11,055 under cost minimization objective, from €11,648 to €11,522 subject to the peak-shaving constraint, and from €11,416 to €11,25…
