Application of long short-term memory and convolutional neural networks for real-time bridge pier scour prediction
abstract: Purpose Scour around bridge piers poses a major threat to structural safety, yet existing empirical and machine learning approaches are limited in accuracy, generalisation and real-time applicability. This paper aims to evaluate the effectiveness, efficiency and generalisability of deep learning models for real-time bridge pier scour forecasting. Design/methodology/approach The study formulates scour forecasting as a multivariate time-series prediction problem using real-world sensor data from monitored bridges in Alaska and Oregon (2006–2021). Multiple variants of long short-term memory (LSTM) and temporal convolutional neural network (CNN) models are designed and systematically evaluated. Random-search heuristics and sequential evaluation are used to optimise hyperparameters, improve robustness and assess computational efficiency. Findings Results show that LSTM models achieve high predictive accuracy for larger data sets, with a mean absolute error as low as 0.024 m for one-week-ahead forecasts. Fully convolutional networks deliver comparable accuracy with substantially lower training and inference times. Feature analyses indicate that historical scour time series dominate predictive performance, with flow-related features contributing only marginal or site-specific improvements. Research limitations/implications Model performance depends on data availability, noise levels a…

A deep learning-based method for enhanced prediction of long-term diaphragm wall deflections using multi-source data
abstract: Abstract Machine learning-based autoregressive models are widely applied to deformation prediction of braced excavations, yet they often suffer from pronounced error accumulation and deteriorated accuracy in long-term forecasting. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-source information fusion framework for predicting diaphragm wall deformation that integrates construction information with historical wall-deflection data. By incorporating construction-related dynamic features as auxiliary inputs, the proposed model effectively strengthens long-term dependency learning and reduces the propagation of autoregressive errors. A depth-weighted loss coefficient is further introduced to prioritize accuracy in shallow regions where deformation is most critical, and a 1D U-Net decoder is employed to enhance profile-level reconstruction through multi-scale spatial feature extraction. The framework is validated using two deep excavation projects on Nanjing Metro Line 11. For excavation-induced deformation, the model demonstrates stable and accurate multi-step prediction performance for diaphragm wall deflection, even under long forecasting steps. Comparative analyses further confirm that the proposed fusion architecture provides superior long-term robustness under limited monitoring data. The results highlight the method’s potential as a practical tool for deformation f…

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Next-Hour Prediction Using Three Meteorological Variables and Historical PM2.5 Data
abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) remains one of the most consequential urban air-quality hazards, yet forecasting its next-hour concentration accurately and transparently remains challenging owing to the non-linear, multivariate nature of pollutant-meteorology interactions and the black-box character of high-performing ensemble models. This study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for next-hour PM2.5 concentration prediction that integrates Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with a parsimonious set of predictors comprising three meteorological variables (air temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed) together with historical PM2.5 concentrations. Using 43,824 hourly observations from the Beijing PM2.5 dataset (2010–2014), lag, rolling-statistic, and cyclical calendar features were engineered, and model hyperparameters were systematically tuned through Bayesian optimization using the Optuna framework with the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator over 30 trials under a strictly chronological training validation testing split. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. The tuned XGBoost model achieved a root mean squared error of 16.50 µg/m³, a mean absolute error of 9.89 µg/m³, a mean absolute percentage error of 21.75%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.9478 on the test set, corresponding to reduction…

title: Artificial intelligence for early detection, risk prediction, and prevention-oriented decision support across diabetes-related disability pathways: A structured narrative review
Development and internal validation of prediction models for maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes in HELLP syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China
abstract: Introduction HELLP syndrome is uncommon but can cause serious maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). We investigated whether routinely available clinical and laboratory variables could support outcome-specific risk prediction. Methods We included all women with HELLP syndrome treated at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to June 2023. Five outcomes were modeled: placental abruption (PAB), posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and a severe maternal composite outcome. The primary analysis used repeated nested cross-validation in the full cohort. Missing-data filtering and imputation, predictor screening, model-family selection, hyperparameter tuning, and threshold estimation were performed within each outer training fold so that the held-out fold evaluated the entire modeling process. Candidate families were ridge logistic regression, elastic-net logistic regression, and random forest. A paired sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was conducted to assess the effect of replacing mean/mode imputation. Results Among 272 women, PAB occurred in 33 (12.13%), PRES in 23 (8.46%), PPH in 19 (6.99%), DIC in 9 (3.31%), and the severe composite outcome in 25 (9.19%). The corresponding AUCs were 0.715, 0.677, 0.833, 0.907, and 0.742. Ri…

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and clinical features for preoperative prediction of high-grade meningioma: a two-centre retrospective study
abstract: Background Preoperative identification of high-grade meningioma remains challenging using clinical and conventional imaging features. We compared MRI radiomic and clinical models and assessed whether their integration improved external discrimination. Materials and methods This retrospective two-centre study included 284 patients, with 227 used for training and 57 for independent external testing. Radiomics from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI), T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) underwent training-cohort screening, correlation filtering, and LASSO selection. The primary comparison assessed external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for joint-clinical versus clinical logistic regression (LR) models. Secondary comparisons assessed adding clinical predictors to joint imaging and combining sequences relative to T2WI. Bootstrap-based normal-approximation comparisons with paired resampling and Holm correction evaluated these three contrasts. Calibration, decision curves, and K-nearest neighbour (KNN) models were exploratory. Results The external cohort contained 48 low-grade and 9 high-grade tumours. All four imaging-only LR models had higher external bootstrap-mean AUC point estimates than the clinical model (0.663; 95% CI, 0.467–0.840). CE-T1WI yielded 0.863 (0.755–0.949), and FLAIR yielded 0.838 (0…

title: School leader coaching: building principal capacity in small, rural districts
abstract: Purpose Leadership coaching can help build the capacity of school leaders and support school improvement efforts. The purpose of this research is to describe how leadership coaching methodologies, grounded in traditional community building practices, change based on context and location. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual autoethnographic approach reflects on and explores how Community Learning Exchange (CLE) axioms were used as a framework to coach school principals in small, rural districts. The CLE framework shaped the interpretation of this experience by emphasizing the social, dynamic, and asset-based nature of learning and leadership. Findings Coaching school leaders in small, rural districts required an approach that incorporated building relational trust, collaborative problem-solving, contextualized coaching, embedding self in the community, and the identification of school and community assets. Originality/value Community Learning Exchange axioms have traditionally been used in settings to bring together communities and in classrooms to establish community among students. These same principles were reimagined and utilized successfully in two small, rural districts to build a foundation for improving schools.
venue: International Journal of Mentoring and Coaching in Education

title: Equivariance of the Source Measure Off the Pure Limit: Contact Sensitivity, Channel Capacity, and the Invariance of Selection Cost
abstract: This paper quantifies how partial sidechain cleavage affects the orientation sensitivity and alignment selection cost of stacking contacts in a self-separating substituted-chrysene stock. In the one-reagent limit where every sidechain is a hydroxyethoxy arm, the registration filter of the self-separating source reads the alignment of a stacking contact solely through the initiator, pricing the exogenous supply of alignment at one bit per contact. Extending this analysis to mixed arm words generated by partial cleavage establishes the exact magnitude of orientation sensitivity across operating regimes and demonstrates that the unconditional alignment price of one bit per contact remains invariant. The orientation sensitivity exhibits a sharp quadratic onset. Writing σ(π_h) for the probability that a contact drawn from the admitted stream is orientation-sensitive when each arm is cleaved to the phenol h independently with probability π_h, exact arithmetic shows that σ is a degree-8 polynomial with rational coefficients. At the uncleaved limit, σ(0) = f_I² = 2.47 × 10⁻⁷, arising solely from initiator pairs; the linear correction carries a coefficient of 9.40 × 10⁻⁶, while the quadratic π_h² term dominates with a coefficient of 4.00009. Across the three standard operating points of the separation process, partial cleavage increases orientation sensitivity over the pure limit by fac…

title: Aqueous Extract of Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) Tubers Exceeds Its Ethanol Fractions in Phenolic Content and Antioxidant Capacity
abstract: Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) tubers are used in Indonesia mainly as a source of inulin, recovered from hot-water extracts by ethanol precipitation, but how antioxidants partition during this step is unknown. A hot-water extract (AE) was compared with its ethanol-insoluble (EIF) and ethanol-soluble (ESF) fractions for total phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) contents and for 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) activities. AE had the highest TPC (214.9 ± 6.1 mg gallic acid equivalents/g) and TFC (159.7 ± 6.5 mg quercetin equivalents/g), the lowest IC50 values (DPPH 30.0 ± 0.8; ABTS 28.5 ± 1.9 µg/mL), and the highest FRAP (269 ± 42 mg ascorbic acid equivalents/g). EIF exceeded ESF in all assays except FRAP (p < 0.001), and antioxidant capacity followed TPC across nine determinations (DPPH IC50, r = −0.94). The inulin-rich precipitate therefore retains part of the antioxidant capacity of the tuber.

title: Ion-Conductive Elastomers with Enhanced Mechanical Performance and Electrical Conductivity via a Nano-Synergistic Transport Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Flexible ion-conductive elastomers have emerged as promising materials for wearable humidity sensors owing to their excellent stretchability and efficient ion transport capability. However, simultaneously achieving high ionic conductivity and excellent mechanical performance remains a significant challenge, primarily because the incorporation of high loadings of ionic components often induces solvation effects within polymer networks and compromises their mechanical stability. To address this challenge, we developed an ion-conductive elastomer with enhanced mechanical robustness and efficient ion transport capability by constructing a hydrogen-bond-anchored micro/nanostructured conductive network. Specifically, amino-functionalized SiO2 serves not only as a nanoreinforcing phase but also as a “bridging node” for ion transport through multiple hydrogen-bond anchoring interactions with polyurethane chains, enabling the formation of a continuous micro/nanoscale ionic conductive network while preserving the structural stability of the polymer matrix. The resulting ion-conductive elastomer exhibits high ionic conductivity (1.4 × 10–2 S/m), high tensile strength (2.17 MPa), and recyclability, achieving an effective synergy between mechanical performance and ion transport properties. Based on a humidity-induced ion transport mechanism, the fabricated flexible humidity sensor …

title: How does perceptual distortion occur? Unraveling the interference mechanism of environmental color in the perception of original colors of cultural artifacts
abstract: Color design within museum interiors constitutes a critical factor in shaping visitors’ perception of the authenticity of the original colors of cultural artifacts. Drawing upon multi-source qualitative data, including in-depth interviews and professional texts, this study employs grounded theory to exploratorily construct a theoretical model of the interference mechanism through which environmental colors affect the perception of artifact original colors. The findings reveal that optical-physical, cognitive-psychological, semantic-cultural, and emotional-value jointly constitute four core dimensions underlying such interference effects. At the physical level, environmental colors generate initial chromatic signals, which subsequently produce perceptual deviations through cognitive processing, trigger semantic reconstruction, and ultimately influence value judgments via emotional experiences. These dimensions may operate independently or synergistically, with cognitive processing and semantic association functioning as the central mediating pathways. The study provides an empirically grounded cognitive-psychological explanatory framework for understanding the dynamic relationship between environmental colors and the perception of artifact original colors, thereby offering theoretical support for museums to more effectively address the challenge of chromatic distortion in artifa…

title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles for intrauterine adhesions: from cargo and mechanism to product standardization and local delivery
abstract: Background Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) are being developed as cell-free regenerative products for intrauterine adhesions (IUA), but the translational literature is limited by inconsistent terminology, heterogeneous products, and predominantly rodent evidence. Main body This review integrates the inflammation-fibrosis circuit of IUA with reported MSC-EV cargo-target pairs, including galectin-1/JAK-STAT, miR-202-3p/MMP11, miR-543/N-cadherin, UBR4/YAP, and miR-340-3p/METTL3-HMOX1. It distinguishes direct uterine evidence from mechanistic extrapolation, discusses parent-cell source and culture effects, and evaluates collagen scaffolds, decellularized matrices, and injectable hydrogels as local delivery systems. Recent pooled animal evidence supports improvements in endometrial thickness, gland number, fibrosis, and embryo-related outcomes, but pregnancy-rate evidence remains uncertain. MISEV2023-aligned characterization, mechanism-linked potency assays, standardized dose metrics, biodistribution, and reproductive toxicology are essential before efficacy can be interpreted across studies. The trial landscape has also changed: an IUA-specific study of intrauterine hUCMSC-EV administration was registered in 2026, although peer-reviewed clinical efficacy data remain unavailable. Mechanistic claims are graded by whether primary experiments provide c…

title: Low-overhead trust mechanism for efficient cross-domain authentication in internet of vehicles based on blockchain sharding
abstract: Introduction To solve the problems of inadequate scalability, sluggish synchronization of authentication information, and high authentication overhead, an efficient authentication strategy based on a double-layer shard blockchain was presented for the cross-trust domain of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). A double-layer shard blockchain architecture was developed for multiple cross-trust domain message authentication by constructing blockchains on different entity levels in all domains in order to boost system scalability and provide secure and efficient cross-domain information flow. Methods A blockchain sharding technique based on the Metis graph partitioning algorithm for IoV was presented to increase the efficiency of syncing a large quantity of authentication data on the chain. This technique adjusts to the unequal distribution of authentication data on various road segments in the IoV and balances the burdens of each shard. A batch authentication method based on certificateless public-key cryptography (CL-PKC) was proposed, which reduced the authentication overhead of cross-domain messages by permitting batch authentication of communications from several trust domains. Results and Discussion The suggested technique successfully increases the authentication efficiency of cross-trust domain communications, according to experimental data. It decreases the computational overhe…

title: Preventive Health and Health Services Block Grant Flexible Funding Mechanism Is Associated With Improved Population Outcomes
abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives: To investigate the association between Preventive Health and Health Services (PHHS) Block Grant (BG) funding and population health outcomes. Design: A state-level panel data set (2000–2019) for 50 US states was compiled from USA Spending, PHHS BG administrative system, US Census Bureau, and America's Health Rankings. The long-term population health outcome was years of life lost (YLL), measured as deaths before age 75 years per 100 000 population. We used a generalized method of moments (GMM), along with a Koyck distributed lag model and a 2-way fixed-effects approach, to assess the impact of PHHS BG funding on YLL. We also provided several sensitivity analyses. Setting: This study examines the effects of PHHS Block Grant flexible funding on the population health outcomes during the period of 2000–2019. Participants: Fifty US States were included in the study. Main Outcome Measure: YLL before age 75, per 100 000 population. Results: During 2000–2019, a $1 per capita increase in PHHS BG funding was associated with a 1.5%–11% reduction in YLL (110–832 fewer years lost per 100 000 population). Conclusions: Increasing use of PHHS BG funds is associated with substantial years of life savings.
venue: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice

Nipa Palm (Nypa fruticans) Utilization: Implications for Blue Carbon and the Sustainable Bioeconomy – A Systematic Review
abstract: Background Nypa fruticans (nipa palm) provides ecological and economic benefits in tropical mangrove ecosystems but remains underrepresented in blue carbon inventories and bioeconomy policy. This review assessed its uses, carbon sequestration potential relative to other mangroves, and contribution to a sustainable bioeconomy. Methods A systematic review followed PRISMA 2020. Scopus was searched for “Nypa fruticans,” “Nipa Palm,” and “Nipah.” English-language, open-access journal articles published from 2016 to 2026 were screened in six stages using predefined criteria. Data were extracted into a structured database and analysed using bibliometric analysis and qualitative synthesis. Results Of 454 records identified, 175 studies were included. Research mainly originated from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with publication output increasing after 2019. Eight themes emerged: bioenergy; food and functional products; health and pharmaceutical products; materials; livelihoods and value chains; cultural ecosystem services; blue carbon and ecosystem support; and sustainability risks, including invasiveness. Mean carbon fraction was 42.48% (range 41.45–43.50%), while reported carbon stocks ranged from 7.26 to 38.10 Mg C ha −1 , below values reported for Rhizophora apiculata and Bruguiera gymnorrhiza. Nipa may contribute to carbon storage in degraded coastal areas and dense stands, w…

title: Heteroatom-doped carbon quantum dots for selective adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pharmaceutical contaminants in wastewater
Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses reveal effects of nitrogen deficiency on photosynthesis and carbon metabolism in wheat
abstract: Key message Combined transcriptome–proteome profiling revealed coordinated RNA–protein regulation of key photosynthesis and carbon metabolism genes in wheat shoots and roots responding to nitrogen deficiency. Abstract Excessive nitrogen application poses a significant challenge to sustainable agriculture. Exploring potential genes involved in photosynthesis and carbon metabolism holds promise for enhancing the nitrogen use efficiency in wheat and advancing molecular breeding efforts. However, the coordination between transcriptomic and proteomic responses to nitrogen deficiency, particularly those associated with photosynthesis and carbon metabolism in wheat, remains poorly understood. In this study, we analyzed transcriptomes and proteomes of winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) grown under normal (N1) and nitrogen-deficient (N0) conditions. We found that nitrogen deficiency reduced the fresh weight, nitrogen content of shoots and roots, as well as the net photosynthetic rate in shoots. Under the two conditions, we identified 3,949 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 164 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in shoots, and 3,911 DEGs and 129 DEPs in roots. Among them, 13 shoot and 26 root genes showed positive RNA-protein correlations (i.e., DEGs and DEPs were both up- or downregulated), while 1 shoot and 4 root genes had negative correlations (i.e., DEGs and DEPs wer…

title: Can digital infrastructure construction promote the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction? A quasi-natural experiment based on the “Broadband China” pilot policy
abstract: Abstract Digital infrastructure (DI) presents a critical opportunity for China to address the dual challenges of climate change and environmental pollution. In this study, we empirically investigate the effects and mechanisms of DI on the synergy between pollution and carbon reduction (SPCR) using balanced panel data from 273 Chinese cities during 2011–2023. The results reveal that DI significantly reduces CO 2 and SO 2 emissions, thereby promoting SPCR. The mechanism analysis shows that DI facilitates synergistic governance by limiting the entry of heavily polluting enterprises and increasing government expenditure on environmental protection. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the synergistic effects of DI are more pronounced in cities with small and medium size, high digital innovation capacity, advanced economic development, and greater government digital attention. This study clarifies the micro- and macro-mechanisms through which DI empowers cities to achieve SPCR, and provides empirical evidence and policy implications for improving DI construction and promoting urban green transformation.

title: Effect of Hydrothermal Treatment Temperature and Time on Carbon-Supported Pd Catalysts for Rosin Disproportionation
abstract: Hydrothermal modification of activated carbon has been recognized as an effective strategy to improve catalyst performance through pore structure limitation and metal dispersion enhancement. In this study, the effects of hydrothermal treatment temperature and time on carbon-supported palladium (Pd/C) catalysts were investigated for rosin disproportionation. Activated carbon derived from coconut shells was treated hydrothermally at temperatures of 180 - 200 °C for 3 - 5 h. The modified carbons were subsequently impregnated with palladium and evaluated in abietic acid disproportionation. The highest abietic acid conversion is 99.2% by catalyst prepared at 200 °C for 5 h. The nitrogen adsorption–desorption (BET) revealed that hydrothermal treatment significantly enhanced surface area and mesoporous structure, promoting uniform Pd dispersion. Improved catalytic activity was attributed to enhanced crystallinity, pore accessibility, and mass transfer. This work demonstrates that hydrothermal treatment is an efficient approach for developing high-performance Pd/C catalysts for biomass-derived resin acid valorization.

title: Fabrication of all-carbon micropillar electrodes for electrochemical glucose detection
A metabolic flux efficiency model reveals mitochondrial triage: H2S reallocates carbon skeletons to match cysteine under cyanide stress in rice
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) achieves comparable growth recovery to cysteine (Cys) in rice under cyanide (CN - ) stress, despite Cys being the direct substrate for CN - detoxification and driving a substantially higher assimilation rate via β-cyanoalanine synthase (β-CAS). This paradox implies a fundamental trade-off between immediate detoxification and long-term resilience. Here, we profiled tissue-resolved metabolomics of the TCA cycle intermediates oxaloacetate (OAA) and α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), and their cognate aspartate (Asp)- and glutamate (Glu)-family amino acids, the branches most intimately linked to CN - assimilation, together with transcriptional analysis of their biosynthetic genes. We then developed a Metabolic Flux Efficiency ( MFE ) model, a proof-of-concept framework that integrates these data to estimate relative flux efficiency within the TCA–amino acid (AA) cycle. H 2 S is proposed to execute a mitochondrial triage strategy, depleting root nitrogen reserves (Asn and Gln reduced by 92% and 67%) to liberate carbon skeletons, while boosting root α-KG (+93%) to sustain anaplerotic TCA cycle flux. The calibrated MFE model (Asp family: α = 0.39, β = 1.52; Glu family: α = 0.37, β = 1.64) suggests that metabolic conversion dominates over transcription in governing flux under CN - stress, and predicts that H 2 S redirects flow away from primary nitrogen assimilation (Glu→…

title: Decoupled regression rate and stability characteristics of carbon-black and aluminum-doped paraffin fuels for hybrid rocket engines
abstract: Abstract Hybrid rocket engines offer inherent safety and throttling by separating fuel and oxidizer, yet their wider use is hindered by low fuel regression rates and by combustion instabilities that frequently accompany performance-enhancing additives. This paper presents an experimental framework in which these two aspects are assessed separately on a single dataset. A campaign of 31 firings was conducted on paraffin-based fuels doped with carbon black (PC, 1 wt%), conventional micron-aluminum (PA, 14 wt%), and activated nano-aluminum (PAA, 14 wt%), all burned with gaseous oxygen. A covariate-adjusted equivalence analysis (ANCOVA with $$\log (G)$$ as covariate) over the tested flux range (31–71 kg/m $$^2\cdot$$ s) indicates that the three fuels are practically equivalent on average , with model-predicted mean differences inside a $$\pm 10\%$$ margin. This average equivalence is not uniform in flux: evaluated at a single representative flux of $$G = 45$$ kg/m $$^2\cdot$$ s, the fitted curve for PA lies about 13% above that for PC, just outside the same margin. In contrast to the regression-rate similarity, the pressure spectra separate the formulations, though less sharply than the regression data might suggest. Narrow-band modes are resolved in 28 of 30 usable records, and they fall into two tight clusters at $$224 \pm 17$$ Hz and $$414 \pm 16$$ Hz that recur in all three form…

title: Warehouse carbon emission of automation equipment’ using LCA approach: a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose The rapid commercialisation of automated warehousing spanning automated guided vehicles (AGVs), robotic arms and automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS) has significantly elevated energy consumption and carbon emissions across global supply chains. Despite growing policy attention and the adoption of standards such as ISO 14001, warehouse-level carbon accounting for automation equipment across its full life cycle remains fragmented and underdeveloped. This paper aims to systematically review existing literature on carbon emissions generated by automation equipment used in warehouse management system (WMS) processes, and to examine methodologies available for measuring CO2 emissions in both manufacturing and warehousing contexts, with a specific focus on the cradle-to-grave environmental accountability of automation technologies. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-aligned guidelines, covering 64 peer-reviewed papers published between 2001 and early 2026, sourced from Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science. Search terms were refined through expert consultation and industry discussions. An initial pool of 130 papers was screened against defined inclusion criteria relevance to warehousing sustainability, English-language peer-reviewed publicati…

title: Molybdenum-Catalyzed Reductive C–N Coupling/Cyclization Cascade for the De Novo Construction of N -Substituted Oxindoles
abstract: Abstract A simple and practical Mo-catalyzed method has been developed for the de novo and efficient synthesis of versatile N-substituted oxindoles via a reductive C–N coupling/cyclization cascade. This protocol features inexpensive starting materials, broad functional group tolerance, and is applicable to the late-stage modification or synthesis of biorelevant targets.

title: Rockfall risk management on transportation corridors: coupling risk assessment with terrestrial mobile LiDAR survey on the A22 motorway (South Tyrol, Italy)
abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated approach, coupling rockfall risk assessment with a vehicle-based surveying for the large-scale management of slope assets along transportation corridors. Rockfall risk was assessed qualitatively using relative rating scales. To reduce the subjectivity inherent in expert judgment, susceptibility was estimated through probabilistic methods, while vulnerability was informed by conventional runout simulations. Despite the associated uncertainties, the occurrence of a January 2024 rockfall within an area classified as high risk provides independent qualitative support for the consistency of the first-level screening results. Terrestrial Mobile LiDAR (TML) survey conducted from a car was designed to maximise effectiveness and efficiency in capturing rockfall-prone slopes and establishing a baseline for long-term monitoring. Its actual effectiveness, efficiency, potential and limitations were evaluated through a survey conducted in April 2023. Approximately 3.5 km of the A22 motorway, representing more than one-quarter of the analysed section, were found to be potentially exposed to rockfall risk, originating from 27 of the 55 identified potential detachment zones. The TML survey successfully detected over 70% of these zones, achieving a point density potentially sufficient to identify volumes greater than approximately 10 dm 3 . The scanning…

title: Enhancing phase retrievability of quantum channels via interferometric coupling
abstract: Abstract Phase retrievability of a quantum channel asks whether its output determines an unknown pure input state. We study how coherent interference can improve this property, using complementary channels and operator-valued frames. A formulation of the established pure state injectivity criterion using complementary channels yields dimension obstructions, including consequences for entanglement breaking and twirling channels. Our main focus is a two-arm interferometer, where coherent recombination produces port operators A i + e i θ B i . Their cross terms can supply input observables absent from both arm channels. We identify a necessary frame condition for pure state injectivity and construct qubit examples in which a coherent port is injective although every classical mixture of the same two arm channels is noninjective. To quantify robustness, we interpret the CP injectivity index as the sharp minimum Hilbert Schmidt separation ratio for state pairs. Its reciprocal controls sensitivity to errors in estimating the output. Positivity characterizes injectivity on all states and, for qubits, is equivalent to pure state injectivity. Exact calculations explain the phase dependent conditioning, distinguish minimum from average separation, and show how port success probabilities enter the interpretation of the indices.
venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical

Thermal Safety Frontiers in Electrochemical Energy Storage: Thermal Runaway Mechanisms, Intelligent Sensing, and Multiscale Suppression Strategies
abstract: Abstract With the continuous pursuit of high energy density in electrochemical energy storage systems, the thermal safety of lithium-ion batteries has emerged as a critical bottleneck restricting their large-scale application. This article systematically reviews the frontier advances in the field of lithium-ion battery thermal safety, innovatively establishing a comprehensive knowledge framework spanning from microscopic mechanisms to macroscopic system-level protection. First, it provides an in-depth analysis of the triggering mechanisms of thermal runaway and the cross-scale chain reaction evolution pathways, summarizing mechanism-based and data-driven modeling and prediction methods. Second, it focuses on real-time intelligent monitoring and early warning technologies for thermal runaway, constructing a full-process technical system covering “sensing-identification-warning”. In terms of cell-level protection, it systematically outlines the paradigm evolution of cell materials from traditional passive protection toward active-response approaches. Finally, it discusses thermal management and engineering protection strategies at the system integration level, summarizing the critical pathways for enhancing system safety design and failure response capabilities. This review aims to provide a systematic theoretical perspective for resolving the inherent trade-off between energy an…

title: Global classrooms: a tri-national study on AI integration by higher education students
abstract: Collaborative cross-cultural learning expands higher education students’ (HES’) intercultural and language awareness, enhances their intercultural competence, has an impact on attitudes towards technology and AI as well as towards the course design and general satisfaction with the collaborative experience in the course. Furthermore, their self-perceived role in a digital setting and their self-perceived English proficiency were measured. The CoGIH Project encourages HES to explore the educational potential of artificial intelligence (AI) for learning and teaching in the school setting. A special focus is on the impact AI might have on the language learning process in English as a lingua franca in a multilingual setting. N = 113 HES, including both pre-service and in-service teachers as well as students preparing for educational administration, from five institutions in Israel, Germany, and Hungary collaborated in 14 international groups, representing five higher education institutions; n = 91 answered the questionnaires. Each group investigated the educational potential of a specific AI application and developed an AI-supported, results-based webpage. The study employed a multi-method research design. Questionnaires were administered to the HES to investigate their experiences at the beginning and at the end of the course. While quantitative data were used to investigate the r…

title: Qi-Blood Harmony Formula mediates post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis: a multi-omics validation
abstract: Abstract Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Persistent myocardial fibrosis and dysregulated energy metabolism following MI contribute to adverse cardiac remodeling and are associated with poor clinical prognosis. Currently, no guideline-recommended therapy provides effective long-term intervention simultaneously targeting both of these core pathological mechanisms. The Qi-Blood Harmony Formula (QBHF), a classical Chinese herbal prescription, has demonstrated cardioprotective potential on attenuating fibrosis, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and restoring myocardial ATP levels in MI, yet its underlying mechanisms and therapeutic targets remain unclear. Using an integrated multi-omics approach in a mouse MI model, we showed that QBHF reactivated genes related to energy metabolism while suppressing pro-fibrotic pathways, as revealed by bulk RNA-sequencing. Non-targeted metabolomics further confirmed its efficacy in counteracting metabolic dysregulation. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that QBHF altered cardiac cellular composition characterized by reducing a major profibrotic fibroblast subpopulation and expanding a metabolically robust cardiomyocyte subset. Integrative multi-omics analysis identified the fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) as a central regulatory hub modulated by QBHF across bulk heart tissue, fibroblasts, …

title: AZƏRBAYCANDA RƏQƏMSAL ÖDƏNİŞ INFRASTRUKTURUNUN REGİONAL FƏRQLƏRİ VƏ ƏLÇATANLIĞIN QİYMƏTLƏNDİRİLMƏSİ
abstract: Tədqiqat Azərbaycanda rəqəmsal ödəniş infrastrukturunun regional bölgüsünü əhali və pərakəndə ticarət göstəriciləri ilə əlaqələndirərək qiymətləndirir. Məlumat bazasını Mərkəzi Bankın 2025-ci ilin sonuna ödəniş xidməti şəbəkəsi, Dövlət Statistika Komitəsinin 2026-cı ilin əvvəlinə əhali və 2025-ci il üzrə pərakəndə ticarət məlumatları təşkil edir, ölkə üzrə dinamika isə 2022–2025-ci illəri əhatə edir. On dörd iqtisadi rayon üzrə adambaşına təminat, terminal sayının əhali və ticarət paylarına nisbəti, sıralama dəyişiklikləri və seçilmiş əhatələr üzrə həssaslıq təhlili aparılır. Hesablamalara görə, Bakı ölkə POS-terminallarının 62,26 faizini, əhalinin 22,96 faizini və pərakəndə ticarət dövriyyəsinin 61,06 faizini birləşdirir. Hər 10 min nəfərə düşən POS-terminal sayı Bakıda 486,75, digər iqtisadi rayonlar birlikdə götürüldükdə 87,94 təşkil edir, ticarət həcminə görə normallaşdırma isə regional sıralamanı əhəmiyyətli dərəcədə dəyişir. Təmassız ödəniş qəbulunun regionlar üzrə payındakı nisbi səpələnmə adambaşına terminal təminatındakı səpələnmədən xeyli aşağıdır. Nəticələr əhali üzrə əlçatanlığın, iqtisadi tələblə uyğunluğun və texniki funksionallığın ayrıca izlənməsinə əsaslanan regional monitorinq sistemini əsaslandırır. Açar sözlər: rəqəmsal ödənişlər, regional əlçatanlıq, ödəniş infrastrukturu, POS-terminal, maliyyə inklüzivliyi.
venue: ENECO-Proceeding of Energy Economic Research Center

title: Adoption potential, timeline and implementation measures for bio-digital integration in South African construction: a modified Delphi study
abstract: Purpose Limited empirical evidence exists on the adoption potential, expected implementation timeline and measures required to support bio-digital integration in developing-country construction contexts. This study aims to examine expert perspectives on these dimensions within the South African construction industry. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory modified Delphi approach was adopted with 12 built environment experts. Adoption potential and expected timelines were assessed using categorical scales and descriptive statistics. Fifteen implementation measures were evaluated using a ten-point Likert scale and reassessed in a second round following controlled feedback. Consensus was assessed using median, interquartile deviation and percentage agreement, with mean and standard deviation additionally reported for Round 2. Findings The expert panel indicated moderate adoption potential and predominantly anticipated adoption within 6–10 years and beyond. Regulatory frameworks, circular economy principles and workforce training were among the most highly rated implementation measures. However, consistently high ratings across all measures indicate limited differentiation between their relative importance. A structured adoption pathway is proposed to support implementation. Research limitations/implications The findings reflect the perspectives of a small, predominantly acade…

title: Energy hardship in home-based palliative care: how augmented reality technology can play a role
abstract: Purpose Energy hardship is a critical, underexplored challenge and sometimes a barrier for patients who are residing and receiving palliative care at home. Unaffordable energy costs or interruptions to an energy supply can compromise clinical care of the patient at home, causing undue stress, and reduce their quality of life (QoL). This paper shares a viewpoint on how augmented reality (AR) technology applications can contribute in an educational manner. Design/methodology/approach This paper provides a viewpoint into energy hardship, its definition and indicators as well as an insight into the level of awareness and perception of energy hardship and current challenges faced specifically by palliative care patients. The paper investigates the capabilities of AR technology and how it can be used as an awareness and educational support tool relating to energy efficiency in the home and as an engaging educational method providing information on the user energy habits and energy saving tips. Findings We detail how a human centric co-creation-based approach can be applied to develop such useful AR applications to meet energy hardship challenges faced by palliative care patients. A synthesis of current Irish-based policy responses and interventions alongside forward looking recommendations provides an insight into how AR technology can be used as a means to raise awareness, educate s…

Continuity between Preschool and Primary Education: Integration of Pedagogical Technologies of the New Ukrainian School
abstract: The transition from preschool to primary education is a critical stage in a child’s development, as it is accompanied by a change in the educational environment, the nature of learning activities, the expectations of independence and approaches to pedagogical interaction. In the absence of coordination between the two levels of education, the competence-based and child-centered potential of the New Ukrainian School is implemented inconsistently, and the adaptive load is largely transferred to the individual child. The purpose of the study was to identify organizational, curricular, and pedagogical conditions for ensuring continuity between preschool and primary education; the analysis focused on pedagogical approaches, technologies and tools suitable for consistent application at adjacent educational levels. The study was conducted in the form of a structured thematic review of 30 scientific and analytical works and a comparative analysis of nine Ukrainian regulatory and methodological documents using an analytical matrix and thematic coding with the possibility of assigning one source to several categories. The analysis indicated that pedagogical continuity is formed through the interaction of three dimensions: organizational coordination, alignment of competency expectations and technological continuity. The Ukrainian regulatory framework generally supports alignment between …

title: Unlocking the potential for grid-interactive buildings through unified building automation system standards
abstract: Building automation systems (BAS) have revolutionized the way the built environment is designed, managed, and operated, improving occupant comfort and reducing costs. Yet after a century of incremental advancement, inconsistent building code standards are limiting the potential benefits of building controls and demand response. A standard approach to BAS deployment and operation can enable grid-responsive buildings that provide broader benefits to society through improved grid reliability, lower-cost electricity, room for load growth, and higher penetrations of clean energy. This study reviews the history of standards development in three adjacent sectors-building electrical systems, electrical grid systems, and computer network systems-and uses a comparative analysis of these industries to extract generalized lessons for the standardization of BAS and their interoperability with electric utilities. The comparative analysis yields a four-part framework for BAS standardization: strengthening the role of a governing standards body, incorporating BAS interoperability requirements into building codes, enhancing grid compatibility through utility interconnection requirements, and adopting common communication protocols to enable automated demand response. Examples show how these actions can overcome the challenges of vendor lock-in, closed systems, obsolescence, maintenance, cost, a…

title: Integration of Charged Peptide Amphiphiles within Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs) for Enhanced Targeted mRNA Delivery
abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) play a pivotal role in mRNA-based therapy; however, achieving targeted delivery remains challenging. We developed an LNP platform integrating peptide amphiphiles (PAs) to exploit their dual bioactivity and electrostatic tunability. Two PAs, cationic C16TAT (derived from a cell-penetrating peptide) and anionic C16HA2 (based on an endosomolytic peptide), were co-assembled into LNPs. In vitro, C16TAT/LNPs significantly enhanced mRNA delivery across multiple cell lines via improved cellular uptake. Due to the potent charge-modifying capacity of C16HA2, C16HA2/LNPs exhibit spleen-selective tropism in vivo, achieving >100-fold higher mRNA expression in the spleen than in the liver. While the commonly used surface-conjugated TAT-PEG-LNPs enhanced transfection in vitro, their in vivo performance was inferior relative to the C16TAT/LNP system due to the lack of stability, highlighting the advantage of PA integration. Critically, effective tissue targeting required substantial LNP charge alteration (pKa and zeta potential), which was achievable with C16HA2 but not C16TAT, likely due to the former’s higher aggregation tendency. Dual PA-PEG modifications may improve spleen targeting but required formulation optimization. This work establishes a simple PA/lipid co-assembly approach as a robust method for modulating LNP tropism, advancing the rational d…

title: Isotope-specific fractionation corrections improve doubly labelled water estimates of energy expenditure in mice
abstract: Abstract There has been debate over the appropriate equations for calculation of daily energy expenditure (DEE) in doubly labelled water (DLW) studies. Previous studies that have used tritium as the hydrogen label have generally not corrected for fractionation effects, while studies using deuterium generally have. Some validation data are available to support both positions, but as yet very little work has compared the different approaches in animals simultaneously injected with both isotopes. We compared the metabolizable energy intake (MEI) of mice ( Mus musculus , outbred MF1, n = 15) averaged over 5 days, to the calculated DEE measured on day 6 using the DLW method, for mice injected simultaneously with tritium, deuterium and 18 oxygen. This allowed us to compare in the same animals the validity of the contrasting equations. Using the deuterium data and the equations that correct for deuterium fractionation, the average difference between DEE and MEI was 0.6 ± 11.4%. Using tritium data and equations that account for tritium fractionation, the average difference was 1.2 ± 11.6%. The discrepancy was greater if fractionation effects were ignored. Using the deuterium data, the discrepancy averaged 2.5 ± 11.4% and using the tritium data it averaged 3.7 ± 11.7%. Applying the tritium data in the equations that correct for deuterium fractionation resulted in an intermediate discrep…

title: Precision Social Medicine: Bridging the Gap Between Social Care and Health Systems Integration
abstract: Health systems serving children have increasingly invested in social care initiatives, yet these programs frequently demonstrate inconsistent effectiveness and face challenges in sustainability and scalability. Precision social medicine (PSM) offers a framework for addressing this gap by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models to match social care interventions to patients’ clinical and social context. This article presents a practical, 3-step approach for operationalizing PSM within health systems serving children. These steps are to (1) codefine precision in social care with patients and frontline staff, (2) translate that definition into an AI/ML-informed strategy for identifying risk and assigning services, and (3) test the approach in workflows before it impacts care. We highlight integrating such a framework using pediatric asthma as a case example, tailored for the pediatric hospitalist managing the transition from hospital to home.

abstract: The study was designed, synthesised, characterized, and evaluated by using MTT Assay as a potential anticancer agent, new Saccharin-7-Sulphonamide derivatives will be tested on human Neuroblastoma SY5Y cancer cell lines. These are potential anticancer agents that target the Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase receptor. As part of the computational design process, a variety of software tools were used to generate the structural models for the synthesized compounds, including Chemsketch, Swiss ADME, Molinspiration, OSIRIS property explorer, and PyRx. According to Lipinski rule predictions made using Swiss ADME, the properties of the Lipinski rule are not violated. As part of the assessment of the effectiveness of the synthesized compounds as anticancer agents, molecular docking studies were conducted with ALK, which demonstrated promising binding affinities between the synthesized compounds and ALK molecules. There was a determination and characterization of the percentage yield, molecular formula, solubility, melting point, appearance, and molecular formula of the compounds that were investigated. In order to confirm the purity, TLC was used and Rf values were calculated to determine the purity. It was further characterized by IR, NMR, and Mass spectroscopy in order to determine the nature of the compound. It has been demonstrated that all synthesized compounds exhibit anti-cancer activi…

title: Critical behavior, variable range hopping, and probable topological Hall effect in VCr2Te4 single crystal
abstract: Chromium tellurides are taken as a board for probing nontrivial spin interactions. Besides changing the Cr/Te ratio or dimension, doping can also tune the physical properties of these compounds. However, only magnetic properties of doped chromium tellurides polycrystalline have been reported, and physical properties of heteroatom-substituting chromium-tellurium single crystals are few. Here, we prepared VCr2Te4 single crystals and studied the electrical transport, magnetic properties, and Hall effect of the single crystals. VCr2Te4 displays perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and a ferrimagnetic-to-paramagnetic transition at ∼74 K. Magnetic critical exponents β = 0.446(2) with TC = 74.512(1) K and γ = 1.081(2) with TC = 74.526(1) K are obtained from the Arrott–Noakes equation of states with long-range interactions between spins that decay as J(r) ≈ r−4.638, indicating intricate magnetic interactions in the VCr2Te4 single crystal. The sample shows a semiconductor-like behavior above 100 K due to variable range hopping. VCr2Te4 has n-type carriers and a larger anomalous Hall conductivity σxy ∼ 104 Ω−1 cm−1 at 3 K. Based on scaling analysis, the anomalous Hall effect mechanism is the skew scattering. A topological Hall effect can be observed up to 20 K due to the noncoplanar spin configuration. Our results reveal the interesting physical properties in VCr2Te4 single crystals and giv…

title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversati…

title: From risk management to AI-enabled governance: five intellectual orientations in EPC and infrastructure project risk governance
abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesise the intellectual development of engineering–procurement–construction and infrastructure project risk governance and examine whether bibliometric evidence supports five overlapping intellectual orientations. Design/methodology/approach The study combined bibliometric analysis with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and a scripted workflow to examine 173 Scopus-indexed publications (1999–2026). The analytical corpus was derived through relevance validation of 678 candidate records, with provenance checked against an 801-row master ledger. Fifteen provisional 2026 records were excluded from temporal comparisons. Findings The analysis identified five orientations: risk analysis and control (53 documents), performance and overrun (80), governance and relational mechanisms (52), digital information integration (7) and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support (18). The share of period publications addressing performance and overrun increased from 34.7 % in 1999–2018 to 59.7 % in 2023–2025, whereas the digital and AI orientations remained comparatively limited. These patterns concern the published literature and do not establish organizational maturity or realised capability. Research limitations/implications Scopus coverage, title/abstract-based relevance validation, citation lag, analytical thresholds and interpretive coding delimit…

title: Conserved and species-specific guard cell transcriptional responses and drought physiology in Arabidopsis and tomato
abstract: Crop productivity is severely threatened by climate change-related stresses, including drought stress. During drought, physiological and transcriptional changes occur in guard cells to regulate stomatal closure and minimize excess water loss. Tomato is an important crop species in temperate regions, with a high water requirement. To further understand the drought response in tomato, we performed RNA-seq on guard cell-enriched samples of plants subjected to severe drought stress. We investigated drought-responsive changes in gene expression and alternative splicing, including the role of ABA signaling genes. Comparing this data to previous work on the model species Arabidopsis thaliana , we highlighted an increased level of transcriptional reprogramming in tomato. These differences translated to the physiological level, where we observed earlier stomatal closure during progressive drought in tomato compared to A. thaliana using thermal imaging. Overall, this study sheds new light on tomato GCs during drought, and emphasizes the importance of translational studies on crop species.

title: Adult plant resistance genes in wheat: mechanisms, interactions, and breeding strategies for durable rust resistance
abstract: Abstract Wheat stem rust, stripe rust and leaf rust pose severe threats to global wheat production. While chemical control becomes increasingly limited by fungicide resistance, genetic resistance remains the most economical and sustainable management strategy. Adult plant resistance (APR) has been widely deployed to protect wheat crops and herein six wheat APR loci that have been cloned and/or extensively used are considered. Four of these loci i.e., Lr34/Yr18/Sr57/Pm38/Ltn1 , Lr67/Yr46/Sr55/Pm46/Ltn3 , Lr46/Yr29/Sr58/Pm39/Ltn2 and Sr2/Yr30/Lr27/Pm70/Pbc1 provide broad-spectrum protection against rust and powdery mildew pathogens while the remaining two, Yr36 and TaEDR2 , provide stripe rust resistance only. Each APR locus confers partial, slow rusting resistance in post seedling plants and is generally insufficient by itself to provide effective levels of disease protection. However, the protection provided by these loci is not race-specific and can also be highly durable, with the Lr34/Yr18/Sr57/Pm38/Ltn1 , Lr46/Yr29/Sr58/Pm39/Ltn2 and Sr2/Yr30/Pm70/Lr27/Pbc1 loci having been widely deployed for many decades without being overcome. In some instances, these APR loci act additively with each other as well as with all-stage resistance genes to confer higher levels of disease protection. The mechanistic basis of APR is not well understood, however causative genes for four of thes…

abstract: งานวิจัยนี้ศึกษาแอคติโนมัยซีทส่งเสริมการเจริญของพืชจากดินรอบรากข้าวใน 6 อำเภอของจังหวัดพระนครศรีอยุธยา เพื่อเป็นแนวทางในการใช้จุลินทรีย์ทดแทนสารเคมีและเพิ่มมูลค่าผลผลิต จากการคัดแยกแอคติโนมัยซีท 111 ไอโซเลท พบไอโซเลทที่ละลายฟอสเฟต ผลิตกรดอินโดลอะซิติก (IAA) และเจริญบนอาหารไร้ไนโตรเจนจำนวน 24, 106 และ 66 ไอโซเลท ตามลำดับ ไอโซเลท RS5A07 มีดัชนีละลายฟอสเฟตสูงสุด (2.46±0.05) พร้อมทั้งสร้าง IAA และเจริญบนอาหารไร้ไนโตรเจนได้ และไอโซเลท RS4A07 เจริญเติบโตเร็วและผลิต IAA ได้สูง (35.03±0.74 ไมโครกรัมต่อมิลลิลิตร) จากการวิเคราะห์ยีน 16S rRNA ระบุว่า RS5A07 และ RS4A07 คล้ายคลึงกับ Streptomyces viridiviolaceus (99 เปอร์เซ็นต์) และ Saccharopolyspora endophytica (99 เปอร์เซ็นต์) ตามลำดับ การทดสอบประสิทธิภาพการส่งเสริมการเจริญของข้าวแบ่งเป็น 4 กลุ่ม ได้แก่ กลุ่มควบคุม (ไม่เติมหัวเชื้อ) กลุ่มเติม RS5A07 กลุ่มเติม RS4A07 และกลุ่มเติมหัวเชื้อผสม (105 โคโลนีต่อมิลลิลิตร ปริมาตร 200 มิลลิลิตร ทุก 15 วัน) พบว่าหลังปลูก 26 วัน ข้าวกลุ่มเติมหัวเชื้อมีอัตราการเติบโตสูงกว่ากลุ่มควบคุม หลัง 50 วันกลุ่มเติมหัวเชื้อผสมมีความยาวรากมากที่สุดอย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติ แต่ทุกกลุ่มทดลองไม่พบความแตกต่างอย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติในด้านความยาวต้น น้ำหนักสดและแห้งของลำต้นและราก รวมถึงปริมาณคลอโรฟิลล์ ดังนั้น แอคติโนมัยซีทจากการศึกษานี้ยังไม่สามารถเพิ่มอัตราการเจริญของต้นข้าวในระยะ 50 วันได้ แต่การใช้จุลินทรีย์หลายสายพันธุ์สามารถเพิ่มความยาวรากได้ ซึ่งจำเป็นต้องเพิ่มระยะเวลาในการศึกษา และปรับรูปแบบการใช้หัวเชื้อร่วมด้วย

Microbiome-mediated effects of Bacillus subtilis inoculants on rice straw decomposition, residue chemistry, and nutrient release in double-cropping paddy fields
abstract: Returning rice straw to fields is key for sustainable agriculture, yet its slow decomposition conflicts with tight schedules in double-cropping rice systems. Whether laboratory-effective microbial inoculants can consistently enhance straw decomposition and nutrient turnover in the field remains unclear. We conducted a two-season field experiment using nylon-mesh bags that prevented direct mixing of straw from soil-applied inoculants (laboratory-developed decomposing inoculant, LABIN; conventional commercial decomposing inoculant, COMIN, both Bacillus subtilis-based), thereby evaluating their primarily indirect effects via stimulation of the indigenous soil microbiome. Neither inoculant significantly increased net dry matter loss in either season ( p >0.05). However, LABIN exerted profound effects on nutrient release dynamics, it markedly elevated phosphorus release in the late-season period and persistently drove greater lignin degradation as well as unique structural alterations within straw residues, which was verified via Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). LEfSe analysis identified enrichment of putative decomposer taxa such as Vicinamibacter and Candida tropicalis , without affecting alpha diversity. Collectively, these results indicate that LABIN did not accelerate overall mass loss under conditions of limited direct inoculant–straw contact. Nevertheless, i…

The Digital Divide in Global Communication: Inequality, Governance, and the Contest for Narrative Power
abstract: The spread of information and communication technologies has made connectivity central to global communication, yet the benefits of this transformation are distributed unequally. This article examines the digital divide as a structural feature of contemporary global media rather than a mere gap in hardware access. Drawing on scholarship that treats the divide as a complex and dynamic phenomenon, it argues that the divide operates on at least three intersecting levels: access, usage and skill, and algorithmic and infrastructural power. It then traces how the divide is deepened by the politics of platform governance and by asymmetric control over digital content, and considers how these asymmetries become acute in armed conflict, where the ability to generate, moderate, and frame information is itself a weapon. The article concludes that bridging the divide requires not only connectivity and digital literacy but a redistribution of the power to produce and govern the global media environment.

title: Harnessing genotype × environment interactions and multi-trait selection indices to identify nutritionally superior pearl millet accessions from global PMiGAP germplasm
abstract: Abstract Background Pearl millet is a climate-resilient and nutrient-dense cereal with immense potential to alleviate micronutrient malnutrition. However, the development of nutritionally superior and stable cultivars is challenged by the complex inheritance of nutritional traits and their strong genotype × environment interactions. Results In the present study, 218 pearl millet genotypes were evaluated across four environments for grain nutritional quality, anti-nutritional factors, and seed yield per plant. Multi-trait genotype selection was performed using the MTSI, followed by stability assessment using AMMI, ASV, GSI, WAASB, BLUP, and GGE biplot analysis. Factor analysis grouped the seven traits into five latent factors and predicted favourable selection gains for Fe (26.38%), Zn (9.81%), P (4.94%), and seed yield per plant (1.38%), while reducing the anti-nutritional traits, total tannin content (TTC; -16.36%) and phytic acid content (PAC; -0.78%). A modest negative response was observed for Mn (-6.89%), reflecting a trade-off under simultaneous multi-trait selection. Broad-sense heritability was high for all traits (0.83–0.99). Combined ANOVA revealed highly significant effects of genotype, environment, and G×E interaction for all traits. Based on MTSI values, 33 superior genotypes were shortlisted for detailed stability analysis. BLUP analysis identified G158 as the bes…

title: High-pyrolysis-temperature acidified straw biochar improves soil hydrological functioning and increases maize yield in saline soils
abstract: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mechanisms by which acid-modified maize straw biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures regulates the hydrological properties of saline soils remain unclear. In this study, a four-year soil amendment experiment was conducted in moderately saline soils of the Hetao Irrigation District in China to evaluate the effects and underlying mechanisms of acidified biochar produced at three pyrolysis temperatures (C1: 300 °C, C2: 500 °C, and C3: 700 °C) and applied at two rates (T1: 10 Mg ha - ¹ and T2: 20 Mg ha - ¹) on soil hydrological properties. The results showed that: (1) application of acidified biochar significantly decreased soil salinity, pH, and bulk density, while increasing soil water content and organic matter. Moreover, it markedly enhanced crop yield and biomass; (2) acidified biochar markedly improved soil hydrological properties (0–40 cm), with the C3T1 treatment performing best, increasing soil saturated water-holding capacity, field capacity, soil water storage, and saturated hydraulic conductivity by 17.35%, 27.91%, 14.31%, and 26.92%, respectively; (3) Principal component analysis (PCA) and Mantel test results indicated tha…

title: Physiological responses of early-season rice to simulated root damage from mechanical transplanting
abstract: Yield loss from mechanical transplanting in early-season rice is often attributed to root damage, yet the physiological mechanism remains poorly understood. A two-year field experiment was conducted in early-season rice with two varieties (Lingliangyou 211, hybrid; Zhongzao 39, conventional inbred) under three root damage treatments: no damage (CK), mild (roots trimmed to 2 cm, T1), and severe (roots trimmed to 1 cm, T2). Root regeneration, leaf water status, antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT), malondialdehyde (MDA), soluble protein, and PSII maximum quantum yield (Fv/Fm) were measured at 1, 3, 5, and 7 days after transplanting in 2022, whereas grain yield and yield components were evaluated in both 2021 and 2022. Results showed that T2 reduced grain yield by 8–9% across both years, whereas T1 had no significant effect. The two varieties exhibited consistent physiological responses to root damage. Both T1 and T2 stimulated compensatory new root proliferation, with significantly higher new root numbers at days 5–7 relative to CK. However, T2 induced sustained oxidative stress, as indicated by elevated MDA in roots throughout the recovery period and in leaves from day 5 onward. In contrast, T1 caused only a transient increase in root MDA. T2 reduced Fv/Fm by 23–26%, pre-heading biomass production by 13%, and highest tiller number by 10–21%. Conversely, T1 maintained al…

title: Disentangling environmental, irrigation, and clone effects on the cacao soil microbiome in a multi-location trial
abstract: Introduction Plant-associated microbiomes can shape host phenotypes, yet plant breeding programs rarely incorporate microbiome data into their selection criteria. For example, multi-location trials are central for studying genotype-by-environment interactions, yet the microbiome is a poorly characterized component of environmental variation. Methods This study sought to better understand effects of region, irrigation and nutrient management, and scion on variation in the cacao-associated soil microbiome within a multi-location breeding trial. Samples were sent for amplicon sequencing from four regions of Brazil and represented two cocoa scions and an irrigation trial comparing drip-irrigated and rainfed plots. Results Samples clustered by region for both prokaryotes and fungi, though the effects were not significant due to low statistical power and differences in multivariate dispersion. A conserved core microbiome was identified that included a complete prokaryotic nitrogen-cycling functional core as well as two omnipresent fungal ASVs belonging to the genus Fusarium . Irrigation and nutrient management explained 13% of fungal beta diversity and affected the relative abundance of 156 irrigation-responsive taxa across taxonomic levels. Depletion of irrigation-sensitive prokaryotes was linked to lower alpha diversity in drip-irrigated/fertigated plots relative to rainfed plots r…

title: Power Storage with Pumped-Hydro Storage Systems in the Island of Crete, Greece. A PESTEL Analysis
abstract: The deployment of pumped-hydro storage (PHS) systems in the island of Crete, Greece allows the higher integration of the abundant renewable energies of the island into the electric grid increasing its stability and quality. Pumped-hydro storage is broadly used worldwide for energy storage having many advantages compared with other energy storage technologies. The clean energy transition in Crete requires the higher use of solar and wind energy for power generation while power storage is necessary for integrating intermittent energy sources, like solar and wind energy, into the grid. A Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental and Legal (PESTEL) analysis regarding the development of PHS systems in Crete has been conducted. The external factors affecting their deployment have been analyzed. It has been indicated that the Greek and EU policies regarding the promotion of renewable energies and the mitigation of climate change affect their deployment in Crete. Additionally, the acceptance of PHS systems from local communities, the increase of local employment and the public concern about water availability as well as the maturity and reliability of PHS technology, the good morphological characteristics in Crete affect the deployment of PHS systems in the island. Finally, the impacts of PHS systems on natural ecosystems, landscapes, natural habitats, water resources a…

title: Assessing acceptability, feasibility, and utilization in a peer-to-peer tele-critical care model: a mixed-methods analysis to inform scalable remote ICU models
abstract: Abstract Introduction Critical care in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Pakistan, particularly in remote areas, is constrained by limited infrastructure and expertise. Telemedicine can bridge this gap by connecting frontline ICU physicians with remote critical care experts. While tele-ICU models have been evaluated in high-income settings, limited evidence exists from LMICs. This study evaluated the acceptability, feasibility, and utilization of a peer-to-peer tele-ICU consultation service launched by Aga Khan University in Pakistan. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods study using 145 survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews of physicians who had utilized a national Tele-ICU consultation service. Quantitative data were collected using a structured survey. Qualitative data were obtained through open-ended survey responses and 10 in-depth interviews. Survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis by two independent reviewers to identify key themes related to service use, quality, and feasibility. Results Of 219 physicians, 145 (66.2%) responded. Consultations primarily occurred via voice (77.2%) and text (43.4%). Respondents reported high satisfaction across clinical (mean 4.50), process (3.82), and technical (4.18) domains. Key benefits included knowledge enhancement, support for complex …

title: Peer Assessment of Item Relevance in Mathematics Ability Test Instruments Designed by Mathematics Education Students: A Gregory Coefficient Approach
abstract: Designing test items that are relevant to their intended indicators is a core competency for prospective researchers and mathematics educators, yet empirical evidence from peer assessments of student-designed instruments remains limited. This study examined item–indicator relevance in mathematics ability test instruments developed by mathematics education students using peer assessment and the Gregory coefficient. A descriptive quantitative approach with a document-analysis design was employed, involving 15 constructed-response test instruments comprising 150 items assessed by two peers. Relevance ratings on a four-point scale were analyzed using the Gregory technique, descriptive statistics, and categorical agreement percentages in Microsoft Excel. The mean Gregory coefficient across instruments was 0.91; ten instruments achieved coefficients of 1.00, and twelve had coefficients ≥ 0.80. For the nine instruments with traceable item-level scores, the analysis covered 180 ratings, of which 77% were assigned the maximum score of 4. The mean rating was 3.76, and categorical agreement was 96.7%. For the remaining six instruments, coefficients were available only in student summary tables, with a mean of 0.83. The analysis also identified discrepancies between rating sheets and summaries, identical summaries, and misinterpretations of the coefficient. Although peer assessment provide…

title: The School-Bell Flywheel: peer reconvening and the delayed youth breakout of “Golden”
abstract: Purpose Diffusion models used in strategic marketing planning do not specify how calendar-driven transitions in peer-network density govern adoption timing among youth demographics, which may lead managers to withdraw support before conversion windows open. This study aims to introduce the School-Bell Flywheel, referred to as the BELL framework, which comprises four sequential processes: Build a Reservoir, Energize Rituals, Lift into Households, and Leverage Platforms. The framework aligns marketing resource allocation with network state transitions. Design/methodology/approach The study develops theory through integration of complex contagion theory, media richness theory and consumer socialization research, using an in-depth illustrative anchor case (Netflix’s KPop Demon Hunters and the delayed breakout of its song “Golden”) with a corroborating illustration from Disney’s Encanto. Findings The study proposes that summer visibility converts to mainstream adoption when reconvening peer networks enable crossing complex contagion thresholds. Under specified conditions, institutional device restrictions are proposed to amplify adoption by channeling influence into richer face-to-face interaction. The framework is formalized in six testable propositions. Practical implications The study provides a Sleeper-Hit Risk Map assessing delayed diffusion candidacy, a phase-by-phase resource…

title: BÜDCƏ SİYASƏTİN REALLAŞDIRILMASI NƏTİCƏSİNDƏ VERGİ POTENSİALININ FORMALAŞMASI
abstract: Məqalədə büdcə siyasətinin həyata keçirilməsi nəticəsində vergi potensialının formalaşması məsələləri araşdırılmışdır. Büdcə siyasətinin iqtisadi inkişafın təmin edilməsində, dövlət gəlirlərinin artırılmasında və vergi bazasının genişləndirilməsində rolu təhlil edilmişdir. Dövlətin fiskal siyasət vasitəsilə iqtisadi proseslərə təsir mexanizmləri, büdcə xərclərinin strukturunun vergi potensialına təsiri və Azərbaycanda həyata keçirilən büdcə islahatlarının nəticələri yerli alimlərin elmi yanaşmaları əsasında qiymətləndirilmişdir. Tədqiqat nəticəsində müəyyən edilmişdir ki, səmərəli büdcə siyasəti vergi potensialının artırılmasının əsas iqtisadi alətlərindən biridir. Açar sözlər: büdcə siyasəti, vergi potensialı, fiskal siyasət, dövlət maliyyəsi, büdcə gəlirləri.
venue: ENECO-Proceeding of Energy Economic Research Center

title: MÜƏSSİSƏLƏRİN RƏQƏMSAL SİSTEMƏ İNTEQRASİYASI ŞƏRAİTİNDƏ İNNOVATİV İDARƏETMƏ MEXANİZMLƏRİNİN FORMALAŞMASI
abstract: Müasir dövrdə qloballaşma və sürətli texnoloji transformasiyalar biznes mühitini köklü şəkildə dəyişərək vahid rəqəmsal ekosistemin formalaşmasına zəmin yaratmışdır. Belə bir dinamik şəraitdə müəssisələrin rəqabət qabiliyyətinin qorunması və davamlı inkişafının təmin edilməsi, onların daxili biznes proseslərini innovativ idarəetmə mexanizmləri əsasında yenidən qurmasından asılıdır. Tədqiqatın əsas məqsədi müəssisələrin rəqəmsal ekosistemə inteqrasiyası prosesində qarşıya çıxan çağırışları təhlil etmək və effektiv idarəetmə modellərinin formalaşması yollarını müəyyənləşdirməkdir. Məqalədə ənənəvi iyerarxik idarəetmə strukturundan çevik (Agile) modellərə keçidin zərurəti əsaslandırılmış, verilənlərə əsaslanan (Data-driven) qərarvermə mexanizmlərinin əhəmiyyəti araşdırılmışdır. Eyni zamanda, açıq innovasiya strategiyalarının daxili korporativ mədəniyyətə inteqrasiyası mexanizmləri təhlil olunmuşdur. Aparılan tədqiqat nəticəsində müəyyən edilmişdir ki, rəqəmsal ekosistemdə uğurlu fəaliyyət sadəcə texnoloji infrastrukturun yenilənməsini deyil, həm də strateji idarəetmə metodologiyasının fundamental transformasiyasını tələb edir. Burada əsas hədəf rəqəmsal platformalar şəraitində müəssisələrin şəbəkələşmə prinsiplərinə əsaslanan inteqrasiya modelinin təklif edilməsidir. Açar sözlər: rəqəmsal ekosistem, innovativ idarəetmə, biznes proseslər, çevik idarəetmə (Agile), korporativ transfo…

title: İSTEHSAL HEYƏTİNİN İNKİŞAFINDA KARYERA İDARƏÇİLİYİNİN ROLU: MÜASİR YANAŞMALAR VƏ PERSPEKTİVLƏR
abstract: Məqalədə müasir istehsal müəssisələrində istehsal heyətinin inkişafında karyera idarəçiliyinin rolu araşdırılır. Texnoloji dəyişikliklərin sürətlənməsi, istehsal proseslərinin rəqəmsallaşması və əmək bazarında kompetensiyalara olan tələblərin dəyişməsi müəssisələrdə insan kapitalının davamlı inkişafını zəruri edir. Bu şəraitdə karyera idarəçiliyi işçilərin peşəkar potensialının müəyyənləşdirilməsi, kompetensiyalarının inkişaf etdirilməsi, daxili mobilliyinin təmin olunması və gələcək vəzifələrə hazırlanması vasitəsi kimi çıxış edir. Məqalədə karyera idarəçiliyinin nəzəri əsasları, ənənəvi və müasir yanaşmalar, istedadların idarə edilməsi, kompetensiya əsaslı inkişaf, fərdi inkişaf planları, mentorluq, varislik planlaşdırılması və rəqəmsal HR alətlərinin istehsal heyətinin inkişafına təsiri təhlil edilir. Eyni zamanda istehsal müəssisələrində karyera idarəçiliyinin təkmilləşdirilməsi istiqamətləri müəyyənləşdirilir. Tədqiqatın nəticələri göstərir ki, karyera idarəçiliyinin strateji insan resursları siyasəti ilə inteqrasiyası istehsal heyətinin peşəkar potensialının inkişafına, daxili kadr ehtiyatının formalaşmasına və müəssisənin dəyişən texnoloji tələblərə uyğunlaşmasına şərait yaradır. Açar sözlər: karyera idarəçiliyi, istehsal heyəti, insan kapitalı, karyera inkişafı, istedadların idarə edilməsi, daxili mobillik, varislik planlaşdırılması, rəqəmsal HR.
